title: Bills Declare Dalton Kincaid Ready to Go, Scratch Top Cornerback vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills tabbed two key starters as questionable to face the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.
As it turns out, one is suiting up while the other is sitting for the 8:20 p.m. ET holiday kickoff in Orchard Park.
Bills' tight end Dalton Kincaid is active, but cornerback Christian Benford will miss his second game in a row due to a groin injury suffered on November 15 against the New York Jets.
Benford headlines the list of six gameday scratches with the Bills dressing 48 players for the Week 12 home game. Three rookies are amongst the inactives with wide receiver Skyler Bell, safety Jalon Kilgore and offensive tackle Jude Bowry all sitting.
Veteran defensive tackle Greg Gaines and edge rusher Mike Danna round out the list. Danna will not dress against his former team with whom he won two Super Bowls.
Prior to submitting their inactives, the Bills announced a game day elevation for practice squad cornerback Kani Walker. The undrafted rookie will presumably provide insurance in Benford's absence.
When Benford was inactive in Week 11 , the Bills deployed practice squad veteran Tre'Davious White against the Miami Dolphins on November 22. While White gets spared for having to play a second game in five days, Walker will make his NFL debut. Maxwell Hairston will presumably earn the start at outside cornerback opposite second-round rookie Davison Igbinosun.
Kincaid missed a game for the first time this season this past Sunday after injuring his thumb in Week 10. The Bills played a lot more 11 personnel (three WR sets) as a result.
In last year's 28-21 home win over the Chiefs, Kincaid caught all six of his targets for a game-high 101 yards and one touchdown.
Over nine games this season, Kincaid has 32 receptions for 487 yards and two touchdowns.
On the other side, the Chiefs will be without a key offensive weapon . Running back Kenneth Walker, the Super Bowl LX MVP, is out with a groin injury.

title: Josh Allen Has Feasted in Three Career NFL Thanksgiving Games, Will He Eat Again vs. Chiefs?
full_text:
Buffalo Bills ' quarterback Josh Allen has shown the tendency to shine when the lights are brightest.
Over 15 career playoff games, the five-time MVP finalist has 39 total touchdowns. And when it comes to high-stakes regular season games, Allen is just as good.
Set to write another chapter in the rivalry between AFC juggernauts on Thanksgiving night , Allen owns a 5-1 record against the Kansas City Chiefs. He averages 282.4 pass yards per game excluding the lone loss from 2020. Over that six-game span, Allen has passed for 11 touchdowns and rushed for five touchdowns.
"It feels like we've played them every year since I've been here," said Allen on Tuesday. "But it's a great opponent. Obviously, a historic quarterback on the other side in Pat [Mahomes]. They've got some unbelievable players on the defensive side, too. You gotta play your best to beat this team."
When it comes to playing on Thanksgiving, Allen has already done so thrice in his NFL career with the Bills winning all three games on the road.
In somewhat of a national statement game, Allen and the Bills moved to 9-3 overall by handling the Dallas Cowboys, 26-15, in 2019. He went 19-of-24 passing for 231 yards, one touchdown and a 120.7 quarterback rating. The dual threat added 43 yards and one touchdown on the ground.
Allen made multiple iconic plays against the Cowboys. There was the 4th-and-1 conversion at the Dallas 30 where Allen fumbled the snap but grabbed it out of scrum and plowed forward for a three-yard gain.
Earlier, he converted a 3rd-and-10 from his own 2. Allen stepped up in the end zone and fired a seed to Cole Beasley over the middle for a 29-yard gain.
The Bills cruised past the New Orleans Saints, 31-6, in a 2021 Thanksgiving night game. Allen finished 23-of-28 passing for 260 yards and four touchdowns. He added 43 yards rushing.
In 2022, Buffalo was pushed to the brink by the Detroit Lions, but prevailed, 28-25. Allen  accounted for 331 yards of total offense and three touchdowns (2 pass, 1 rush).
With 00:23 remaining in a tie game, Allen made an unbelievably impressive throw to Stefon Diggs for a 36-yard gain into Lions' territory. The quarterback picked up 12 more yards on the ground to set up a 45-yard game-winning field goal by Tyler Bass.
2022 at Lions: 57.1 completion pct., 253 pass yards, 2 TD passes, INT, 80.8 QB rating, 78 rush yards, TD rush 2021 at Saints: 82.2 completion pct., 260 pass yards, 4 TD passes, 115.2 QB rating, 43 rush yards 2019 at Cowboys: 71.9 completion pct, 231 pass yards, TD pass, 102.7 QB rating, 43 rush yards, TD rush
Allen has played some of his best football against the Chiefs, and the Bills need him to step up again on Thursday night in Orchard Park. Despite cold, rainy weather , Buffalo's dual threat should be able to engineer his fair share of scoring drives against a Kansas City defense that has yet to be tested by a quarterback of Allen's caliber.
In a snow game against the Cincinnati Bengals last December, Allen passed for 251 yards and three touchdowns. He also ran nine times for 78 yards and one touchdown.
Allen has recorded at least one touchdown pass and one touchdown rush in five of 10 games against the Chiefs, including playoffs.
On the betting line, the Bills are a 3.0-point home favorite over the Chiefs ( per DraftKings ) for the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff on NBC. Sports Illustrated's expert panel is split on which team will prevail on November 26.

title: Buffalo Bills Must Be Wary of These Three Chiefs Rookies During Thanksgiving Game
full_text:
As the Buffalo Bills finish their Thanksgiving preparations, gameplanning for Patrick Mahomes the Kansas City Chiefs, special attention should be devoted to KC's 2026 draft class.
The Chiefs have leaned on the contributions of their first-year players on both sides of the ball, and Thursday night won't be any different.
Will their successful debut seasons continue? Or will the bright lights, big stage and stormy weather in Orchard Park be too much for the rookies? Here's which three Buffalo will need to look out for on turkey day.
Delane was drafted sixth overall for a reason. He's been one of the best rookies in the NFL, allowing a completion percentage of just 53.6% when targeted, per PFF. The LSU product has given up just one touchdown in coverage, while recording an INT and five pass break ups this season.
He has one of the best on ball grades in the league, quantifying how well he performes when targeted. His score, above the 90th percentile, is in line with some of the league's top corners like Denzel Ward, Trent McDuffie and Quinyon Mitchell.
Josh Allen would be wise not to force the ball downfield, especially if it's in Delane's direction.
With Kenneth Walker out of the lineup for the last two weeks, Johnson has taken full advantage of the opportunity.
On the first 34 touches of his career, he forced 21 missed tackles , giving KC a preview of what was to come. In just those two games without Walker, he's produced 206 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground, and 10 catches for 108 yards and two touchdowns through the air.
With Walker slated to miss another game, Johnson will be leaned on heavily to produce for the offense.
KC's rookie edge rusher from Oklahoma hasn't produced much on the stat sheet, with just one sack in his first campaign. But hte advanced analytics say there's more to his play than what's in the box score.
Thomas is 15th in the NFL in pass rush win rate, with 27 wins on 121 plays (22% win rate). Those wins have turned into 22 QB pressures, 18 hurries and a batted pass. He's also tallied seven defensive stops in the run game, per PFF.
Dion Dawkins and Spencer Brown will need to be ready for the speedy edge rusher on Thursday night, and using Dawson Knox or Jackson Hawes to help chip could be a good solution.

title: Panthers Have Important Question to Answer Behind Tetairoa McMillan
full_text:
Tetairoa McMillan didn't sound concerned about his foot injury today. The Carolina Panthers have to prepare in case they play without their top receiver on Monday night against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, though.
McMillan stated he was "good" when asked about the foot injury that he suffered during the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens. McMillan was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's estimated injury report, although the Panthers did not hold a practice that day.
While Canales has been optimistic about McMillan's chances of playing in the Panthers' game on Monday night, Carolina's top receiver could be limited or even out of the game.
Coker is already showing he can be productive in the passing game for Carolina and would likely be the player to step up and receive more targets in the event of McMillan's absence.
Coker was checked for a possible concussion after the win over Baltimore, but he was later cleared. That puts him in position to take on a larger role if McMillan can't play. The Panthers also got positive news on Coker following the Ravens game.
John Metchie III is another experienced option for the Panthers in the passing game. McMillan's production won't be easy to replace, but Metchie can help distribute the load to the rest of the receiving core.
If McMillan can't play, Young will have to find other ways to move the ball through the air. He has built a strong connection with McMillan, so losing that option would put more responsibility on the rest of the receiving group.
Legette is another player who could benefit from McMillan's absence. He is back after dealing with a knee injury, but hasn't produced much this season, recording just two catches for 64 yards. Monday could give him a chance to become more involved, especially if the Panthers need another receiver who can make plays downfield.
Coker has already shown he can make plays alongside McMillan, and that could become important if the rookie receiver can't go. He would likely get more chances to work with Young, while Metchie and Legette could also see their workloads increase.
It won't be an easy adjustment for the Panthers. McMillan has become one of Young's favorite targets, and losing him would take away a big part of what Carolina wants to do offensively. The other receivers will have to make the most of their opportunities against Tampa Bay.
McMillan still believes he's good, and the Panthers are hoping that's the case. His availability will become clearer once he gets back on the practice field. Until then, Carolina has to be ready for either possibility.
Their connection was also discussed in an earlier look at how the two receivers fit into the Panthers' offense.

title: Panthers Have a Major Advantage They Didn't Have During Last Year's Playoff Push
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are about to embark on a crucial stretch of their season, and this season’s team is different from last season’s team in one important way: it has experience.
In last season’s run to the playoffs, only two players on Carolina’s roster had appeared in a postseason game with the Panthers. This season, 25 players on Carolina’s roster have postseason experience with the organization, and 38 players on the Panthers’ roster have played in a postseason game during their NFL careers.
With the Panthers trying to build on last season’s success, that experience could be a major positive for the team as it heads into a meaningful December. Carolina is no longer trying to figure out how to play in meaningful December games.
There are a lot of differences between this year’s roster and the one that was on the field last season for Carolina’s playoff push. Only two players on last season’s roster had any postseason experience with the organization: long snapper JJ Jansen and offensive tackle Taylor Moton.
Now, that group includes several of the team’s most important players. Bryce Young , Derrick Brown, Chuba Hubbard, Robert Hunt, Damien Lewis, Mike Jackson, Tre'von Moehrig and Tetairoa McMillan are among the players who experienced the postseason with Carolina last year.
The group also includes young players like Princely Umanmielen, Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette. So, while veteran leaders are always nice to have, there are a lot of young guys on this team who have already experienced what it’s like to play in the postseason.
The fact that the team has so many more experienced players doesn’t guarantee another playoff run for the Panthers, but it does mean there are many more players on this team who understand what the organization is trying to achieve.
Carolina Panthers defensive tackle Derrick Brown knows how important this part of the season is. The Panthers are 5-5 and have a chance to put themselves in a great position for the rest of the season. Teams can start off very well in September and October, but that doesn’t mean they’ll make the playoffs.
In terms of Carolina’s remaining schedule, the Panthers still have several division games, which could put the team in a great position to separate itself in the NFC South.
Coach Dave Canales recently discussed the value of having players on the roster who have experienced a playoff game at home and the excitement that surrounds playing in the postseason. Canales noted that the players on the roster are motivated by the chance to play in the postseason again.
That experience can shape the way players prepare for the upcoming weeks. Canales wants his team to prepare for each division game as if it is a playoff game.
One of the greatest things to come from last season’s playoff run was that the team learned how to handle the ups and downs of a long season.
Bryce Young, Carolina’s quarterback, discussed in a recent press conference how Canales’ approach helps keep players focused on the task at hand instead of getting caught up in outside expectations.
This is going to be especially important as the team approaches the final stretch of the season and every game means so much in terms of the division. The team experienced adversity last season and still managed to make the playoffs. The players also know how quickly things can change and how much momentum they can lose with just one loss.
This is a different team than last year. There is more postseason experience on this team, and some of the key players from last season’s playoff run are now leaders on this team.
The team still has a lot of work to do to get back to the postseason, but it is better equipped to handle the pressure of the remaining games on the schedule than last year’s team was.

title: Panthers Lose Another Offensive Lineman for Season as Unexpected Development Offers Hope
full_text:
Carolina Panthers offensive lineman Brady Christensen will not be able to return to the team this season after his 21-day practice window expired without the team activating him from injured reserve on Tuesday.
Christensen was designated to return from IR on Nov. 3 after suffering a hamstring injury. He will revert to injured reserve for the remainder of the season, leaving the Panthers without a versatile veteran offensive lineman who can play multiple positions.
That being said, the decision not to activate Christensen is not as dire as it would have been a few weeks ago, as the Panthers’ offensive line is starting to show signs of life.
The deadline has come and gone and the #Panthers are not acting OL Brady Christensen to the active roster. Christensen was Designated to Return on Nov. 3, but he will now revert to Injured Reserve for the remainder of the season.
The Panthers had been playing without some of their top linemen for several weeks, including Damien Lewis, Corey Bullock and Torricelli Simpkins III. Taylor Moton was placed on season-ending injured reserve on Oct. 26 .
Christensen would have given Carolina another option because of his ability to play guard, center and tackle during his Panthers career.
According to head coach Dave Canales, several players have returned from injury, and Stone Forsythe is now the Panthers’ backup at both tackle positions. Canales said the Panthers are in a good spot as far as offensive line depth is concerned.
His comments indicate that the Panthers’ situation is better than it was when Christensen’s 21-day practice window opened.
Another positive sign for the Panthers is the recent play of Robert Hunt. The veteran guard has had a rough start to the season, but offensive line coach Joe Gilbert recently said Hunt was starting to get more comfortable playing alongside rookie Monroe Freeling. Gilbert previously discussed Hunt's adjustment to playing beside Freeling.
Gilbert also said Hunt had improved over the previous couple of weeks, and that progress has started to show up on the field in recent games.
Hunt’s overall grade of 80.6 against the Ravens on Nov. 22 was the second-highest among Panthers offensive players. His 85.5 run-blocking grade was the best among Carolina's offensive players in the game.
Though Hunt’s season stats are still below average, his recent play is a good sign for the Panthers. Hunt can play at a high level and be a big help to the Panthers’ offensive line, which has been dealing with injuries and rotating players all season.
The Panthers are not suddenly in a perfect position up front. Christensen's absence removes another experienced option, and the group still needs to prove it can maintain consistency against stronger defensive fronts.
The recent improvement of Freeling and the progress of Hunt are positive developments for the offensive line as the Panthers look to continue improving as the season progresses. Carolina's offensive line has faced questions about its personnel and consistency throughout the season .
With Christensen reverting to injured reserve on Tuesday, Carolina will need more of the same from Hunt and Freeling as the team continues to develop as a unit.

title: Panthers' Defensive Changes Raise Questions About Ejiro Evero's Approach
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers recently named Todd Wash their interim defensive coordinator. Comments from second-year outside linebacker Princely Umanmielen offer some insight into the changes that have been made.
Umanmielen spoke about the differences between Wash's coaching style and that of former coordinator Ejiro Evero on Thursday. His comments offer some insight into the direction of the Panthers' defense.
"I think now we're trying to impose our will on the offense instead of trying to stop what they're doing," Umanmielen said in a video shared on X.
“I think now we’re trying to impose our will on the offense instead of trying to stop what they’re doing” -Princely #KeepPounding
Although he did not criticize Evero, his comments point to differences in the two coaches' approaches to defense. Those differences are worth considering, especially after the Panthers' defense struggled during the 2024 and 2026 seasons.
Evero was hired in 2023 to coordinate the defense for the Panthers. The defense had a strong first season under Evero, but things changed in 2024. The unit finished last in the league in points allowed that year. Dave Canales was named the new head coach of the Panthers in 2024 and retained Evero as defensive coordinator. The defense improved to 15th in points allowed in 2025, but struggled again this season.
Prior to their game in Week 8, the Panthers allowed opponents to score an average of 27.6 points per game and amass 349.6 yards of offense. Additionally, they were giving up 140.7 yards on the ground per game, which ranked 30th in the NFL.
The Panthers lost 43-13 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7 and 27-19 to the Green Bay Packers the following week. After those losses, the team let go of defensive coordinator Evero and defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley. They also named Wash as the interim defensive coordinator for the rest of the season.
There is only so much Wash can change at this point in the season with the roster he has available, considering there is still much of Evero's system in place.
Wash's first game as defensive coordinator was a 26-21 loss to the Denver Broncos. After that, they beat the New Orleans Saints 20-17 and the Baltimore Ravens 35-33. In the Ravens game, they allowed 157 yards on the ground and 421 total yards, but took the ball away three times. Umanmielen had 1.5 sacks in the game and looks to be developing into the player they need him to be. His performance was also highlighted in On SI's breakdown of the Panthers' win over Baltimore.
The Panthers may have been better off firing Evero sooner, as many of the issues plaguing the defense extended beyond him. With a number of injuries and personnel limitations, Wash may not have the luxury of time to fully implement his system with the defense.
Umanmielen’s comments about being proactive and not reactive to the offense were very telling. This is the mentality the Panthers defense must embody. They must be proactive in attacking the opponent’s offense, particularly the quarterback.
Under Wash, the Panthers defense has begun to show signs of improvement. Consistency is something the team needs, but Wash is bringing some much-needed change to the defense, as Umanmielen alluded to.

title: NFL Week 12 Expert Picks Reveal Panthers' Chances of Winning 3rd Straight
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have played some important games this season, but perhaps none of them are as important as this one. They visit the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with a two-game NFC South lead and hopes of revenge.
The Buccaneers whalloped the Panthers a few weeks ago in Charlotte, destroying them by 30. It was the ugliest game the Panthers have played all year by far. Now, they risk being swept and giving the Buccaneers a one-game deficit with the tiebreaker in hand.
On the Tampa side, their playoff hopes hang in the balance. This is basically a must-win for them, so it's hugely important for both teams. What are the experts saying?
CBS Sports analyst Pete Prisco has rarely picked the Panthers to win this year (or ever), and he's going with the Buccaneers to get a close 23-17 victory to remain alive in the NFC South .
"The Panthers can take a stronghold on the division with a victory here.  They come in with defensive issues, but the Bucs have problems in the passing game. So what gives? I think the Tampa Bay defense will play well here, and the Bucs will run it right at Carolina to win it like they did in the first meeting," he argued.
His CBS colleague John Breech is also taking the Buccaneers, but 23-20 this time. Here's how the Sports Illustrated staff is picking:
With low confidence, David Fucillo of SB Nation is taking the Panthers to topple the Buccaneers. At USA Today, Nick Brinkerhoff and Adam Kaufman are taking the Panthers. Jarrett Bell, Chris Bumbaca, Nate Davis, and Mike Middlehurst-Schwartz are all taking the Buccaneers.
At The Athletic , Chad Graff, Larry Holder, and Nick Kosmider are taking the Panthers, while Zach Berman, Jon Greenberg, Josh Kendall, Austin Mock, and Steven Louis Goldstein are picking the Buccaneers.
The picks are somewhat split, but clearly leaning towards the Bucs. This is the exact sort of game the Panthers lose. It's a team that isn't better than them and is below them in the standings that they could beat, but the Panthers inevitably play down to their level, let them hang around, and then lose.
But this is also the sort of game the Panthers inexplicably win. They're underdogs on the road. Most people don't believe in them. They got absolutely embarrassed by this team mere weeks ago, and that may not even do it justice.
The Panthers are healthier, without Ejiro Evero, and playing decently well right now . It's hard to predict this one, even if most are going with the Bucs on Monday night.

title: Cam Newton's Hall of Fame Case Is Complicated, and the Committee May Have Gotten It Right
full_text:
Cam Newton is one of the best players in Carolina Panthers history. However, his first year of eligibility for the Pro Football Hall of Fame was not as many predicted it would be.
Newton did not make the list of 52 players to advance in the voting process for the Hall of Fame Class of 2027. This means that, of the former Panthers players, only Steve Smith Sr. is still being considered.
It is definitely strange to see a former face of the NFL not make the first reduction of players being considered for Hall of Fame eligibility. Newton had an outstanding season in 2015 when he was awarded the NFL's MVP and led the Panthers to the Super Bowl after finishing the regular season with a 15-1 record.
Nevertheless, there are many questions regarding the overall strength and depth of his Hall of Fame credentials. Newton had one of the best seasons of any quarterback in NFL history in 2015. He became the first player to pass for over 30 touchdowns and rush for over 10 touchdowns in the same season.
That year, Newton passed for 3,837 yards with 35 touchdowns and ran for 636 yards with 10 touchdowns. Newton's contributions to the game should be recognized with Hall of Fame consideration.
Newton led the Panthers to a 15-1 record and a Super Bowl appearance. He lost Super Bowl 50 to the Denver Broncos. Newton, known for both passing and running the ball, created many headaches for opposing defenses.
He played at a level that no other quarterback had ever played at before. Newton's stats are very Hall of Fame-worthy.
Over the course of his 11-year career, he threw for 32,382 yards, 194 touchdowns and 123 interceptions. He also rushed for 5,628 yards and scored 75 touchdowns on the ground.
At the time his career ended, Newton held the record for the most rushing touchdowns by a quarterback with 75. This record has since been broken by Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills.
The main criticism of Newton's Hall of Fame candidacy is that he played only 148 games. Injuries hampered his career, and he was never able to repeat his MVP season of 2015.
Newton's high peak definitely warrants Hall of Fame consideration. However, his total body of work makes it difficult to make the case for his enshrinement.
Of the quarterbacks still being considered for the Hall of Fame Class of 2027, only Ken Anderson, Eli Manning and Ben Roethlisberger advanced to the group of 52. Newton did not make that list, despite having won the NFL's MVP award and appeared in a Super Bowl.
Newton wasn't excluded from the final voting stage. He simply didn't make the first reduction. This is especially telling since this is his first year of eligibility.
Many would argue that Newton deserved more consideration, especially when compared to the quarterbacks still under consideration. Newton deserves more consideration than many other candidates, considering his overall influence on the quarterback position as well as his individual accomplishments, which include an NFL MVP award.
Newton had one of the most exciting individual seasons in recent memory, but voters may feel Manning and Roethlisberger have better overall bodies of work to warrant election into the Hall of Fame. Manning won two Super Bowls and was named Super Bowl MVP in both. Roethlisberger won two Super Bowls as well and has better career stats than Manning. In voters' minds, Newton's comparatively short career may also be a negative when considering his candidacy.
It's possible Newton will get another chance to make his case in the future, but for now, voters have indicated they don't consider him to be a front-runner among candidates in this class.
Newton's career is one of the most entertaining and unique in the NFL and, therefore, Hall of Fame-worthy. Whether Newton deserves to be in the Hall of Fame is debatable, but the committee made the right decision for the time being with respect to Newton.
He won't be able to make his case again for quite some time. New voters on the committee may eventually consider Newton's long, productive career and recognize that there is plenty of merit to his candidacy beyond his peak. For now, however, the committee got this one right.

title: How Panthers Have Emulated 49ers’ Offense & Why It’s Hugely Important for the Future
full_text:
It's been an up-and-down season for the Carolina Panthers , who are 5-5 with clear holes on the roster, yet are in first place in the NFC South anyway. The defense is still a major work in progress, and the Panthers haven't won more than two games in a row, but one bright spot has emerged.
The offense has taken a step forward, now ranking 10th in the NFL at present, and showing growth from its biggest stars. Chuba Hubbard has been outstanding this season, having a career year thus far.
Through 10 games, Hubbard has eclipsed 1000 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns. The only other Panther to do so is Christian McCaffrey, who's now on the 49ers.
McCaffrey has sustained his success from Carolina and brought his production to a real contender, linking up with one of the best play callers in all of football, Kyle Shanahan.
Under Shanahan, the 49ers have had one of the best offenses in the NFL, and that hasn't changed this year, as the 49ers are No. 1 in scoring offense. That offense shone against the NFL's best defense in the NFL, scoring 35 points against the Minnesota Vikings.
Carolina's offense seems to take influence from the 49ers, especially with assistant coach Darrell Bevell on staff, who was under Mike McDaniel, who is from the Shanahan tree.
That influence will be extremely important soon, as the Panthers play the Vikings in Week 13.
ESPN's Ben Solak dropped his seven things he thinks he knows entering Week 12. One of those seven things was that the 49ers exposed the formula for attacking the Vikings' defense.
Running condensed formations, using the RB in the passing game, and throwing quick passes between the numbers. All things that the 49ers excel in, that Carolina does as well.
Minnesota's defense is ultra-aggressive and will bring the blitz early and often, so quick throws and passes to the running back in the flat will be key to keeping Carolina on schedule and sustaining drives.
With Hubbard's success this season, the formula is certainly feasible. That doesn't mean Carolina will execute as well as San Francisco did; Carolina has the No. 10 offense in the league, compared to San Francisco's No. 1.
That said, it's still the only game plan thats dominated Brian Flores' defense this season, and Carolina has the pieces to be able to try to succeed in similar fashion.
The game will be ugly, just as Minnesota wants it to be, but now, after Week 11, we know that the Vikings' defense can be exploited. Now the only question is whether Carolina can execute for four quarters to do so.

title: Panthers Can Deliver Major Blow to Buccaneers' NFC South Hopes With One Win
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are in a good spot to win the NFC South title once again, but they can’t start planning their celebrations just yet.
Currently, Carolina is 5-5 and leads the division by two games. Last week, they defeated the Baltimore Ravens 35-33. Meanwhile, Tampa Bay and New Orleans both lost. Atlanta was on its bye.
With seven games remaining, they have ample opportunity to secure the division title. Monday’s game against Tampa Bay is critical to achieving that goal.
Winning divisional games is crucial, and Carolina can do that on Nov. 30 when they play the Buccaneers on Monday Night Football.
This is a game Carolina would especially like to win, given that earlier this season they were beaten by Tampa Bay 43-13. At the moment, Tampa Bay owns the head-to-head advantage over the Panthers, so a win by Carolina would even the season series and remove that advantage.
The Next Gen Stats model by NFL.com suggests that prior to Week 12, the Panthers had a 56% chance of winning the NFC South. With a win over Tampa Bay, that number increases to 80%. Conversely, with a loss, it decreases to 41%.
If Carolina wins, Tampa Bay would be three games back with six games remaining on the schedule. At that point, the Buccaneers would be under considerable pressure to make up ground during the final weeks of the regular season.
In addition to Tampa Bay, the other two NFC South teams Carolina still has left to play are New Orleans and Atlanta.
Carolina already won both of those games earlier in the season. The Panthers played New Orleans in Week 10 and won 20-17. They played Atlanta in Week 2 and won 34-3.
Should these final games decide the divisional tiebreaker, the current division records are important. Carolina is 2-1 against NFC South teams, Atlanta is 1-2, New Orleans is 0-2 and Tampa Bay is 2-0.
Carolina can’t take any of these divisional opponents for granted just because of their records. This late in the season, teams are looking to overtake each other in the division.
Carolina has four games outside the NFC South remaining as well. They play Minnesota on the road in Week 13, and then host Cincinnati in Week 15.
They will play in Pittsburgh against the Steelers in Week 16 and in Carolina against the Seahawks in Week 17. These games will be further tests for the Carolina team to see if they can win games that will, more likely than not, come down to the final play.
The Panthers have shown they can compete in difficult situations, particularly with Bryce Young leading the offense late in games. However, the defense will need to become more consistent, and Carolina cannot continue relying on late-game heroics to get through the schedule.
Carolina can't depend on Young to bail them out each game. The defense came up with a big play to end the game against the Ravens to secure the win, but they gave up 421 total yards in the process.
To further increase their lead on the other teams in the NFC South, Carolina will need to win on the road against Tampa Bay in the next game. Currently, Carolina has a two-game lead on the rest of the division and has three games left against NFC South opponents.
Winning on Monday night would provide some breathing room for the Panthers’ playoff hopes.
No divisional team is out of the playoff race yet, but Carolina can make things very difficult for the rest of the division over the next few weeks.

title: Bryce Young Just Landed Ahead of Patrick Mahomes in Surprising NFL Ranking
full_text:
Bryce Young may not be considered one of the top quarterbacks in the NFL, but a recent statistic should bring some comfort to Carolina Panthers fans.
Steven Patton, a football analyst, posted a leaderboard ranking quarterbacks by their expected points added (EPA) per completion. Young is currently ranked seventh with an EPA of +0.79. Others further down the list include Patrick Mahomes (+0.76), C.J. Stroud (+0.74) and Dak Prescott (+0.73).
Young's placement on this list may seem ironic, considering some of the media coverage and commentary directed at the quarterback since he was drafted in the first round by Carolina. However, this is more evidence of the positive progress Young has made this season. His development has been a recurring topic, including in a recent look at Young's regression and continued progress.
EPA per Completion Leaders: 1. Trevor Lawrence (+0.94) 2. Brock Purdy (+0.88) 3. Drake Maye (+0.83) 4. Josh Allen (+0.81) 5. Jordan Love (+0.80) 6. Jared Goff (+0.80) 7. Bryce Young (+0.79) 8. Patrick Mahomes (+0.76) 9. CJ Stroud (+0.74) 10. Dak Prescott (+0.73) pic.twitter.com/00FVfTJoDc
Some of the other players ranked on Patton’s leaderboard include Brock Purdy at second with an EPA of +0.88, Drake Maye at third with an EPA of +0.83, Josh Allen at fourth with +0.81, and Jordan Love and Jared Goff at fifth and sixth, respectively, with an EPA of +0.80 each.
Young being ranked seventh is extremely positive, considering some of the quarterbacks mentioned previously on the list are widely considered among the best in the NFL.
One statistic used to evaluate quarterback performance is expected points added (EPA). Rather than just looking at standard quarterback stats like completions and yards, this statistic analyzes how each play changes a team's expected scoring outlook.
It’s important to note that this ranking doesn’t measure EPA on each quarterback dropback, which includes pass attempts, sacks and scrambles. Patton’s ranking of Bryce Young is specifically for completions.
This is one advanced quarterback statistic in which Young ranks ahead of several of the best players in the NFL.
Through Week 11, Young was among the best in the league with 2,651 passing yards and 18 passing touchdowns. He also had the 32nd-best completion percentage at 61.1%.
Young’s EPA per play ranked 17th, while his QBR ranked 15th.
Though those numbers don’t seem very impressive on their own, they provide some additional context for Young's ranking on Patton’s list.
Young completed 22 of 30 passes for 254 yards and two touchdowns in Carolina’s 35-33 win against the Baltimore Ravens.
That win helped the Panthers extend their win streak to two games and keep first place in the NFC South. Young has been clutch in the second half of games, making key plays that have helped the team win. More of those plays will be needed down the stretch. His ability to protect the football has also been a positive, as one recent statistical breakdown highlighted another encouraging part of his game.
In Young’s previous matchup against the Buccaneers, he was held to 163 passing yards, with one touchdown and two interceptions in a 43-13 loss.
This rematch provides the Panthers with an opportunity to extend their lead in the NFC South, and Young will need to improve on his previous performance to outduel Tampa Bay’s pass rush.
The EPA per completion ranking isn't the be-all and end-all of Young's standing among NFL quarterbacks. For now, though, being listed ahead of Patrick Mahomes, C.J. Stroud and Dak Prescott is a positive development Young can build on.
Young doesn’t need to outperform his opponents in every metric, but he must continue to make good decisions with the football and protect it while giving the team the big plays it needs on third and fourth down.
The Panthers' quarterback situation will likely be less of a liability moving forward if Young continues to play the way he has recently.

title: Have the Panthers Played on Thanksgiving? Full History and Potential Future
full_text:
On Thanksgiving, the NFL reigns supreme. It's been that way forever, and there are more games on the holiday than ever before. You can conceivably sit at the television and watch football the entire day, like it's a Sunday slate.
The Carolina Panthers aren't involved, though. They are going to play a rivalry game on Monday night rather than a holiday game on Thursday. So, Panthers fans will have to settle for the Lions, Cowboys, and other teams.
The Panthers have played on Thanksgiving once, and it was one of the most iconic games in their history. They dominated the Dallas Cowboys in 2015. The Cowboys, famously, play every Thanksgiving, so beating them on "their day," so to speak, was huge .
The undefeated Panthers won 33-14. Cam Newton threw for 183 yards and added 45 and a touchdown on the ground. The Panthers' defense picked off Tony Romo three times, and Kurt Coleman and Luke Kuechly each returned one for a score.
Perhaps that's why the Panthers haven't been on the holiday since. They crashed the party too hard. For now, that is the lone appearance on Thanksgiving, which is honestly pretty strange. Only the Jacksonville Jaguars (also a 1995 expansion team, weirdly) have never played. Otherwise, the Panthers have the least amount of Thanksgiving games.
Could they play on Thanksgiving again? Absolutely. Someday, they probably will. However, it is very strange that they haven't played on the holiday since 2015. In 11 seasons since then, they've faced the Cowboys six times, yet it never ends up on Thanksgiving.
The Panthers have faced the Lions six times as well, but it has never been on Thanksgiving. Carolina has also never gotten lucky with being picked as one of the non-guaranteed teams. The Lions and Cowboys play on the day every year, but other teams get picked by the NFL.
So, it stands to reason that one day, you'll be able to watch the Panthers on Thanksgiving. But it is odd that it has been so long since the last one and could be a while. The Panthers will play the NFC North sometimes and get the Lions added to the schedule some years. The same goes for the NFC East and the Cowboys.
So, when that happens, the Panthers might just get lucky and get to grace the Thanksgiving game for the second time in franchise history.

title: Bears Announce Colston Loveland Injury Update That Offers More Optimism Than Reports
full_text:
After multiple reports broke earlier in the day about the status of Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland's injury, the team has now provided its own update.
According to the Bears, Loveland is considered week to week with his knee injury, which confirms what ESPN's Courtney Cronin had reported earlier in the day.
"The Bears on Friday announced that tight end Colston Loveland is week-to-week with a knee injury that forced him to exit Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions," Larry Meyer of ChicagoBears.com said.
This is great news for Loveland, who suffered the injury on the Bears' second offensive series on Thursday.
It looked like Loveland might have suffered something catastophic at first after he was carted off the field and appeared to be in tears while holding a towel over his head, CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson said.
A pair of reports suggested Loveland was going to be placed on injured reserve, but clearly the Bears are keeping the door open for Loveland to avoid the dreaded list, which would force him to miss at least four games.
Earlier in the day, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the belief is Loveland will need a stint on injured reserve , which would force him to miss at least four games, but won't be lost for the remainder of the season.
"The knee injury that Bears TE Colston Loveland suffered on Thanksgiving vs. the Lions is expected to land him on injured reserve, which would sideline him a minimum of four weeks, per sources. There still is additional testing to be done, but the current belief is that Loveland could return later this season," Schefter said.
Then, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport revealed Loveland is dealing with a knee sprain and the hope is that he will be back before postseason play.
"Some optimism. A knee sprain for Loveland is the initial diagnosis, sources say. The hope is that Loveland is back right against the end of the season and ready for the playoffs," Rapoport reported.
Then, Cronin came through with a report that said Loveland is week-to-week and no decision on injured reserve has been made.
"Per league source, Bears tight end Colston Loveland is considered week to week with the left knee injury. He will get a second opinion soon but no determination on whether he is an IR candidate has been made," Cronin said .
Now, none of this is to say that Loveland will avoid injured reserve because being week-to-week leaves open that possibility, but clearly the situation isn't as definitive as Schefter said.
As we've discovered multiple times this season with Bears injuries, you just can't rest your laurels on what is being reported and it's important to wait it out until the team gives an update.
Regardless, everything we're seeing on Loveland confirms that the second-year tight end has avoided a season-ending issue and that's the biggest point to take away from all of it.

title: Where Bears' Epic Thanksgiving Game Ranks Among Recent Comeback Victories
full_text:
If there's one defining characteristic of the Chicago Bears in the Ben Johnson era, it's resiliency in the clutch. After going five games without trailing for a single second, the 'Cardiac Bears' made a cameo appearance on Thanksgiving, and they pulled off another thrilling comeback victory over the Detroit Lions , moving to 9-2 on the season and picking up a badly needed division win. It wasn't perfect, and the Lions exposed the Bears' glaring weaknesses , but it was a statement win nonetheless.
Some fans are calling that game the Bears' best comeback win of the last two years, but does it really take the top spot? Let's review five of Chicago's most improbable victories and see where it ranks.
The Ben Johnson era did not get off to a good start last year as the Bears started the season 0-2. They managed to get to 2-2 before their Week 5 bye, but only one of those wins was convincing. A win over the Washington Commanders, who were thriving at the time, would not only prove that they could win tough games, but would also avenge the infamous 'Fail Mary' loss in 2024 .
After recovering a Jayden Daniels fumble late in the fourth quarter, the Bears ran the ball to milk the clock, got into field goal range, and Jake Moody booted the walk-off field goal. It was a huge morale boost to the Bears that got one particularly huge monkey off their back.
What should have been a blowout win for the Bears turned into a nailbiter as they gave up a late touchdown, lost an onside kick attempt, and then gave up another touchdown to the Joe Flacco-led Bengals in the game's final minute, putting the Bengals ahead 42-41. That's when Caleb Williams took the field, and his journey to becoming the Iceman began.
Williams moved the Bears to midfield and called a timeout with just 25 seconds remaining. On the next play, he hit Colston Loveland right at the line where a field goal attempt would be feasible, but Loveland wasn't about to let the game come down to a field goal. He broke a tackle and outraced Cincinnati's defense to the endzone for the game-winning touchdown.
This is where I put Thursday's win. Some fans may disagree, and I understand the reasoning. This was arguably the highest quality win the Bears have had at any point over the last two years. They played complementary football and beat a Super Bowl contender on national television, and the Iceman's winning touchdown to Rome Odunze was picture-perfect. But there's two more games that, in my opinion, have been more impactful for the Bears, and I'm going to explain myself.
Beating the Lions is great, especially since Dan Campbell took over and turned them into a legit contender. But beating the Packers just means more, and that's what the Bears did last year in Week 16 in dramatic fashion. They scored 13 points in the fourth quarter to force overtime, including a sensational last-second, fourth-down touchdown pass to rookie Jahdae Walker.
In overtime, the Bears stopped the Packers on fourth down, and one of the greatest touchdowns in franchise history came next. On first-down at midfield, Caleb Williams went deep to DJ Moore in the endzone. Moore caught the ball with a defender draped across his back like a cape and secured the walk-off win.
He didn't drop the winning pass, but Moore did drop an iconic Bears-Packers rivalry quote moments later. And for that reason, alongside the intense drama and the weight of history, this comeback win ranks at No. 2 for me.
I don't think I need to say much to justify making the Bears' triumphant Wild Card victory over the Packers their best comeback win in recent history, or perhaps ever. We're talking about a playoff win at Soldier Field, ending a 15-year stretch without any playoff wins, and it came against their biggest rival.
Despite being down 21-3 at halftime, Caleb Williams put the team on his back and once again connected with DJ Moore for a go-ahead touchdown. The Packers had a chance to win as time expired, but Jordan Love's last-second pass into the endzone was broken up by Kyler Gordon, and the Bears advanced to the Divisional round.
It's going to take a Super Bowl victory to top this one, and the way the Bears are playing right now, that may not be far off.

title: Jeffery Simmons Issues Warning to 'Frontrunner' Lions Guard After Bears' Week 12 Win
full_text:
There is no doubt things got testy between the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears during the Week 12 game , as many players got into dust-ups throughout the contest, although thankfully none of them escalated into anything major.
As you'd expect, fiery Bears defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons was involved in some of those dust-ups. In fact, he might have had the earliest one in a little grabbing match with Lions tackle Penei Sewell in the first quarter.
But it's safe to say he won the mental battle on Thursday, as Lions players were frustrated with him and accused Simmons of trying to emulate Detroit's snap count , which is against the rules.
One of those players was Lions guard Christian Mahogany, who taunted Simmons during the game, drawing a flag.
Simmons called Mahogany a frontrunner and issued a warning for the second game between the NFC North rivals in Week 17.
“That’s what you call a frontrunner. He’s a big frontrunner. Half the time, I wasn’t even on his side, and he was just talking," Simmons said.
“When we get the opportunity to attack him — we’ll see him again, I’ll tell you that. After the game, he went missing. There’s a lot of frontrunners. We’ll see him again," Simmons said, according to Jason Lieser of the Chicago Sun-Times .
I would venture to guess that Simmons' warning has to do with his plan to line up across from Mahogany more the next time these squads face off.
After the game, Mahogany accused Simmons of emulating the Lions' snap count, which is believed to have led to center Juice Scruggs committing a false start multiple times in a short span.
Simmons wasn't flagged for that, but CBS announcer J.J. Watt wondered if that's what Simmons was doing to get Scruggs to jump, and an official approached him during the game for a sideline chat, although we don't know what was said.
“No b******* and complaining. We had self-inflicted wounds,” said Mahogany, according to Brad Galli . “The league can investigate.”
Simmons shot back at Mahogany, though, saying he did not do what he's being accused of. And, he made his own accusation, jokingly saying the Lions were "crying."
"It's a lot of crying on that side of the ball when that happened," Simmons said, according to CHGO Bears .
"As a defensive lineman, if the quarterback checks, I'm allowed to say, 'He checked into a run.' ... I mean, it's not my fault that your center jumped. I think that's literally the only time that I said somethins," Simmons added.
Simmons has only been with the Bears for four games , but he has already done a great job getting involved in the heated rivalry between Detroit and Chicago.
Simmons had his quietest game as a Bear on Thursday with just three tackles, including one for loss, and he didn't notch a sack, something he did at least once in each of the last three games.
But he was clearly very loud in the heads of the Lions, both during and after the game.

title: Bears Injury Woes Get Even Worse with Dayo Odeyingbo's Season-Ending Surgery
full_text:
Health is fast becoming a big problem for the Chicago Bears, a problem that could derail their Super Bowl aspirations. Nickel cornerback Kyler Gordon has missed the last two games after already missing the first five games of the season, and Colston Loveland's injury in yesterday's game looked serious. Now, Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune is reporting that Dayo Odeyingbo has received surgery that will end his season.
Odeyingbo left the Bears' disastrous Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers with a quadriceps injury. At the time, the latest injury update for Odeyingbo was that he'd 'miss some time' but wouldn't go on injured reserve. In the end, he did in fact go on injured reserve and now his season is over.
While the Bears have thrived in his absence, this is still a big loss. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen was counting on getting Odeyingbo back at some point to reinforce his defensive line, which is now precariously thin in depth. Plus, Odeyingbo had been putting together quite a bounce-back season. Entering Week 5, he was second on the team in sacks and pressures.
Adding insult to injury, this latest update is almost certainly going to get Odeyingbo released from the roster in the offseason. The cold, hard truth of the matter is that he hasn't come anywhere close to giving Chicago a return on its investment in him. Last year, Odeyingbo was a complete non-factor before suffering a season-ending Achilles injury in Week 9, and he needed a big season to convince the Bears to keep him around in 2027 and beyond.
He appeared to be on pace to do exactly that through the first month of 2026. He was living up to the 'Motivated Dayo' meme and helping the get out to a 3-1 start. Alas, another season-ending injury, combined with his albatross of a contract, makes his release all but assured.
Odeyingbo has just one year left on the three-year, $48 million contract he signed in March of 2025, and the Bears can free up $15 million worth of salary cap space in 2027 by cutting him, according to Over The Cap . The Bears are likely going to need every red cent of that money to keep the core of this roster together, especially after trading for superstar Jeffery Simmons .

title: Bears Weigh Tight End Options After Colston Loveland Was Carted Off vs. Lions
full_text:
Bears GM Ryan Poles needs to be doing his due diligence now as a result of the knee injury suffered by Colston Loveland.
The Bears haven't offered information yet on how severe the injury is but at the very best he'd be out for a while because he had to leave on a cart.
It's post-trade deadline, so options are extremely limited. They have two tight ends in Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson and can count on them in 12-personnel packages. Roush's five catches on Thursday for 31 yards proved big and show he can at least provide basic help.
"We’ll see if he needs to have a bigger role here going forward," coach Ben Johnson told reporters in Detroit after the game. "And then Carlson, I mean, when I first came to the building a year and a half ago, (tight ends coach) Jimmy Dray, he just pounded the table like, 'You’re going to love this guy.' He’s dependable. He does everything right, and we’re going to use him at some point.'
Stephen Carlson makin' plays 👀 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/db3HlWdlZa
"And here we go, in one of the biggest games that we’ve had in a year and a half, and he doesn’t miss a beat."
Carlson added two catches for 30 yards Thursday. Both will do fine in games, as they did Thursday.
"We're a next man up team," QB Caleb Williams said. "And I trust those guys. I mean, they got a couple passes today, a lot of passes I'd say of either checkdowns or going across the middle and in the flats and things like that. So like I said, I trust them.
Remember when fans questioned Sam Roush? Over the last three weeks, he leads all rookie Tight Ends in receiving EPA, catch rate, first downs per target, and drop rate. Already a top 10 run-blocking TE in the entire NFL, Roush is proving to be a promising piece that King Poles… pic.twitter.com/NotJ6UhDLn
"We get a lot of reps together throughout the training camp, throughout OTAs, and then throughout the weeks when guys are banged up or anything like that, they step up, they show out. And I think they did that today for us.”
The problem is, there really is no next man up now for third tight end unless they believe in practice squad tight end Qadir Ismail, who is a bit of a string bean as tight ends go at 232 pounds and 6-foot-6. The former Samford player has never appeared in an NFL game and has been with practice squads for Jacksonville, the Giants, the Raiders and the Ravens since 2024.
There is another option if he's healed and that's former Iowa tight end/fullback Hayden Large. He's been on injured reserve since Week 1 because of a core injury. He was known as a blocker and that would be ideal because it would complement both Carlson and Roush, but he has absolutely no experience.
Bears TE Hayden Large on an island with the Bengals' DE. pic.twitter.com/UzQMa4DjHB
Some teams might get by with playing two tight ends much of the time but the Bears are playing three tight ends at 14.9% of plays, the fourth highest rate in the NFL according to Sumer Sports analytics. The league average is 9.3%They don't do it very well, either as they rank 24th in rushing EPA and in passing EPA when in 13-personnel.
It's always possible to find an unsigned veteran journeyman but what they're looking for is a third tight end. There are no No. 1 tight ends sitting around waiting to come in now who could immediately help.  Former Seahawk Will Dissly, former Brown/Texan Jordan Akins and former Raiders tight end Albert Okwuegbunam. might be the best of that lot.  Dissly is the most accomplished of the group, and no doubt could fill the need. But Akins has been around a while and is 34.
Dissly has 188 career receptions for 1,999 yards and 15 TDs since 2018 but hasn't been with a team this season. He  had a shoulder injury at the end of last season and played only nine games for the Chargers.
Instead, raiding a practice squad looks like a potential option if they don't want to rely on Large or Ismail. This could supply a  player familiar with their offense or coaches, but the problem with raiding a practice squad is they need to immediately put this player on the 53-man roster and not their practice squad.
If he's inexperienced, this becomes an issue while he catches up.
Never getting over this Will Dissly BEAST MODE moment 😂 😤 @Will_Diss #Seahawks pic.twitter.com/6GWN4gRqS0
They had a ready-made option on Dallas' practice squad. James Mitchell played for Johnson in Detroit for a few years, but the Cowboys have added him to their 53-man roster and this protects him. Here are some other practice squad options to eye.
The former Packers and Georgia tight end is 6-7, 250, 26 years old. The Packers liked him enough to sign him to their 53-man roster off the Atlanta practice squad in 2024. He has 14 catches for 86 yards in 33 games and four starts, 12 for 72 last year in Green Bay. He's behind some good tight ends in KC. He's playing in Andy Reid's offense but for offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, the former Bears running backs coach.
Former Packers TE John FitzPatrick, who underwent surgery on a torn Achilles in late December, now has been cleared to resume all football activities by his surgeon, Dr. Martin O’Malley. The 26-year-old FitzPatrick remains a free agent.
The 6-6, 260-pounder has 29 career catches for 262 yards in four season, including three with Denver. He was a Bronco when former Bears offensive coordinator Declan Doyle was on staff there. He came into the league with New Orleans in 2022 undrafted when Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen was the Saints' head coach.
when coaches talk about "that dawg in him" that's kitan oladapo setting the edge on 260-lb. lucas krull pic.twitter.com/bivPSqePcs
Speaking of Doyle, he is Ravens offensive coordinator and his current team has a veteran who might be an ideal fill-in type. Vannett is 6-6, 261 and 33 years old. Nicknamed Baby Gronk -- there are about 20 Baby Gronks in the league aren't there? -- he was a Seahawks third-round pick in 2016 and has a career high of 29 catches with Seattle in 2018. He has played for the Rams and Vikings besides the Seahawks and Ravens. He has 108 catches for 1,012 yards and nine TDs.
Ravens Tight End Nick Vannett Signed to the 53 man roster last week. Did a very nice job climbing to level 2 and sealing off running lanes. pic.twitter.com/xlZPtTDR4Y
Stealing a practice squad tight end from their next opponent wouldn't be a bad idea. He's 6-5, 255 and the former Kentucky tight end has been with the Jets, Browns, Texans and Jaguars with eight career receptions. Although he's with Jacksonville now, he wasn't there when current Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor was there.
The Chicago Bears have a Tight End problem now with Loveland likely out for the foreseeable future. Ryan Poles should look to UFDA Brenden Bates. He's 6'5 255, a pretty decent blocker, & underrated athlete. Just rotting on Jaguars practice squad. Bates is better than Carlson rn.
If the Bears really wanted to tick off Detroit after beating them Sunday, they could sign Gordon. He was with the Bears in 2025 training camp, was released and added to the practice squad in December, then was released after the season. The former Northwestern standout is 6-4, 250. The Lions also have two other tight ends on their practice squad. Miles Kitselman, a rookie from Tennessee and Jackson Meeks, a first-year player from Syracuse.
The Detroit #Lions are signing TE Thomas Gordon to their practice squad, per source. Former #UFL Brahmas product, and Northwestern standout had a pair of catches this past preseason. Gordon is a versatile tight end who can block and catch at a high level.

title: Historically Bad Bears Defense Sufficient to Stop Mistake-Prone Lions
full_text:
Bears coach Ben Johnson finally got his first win over his former boss on Thanksgiving 39-35, and afterward Lions coach Dan Campbell had to admit his team helped the Bears out a good deal.
One of the culprits was Campbell himself.
The Lions' decision to go for first down on fourth-and-4 at the Bears 33-yard line with 2:22 to play with a pass to Jahmyr Gibbs in the flat was a sound play, but perhaps a questionable tactic. A field goal would have left the Bears behind 38-32 instead of 35-32, but T.J. Edwards made a spectacular open-field tackle on Gibbs for a 1-yard gain and set up his offense and Caleb Williams with good field position to start their final winning drive.
Campbell admitted to reporters he just didn't want to give Williams the ball back, and this triggered his gamble.
Without this T.J. Edwards stop — during an iconic Jahmyr Gibbs game, no less — that Bears GW drive almost certainly wouldn’t have happened, in which case Chicago would be 0-3 in the division. Tackle could have saved the Bears a chance at the NFC North. pic.twitter.com/5Ea4C9e1ZN
"I thought we'd get it, first of all," he said. "I really believed we were going to get that. But then yeah, if you don't, it incentivizes a little bit the four downs.
"You're playing more for a field goal, but if you get down fast enough, you'll have some shots at the end zone, which they did. So, I don't regret that. I wish we'd have made that, but listen, sometimes that happens.”
Edwards received a game ball from Ben Johnson afterward and that tackle was just what the Bears needed after Detroit's offense had a four-possession stretch with three TDs and a field goal. "I thought probably the biggest play there at the end probably was T.J. Edwards' fourth-down tackle," Johnson said. "I thought that was absolutely massive. He's steady Eddie himself, as always."
T.J. Edwards on his game saving 4th down stop: “You got to take your shot. Especially in this short yardage, game on the line. You got to go take your shot. I’d rather die by throwing everything out there than sitting and letting him make a play.” pic.twitter.com/vSyUC02B4k
Edwards also deflected a pass Dillon Thieneman picked off with 5:34 left in the fourth quarter to set up the Bears for what looked like could be the needed points, but that drive fizzled on downs when Jahdae Walker couldn't hang on to a fourth-down Williams heave.
The Lions had other critical and stupid mental errors that fueled the Bears comeback. They had two taunting penalties, one on defensive tackle Anthony Lucas that didn't prove as critical but did set his team back 15 yards to start a fourth-quarter drive. The other was on Lions guard Christian Mahogany for taunting Jeffery Simmons after a trap block worked on Gibbs' 70-yard TD run.
That penalty forced the extra point back to the 48 and Lions kicker Jake Bates missed it. The kick easily would have been through from 33 yards but the extra yards allowed the kick to move outside the upright and leave the Bears within two scores at 35-24.
"Yeah, we had other penalties that killed drives offensively, but those taunting killed us too," Campbell said. "One of them, it changed the dynamic of the points because now you're going for two instead of just kicking a field goal, and now it changes the end of that game. But we talked about it, man, keeping your composure, and we didn't do that. We had two of them, and those hurt."
As it was, the Bears didn't need to worry about it because they scored two more touchdowns but it took some of the pressure off them on the final drive knowing they needed only a short field goal for the tie and overtime. And that situation resulted from the second penalty.
Campbell was asked by Detroit reporters if something done by the Bears caused several Lions penalties.
WOW: #Bears superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons fired back at the #Lions after being accused of mimicking their snap count and causing four false starts. “I DON’T HAVE TO CHEAT.” “IT’S A LOT OF CRYING ON THAT SIDE OF THE BALL.” 😳😳😳 pic.twitter.com/nvBtyIazSe https://t.co/2CCFC16p11
“I’m not discussing that," he said.
Lions players afterward accused Simmons of calling out snap counts to disrupt them. Something caused them to jump three times. Simmons was warned by officials but ultimately Detroit moved it anyway. The Lions' 549 yards were the third most ever allowed by a Bears defense.
"I don’t think that should be overblown," Lions QB Jared Goff told reporters about Simmons' tactics. "I think that happened a couple of times. The officials talked to them, and if they were trying to simulate the snap count, or if they weren’t, I don’t know. They can probably say they aren’t, and it’s impossible to officiate, and (officials will) never throw a flag on that.
"But it happens, this isn’t the first game it’s happened. We got to be able to handle that a little bit better than we did.”
It wasn't all the Lions needed to handle better. They couldn't handle Williams on the final drive, but they're not the first team to say this.
Goff’s pass is tipped and picked off by Dillon Thieneman! CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/5nsUkdGRx1

title: Salvon Ahmed is Turning Limited Bears Touches Into 2027 Free Agency Audition
full_text:
For all the various injury and inconsistency issues the Chicago Bears are facing at the running back spot behind D'Andre Swift on the depth chart, the team is certainly catching a break with Salvon Ahmed's emergence.
It's unclear what the Bears are going to do about Ahmed, though. After a 46-yard run during Chicago's third drive in a 39-35 win over the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving, Ahmed only got two more carries.
It's hard to tell if that means Ahmed isn't going to get a roster spot on the Bears before the end of the season. Having been elevated from the practice squad three times this season, Ahmed has to either stay on the PS or get a new contract.
Of course, that contract doesn't have to be with Chicago. Still, it'd be an interesting risk for another team to take on Ahmed with such few reps since his stint with the Miami Dolphins, which concluded in 2023.
Regardless of Ahmed's immediate future, his 108 yards over the past three weeks against the Lions, New Orleans Saints, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers has already served as an audition for 2027 free agency.
Ahmed was elevated this week because of Roschon Johnson's absence. Johnson left the team's 21-13 win over the New Orleans Saints with an ankle injury and was ruled out of the Thanksgiving Day clash at Ford Field.
Ben Johnson didn't seem too concerned about the injury after it happened, but it's clear that the last week or so didn't prove that Roschon Johnson could go. At least the coaching staff didn't seem to think so.
In a perfect world, Johnson would be able to return and serve as a seldom-used short-yardage back behind Swift and Kyle Monangai. Against Detroit, Monangai still didn't seem to have shaken off rust from missing five games with toe and thumb injuries .
Perhaps the offense has gotten what it's needed from Ahmed. There's still a chance that Ahmed snags a contract for the rest of the season if Johnson isn't back soon.
Whatever the case, it's clear that Ahmed isn't set up for a big role, and won't have one the minute Johnson is healthy again.
That won't matter for Ahmed's long-term future. Ahmed will earn a spot in someone's running back room during 2027 training camps, and may stop being mostly a practice squad player by next September.

title: Bears' 10-Day Mini-Bye Week is a Lifeline After Colston Loveland's Injury
full_text:
There's never a good time to lose one of your best offensive weapons. The Chicago Bears are a lot worse off after potentially losing tight end Colston Loveland for the rest of the season with a knee injury. Still, the 10-day mini-bye week may come in handy before the stretch run of Chicago's season.
Loveland was ruled out within 15 minutes of going down during a 39-35 win over the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on Thanksgiving Day. It's likely that the news on Loveland won't be good, but the medical team now has extra time to fully assess the damage.
Who knows? Maybe this is a Caleb Williams situation where the initial injury looked worse than what ends up being ruled. Bears fans everywhere are hoping for that, anyway. Well, maybe not all of the drama that came with the Williams situation .
At least the extra time gives this franchise more time to process this injury, regardless.
That's what makes what comes next for Ben Johnson easier.
Johnson wasted no time featuring 2026 third-round draft pick Sam Roush at the tight end position after Loveland went down on Thursday afternoon in the Motor City. Roush had five catches for 31 yards but was more of a factor as a blocker.
Veteran Stephen Carlson also got a look, hauling in two catches for 30 yards. Johnson spoke highly of both after the comeback win that featured both tight ends easing into their new roles nicely.
"Sam just continues to get better and better and better. I got a lot of confidence in him as a blocker. We saw him when we threw to him, I think he had five catches this game, and so he's become a security blanket there for our quarterback as well," Johnson said postgame .
"And then Carlson, he's dependable, he does everything right, in one of the biggest games that we've had in a year and a half, and he doesn't miss a beat."
You feel a lot less anxious about the Jacksonville Jaguars on December 6 with a week and a half for Johnson to figure out how to feature his tight end options without overexposing them. While the tight end position wasn't as featured earlier in the season with Williams out, it is now likely forced to be into the background with the natural downgrade in talent from Loveland and Cole Kmet .
Johnson can figure it out. He's navigated tough losses before. There's no reason to think he can't do it again.
When you hit tough times, you want a coach like Johnson to get you out of it without setting the franchise on fire at the press conference. When those tough times happen on a Thursday, and you have 10 days to figure it out with Johnson at the helm, you're very lucky.

title: The Iceman Returns With Late Bears Rally and Winning TD to Rome Odunze
full_text:
As Caleb "Iceman" Williams miracles go, this Bears win ranks right up just below the comeback playoff win over Green Bay.
It was probably only the distance between Rome Odunze's toes and the sidelines in the end zone on the game-winning catch away from being their best comeback, largely because of how much coach Ben Johnson needed it over his former team and the team needed an NFC North win.
A 39-35 comeback win on Odunze's 6-yard touchdown catch in the back right corner to end a 68-yard, 13-play drive extended the Bears' winning streak to six, made them 9-2 and gave them first in the division. It also further cemented the Iceman's comeback legend.
They persisted with rallies back from deficits of 10-0, 19-10, 26-17, and finally 35-24 in the final 8:24.
Caleb Williams: "That's me. I'm too cold.” ❄️ pic.twitter.com/2OjgsPXVyr
"It's a little bit unique because we have not had one of these this year, not quite like this at least," Johnson told reporters afterward, thinking back to last year's seven fourth-quarter comebacks. "And so, it's good to know we've still got that tool in our arsenal."
Williams cooly, methodically pushed the ball downfield in Iceman fashion. It even started to look like they were going to waste too much clock on their final drive the way they had in Matt Eberflus' final game as Bears coach two years earlier. But the pass on third down from the 6 gave the Bears their only lead of the day.
They persisted despite losing Colston Loveland to a knee injury early and giving up nine points on a safety and ensuing TD just before halftime to fall behind two scores. Then, when it appeared they had reeled in the Lions after a day of rallying, Jahmyr Gibbs delivered a crushing 70-yard TD run en route to his 205-yard rushing day.
🚨 TRENDING: DAN CAMPBELL IS GOING TO HAVE A VERY LONG NIGHT! DETROIT FANS ARE NOT GOING TO FORGET THIS ONE! 😳🤦‍♂️ The Lions had this game RIGHT IN THEIR HANDS, but questionable clock management, costly decisions and missed opportunities allowed the Bears to pull off an…
However, Williams hit Odunze right away with a 41-yard TD pass and ran in the two-point conversion. They were poised for the comeback and finished it on Odunze's second TD catch.
"Late in games you go to matchups, late in games you go to your guys and i think that was one of those moments that I felt good," Williams said. "I told Rome that I was going to keep coming back to him. I ended up missing him early in the game, or earlier in the game, I ended up checking it down to Sam (Roush).
"But I told Rome I'd come back to him and having that faith, having that belief in each other and it showed up in big moments today."
Rome Odunze. CLUTCH CATCH 😤 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/9s0sSOYwBu
Williams went 30 of 44 for 345 yards as the running game wasn't reliable enough all day to consistently move it, D'Andre Swift gaining 65 on nine carries with a TD. However, Swift was the reason the passing game opened up as Williams started throwing it too the outside and to his backs. Swift finished with seven receptions for a career-high 97 yards, Odunze with six for 87 yards.
Johnson said Odunze wasn't even the primary receiver on the game-winning pass.
"Rome and I, we've thrown that route in practice with the clock winding down so many times," Williams said. "For us we've put ourself in that situation so many times mentally and physically and we take it extremely serious."
Absolutely love they keep the Madden tradition going.  Got to love that Turducken #Bears #Lions #CHIvsDET #MaddenThanksgiving pic.twitter.com/NDm3Dbis6O
The win couldn't erase all of the problems they had throughout, especially two first-half lost fumbles -- their 10th and 11th of the year. They came into the game tied for third in fumbles.
The injury to Loveland going forward at a minimum means temporarily trying to run an offense requiring two or three tight ends with rookie Roush, Stephen Carlson and anyone's guess on the third guy.
Here’s where the Turducken came from and how it’s made pic.twitter.com/q3JSVqcES6
The running game continues to sputter as Swift had 65 yards but they had 46 of their 146 yards on one run by practice squad player Salvon Ahmed.
However, those problems seemed to all vanish when they got to share the traditional Thanksgiving Madden turducken, then saw Johnson's "stanky legg" in one of their most jubilant celebrations.
"Once again, it's a credit to our guys just being able to weather that storm," Johnson said. "We talked about adversity last night, (it) was going to happen in this game. It's too good of a team for them not to make a lot of plays themselves. And they did that.
"And yet, our guys were able to stay the course and nobody panicked."
D’Andre Swift breaks free for a 30-yard touchdown! CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/vSL3VFjIMk

title: The Glaring Bears Weaknesses That Beating the Lions Didn't Cover Up
full_text:
Not to be a downer, but the Chicago Bears didn't exactly look dominant in a 39-35 win over the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on Thanksgiving day.
By any stretch, Chicago proved contender status in taking the NFC North divisional lead with 11 games down and six to go. Still, the Bears' leaky defensive performance and familiar struggles in the offensive trenches prove that 9-2 doesn't automatically mean this is a championship season.
Chicago has these three glaring weaknesses to address before booking any parades down LaSalle Street:
The Bears traded for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons before the trade deadline to address the team's run defense.
Simmons himself has drawn plenty of double-teams, so the issue have been on his teammates' inability to plug gaps. Thursday was a particularly rough day for the interior defensive trenches against Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs.
Gibbs had 205 yards and three touchdowns on the ground, finding success between the tackles all afternoon.
Being so vulnerable against the run, especially with a secondary that's prone to big games from opposing quarterbacks, is not where Dennis Allen wants this group to be.
Theo Benedet is seriously struggling to protect quarterback Caleb Williams' blindside in pass-protection this season. It may only be a matter of time before Ozzy Trapilo is given the nod at the left tackle spot after Benedet had his worst game of the season in Detroit.
Benedet gave up multiple instant pressures and was responsible for a sack in the second quarter. Granted, he was battling a quad issue from the team's 21-13 win over the New Orleans Saints this past Sunday, but Benedet didn't look capable of the responsibility.
Ben Johnson cannot keep relying on Williams' shiftiness to evade pressure created by Benedet getting burned right after snaps.
This isn't a self-inflicted wound. Chicago is experiencing an unbelievable string of bad luck in the tight end room after Colston Loveland's potentially season-ending knee injury . The Bears already lost Cole Kmet to a season-ending knee injury earlier this season.
Rookie Sam Roush looked capable in the snaps he got after Loveland was carted off the field, while veteran Stephen Carlson could be a reliable body in a pinch. Johnson spoke highly of both postgame and indicated that they'd factor into the offense in some form moving forward.
Still, one of Chicago's strongest positions has become a weakness until further notice. It's on Johnson to make sure that narrative doesn't stick.
