title: 'Spent A Lot Of Quality Time With Fiona' - Barrett Carter Unveils Special Cleats Honoring Fallen Hippo
full_text:
The Bengals have a really cool My Cause My Cleats design hitting the field this weekend against the Saints. Starting linebacker Barrett Carter is rocking a purple Hippo Cove cleat set featuring fallen Cincinnati icon and Zoo star, Fiona The Hippo , who passed away last week.
The beloved animal was named Cincinnatian of the Year by CityBeat readers multiple times this decade. Sadly, she ingested a knit hat that got into the Hippo Cove enclosure accidentally and was unable to pass it through her complex digestive system.
The exhibit has since reopened with Fiona's family members back on display to the public and all of the dangerous features of the exhibit removed. The Cincinnati Zoo got rid of the ceiling fans that launched the hat and put a mesh blocker in the gap where it went through.
Carter loves the zoo and has personally met Fiona inside her enclosure multiple times.
"I'm Barrett Carter, and this is my cause, my cleats. This is my first time seeing them. Surreal, honest reaction. I'm excited to see what all went into making these cleats. So let's get into it," Carter said before revealing the beautiful design. "Wow, these are so nice! Wow, I look. Oh my God, I can't even.
"This is near and dear to my heart. Spent a lot of quality time with Fiona, so hearing the news that she passed was really, really heartbreaking for me. Really unfortunate news, and sad to see her go. But I know that she's in a better place now. So I'm glad that I can wear these cleats in honor of her, and just show my support, my continued support, and know that we're always going to be thinking of her."
Just a tragic, tragic event for the City of Cincinnati and the Cincinnati Zoo, which was expecting to house and feature Fiona for decades to come.
According to A-Z Animals , Hippos typically live between 40-50 years in captivity. Fiona was nine years old.

title: Zac Taylor Drops Dalton Risner's Game Status Entering Week 12 Saints Matchup
full_text:
The Bengals returned to practice on Black Friday after celebrating Thanksgiving. No new injuries are popping up in the Friday update from Zac Taylor, but things are still murky surrounding Dalton Risner and his knee injuries.
He was a projected DNP in the Wednesday walkthrough and did not suit up on Friday. Things aren't trending in a great way for him to return from a one-game absence, and Taylor said he will be out for Sunday's game against the Saints.
"Zac says Dalton Risner is out this week but is truly day to day, so could be in play for Cleveland," Our Jay Morrison posted on X .
Risner is the only major starter to worry about right now as Cincinnati could return WR3 Andrei Iosivas to the field. They are not worried about Bryan Cook after he left the Commanders' loss briefly on Monday night.
"I think he's sore," Taylor said bout Cook on Wednesday. "So again, he may be a little limited. Again, I keep saying don't read too much into today because I don't know how it shakes out in the walkthrough. If he'll take every rep or not, but he finished the game, and so we'll just continue to see how he progresses each day. But right now I feel pretty good about it."
Cincinnati is still dealing with a thin defensive end room due to Cashius Howell's injury, and fans would love to see Shemar Stewart start getting some chances to prove his worth.
He has played just 52 snaps this season.
"He'll bounce back. He'll bounce back. Look, it's the NFL, man," Bengals defensive coordinator Al Golden said this week about Stewart. "We had chances to close out, and we didn't close out, and you can't let a team like that linger. We saw it versus Seattle. We saw it in their game versus the Giants, their game versus LA."
Cincinnati got even further away from the AFC's No. 1 seed over the holiday after Buffalo stayed at one loss by beating the Chiefs 13-10 at home on Thursday night.
Full focus is on the AFC North for Cincinnati as they try to win the division as the current leaders for the first time since the 2022 season.

title: Bengals Should Regret Not Making Trade Deadline Move After Latest Loss
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals came into their Monday night matchup with the Washington Commanders riding the wave of an emotional win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Unfortunately, Zac Taylor's team couldn't keep the good vibes going.
In a rain-soaked prime time affair, the Bengals watched as Commanders kicker Drew Stevens drilled a 26-yard field goal to shock the leader of the AFC North, 22-20. The Bengals had plenty of chances to secure the road victory, yet they dropped one that would have been massive in keeping up with the other leaders of the AFC.
The Bengals' last offensive drive was a nightmare. Quarterback Joe Burrow nearly threw an interception on a second down, then took an untimely sack on third down that left the team settling for a field goal. Putting this game away would've meant finding the end zone. Something the Bengals may struggle to do moving forward with their current rushing attack.
It was no surprise that the Bengals had the ball in Burrow's hands when it came to crunch time. However, it would still be nice if the MVP candidate could trust his run game to have some kind of pulse in a moment like this.
The Bengals finished Monday night's loss with 31 rushing yards. Yes, 31. Weather can't be the excuse because, on the other side, the Commanders had 150 rushing yards.
The running game was a problem before last night, but in the spotlight, it proved that the Bengals' struggle to get anything going on the ground could cost them any chance at a Super Bowl dream.
Shawn Syed shared that the Bengals' run game produced a first percentile EPA/designed rush and below a first percentile rushing success rate on Monday night.
As a team, the Bengals don't even have 800 yards rushing on the season. The Green Bay Packers are the only other team in the league that hasn't rushed for 800 yards.
There was a lot of talk about whether or not the Bengals would add a running back before this year's trade deadline. The team decided they were okay with Chase Brown and Samaje Perine continuing to lead the unit, and sadly, these are the results.
The conversation about what it would've taken to bring in a talented running back is irrelevant when a team with this much talent on its offense has just one missing piece. This season could quickly turn into a what-if year in a season where Coach Taylor needs a deep postseason run.

title: Bengals Legend Voices Frustrations After Team's Disappointing Loss vs. Commanders
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals allowed a golden opportunity to slip through their fingers with their 22-20 loss to the Washington Commanders on Monday night.
In a week that saw the Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore Ravens both lose, the Bengals had a chance to extend their lead in the AFC North. Instead, the Bengals watched a three win team earn their fourth victory of the season on a last-second field goal.
It's going to be a long week for this team and the fan base. Not only that, but former players are even frustrated with how things played out on Monday night.
Bengals legend T.J. Houshmandzadeh shared his feelings on the team's final defensive drive during a recent episode of 'Speakeasy'.
"There's just no way on God's green earth they go down the field in two plays with no timeouts," Houshmandzadeh exclaimed . "Nobody's doing that on Madden to me, let alone in real life."
The final drive of the game was a backbreaker for the Bengals. In just two plays, the Commanders were in chip-shot territory for kicker Drew Stevens. As Houshmandzadeh said, it almost felt like it wasn't possible for this Commanders team to get down the field this quick on the Bengals.
The Bengals legend also mentioned the team not having its best offensive performance of the season. In the Bengals' last two plays before Evan McPherson drilled a 56-yard field goal, quarterback Joe Burrow nearly threw an interception and took a terrible sack.
How did the Bengals offense get to that point? The answer could be found in the non-existent run game. The Bengals rushed for just 31 yards on Monday night. Sure, the weather was poor, but that didn't stop the Commanders from rushing for 150 yards.
Burrow is an elite quarterback, and it makes sense for him to have the ball in his hand during winning time. However, it couldn't hurt to also equip his offense with a running game that has a pulse.
It feels like the Bengals have been flying too close to the sun without a reliable run game.
Burrow has put the team on his back through the air, but since this offense seems to be so one-dimensional, it seems as though defenses are going to be able to make plays like the Commanders did on Monday to put the Bengals in more uncomfortable situations.

title: Joe Burrow Addresses Aaron Rodgers' Release, Chasing Drew Brees' Record and Giving Thanks
full_text:
Joe Burrow has always spoken fondly and with a lot of reverence for Aaron Rodgers in the past, but the Cincinnati Bengals quarterback didn’t want to say too much about the ongoing dysfunction in Pittsburgh that led to the Steelers releasing the future Hall of Famer today.
“I don't know much about the situation,” Burrow said. “It's certainly surprising, but I don't know much.”
With the Steelers sitting just one game behind the Bengals in the AFC North standings, a quarterback switch in Week 12 isn’t ideal.
And it could be something that benefits the Bengals in their pursuit of a division championship for the first time since 2022.
One way Rodgers release does resonate with Burrow is that it’s a reminder of how fortunate he feels to be in the position he is.
“I'm always thankful to be to be playing and certainly don't take being a quarterback in the NFL for granted,” he said. “I've worked really hard for it, certainly. But it takes a lot of luck and being in the right place at the right time to be in this spot, and I've had a lot of people that have helped me get here, and I’m super, super grateful for all those people.”
Burrow enters Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints with a 74.2 completion percentage, which is just shy of the NFL record Drew Brees set while playing for the Saints.
Brees posted a 74.4 in 2018 and 74.3 in 2019.
“It's a huge, huge part of playing quarterback, is being accurate enough to let those guys go to work,” Burrow said. “It's something I take pride in.
“Certainly gotta keep improving and would love for my career at the end of it to look like his.”
Despite the admiration for Brees, Burrow said he doesn’t feel any extra oomph in facing a Saints team that Brees led for 15 seasons.
“I think it would mean a little more if we were playing down there,” Burrow said.
Burrow still has a lot of fans in the Louisiana region after leading LSU to the national title and winning the Heisman trophy there in 2019.
He admitted it’s meaningful to have that support from so far away.
“People in Louisiana love their culture, they love their football, and they love their people, and I became that,” he said. “Certainly it doesn't surprise me in Louisiana, but when we played in Houston this year, I always forget how many people relocated after Katrina to Houston. I saw a lot  of No. 9 jerseys in the stands that day – purple ones – and a lot of people saying, ‘Go Tigers.’ I always forget about that, but that was a pleasant surprise.”

title: Bengals Injury Report: Initial Saints Practice Status Revealed For Dalton Risner And More
full_text:
The Bengals dropped their opening injury report for Saints week on Wednesday.
All eyes are on Dalton Risner's knee injuries over the next few days as things got off to a poor start projecting his return on Sunday. He is listed as a DNP on the projected Wednesday report after Cincinnati just went through a walkthrough after playing so recently on Monday night.
Zac Taylor did say earlier today to not read into Risner's status until later in the week.
Stars like Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins know one loss isn't the end of the world for Cincinnati.
The Bengals are still heavy favorites to win the AFC North. ESPN's Football Power Index gives them a 91.2% chance to win the division.
"I mean, we started off playing in the rain. I'm not going to make an excuse; you know what I'm saying? But I think that's a different start for us trying to find rhythm. But once we got going, we just got to make those great decisions. Get the right looks, read the right coverages, and you know, execute it," Chase said to the media on Monday. "One loss doesn't determine anything. It's the NFL. You got a loss, you learn from it. We learn from our mistakes. That's what we're going to do. We're going to watch the film, we're going to correct it and move on."
Higgins echoed a similar sentiment as the Commanders found a way to slow him and Chase down in the 22-20 loss during Monday Night Football.
"I mean, no, but, yeah, they were doing a lot of doubles and things like that, a lot of stick strong and stuff like that, especially to [WR] Ja'Marr [Chase]. But we were able to figure it out, there in the second half. We made some plays, but just not enough," Higgins said. "When you win some, you lose some; you just gotta live to see the next day. Go back to practice, correct what we did wrong, and be ready for next Sunday."
Cincinnati is widely expected to bounce back with a home win over the Saints on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET inside Paycor Stadium.

title: 'It Depends' - Joe Burrow Dives Into Bengals Run Game Struggles as Cincinnati Prepares For New Orleans
full_text:
Joe Burrow is the heavy engine of Cincinnati's offense, but he's willing to let off the passing gas to help spark the Bengals' run game back up after a brutal showing against the Commanders (14 carries for 31 yards).
He gave his view on the ground attack, which now ranks 19th in EPA/rush and 16th in success rate, noting they "just gotta execute." They didnt do that enough in Monday's 22-20 loss.
"It depends," Burrow said about the Bengals needing to run the ball more. Or just more effectively. "Obviously, you'd love to be super explosive in both, but we'll play the game however we need to play to win it, and I'm certainly prepared for either one. I'm prepared to throw it no times. I'm prepared to throw it 70 times. Whatever it takes to win."
Cincinnati has the best pure passer in the NFL and almost all of its offensive money in the passing game, but it sputtered in the rain to start against Washington. One possession (and one more score) was the difference between a real shot at AFC's No. 1 seed and the longshot reality now.
The Bengals are battling a New Orleans defense playing solid football of late, ranking 14th in EPA/play allowed and 11th in success rate allowed since Week 6.
Burrow has full respect for another NFC opponent.
"Yeah, their linebackers are good at blitzing," Burrow said about the Saints. "Their front is explosive, and they're good rushers. When you put those two things in combination, it makes it hard."
The Bengals are at the top of the AFC North and still riding great team chemistry, while the second-place Browns own a -32 point differential this season and the fellow 6- 4 Steelers deal with crazy locker room turmoil.
Aaron Rodgers got released today, and Cincinnati can now take full control of the division; Burrow is just focusing on getting to 8-3.
"Just worried about trying to win this week," Burrow said. "Landscape will play out the way it plays out, and we just got to keep winning."

title: Bengals Coaches Taylor, Golden Weigh In on Why Shemar Stewart Can't See the Field
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have been down an edge rusher since rookie Cashius Howell went on Injured Reserve with a broken wrist Nov. 3.
And yet 2025 first-round pick Shemar Stewart still can’t find his way onto the field.
Monday night in the 22-20 loss at Washington, Stewart was active but didn’t play a single snap on defense.
Stewart, who suffered a knee hyperextension in the first practice of training camp and didn’t return until just before the season opener, has been active for seven of the team’s 10 games this  year.
Monday marked the second time he failed to play in a game when he dressed, and in four of the others, his snap counts were in the single digits.
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor and defensive coordinator Al Golden both continued to throw their support behind Stewart on Wednesday.
Taylor said Stewart’s inability to get off the sideline was more a product of how the game played out.
“The first half was very unique in that I think they had a five- or six-play drive to start and then three and out, three and out, three and out, and then they finished with a six-play drive that scored,” he said. “So those (defensive linemen) felt really good because they were on the sideline quite a bit. I think in the second half they felt pretty good, too.
“With that being said, you've got to find some opportunities for Shemar and Cedric (Johnson) to get in there and mix in,” Taylor added. “It was just a strange first half the way it played. In the second half, those guys felt really good. But we'll rotate those guys a little more than we have.”
Taylor has spoken positively about Stewart all season, and he said the lost time in training camp is no longer affecting the decisions to not play him.
“I've been pleased with Shemar,” he said. “  know I sound a little bit like a broken record up here and then he doesn't take any snaps. I get that. But he's controlling everything he needs to control. He's in a positive spot right now for us.
“We'll provide him with some opportunity to go make some plays for us,” he continued. “I like where he's at. Just the way it unfolded last week wasn't any sort of indictment on him.”
Golden said it’s on him, not Stewart, to make sure the young edge rusher sees action.
And Golden expects that Stewart will as the season moves into December and January.
“He will (play),” Golden said. “We're gonna need him. I keep saying it. This is a long stretch we have in front of us, and whatever I have to do to help him and to get him into the game and impact the game, I am committed to doing that. I have to do a better job with that.”
The next opportunity comes Sunday against the Saints.
Stewart played 280 snaps in eight games as a rookie. He’s logged just 52 in seven games this season.

title: Zac Taylor Updates Dalton Risner's Health, Shemar Stewart's Lacking Impact Entering Saints Week
full_text:
Zac Taylor returned to the podium on Wednesday for the first time since the Bengals' five-game win streak ended against the Commanders.
The 22-20 loss featured one of the worst rushing performances in team history (14 carries for 31 yards), and Jalen Rivers' 58 snaps at right guard had something to do with it.
The backup right guard filled in for Dalton Risner (knees) and only notched a 55.3 Pro Football Focus grade (50.5 run-block grade). Getting Risner back to complete the offensive line continuity this week would be massive.
Taylor updated his status.
"He'll be day to day, so we'll see," Taylor said about Risner. "Just talked to him this morning, and we'll just take it day to day and see where he ends up on Sunday. Today's a walkthrough-only day, so I wouldn't read too much into how that goes today."
Bryan Cook suffered an injury in the first half of the game but ended up playing 64 snaps and should be good to go this week. Taylor said he is just "sore" after the recent loss. Meanwhile, Cincinnati desperately needs help at defensive end amidst Shemar Stewart's shutout from the lineup.
He didn't play a snap Monday, and the week prior, he didn't enter the game until the Bengals were up 31-3. The three weeks prior to that, he played five, six, and zero total snaps.
"I've been pleased with Shemar," Taylor said, noting the game flow led to no snaps for Stewart because Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy didn't play a lot in the first half. "I know I sound a little bit like a broken record up here, and then he doesn't take a snap, so I get that. But he's controlling everything he needs to control. He's in a positive spot right now for us. We'll provide him some opportunity to go make some plays for us, and I like where he's at. So just the way it unfolded last week wasn't any sort of indictment on it."
We will see if the Bengals put weight behind Taylor's words by actually playing Stewart a significant snap diet this week.
All in all, Cincinnati is pretty healthy entering Week 12 as they get their first normal game week in nearly a month to enjoy at home.

title: Referee Report: Bengals, Saints Should Expect Lots of Flags in Sunday's Game
full_text:
Not only are the Cincinnati Bengals wearing the same uniform combo they wore when they blew a 15-point lead against the New York Jets last year, they’ll also have the same referee they had that day.
Scott Novak will be on the call for Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints at Paycor Stadium, marking his first Bengals game since the team’s infamous 39-38 loss in Week 8 last year.
Novak has been a head referee since 2019 and has been an NFL official since 2014.
The Bengals are 3-5 with Novak. The Saints also are 3-5 with him.
Novak and his crew are averaging 17.4 accepted penalties per game, which is a close second to Craig Wrolstad (17.44) for second most in the league.
Last year Novak ranked 11th (11.82), and in 2023 he was 10th (12.24).
Novak and his crew have called 46 offensive holding penalties this year, most in the league. The next highest number is 37 by Alex Moore, who has only worked nine games this season to Novak’s 10.
The next highest number for a referee that has worked 10 games is 32 by Shawn Smith.
Novak and his crew also lead the league with 13 unnecessary roughness penalties, which is almost 50 percent more than the next highest total, which is nine by Shawn Hochuli.
In Week 4, Novak’s crew had 30 accepted penalties for 280 yards.
The penalties are the most this season, and the yards are second most behind 289 in a Week 2 overtime game between the Packers and Jets, which Novak also worked.
Novak has one career playoff assignment, which was an NFC Wild-Card game between the Buccaneers and Commanders way back in 2020.
Here is the full list of eight Bengals games Novak has worked:
Week 8, 2025: Jets 39, Bengals 38
Bengals 2-15; Cowboys 4-25
Week 14, 2024: Bengals 27, Cowboys 20
Bengals 10-77; Cowboys 4-36
Week 8, 2024: Eagles 37, Bengals 17
Week 14, 2023: Bengals 34, Jaguars 31
Bengals 6-35; Jaguars 7-55
Week 5, 2022: Ravens 19, Bengals 17
Week 9, 2021: Browns 41, Bengals 16
Bengals 4-31; Browns 10-84
Week 8, 2020: Bengals 31, Titans 20
Week 10, 2019: Ravens 49, Bengals 13

title: The NFL is synonymous with Thanksgiving, but it hasn’t always been a holiday for the Browns
full_text:
Football has become synonymous with Thanksgiving ever since the American Professional Football Association played six games on Thanksgiving Day back in 1920, its inaugural season, and two years before rebranding as the National Football League.
And there’s no sign of slowing down, with the NFL currently slating games for Thanksgiving Eve and Black Friday, in addition to three yearly Thanksgiving Day contests.
Even so, the Cleveland Browns haven’t figured prominently on Thanksgiving in recent seasons, with their last appearance occurring back in 1989.
For the Browns, as a franchise, Thanksgiving Day games have been a mixed bag. Here’s how they’ve fared through six total appearances:
As the premier franchise of the extinct All-American Football Conference, it comes as no surprise that Paul Brown's teams did really well on Thanksgiving during this era.
In ‘47, the Otto Graham-led Browns turned an early 10-point deficit into a 27-17 beatdown in the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.
Marion Motley ran for 75 yards and a score, while Lew Mayne added two catches for 123 yards and another touchdown. On defense, Mac Speedie picked up a fumble and returned it 8 yards the other way for the game’s final touchdown.
The year after, the AAFC once again featured Cleveland at L.A., and once again the Browns erased an early deficit and turned it into a lopsided win, this time by a score of 34-14.
Otto Graham threw for two touchdowns and ran in another one; Dante Lavelli reeled in seven grabs for 128 and a touchdown, and Edgar Jones led Cleveland’s rushing attack with seven carries for 37 yards while also catching a touchdown pass.
Attendance numbers point to a little over 60,000 that day, about 15,000 more spectators than the year before.
Finally, a close one, the Browns edged out the Hornets by a score of 14-6 in front of a reported minuscule crowd of just over 5,000 at Soldier Field. This was the same team that Cleveland had dismantled by 35-2 earlier that month.
Weather conditions limited Graham’s air attack, managing just 88 yards on six completions. Motley and Bill Boedeker provided Cleveland’s touchdowns en route to the club’s fourth and final AAFC crown.
Two weeks later, the NFL would officially announce that the Browns would be joining the league as part of a merger agreement, along with the San Francisco 49ers and the original Baltimore Colts.
One season after falling to Vince Lombardi’s Green Bay Packers for the NFL Championship, Cleveland met the Cowboys at the Cotton Bowl in front of a crowd of over 80,500.
Dallas, then an up-and-coming team, managed to defeat Cleveland 26-14 despite getting outgained in total yards, 321-304, thanks in part to four Danny Villanueva field goals.
Leroy Kelly scored on the ground, and Ernie Green caught Frank Ryan’s lone touchdown pass that day, but the Don Perkins-Dan Reeves rushing attack proved to be too much.
Dallas would go on to lose the NFL Championship to the Packers that season.
The Browns were no match for the Cowboys in ‘82, with the team scoring its only two touchdowns in the fourth quarter when Dallas was already up 31-0.
Danny White threw two touchdown passes, and Tony Dorsett ran for two more, while Dino Hall and Mike Pruitt helped make the score look less humiliating.
This Landry team made its way to the Conference Championship, while the Browns managed to sneak into the playoffs with a 4-5 record in a strike-shortened season, before losing in the Wildcard round to the Raiders.
The Browns came into the Pontiac Silverdome as a genuine Super Bowl contender. The Lions were a team on the mend after picking third in that year’s draft.
However, this Detroit team, led by a rookie head coach in Wayne Fontes and a rookie running back in Barry Sanders, managed to pull off the upset as one-touchdown underdogs over Bud Carson’s Browns .
Sanders ran for 145 on 28 carries, and Eddie Murray kicked two field goals, while Bernie Kosar was held without a touchdown pass and was intercepted once. Another Barry, Redden, scored the Browns’ lone touchdown on a 38-yard scamper, his only carry of the game.
The 3-9 Lions’ win over the Browns sparked a five-game winning streak to close out the season and legitimize Fontes. After the loss, Cleveland went 2-2 the rest of the way and returned to the Conference Championship Game, where they fell for the third time in four years to the Broncos.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: 3 Keys to a Browns Win Over Raiders at Home in Primetime Matchup
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have given fans plenty to be thankful for in 2026. The team entered the holiday week with a 6-4 record and received the honor of being flexed into the Sunday night slot on NBC for the game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
This also comes at a time when the rival Pittsburgh Steelers are imploding , which should be a popular Thanksgiving conversation topic in Northeast Ohio.
The Browns are favorites in this one but can't let that get to their heads, especially after coming off a bye week and enjoying Thanksgiving.
Here are three keys to victory in Sunday's matchup:
The Browns have been comeback experts so far this season. The latest came in Week 10 when Deshaun Watson engineered yet another come-from-behind win, this time against his former team in the Houston Texans.
The comebacks have been thrilling, but at some point the luck may run out. The Browns fell into a quick 17-0 deficit against Houston. In the prior win against Tennessee back in Week 7, the Browns were down 14-0 against one of the worst teams in football.
Alpha DAWGS for SNF 😤 @RiddellSports | #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/2Tm6Tpf2EE
Just one mistake could have been the difference in both wins. The Raiders have lost three in a row, but Fernando Mendoza is coming off a three-touchdown performance in only his second NFL start. He is expected to have star tight end Brock Bowers back as well, so it's important the Browns don't come out sluggish early in this one.
Watson has been relied upon much more as a rusher due to lackluster production from Quinshon Judkins. The quarterback actually led the team in rushing in the win over Houston with 49 yards, compared to only 38 from Judkins. The back did, however, find the end zone with under a minute left in the game.
Again, Watson has been able to overcome early deficits and use his legs effectively. Yet this is a player with a serious injury history and one who spent nearly two years off the field due to an Achilles injury.
The Browns need to be able to rely upon Judkins if he is going to be getting the bulk of the carries. If he struggles, the team may need to limit his carries and go with the other options on the depth chart.
This is a major opportunity for this Browns team now that the rest of the AFC North seems to be dealing with issues. A win Sunday would push the Browns to 7-4 before next week's showdown with the first-place Cincinnati Bengals.
Yet a loss drops the team to 6-5 and could lead to questions about whether this team is an actual contender.
The Browns are incredibly young all over the roster and are coming off a bye week. The offense may also be without Denzel Boston as he deals with a quad injury. That means players like Harold Fannin Jr. and KC Concepcion, in their first Sunday night game, will need to play like experienced veterans.
Browns rookie WR Denzel Boston was dealing with a toe injury previously but now he’s listed with a quad injury. https://t.co/74bLPqM8RK
The Browns are currently a comfortable lock for the postseason. However, the NFL sees drastic change every week, just ask the Steelers, and a loss to the Raiders would mark three losses in the last four games.
It is a rare occurrence for the Browns to not only play on a Sunday night, but to be the betting favorite as well. The team needs to live up to that confidence and not slip up against an inferior opponent.
The same is true for Watson as he seems to finally be advertised by the Browns in the fifth year of his tenure. A bad performance would only lead to more criticism.
Steve is a lifelong Cleveland sports fan who proudly wears his Guardians, Browns, and Cavs gear in his current home of Santa Barbara. He has covered Cleveland sports online for the past decade and is still waiting for the Browns to draft a QB who signs a second contract in town.

title: These 2 Browns Players’ Performances Will Be the Difference Maker in Week 12
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are coming back from their bye week with a huge game the entire country will see.
Cleveland will take on the Las Vegas Raiders at Huntington Bank Field, and the game will air on "Sunday Night Football".
Primetime is a great way for players to showcase their skills to the NFL, and these two players need to step up and be game changers if the Browns want to beat the Raiders.
It feels like every week the Browns have been waiting for Verse to have a breakout game, but it never comes. However, this week he has a great chance to get his first sack of the season.
The Browns will be taking on rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who is making his third career start. It would be an excellent opportunity for Verse to show him what the NFL is all about.
Pro Football Focus posted on X Monday that Verse has 248 pass-rush snaps without a single sack this season, which is the most among defensive ends.
Most pass rush snaps without a sack among DE this season Jared Verse           248 Nick Bosa              126 Derek Barnett      123 James Lynch         123 Tyler Lacy              103 pic.twitter.com/pUyli1pfkD
Verse believed that he is coming off his best game against the Houston Texans in Week 10.
“I think I was my best self that game," Verse said on Wednesday. "I did exactly what I had to do. I closed the B gap with the tackle, I was able to set the edge, I was able to get to [CJ] Stroud a couple times. Didn’t end up getting a sack but getting in his face, hitting him."
If Verse can record a sack or two, then there is a good chance the Browns could make Mendoza feel uncomfortable, forcing him to start rushing decisions.
Cleveland's running back Quinshon Judkins has not had the best season, recording 423 rushing yards on 126 attempts and four touchdowns in nine games. But he could break out on Sunday.
The Raiders are allowing 149.5 rushing yards per game, the second-most in the NFL.
If Judkins can be patient enough and the offensive line can open up holes, then he could have a great day running the ball. If Judkins struggles against this defensive line, it raises the possibility that the offensive line is underperforming or that Judkins is not a No. 1 running back in the NFL. In that case, the Browns will need to address that need in the offseason.
If the Browns can take down the Raiders, they will be 7-4 with a great chance of making the playoffs.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Where the Cleveland Browns Went Right and Wrong in the 2026 NFL Draft
full_text:
By almost any measure, the Cleveland Browns’ 2026 NFL Draft was a huge success, especially when considering it came off the back of another wildly successful draft one year earlier.
Basically, five starters were added with the team’s first five selections through the first three rounds. It’s an impressive feat, even for a roster without top-level depth, as was the case in Cleveland. That’s slowly starting to change.
Nonetheless, not all 10 picks were hits, and that’s a fact, even if there’s still time to reverse course for some of the players selected.
Here are two wins and two loses from the Browns’ 2026 draft class.
There’s no doubt that Boston should have been picked up in the first round. Luckily for the Browns, he was still available in the second, getting selected 39th overall and 15 spots after fellow wideout KC Concepcion.
So far, Boston has shown he’s a legit WR1 in this league. He’s the only rookie over 500 receiving yards for the year, and he also leads all rookies with an incredible 15.8-yard per catch average that has him in the same ballpark as Davante Adams, Tee Higgins, and Rome Odunze in the NFL.
The top candidate for Offensive Rookie of the Year , Boston, along with Concepcion and second-year tight end Harold Fannin Jr., has the Browns set up really nicely for the next few years.
Sure, left tackle Spencer Fano dealt with all the pressure of being a Top-10 pick and getting sent to work frequently on an island, looking out for Deshaun Watson’s blindside, but everyone expected Fano to start right away—Barber was supposed to be a project.
Teven Jenkins was supposed to be the team’s right guard, but a back injury leading up to the start of the season opened the door for Barber, and he hasn’t looked back.
A former left tackle for the Gators, Barber has been the club’s best offensive lineman at times , combining an imposing physique with the nasty disposition that coaches adore. Eventually, he might get a shot at playing tackle in Cleveland, but no one is taking the right guard spot from him in the meantime.
The Browns thought that Royer could play second fiddle to Fannin when they picked him up in the fifth round, but he has become quite the mystery instead.
First, he made the wrong kind of headlines during the offseason due to a number of highly criticized social posts. Then he failed to report to the team’s training camp, missing the entire preseason. The Browns placed him on the non-football illness list, and the club refuses to touch the subject .
It’s starting to feel like Royer's never going to play a down for this team. Meanwhile, standout cornerback Hezekiah Masses has been looking solid for the Raiders after being selected five spots after Royer.
This really doesn’t have much to do with Green, who was a great pickup in the sixth round out of Arkansas, when you consider his potential . As a matter of fact, you might consider it nitpicking.
But since the Browns unexpectedly decided in favor of handing Watson the starting job and against moving on from either Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel before the trade deadline, Green hasn’t really had a chance to show much of anything.
Since Cleveland opted to keep four active quarterbacks on its roster --an unusual move-- Green counts towards the 53-man limit, so he also takes a spot that could otherwise be used at a different position.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: The Browns’ Biggest Underperformer Has a Lot to Prove During the Final Seven Games
full_text:
With the Browns sitting at 6-4 and awaiting a home date with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday Night Football, there is not much to be wary of if you are a Cleveland fan.
Deshaun Watson has now thrown for 300+ yards in three straight games, something he hadn’t done once since joining the Browns in 2022.
The rookies at receiver are as advertised: Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion are first and third among receiving yards by a rookie this season; both have added a couple of touchdowns as well. Second-year Ohio product Harold Fannin Jr. has blossomed into a top-five tight end in the league, continuing to show reliable hands and an unstoppable motor.
Another 2025 draftee has struggled to find his groove in the past couple of games: running back Quinshon Judkins.
After rushing for 96 yards and two touchdowns against the Titans a month ago, Judkins has rushed for 106 yards on 36 carries (2.9 per attempt) and the game-winning score vs. Houston in Week 10.
Cleveland’s run game has been subpar this season, averaging just 97.5 yards per game (24th in the NFL) and 3.8 yards per attempt (25th in the NFL).
The Browns run the ball on 41.2% of their plays, putting them in the lower half of the league. Another stat that puts them down is that they average just 0.94 yards before being contacted per rush, bringing their success rate to 35.5% on runs, which is 26th in the NFL.
Judkins currently has the fourth-worst success rate among qualified rushers this season at 30.2% and the second-worst rushing EPA at -35.7.
These final seven games for the Browns will give Judkins plenty of opportunities to show his worth, as the Raiders give up the second-most rushing yards per game. Cincinnati (which Cleveland plays twice) allows the ninth-most rushing yards per game; Atlanta and New York aren’t exactly world beaters when it comes to defending the run.
Baltimore is solid at stopping it, but Indianapolis is right up there with the Raiders as one of the worst run defenses in the league.
Again, though, Judkins is only in his second season in the NFL, and while we have seen other young Browns players break out almost immediately, there could be some growing pains with Judkins.
He is just 23 years old and has dealt with some injuries early in his career, but if there was any time to break out, now is the time.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: Predicting the Browns’ Quarterback Room for the 2027 Season
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have a ton to be thankful for this season by starting 6-4 and putting themselves in a position to make the playoffs. Todd Monken was a questionable hire at the time, but he has the team bought in and is pressing all the right buttons.
Deshaun Watson has had his best season in Cleveland after a contentious preseason. The young players have stepped up , showing a bright future.
On the other hand, the Browns have put themselves in a pickle going into 2027. They have won too many games to pick a top quarterback in the draft. Watson’s contract expires after the season, and although he has played well, he has not been consistent enough to sign to a long-term deal.
The quarterback room is up in the air for next season, with no real viable answer. The room could stay the same, or a big addition may be made for the future.
The #Browns have no interest in signing QB Daniel Jones, who cleared waivers today after being released by the #Colts .
Watson should be extended on a short-term contract as a bridge quarterback. He has improved every week he has played under Todd Monken and has had three straight 300-yard games. The team believes in him to win games, and he has developed chemistry with the young receivers.
He would have another offseason with Monken. The talent around him would get more time to develop with him, rather than trying to learn a new quarterback's tendencies. The roster will be ready to win next season, and handing the reins to a rookie drafted low in the first round would be a risk for a regression.
The University of Oregon product had an injury-plagued 2026 season. He has not played since early in the season, but in 2025 he was considered the second-best quarterback in his class. Moore chose to stay in college for another year, which hurt his draft stock. Moore took over for Dillon Gabriel at the University of Oregon, and they were teammates in 2024.
The Browns have two first-round picks in the 2027 draft , both of which may be in the back half. They have reloaded their roster in the last two drafts and brought in players at every level of the offense and defense.
Rookies no longer have to come in and start on day one.
Andrew Berry can use the higher first-round pick on a starter, but the second one can be used to take a risk and draft a prospect. Moore would have time to sit behind Watson and learn Monken’s offense while serving as the backup. He has a big upside, but his floor is now lower than it was last year.
Gabriel has been praised for his understanding of the offense. However, his physical tools limit his potential. He can serve as an emergency quarterback, and he is beneficial to have in the quarterback room.
The Browns had the chance to cut Gabriel when he came off the injured reserve list, but chose to keep him on the roster.
The physical tools are off the charts with Green, but he has struggled with accuracy. He did not get a lot of reps as the fourth quarterback, but after another offseason, he may challenge Gabriel for the emergency quarterback position. The Browns should hold onto him and find a way to utilize his skills for niche plays.
The obvious omission from the list is Shedeur Sanders. Monken had a chance to start Sanders at the beginning of the season, but chose Watson.
He made the same decision after Sanders’ lone start when Watson was injured. Sanders has shown that he has a chance to be an NFL quarterback, and there will be a team that would be willing to trade for him and give him a chance .
There are a lot of options out there to play quarterback for the Browns in 2027, but none of them are a no-brainer. Moore may be the future, but for next season, Watson could be the easiest answer to start at quarterback.

title: How This Running Back's Return From Injury Strengthens Browns' Offense
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns' running game will have a chance to bounce back for the back half of the 2026 season.
Through the first 10 games of the year, Cleveland sits with a nice 6-4 overall record and the top spot in the AFC North still within reach.
However, such success has not been thanks to the running game. The unit has posted a measly 975 total yards, averaging fewer than 100 yards per game, numbers that rank the Browns 24th in the league. In rushing yards per carry, they are 25th, and in total touchdowns, they sit right in the middle of the pack.
Fortunately, the Browns did get a positive update on a player who could help the rushing attack regain its form.
On Tuesday, Nov. 24, running back Raheim Sanders was activated off the injured list after missing the last few weeks due to a hip injury he suffered in a Week 5 loss to the New York Jets. In his place, the Browns have leaned on the likes of Audric Estime, who is no longer with the team, and Jaleel McLaughlin to fill his spot on the depth chart.
The #Browns have designated RB Raheim Sanders for return from injured reserve. He is eligible to practice today.
Now that he is back, though, the running back room will likely see Sanders return to the No. 3 spot behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson, with McLaughlin sliding to fourth.
Before being injured, Sanders had played in five games, rushing nine times for 43 yards and one first down . He has not yet scored this season. In the passing game, he complemented the unit nicely, hauling in 11 receptions on 12 targets for 74 yards.
With both Judkins and Sampson struggling to find consistency, Sanders will look to take some of the dirty reps away from them and give them more time to get quality reps. In his role, the 24-year-old will likely be the fill-in back when substitutions are needed.
A look at #Browns RB Raheim Sanders at practice today, who was designated to return from IR after being placed there Week 5 with a hip injury. pic.twitter.com/NuzCpsuXkK
After all, a deeper running back room gives the offense more comfort in giving guys like Judkins and Sampson longer drives, knowing that if a break is needed, they can turn to Sanders. On the counter, they can also spread out drives more, giving each back a chance to shine, saving a player like go-to back Judkins' energy for later in a game.
No matter how the coaching staff decides to use Sanders post-injury, the rushing game simply needs to be better, especially if the Browns want to make a late-season push for a playoff spot.
Sanders' first chance to return to the gridiron will be on Sunday, Nov. 29, when the Browns take on the Las Vegas Raiders from Huntington Bank Field at 8:20 p.m. EST.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns Get Unexpected Help In AFC North Race As Steelers, Bengals Stumble
full_text:
Over the past week, the AFC North had a lot of big events take place to determine its winner in 2026.
For the Cleveland Browns, they got help from all of the other teams losing while they had their bye week . On top of the losses, the Steelers just had some major drama go down within their organization
Let's take a look at all three of the Browns' rivals to see if Cleveland can get their first division win since 1989.
After losing to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, the Steelers swapped places with the Browns in both divisional and playoff standings. Pittsburgh now sits in 3rd in the North and 7th in the Playoffs.
However, that was just the tip of the iceberg.
As the Browns were closely competing with Pittsburgh, drama broke out within the organization between quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy.
Steelers releasing QB Aaron Rodgers. (via @RapSheet , @AdamSchefter ) pic.twitter.com/x4UVthdEoI
After a sequence of events where both parties did not see eye to eye, along with a historical Pat McAfee show appearance from Rodgers, the Steelers have decided to part ways with the 42-year-old.
This is huge for the Browns. While Mason Rudolph is still a solid QB, he is no Aaron Rodgers, who had over 2,200 yards, 16 touchdowns, and six interceptions on the season.
Especially looking at standings, this disaster should help the Browns focus on one team in particular for the title of AFC North Champs.
Cincinnati has been on fire this season, with Joe Burrow looking like an MVP-caliber quarterback. Despite this, the Bengals still lost to the 3-5-1 Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football.
Looking at the standings following that one, the Browns sit one game back at 6-4 compared to the Bengals, who lead with a record of 7-3.
The big news? Cleveland has yet to face off against Cincinnati this season.
In fact, two of the last six games will be against the Bengals, with the first matchup in Cleveland in week 13, and the finale on the road in Cincinnati in week 18.
Realistically, that game could be one of the biggest this season in the entire NFL. For years, the league sets kickoff as "TBD" due to the potential nature of the game we seem to have each year.
Unless the Bengals run away with the division and are able to rest their starters that game, expect that Week 18 matchup to be intense, and maybe even get flexed into yet another prime time game.
The story of the 2026 Baltimore Ravens is quite sad. Lots of injuries, which is hard to deal with while having a first-year head coach, Jesse Minter.
With Lamar Jackson sidelined for potentially the rest of the season, Cleveland needs to capitalize on the opportunity to get a win in Baltimore when it comes time in week 16.
While the Ravens aren't competing for the AFC North title, the divisional record plays a big role in deciding the champs.
For Cleveland, they must win against the injured Ravens roster.
As fun as it is to finally see Pittsburgh go through a similar situation to the Browns with Aaron Rodgers, work still needs to be done.
Cincinnati is a legitimate championship-caliber team, and beating them is going to be a battle for the Browns.
All focus should be on winning games, especially now that the window has opened up just a bit more.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: How the Benching of Aaron Rodgers Benefits the Browns
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are used to bringing dysfunction to the AFC North with their actions both on and off the field.
However, there has not been a peep heard from Berea, and they sit second in the division at 6-4. The stalwart of the division, historically, has been the Pittsburgh Steelers until this season.
The Steelers and coach Mike Tomlin parted ways at the end of last season after 19 years with zero losing seasons. Now the story has changed, as new coach Mike McCarthy benched Aaron Rodgers overnight in favor of Mason Rudolph.
Rodgers has had his lowest completion percentage of his career, but he should still give the Steelers the best chance to win. They are on a two-game losing streak after getting blown out by the Cincinnati Bengals and then dropping a close game against the two-win Philadelphia Eagles.
No matter how Rudolph performs, it looks as though Rodgers is finished in Pittsburgh. He did not show up to the team meeting Wednesday morning, which could signal his end.
Rodgers and McCarthy had a contentious relationship prior to his benching, and the relationship seems to be unsalvageable.
The Steelers’ first team meeting today was scheduled for 8 am, and Aaron Rodgers was not at the team’s training facility at that time. pic.twitter.com/yIYmWfrXKf
The path to the playoffs has now changed for the Browns, as they are the sixth seed in the AFC, one spot ahead of the Steelers.
Both teams are tied, but the Browns have the tiebreaker as of now due to their record within the division.
The Steelers should be underdogs in their next three games, and they play the Baltimore Ravens twice in the last four weeks. The Ravens are having a down year, but the offense has turned around under Jacoby Brissett, and their matchups are always physical. The Browns have the easier schedule for the rest of the season.
The other teams trailing the Browns are the New England Patriots, who lost Drake Maye. Behind them are the Houston Texans at 4-6, and the Browns already beat them head-to-head to win the tiebreaker. The Las Vegas Raiders raced off to a 3-0 start, but have fallen to 4-7. If the Browns can beat them Sunday night, then they will be all but finished .
There is blood in the water for the last wild-card spot, but it’s not the Browns’.
Not only do the benching and fallout with Rodgers benefit the Browns’ playoff hopes, but it also shows the turnaround and shift in the division.
The Browns were on a two-game losing streak, falling to 5-4 and out of a playoff position. Todd Monken did not panic and stuck with Deshaun Watson after missing a week with a concussion.
They fell down 17-0 against the Texans, and fans were ready for Shedeur Sanders to come out and spark the offense. The belief Monken had in Watson paid off as he had his best three-quarters of the season to lead the Browns to a victory and back into the playoff race.
The move to bench Rodgers and his reaction is a typical move the Browns would make in years past, but now the shoe is on the other foot, and the Browns are the ones making responsible decisions. As a result, they are poised to finish ahead of the Steelers in the division. The Browns sit only one game out of the Cincinnati Bengals, and they play each other two times in the last seven games.
The Browns’ roster is so young, and they do not care about the past. Monken has everyone in the organization on the same page, and there has been no discontent .
Rodgers' benching is an alarm that change is coming in the AFC North.
And fortunately, the Browns aren't at the center of negative attention for once.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Jared Verse Believes He's Improving, But One Thing Is Still Missing
full_text:
When the Cleveland Browns traded away future Hall of Fame defensive end Myles Garrett, all eyes were on who his replacement would be.
Fortunately, young edge rusher Jared Verse, who was acquired in the trade, quickly emerged during the offseason. He worked with players outside of practice hours, maintained a vocal and standout presence in the media spotlight and seemed poised for a big 2026 season for the Browns' defense.
But through the first 10 games of the year, Verse has struggled . That role he was expected to fill may have been too much pressure for him to handle.
Multiple times now, his public comments have been used as motivation and a competitive edge for opposing teams, all while he has yet to record a sack and is posting career-low numbers across the board in other areas.
Despite the lack of production in the box score, Verse believes his performance against the Houston Texans in Week 10 was a step in the right direction.
On Wednesday, Nov. 25, Verse spoke to the media ahead of the Browns' primetime Week 12 meeting with the Las Vegas Raiders. He was asked how he felt he played against the Texans, whom the Browns beat to improve to 6-4 on the season.
“I think I was my best self that game," he said. "I did exactly what I had to do. I closed the B gap with the tackle, I was able to set the edge, I was able to get to [CJ] Stroud a couple times. Didn’t end up getting a sack but getting in his face, hitting him.
"I won most of my rushes, so I feel like I impacted the game in the aspect I need to.”
Browns DE Jared Verse on his performance against the Texans: “I think I was my best self that game. I did exactly what I had to do. I closed the B gap with the tackle, I was able to set the edge, I was able to get to Stroud a couple times. Didn’t end up getting a sack but getting… https://t.co/pAyktiUzBv
And while it would have been nice to see a sack recorded, the 26-year-old is right; it probably was his best game this year. He registered season-best marks in pressures with five and total pressure rate with 17.9%, routinely getting into the backfield to disrupt the Texans' passing game.
But there is still work to be done, especially as he searches for his first sack of the season.
In the win over the Texans, after allowing 17 quick points, the entire defensive unit anchored down, allowing just seven points across the next 41 minutes of the game . CJ Stroud, surprisingly, was sacked just once, though.
Browns DE Jared Verse registered season-high marks in pressures (5) and pressure rate (17.9%) against the Texans.
Verse has certainly slowly but surely gotten better since the first few weeks of the season, but that ability to get in the backfield and register sacks is something he needs to start doing, not just for the team's ability to shut down opposing offenses, but for his own confidence.
Prior to the Texans game, he revealed that in order to break out of the slump he's in and regain that mindset he once had, he had been seeing team psychiatrist Dr. Mayur Pandya.
“I’m upset with the way I’ve been playing," Verse said back on Nov. 12. "I don’t think it’s physical; there’s nothing wrong with my body. I think it was the mental aspect of the game and I’ve attacked that very well these past couple weeks. But I think this past week is a key thing that I’ve done. I’m very excited for next week."
Coming out of a Week 11 bye , Verse has all the opportunities in front of him to go out there and break his sack-less streak against a rookie quarterback-led Raiders offense.
The Browns and Raiders will meet from Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 8:20 p.m. EST.

title: Jerry Jones Defends Mike McCarthy's Work Ethic Amid Steelers' Aaron Rodgers Fiasco
full_text:
It's always a surprise when the Dallas Cowboys aren't the biggest circus in the NFL, but thankfully, the Pittsburgh Steelers offered some 24-hour relief earlier this week by benching Aaron Rodgers.
That led to a complete meltdown from the veteran quarterback, which included some damning allegations against former Cowboys head coach Mike McCarthy . The way that all of the chaos played out was a sigh of relief for Cowboys Nation, which avoided a potential McCarthy catastrophe of their own .
On Thursday evening, after the team's humiliating loss to the Philadelphia Eagles at home, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones was asked about his time with McCarthy leading the team.
Longtime Cowboys insider Ed Werder questioned Jones on the issue, but didn't get any drama. Instead, he received a glowing review of McCarthy from the Cowboys' shot caller.
So for the people that SWEAR  Mike Mccarthy was just "SO BAD" that he got fired. Here's more confirmation that he left on his own. JERRY TRIED TO GET HIM TO STAY. THIS IS FROM THE 🐎 MOUTH‼️🤦🏽‍♂️ Give me Sleepy Mike over this Anyday‼️🤷🏽‍♂️😂😂😂 pic.twitter.com/HnRGOwcUf7
“I offered him to stay at least another year when he left, and so I thought he was outstanding as the head coach and had a great command of, frankly, quarterback and the offense. Can't say enough good things about him," Jones told Werder after the game. "He's frankly one of the finest people that around football that I've been around, and I can't say enough about him.
Jones then specifically commented on the allegations against McCarthy, from falling asleep to skipping walkthroughs, and said he has never experienced those moments.
"I never had the type of thing that is being said about him. I never had that in consideration in any of my time with him extending his contract," he added. "Any of that was never on the table, and we never had an issue within the organization.”
At the end of the day, who knows what is going on behind closed doors in Pittsburgh, and Rodgers hasn't always been the most reliable narrator. So we may never know the full truth, but what we do know is the Cowboys have moved on and now have another head coaching disaster on their hands .

title: Cowboys May Not Win Another Game This Season After Inexcusable Week 12 Collapse
full_text:
Sometimes it's hard to find words to describe the 2026 Dallas Cowboys, but after the team's brutal Thanksgiving collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium, there is one word that comes to mind and perfectly encapsulates the team under head coach Brian Schottenheimer : humiliating.
There is no excuse for losing to the Eagles in the fashion that they did, and it's only gotten worse in the hours since the defeat. Cowboys legend Dez Bryant is calling for everyone to be fired , while former backup quarterback turned Eagles hero Joe Milton is shading the Cowboys' culture under Schottenheimer .
It's an embarrassment of failures for the team this season, and it may only be getting worse. After losing to the Eagles, you have to wonder whether the team will win another game this season.
And when you look at the lineup of opponents and strength of schedule , there is a strong chance that they could finish the season 5-12, missing the postseason for the third straight year.
NFL Remaining SOS (strength of schedule) from Week 12 through Week 18 1 = most difficult 32 = easiest pic.twitter.com/rb3LIk94wD
Coming into Thanksgiving Week, the Cowboys had the fourth-hardest strength of schedule for the final stretch of the year.
The schedule includes games in Seattle, at SoFi Stadium to face the Rams, and a home game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Add on two divisional games against the Giants and Commanders, who are ahead of Dallas in the NFC East race, and there's a real chance Dallas doesn't taste victory again this season.
The only week you can confidently predict the result of is the Week 14 bye week. The Cowboys already faced an uphill battle to reach the postseason, and now those odds are even worse, and there's only one outcome that will satisfy the fan base and position the team best for the future: fire Brian Schottenheimer .

title: Brian Schottenheimer Fired Himself With This One Play Call In Cowboys’ Collapse
full_text:
For the past three weeks, the Dallas Cowboys have been at home, but they've managed to secure just one win, and that came over the 1-9 Tennessee Titans , who still managed to hang 30 points on the team's putrid defense.
While the Cowboys have suffered their fair share of embarrassing losses throughout the Brian Schottenheimer era , nothing was as bad as what we saw on Thanksgiving Day. It was a historic collapse, with the Cowboys blowing a 31-10 lead and a 99.4 percent chance of winning .
There was a series of errors throughout the final 20 minutes of the game, but Schottenheimer's decision to line up in shotgun to go for it on fourth-and-one with 55 seconds left is a fireable offense.
EAGLES SACK DAK ON 4TH DOWN PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/HUyLQrz2c5
Dak Prescott gave up a sack, and Joe Milton went on to get the Eagles in position to line up for a 59-yard game-winning field goal. It was a catastrophic error. In that scenario, if you're going to go for it, line up under center and bully your way to that one yard. Dallas didn't, and the lack of situational awareness should cost Schottenheimer his job.
It doesn't help that after the game Milton threw shade at the Cowboys' culture under Schottenheimer .
Schottenheimer built his coaching career on being a good play-caller, but when it was all on the line, he crumbled. And no one can figure out what was going through his mind.
The fourth-and-1 play-call was inexcusable.
ESPN Radio's Evan Cohen was equally as dumbfounded as the rest of Cowboys Nation and those watching at home, because, for a man with a history of being a play-caller, to go in shotgun in that situation, it means you've completely lost your touch.
"Just an absolutely horrific play call. Horrific play call. I mean, I despise the shotgun in general at this point. I despise it on short-yardage situations. I extra despise it on a fourth-and-one. But if you think about it, let's just say situationally, Brian Schottenheimer screwed it up. Punt, field goal, whatever situational football. We could sit here today and say, you know, guy's in his second year. He's still kind of getting his feet wet. He's been a play caller. His specialty is calling plays," Cohen said.
"That is an awful play call. That was not a Dan Quinn decision-making thing. That was a play-call thing. That was, I need to get to Joe, so let me go backwards. No, no, Joe's over there. I've got to go over there to get to Joe. You're laughing at me, Kmart. It's ridiculous. You would laugh at me in general. I know that. But in general, why go backwards?"
“Just an absolutely horrific play call.” @EvCoRadio reacts to the Cowboys' 4th and 1 decision in their loss to the Eagles 👀 pic.twitter.com/3qqyLIQLGI
Sure, you can't put the loss solely on one play, especially after the Cowboys had a punt get blocked, missed an easy field goal, and made several other unforced errors, but Schottenheimer's mistakes are too much to overlook.
When you consistently make questionable calls and your team looks unprepared, it falls on the head coach. Dallas already stripped defensive coordinator Christian Parker of his play-calling duties, and it has made no difference.
Now, after Schottenheimer's unforgivable blunder, it's time for him to give up the reins, and the team should find a competent, experienced coach in the offseason to completely reshape the future of this team.

title: Dak Prescott Indicates Cowboys' Brutal Loss To Eagles Has Finally Broken Him
full_text:
Following the Week 12 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles , Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott sounded like a broken man.
The Cowboys managed to ruin the Thanksgiving of their fans on Thursday when they epically collapsed and lost to a depleted Eagles team led by our old Cowboys friend, Joe Milton.
The collapse featured Dallas coughing up an 18-point halftime lead and a 21-point third quarter lead. In fact, the Eagles had a 2.5% chance to win at halftime and a 2% chance to win in the fourth quarter with 4:14 remaining, per Next Gen Stats .
The loss was just pathetic and there is no other word for it.
After the game, Prescott labeled the loss "stunning" and said despite all of the bad losses the team has had in his tenure, the Thanksgiving Day loss to the Eagles "takes the cake."
“Pretty stunning," Prescott said . "This one takes the cake.”
“I was screaming to these guys on the sideline… finish these guys," Prescott added.
Prescott is not lying. He was seen all fired up and yelling on the sideline as the Cowboys watched the game slip through their fingers. Hey, at least someone was mad about it.
Before Prescott addressed the media, Jerry Jones admitted that the loss to Philly was numbing. Prescott said that is also how he feels.
“It's a good description for for how I'm feeling right now," Prescott said, per NFL Network's Jane Slater . "Yeah, especially I mean this this soon after the game, understanding the plays left out there, the plays could have made, should have made, mistakes we had.”
It's not hard to see why Prescott is as frustrated and broken as he appears to be. Granted, the Cowboys' offense didn't do much in the second half as the Eagles climbed back into the game, but dropping 38 points should have been enough.
Taking it a step further, Prescott and the Cowboys' offense has put up 129 points over the last three weeks, yet the team is just 1-2, which is unfathomable.
Of course, the latest loss to the Eagles only reinforces the idea that head coach Brian Schottenheimer should get canned.
Prescott was asked for his thoughts on a possible change on the coaching staff but played coy.
"I don't know what you're alluding, so I'm going to focus on doing what I can, the best I can, and controlling what I can and handle whatever comes when it comes, as I just try to do in life," he explained, according to FOX Sports .
We say Prescott is playing coy because he knows full well what he's being asked about, which is the future of Schottenheimer.
Perhaps we're reading too much into Dak's response, but his failure to voice any sort of support for his head coach could definitely be construed as a sign that Prescott has reached another level of fed up with Dallas and its embattled coach.
And he doesn't appear to be the only one, as even Jones said after the game that "nothing we saw out there tonight" gives him confidence in Schottenheimer, although Jones also noted he is not making a change right now.

title: Caitlin Clark Left Dumbfounded By Cowboys' Stunning  Collapse vs Eagles
full_text:
If you don't watch the Dallas Cowboys very often and caught the game against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday, you might've been left stunned.
But what transpired on Thanksgiving was nothing surprising or new to Cowboys fans, especially when it comes to the debacle that has been the 2026 season.
As the Cowboys suffered one of the most egregiously bad losses in franchise history, WNBA and Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark couldn't believe what she was watching.
And, more specifically, the Cowboys' fourth-down attempt in the fourth quarter.
"What exactly were the Cowboys doing there," Clark said .
Logical question, Caitlin.
The Cowboys were up 38-36 over the Eagles with 55 seconds left in the game when Dallas decided to try for a fourth-and-1 at the Eagles' 39-yard line instead of kicking a field goal or punting to force Philadelphia's offense into a tough situation.
This was, of course, an incredibly risky move because failing to convert would hand the ball back top the Eagles close to midfield and in great position to get into field goal range for a game-winner.
And, in typical Cowboys fashion, everything that could have gone wrong, did.
Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott was sacked and lost nine yards to set Philly up at its own 48-yard line. From there, Philly drove 11 more yards to set kicker Jake Elliott up for a 59-yard attempt that he of course made because, well, it's the 2026 Cowboys, who are the very definition of a dumpster fire.
Only the Cowboys could find a way to ruin their fan base's Thanksgiving in such a brutal way.
Let's dig the knife a little deeper, shall we?
According to Next Gen Stats , Dallas had a 98% win probability in the fourth quarter with 4:14 remaining. That was when Dallas had the 38-30 lead and the ball at Philly's 25-yard line, and that was one play before Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal.
The 2% win probability the Eagles overcame marked the second time in 2026 that the Cowboys have allowed a team to do that to them. The other time came in Week 8 against the Arizona Cardinals.
Also, lest we forget (we definitely didn't), the Cowboys led by 18 points going into the half, and by 14 points in the fourth quarter before the blocked punt Philly turned into a touchdown.
And, just when you think it can't get any worse, the Cowboys were beaten by a quarterback they cut before the season, Joe Milton, who didn't look like a starting-caliber signal-caller in the two contests prior.
So, not only did the Cowboys collapse, they did so in epic fashion, which is par for the course for this team.
The good news is, Jerry Jones sounds like he's cracking when it comes to his support for head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who should have been fired weeks ago and most certainly after the disaster that was Thanksgiving.
The bad news is, that move isn't likely to come during the season, so we have to endure this pathetic mess for at least another five games.

title: 4 Coaches Cowboys Should Consider to Replace Brian Schottenheimer in 2027
full_text:
Jerry Jones remains adamant that he won't fire Brian Schottenheimer during the season, but the Dallas Cowboys owner sounded as though he's running out of patience on Thursday night. And it's impossible to blame him.
Dallas had a 31-10 lead during the third quarter of their Thanksgiving Day game against the Philadelphia Eagles and somehow still lost the game . Making the loss worse was the fact that Philadelphia was without Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert. Not to mention former Cowboys backup Joe Milton III , who Philadelphia signed off the Dallas practice squad earlier this year, was under center.
As bad as this loss was, it might not be the worst of the year for Schottenheimer . He also watched his team lose to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with Jalon Daniels under center and get torched by Gardner Minshew and the Arizona Cardinals in another epic collapse.
All that said, there's no way Jones can bring Schottenheimer back in 2027. That said, here's a look at four potential replacements the Cowboys must consider.
Jones has often preferred to hire coaches with plenty of experience and the failures of Schottenheimer might turn him off to hiring a coach with no previous head coaching experience. That said, he shouldn't completely shut the door on young candidates with promise.
One such coach is Grant Udinski, the offensive coordinator for the Jacksonville Jaguars. Udinski has been instrumental in helping Liam Coen build an elite offense with the Jags and is widely considered an elite head coaching candidate despite being just 30 years old.
Jones might be turned off by Udinski's inexperience because of Schottenheimer, but the problem was that Jones hired a coach that was on absolutely no one's radar. He likely won't grasp that concept, but will instead decide Udinski isn't a legit candidate due to his resume and age, but he shouldn't.
Sean McDermott had a great run with the Buffalo Bills, going 98-50 in nine seasons. McDermott is a defensive-minded coach who gave the Bills incredible stability and had them in the playoffs eight times, including seven consecutive appearances from 2019-2025.
His only true flaw was not getting past the AFC Championship Game, leaving him short of a Super Bowl appearance. McDermott took this year off, but should be in high demand in 2027. His resume should impress Jones and his stability, and defensive knowledge, could be exactly what this team needs after the Schottenheimer era.
Another defensive-minded coach who needs to be on the radar is Chris Shula, the defensive coordinator of the Los Angeles Rams. He might not have head coaching experience, but Jones should be impressed by Shula's lineage. He's the grandson of legendary NFL head coach Don Shula, the son of former Cincinnati Bengals head coach Dave Shula, and the nephew of former Alabama head coach Mike Shula. If that wasn't enough, he's been working with Sean McVay as an assistant in Los Angeles since 2017.
Shula has held multiple roles on the defensive staff, finally taking over as coordinator in 2024. This season, he has the Rams ranked fifth in points surrendered and they're top 10 against the run and the pass. It won't be long until he's in charge of his own team and Jones would be smart to see if he's a fit in Dallas.
Sticking with the defensive theme, there's one name that stands out as a prime candidate for Dallas to consider. Brian Flores has the experience as a head coach after going 24-25 in three seasons with the Miami Dolphins. After surprisingly being fired after two consecutive winning seasons, Flores spent one season as the senior defensive assistant and linebackers coach under Mike Tomlin with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
He was then hired as the defensive coordinator with the Minnesota Vikings, a job he has held for the past four seasons. Flores is known for being able to produce pressure without elite pass-rushers and this season, he has the Vikings rated second in both defensive points and yardage ,
Flores deserves another chance to prove himself as a head coach and Jones would be foolish not to make him one of the top candidates to replace Schottenheimer.

title: Former NFL Player Says Someone Must Be Fired Following Cowboys Loss To Eagles
full_text:
Just when fans thought they had been through it all, the Dallas Cowboys decided to find a new low on Thanksgiving Day .
The Cowboys blew a 21-point lead in the second half against the Philadelphia Eagles in their Week 12 showdown. They allowed a player they cut this season, Joe Milton III, to light up the scoreboard as he led his team to 22 points in the fourth quarter.
In the end, it was the fourth time this season the Cowboys scored more than 30 points at home and lost. The 39-38 loss is a tough one to swallow, and one former NFL player says jobs should be on the line. After the disastrous performance, Geoff Schwartz says there has to be consequences for losing a game they had well in hand.
Someone is getting fired in Dallas. Can’t lose that game. Has to be consequences for that
Dallas already tried to hold someone accountable this season, taking play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker. They gave the job to Mike Pettine, but not much has changed. The question now is who should take the blame for this loss.
It's tough to point the finger at one area, because the Cowboys had failures with all three phases. After going up 31-10 in the third quarter, the bottom fell out and it seemed everyone forgot how to play football.
The Eagles scored on a 45-yard touchdown pass from Milton to DeVonta Smith to cut the lead to 14. They made it a one-score game when Kenny Moore recovered a blocked punt for a touchdown and Milton responded to a Dak Prescott touchdown by running in one of his own. That was aided by a 55-yard kick return from Britain Covey, which set Philly up nicely.
Despite all the back-and-forth, Dallas had a chance to win thanks to an errant throw from Milton. That pass landed in the arms of Cobie Durant, but the offense managed to move just 26 yards. Still, Brandon Aubrey had a chance to put things away, but missed a 40-yard field goal.
Durant then gave up a touchdown to rookie Makai Lemon, but Caleb Downs made a potential game-saving play by breaking up a two-point try. That's when Brian Schottenheimer made his biggest mistake. With just under a minute to go, he dialed up a pass on fourth-and-one, which resulted in a sack. That set the Eagles up for a game-winning field goal, despite gaining just 11 yards on their final possession.
At this point, it's easy to say the Cowboys should consider moving on from special teams coach Nick Sorensen. There's an even stronger case for Brian Schottenheimer to be on the chopping block.
That said, Jerry Jones rarely makes in-season coaching fires. There's also no clear replacement on the staff, unless Jones believes Pettine can make a difference. Considering he made no change to their defense when he took over that role, that's not likely too appealing for Jones.
