title: Eagles' Joe Milton Takes Massive Shot At Cowboys Culture After Humiliating Dallas
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have had their fair share of embarrassing losses throughout the season, but nothing compares the humiliating collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.
Dallas appeared to have the game in the bag near the end of the third quarter, leading 31-10 and having a 99.4 percent probability to win. Then, the unthinkable happened. Former third-string and practice squad quarterback Joe Milton III activated his heroics and spoiled the Cowboys' holiday feast.
The loss was embarrassing. Milton leading the Eagles' comeback only adds to the pain. Oh, and in case you were wondering, he was named the game's MVP after throwing for 331 yards and three touchdowns with just one interception. He outperformed Dak Prescott, with a QB rating of 121.8.
It doesn't get any lower. At least that's what we thought until Milton spoke after the game and deliverd an absolute fatality by throwing massive shade at the Cowbys' culture under Brian Schottenheimer.
"It was a lot going through my head from when I first got here in Dallas to when I left, all the time I spent doing scout team quarterback, all the times where I was trying to get in the game, when they were up in games, just trying to get more experience," Milton said, via Nick Haris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram. "I mean, it was just great coming back here and playing in this stadium in Jerry's World and seeing the guys that I worked hard with in fall camp and OTAs.
"But I mean, it's about the Eagles. These guys show up every day. Nobody's late to anything. Nobody's complaining about anything . That's all you can ask for. That's the most important thing that I love about this team. I just know they're going to keep fighting."
Read that highlighted part again: "Nobody's late to anything. Nobody's complaining about anything." Say it ain't so. The Cowboys like to paint the picture that Brian Schottenheimer has control of the locker room and that his ability to build a family culture is what makes him so special and valuable to the franchise.
Well, it looks like those family values aren't leading to wins and there is no respect for his authority. If players aren't showing up on time and players are complaining about the way things are operating, it's an issue that starts at the top.
And that is exactly why Jerry Jones and the Cowboys must fire Brian Schottenheimer as soon as possible.

title: Dallas Cowboys Have No Choice But to Fire Brian Schottenheimer After Eagles Collapse
full_text:
It's typical to expect at least one epic collapse from the Dallas Cowboys per season. It's been engrained into the franchise's DNA over the last three decades.
But it's happened one too many times this season. And if it wasn't already obvious before, it's now time for Dallas to fire head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Point blank period.
The Cowboys had a collapse for the ages on Thursday, as Dallas fumbled away a 21-point lead in the second half in a 39-39 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving. It marked the largest blown lead in NFL history on Thanksgiving, and former Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton made sure every Dallas fan in AT&T Stadium felt the pain.
Dallas is now in serious dangerous of missing the postseason, though it's probably for the best so that the Schottenheimer era comes to an end. So what went wrong?
As long as Schottenheimer is the head coach, you can always count on the Cowboys collapsing late with the game on the line.
Here are the blown leads/late collapses/inexcusable results that Dallas has been a part of this season:
- can't convert in red zone during Week 3's loss to the Baltimore Ravens - Week 4's 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay and undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels - Cowboys blow 10-point lead in final minutes to lowly Cardinals before losing in OT - Dallas blows 31-10 lead in second half on Thanksgiving against Eagles
Take your pick. Whether it's blowing a big lead or making poor decisions during a tight game in the clutch, the Cowboys will find a way to lose.
And the blame falls on the head coach.
Sure, the Cowboys likely would have never been in position to lose on a game-winning field goal had Brandon Aubrey handled his business.
But let's not blame one of the best kickers in NFL history. It was Dallas' final offensive play that needs to be what Jerry Jones has on loop when deciding whether or not it's time to part ways with Schottenheimer.
With a chance to ice the game on 4th and 1 in the final minute, Schottenheimer -- who is supposedly an elite offensive mind -- elected to have Dak Prescott line up in shotgun instead on running Javonte Williams up the middle.
If you get stopped, you live with the results. But lining up for a pass is almost inexcusable, especially when the play call clearly wasn't designed well enough to the point where Prescott couldn't even get a pass off in time before being sacked.
The defensive issues are one thing. But Dallas' offense, despite being filled with elite players, continues to fall short time and again. It's unacceptable.
Schottenheimer is clearly unable to make the most of an offensive roster that most coaches would die to have at their disposal. It's simply time to go.

title: Jerry Jones Takes Rare Accountability For Cowboys' Embarrassing Thanksgiving Collapse
full_text:
Every week, the Dallas Cowboys find new ways to lose. On Thanksgiving Day, the holiday was spoiled after an unbelievable collapse at home against the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles .
In what was essentially a must-win game, the Cowboys fell apart, thanks to complete incompetency from the coaching staff, a lack of leadership, and another brutal defensive performance. Dallas lost, 39-38, on a field goal in the closing seconds.
But it should have never even gotten to that point. With the third quarter winding down, the Cowboys held a 31-10 lead.
Thursday's loss will officially go down as the largest Thanksgiving collapse in NFL history, with Dallas' win probability sitting at 99.4 percent after Brandon Aubrey's missed field goal at 3:35 in the third quarter. Then, with less than two minutes remaining in the game, the Cowboys had a 94 percent win probability before their epic collapse.
It was completely unacceptable down the stretch, with the offense, defense and especially special teams falling apart at the seams.
After the game, Jerry Jones spoke to the media and did something he rarely does: accepted some blame for the loss, but he also directed some at the coaches, which is understandable with some of the questionable calls we saw down the stretch.
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones in his opening comments after the 39-38 loss to the Eagles: “Ownership, coaching, all of it is responsible for what we saw at the end of that game.” pic.twitter.com/xEvjukeG2D
"Still having to realize that we ended up on the bad end of that score," Jones said during his post-game media scrum. "This locker room does. It's a bitter disappointment to have done some things early that we did and then turn around and every phase of it, every phase. That's a part of a game like this.
"Ownership, coaching, everybody is responsible for what we saw at the end of the day."
After a collapse of that nature, someone needs to be fired. Fire head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Fire special coordinator Nick Sorensen. Fire the entire staff, because there was no excuse for that loss and it's could be the final nail in the coffin for Dallas this season.
Unfortunately, Jerry Jones doesn't seem like he has any changes in mind.
Jerry Jones says there are no considerations to coaching changes in the next 11 days before the Cowboys’ next game pic.twitter.com/gHGJk8wNGY
"No, I wouldn't anticipate that, no," Jones said when asked if any coaching changes are on the table. "At this juncture, we can give ourselves a better chance to win these coming games and be competitive, in my mind, without coaching changes at this time."
It's going to be a long final five weeks of the season.

title: 5 Bold Predictions for Broncos-Steelers: Jonah Coleman Weathers the Storm
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have to travel to face the Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday .
All the media talk that the 8-2 Broncos are worse than their record suggests can also be applied to the Steelers, though the East Coast media bias doesn't like to acknowledge it. Regardless of what is being said, the Broncos are 8-2 for the second straight year.
Denver needs to emerge from Pittsburgh with a win, especially with the Kansas City Chiefs falling to 8-3 after losing to the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving. If the Broncos can fulfill this week's bold predictions, it will be tough to imagine a loss.
The Steelers allow the third-lowest rushing yards per game and boast the fourth-highest run-stuff rate in the NFL, but they allow the second-highest receiving yards to running backs.
Jonah Coleman is a capable runner and will get some yards on the ground, but he breaks 150 scrimmage yards largely because of his receiving ability out of the backfield. The wet and cold weather forecast only favors the rookie.
The Steelers have only allowed two players to break 100 receiving yards: one wide receiver and one tight end. Denver has been actively trying to get Waddle more involved in the passing game, but the results haven't been great thus far.
Waddle has posted one game over 100 yards (Week 2), and one other game over 50 yards, but on a short week, the Broncos get him back over the century mark.
Pittsburgh is allowing the 25th-lowest pressure rate this season at 31.1%. However, the Steelers have also allowed the ninth-highest sack rate, and that was with Aaron Rodgers at quarterback, who is quick to get the ball out or throw it away.
However, the Steelers decided to make a change at quarterback , turning to Rudolph and releasing Rodgers. Rudolph has a habit of holding onto the ball for too long.
The Broncos can capitalize on that with some sacks and use their pressure to force a couple of takeaways, especially with rain and wind in the forecast.
The Broncos' defense has serious issues stopping the run and limiting explosive plays. Warren leads the NFL in rush yards over expected per attempt and ranks seventh in success rate. He is exactly the type of weapon that Denver struggles to contain.
However, this is a bold prediction, after all. The Broncos' defense figures things out and finally limits an opposing running back as dangerous as Warren. This would be an even bigger feat with the quarterback change, as the Steelers will likely look to rely even more on Warren.
The Broncos got their hands on two punts against the Las Vegas Raiders last week, and special teams coordinator Darren Rizzi has been in his bag with his punt rushes. Cameron Johnston has only had one punt blocked in his career, covering nine seasons and 523 punts.
Denver gets it done again against the Steelers, though, and blocks the second punt of Johnston's career.

title: Broncos Address J.K. Dobbins Fallout With 11th-Hour Roster Moves
full_text:
The Denver Broncos announced a flurry of roster moves on Thursday afternoon, ahead of their Black Friday game against the Pittsburgh Steelers .
The Broncos activated running back Tyler Badie from injured reserve. With J.K. Dobbins serving a one-game suspension , that left only two active running backs on the roster — Jonah Coleman and Badie — so the Broncos also promoted Cody Schrader from the practice squad to the 53-man squad.
Schrader was elevated in each of the past three weeks, so the Broncos were out of elevations on the young running back, so it required signing him to the 53-man roster, aka 'promoting' him. However, to make room for Schrader on the roster, the Broncos placed second-year defensive lineman Sai'vion Jones on injured reserve.
Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last Sunday's 38-24 win over the Las Vegas Raiders and was already ruled out of Week 12's action . He joins Eyioma Uwazurike on IR, which makes the Broncos a lot thinner on the defensive line.
To bolster the D-line depth, the Broncos signed veteran Khalen Saunders to the practice squad earlier this week after working him out on Tuesday. Saunders has played a lot of football and has been in some big games, winning two Super Bowls with the Kansas City Chiefs.
Don't expect to see Saunders on the field in Pittsburgh, though. With only a couple of days to settle in and learn the system, the Broncos didn't elevate the 6-foot, 324-pound defensive tackle.
However, the Broncos did elevate undrafted rookie offensive guard Gavin Ortega once again. This is his third elevation of the season, though he's yet to actually dress for a game.
With temperatures projected in the low 40s , an 85% chance of rain, and plenty of wind in the forecast, Sean Payton would call Black Friday's contest a "weather game." The Broncos are going to need Coleman and their running back stable to shoulder a big portion of the offensive burden in Pittsburgh, which is why they couldn't afford to proceed with only two ball-carriers.
With Coleman, Badie, and Schrader, the Broncos have a full three-back rotation ready to rock and roll. After this game, RJ Harvey will be eligible to return from IR, but the Broncos are going to have to start being strategic with their short-term IR decisions, as they only get eight activations per season, and they're already more than halfway through their allotment.
Last week, Coleman carried the ball 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns. It would be a surprise if he didn't get close to 20 totes again, but this Steelers defense is a much stouter unit against the run than the Raiders are.
Bo Nix will need to be a good decision-maker when the Broncos do pass, and anticipate a slippery ball, much like it was in the season opener in Kansas City.

title: 5 Broncos Sleepers Who Need to Come Up Big on Black Friday
full_text:
The Denver Broncos can’t take the Pittsburgh Steelers lightly , as both teams are pushing for a playoff spot.
Both teams also want to win this one to stay in their respective division races. It's a short week, and the 6-4 Steelers are at home, while the 8-2 Broncos are looking to maintain their perch atop the AFC West in an important conference game.
If Denver is to pull off the win on the road, these five sleepers will go a long way toward making it happen and winning their matchups .
Look, going against TJ Watt is tough enough, but McGlinchey has to do it just a handful of days after facing Maxx Crosby. Those are two of the best edge rushers in the NFL, and facing them back-to-back is tough.
Denver has dealt with some terrible play from McGlinchey this season, but he is vital to the offense's success on the road against the Steelers' defense. McGlinchey played a solid game against the Las Vegas Raiders; now he has to follow that up against Watt and the Steelers.
Watt is the key defensive player, but the Steelers' defensive front is a good and deep unit. Wattenberg has had plenty of issues with his individual play, but the identification of rushers and looks has been bad as well.
Against the Steelers' defense, the Broncos need Wattenberg to be on point. He takes pride in his football IQ, but he hasn’t shown it often this season. It is critical this week.
The Steelers' offensive line has been a solid unit, and their run blocking has been critical to their offensive success. Jaylen Warren is a threat as a rusher and receiver, but the Broncos really need to limit his impact in the running game.
Roach has to step up in a big way against the run, and in a matchup that may not be his most favorable. If he can eat up space and blockers to help the linebackers and safeties coming downhill, that could be enough, but of course, making the big plays himself will always help.
While the Steelers' receivers aren’t a great unit, they do have one of the best tight end groups in the NFL. They have the players to go big with 13 personnel (three-tight-end) sets and still be a serious threat against coverages.
Strnad is massively outmatched against the Steelers' tight ends, both in coverage and in the run game. Denver sent a message to Strnad at the trade deadline with a deal that fell through, and he has a chip on his shoulder; now's the time to prove he can handle his coverage responsibilities.
The Steelers have a threatening return game with Kaden Wetjen, a rookie out of Iowa. He is a consistent returner but hasn’t busted off many long returns, though there have been multiple close calls.
Skinner and Anderson are the main gunners, so there will be a lot of pressure on them to limit Wetjen. However, Wetjen hasn’t been nearly as effective on punt returns as he has on kick returns, and kick returns are far more unit-based than gunners.

title: Steelers' Last-Minute Injury News Is a Double-Edged Sword for Broncos
full_text:
The Denver Broncos released their final injury report on Wednesday , with only two days of practice on this short-week turnaround due to their travel itinerary back east to play the Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday.
The Steelers didn't have to travel, so they practiced on Thursday before issuing the game statuses for their injured players. The one Steeler we've been watching all week is outside linebacker Alex Highsmith, who's dealing with an ankle.
The Steelers ruled Highsmith out of Friday's game against the Broncos. TJ Watt is the feared edge defender in Pittsburgh, but Highsmith is no slouch, sitting with 5.5 sacks this season, which is more than any of the Broncos' three players tied for the team lead (five sacks).
Highsmith is the Jonathon Cooper to the Nik Bonitto that is Watt, if that makes sense. Not having to worry about Highsmith is a bit of a break for the Broncos, which could allow them to focus a bit more on Watt, who has 7.5 sacks this season.
The Steelers also activated wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. from injured reserve, giving new starting quarterback Mason Rudolph another formidable weapon in the passing game. Combined with DK Metcalf, who is playing in this game after the NFL opted not to suspend him for the spitting incident that occurred last week, Pittman's return puts Denver's secondary on high alert.
However, we know who Rudolph is at this stage in his career. He's been in the league almost a decade, with 19 starts under his belt.
If the Broncos sell out to stop Jaylen Warren and Pittsburgh's ground attack, which won't be easy, especially given Denver's issues against the run this year, it could put the onus on Rudolph to stand and deliver from the pocket. With the inside/outside pressure the Broncos can generate with down linemen Zach Allen and Malcolm Roach and Bonitto and Cooper, the opportunity to force Rudolph into some bad decisions will be rife.
Still, Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss have to strap on their helmets for this one. Metcalf can be a handful on his own, and adding Pittman to the mix — and we haven't even talked about tight end Pat Freiermuth — makes the Steelers more dangerous as an offense.
Again, though, it all starts with stopping Warren and the run. That's been a struggle for Denver this season, and Warren's 5.5 yards-per-carry average won't make it easy on them to suddenly find a spine.
With the weather expected to be rainy, windy, and in the low 40s , both teams will look to impose their will on the ground. It'll be a Jonah Coleman day for the Broncos , but the blocking up front will have to be on par with last week's impressive effort, given that Pittsburgh ranks third against the run.
On offense, the Broncos will contend with a combination of Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer in place of Highsmith. The Broncos have pass protected well this season, but it's going to be bad weather in a hostile, loud environment, so everyone's head will have to be on a swivel.

title: Mile High Roundtable: Broncos at Steelers Predictions on Black Friday
full_text:
The Denver Broncos got out to an 8-2 start for the second straight year. That's an exceedingly difficult feat to achieve.
It's especially impressive given the brutal schedule the Broncos faced in the first half of the season. In what remains of the schedule, the Broncos have just two opponents that are currently above .500, and the first one comes this week.
However, the 6-4 Pittsburgh Steelers seem to be reeling after benching quarterback Aaron Rodgers , who promptly went on the Pat McAfee Show the next day and slammed head coach Mike McCarthy for sleeping in meetings, being forgetful, skipping offensive meetings, neglecting the defense, and more. The Steelers released Rodgers on Wednesday.
And so Mason Rudolph will start for the Steelers. It's been a PR firestorm in the Steel City, and a massive distraction, so the Broncos will get the chance to exploit the situation.
Expect rain and wind on Friday, too. Sean Payton is planning on it being a "weather game." How will this one shake out?
Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding on Black Friday.
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 8-2 : Even with the distinctly average Rudolph at the controls, the Broncos never seem to blow anyone out. Inclement weather might make Jonah Coleman the key player on Black Friday football, but Bo Nix's knack for protecting the ball will be massive. Denver's defense ultimately has too much for Rudolph to handle, forcing three turnovers in a crucial road victory.
Pick : Broncos 24, Steelers 14
Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 8-2 : This game has Jonah Coleman written all over it. The Broncos faced their own PR controversy this week when Payton suspended running back J.K. Dobbins, but it paled in comparison to what the Steelers have been through. In Nix's first two career starts, he lost to the Seattle Seahawks and Steelers. Nix avenged the Seahawks loss, so now it's time to balance the scales with Pittsburgh. Look for Vance Joseph to be merciless in his pressure packages to force Rudolph into some bad decisions. And just as I predicted last week that Coleman would notch his first-ever 100-yard rushing day, the rookie has another big game on the ground with two touchdowns, though he comes up short of the century mark against Pittsburgh's third-ranked rushing defense.
Pick : Broncos 23, Steelers 16
Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 8-2 : This feels more like a "trap game" than the Cardinals, Panthers, or Raiders contests did — a weird Friday afternoon game, on the road, against a team in total freefall. Add a little bad weather, and this has the makings of a low-scoring, ugly, run-oriented, defensive battle. But one from which the Broncos should be able to emerge victorious. Don't expect a ton of Nix wizardry; this has "Jonah Coleman statement" written all over it.
Pick : Broncos 19, Steelers 10
Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 8-2 : Current forecast, it’s gonna be an ugly weather game for the Broncos in Pittsburgh. The Steelers have invested heavily on both sides of the line of scrimmage, but are severely lacking on the perimeter, compared to the Broncos. Weather could nullify those advantages. Expect a heavy dosage of run game and reliance on Nix’s legs in an ugly one.
Pick : Broncos 17, Steelers 16
Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 8-2 : While it's easy to think Rudolph starting means a blowout for the Broncos, the Steelers' defense is good against the run, and Jaylen Warren is a good running back . The weather could mean this will be an ugly game and a close one at that. Still, the Broncos can get it done, even if it doesn't look pretty.
Pick : Broncos 17, Steelers 13
Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 7-3 : The Steelers have been a different beast at home this year compared to on the road. This is looking like another close, down-to-the-wire game, with the Broncos relying on their defense to contain on an ugly day.  The Broncos do just enough to escape and get a big win over the Steelers, with Coleman having another 100-yard game.
Pick : Broncos 24, Steelers 20
Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 7-3 : It's going to be ugly in Pittsburgh on Friday, as inclement weather (and a Steelers quarterback change) should drive both teams to the run game. Denver has to key in on Warren, who has been spectacular this year. I'm picking Denver, but if the Broncos allow Warren to get explosives on the ground, things could go poorly, as Pittsburgh's defense is a top five unit against the run.
Pick : Broncos 20, Steelers 16
Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 6-4 : Bad weather with a questionable run defense against a good rushing team? Yeah, there is cause for concern for the Broncos against the Steelers, even with a change at quarterback. Denver should sell out to stop the run defensively and force Rudolph to beat them through the air. Offensively, the Broncos have to find a way to get the run game going against a good rushing defense. Denver finds a way but its a low-scoring grind-it-out win.
Pick : Broncos 18, Steelers 10
Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 6-4 : With Rodgers benched and Rudolph taking his place, the Broncos have the chance to win by more than one score in consecutive weeks. Denver's defense will look down this young Steelers receiving corps. Offensively, the Broncos will do enough to take the victory on the back of Coleman, who will rush for 100-plus yards and two scores.
Pick : Broncos 30, Steelers 17
James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 5-5 : Coleman has been the straw that stirs the drink for the Broncos' offense and although the Steelers will be tough sledding, the rookie will have his chances to shine. Coleman eeks out a couple of touchdowns on the ground and gets another 100-yard game, while Nix connects with Jaylen Waddle for a big score. With the Steelers rolling with Rudolph, the Broncos' defense should be able to get some takeaways as well.
Pick : Broncos 24, Steelers 14

title: Broncos' Black Friday Blueprint: 3 Keys to Beating the Steelers
full_text:
The 8-2 Denver Broncos have a legitimate shot at not only winning the AFC West title for the second straight season, but also the No. 1 seed in the conference again, too.
While the Broncos might be entering the easier part of their schedule, that doesn't mean they are facing pushovers. The Las Vegas Raiders were a challenge last week, and now the Broncos will take to the road to face a solid Pittsburgh Steelers team on Black Friday.
The Steelers are 6-4 for the season and are looking to make the playoffs again. And as much as a win would help the Broncos in their playoff hunt, the same could be said for the Steelers, who are currently the sixth seed and aren't yet out of the running for the AFC North title.
Even amid the PR upheaval in Pittsburgh this week, the Broncos will have to play a good game in all aspects — and they'll have to deal with inclement weather , with rain in the forecast that could potentially turn into sleet.
The weather will be a key factor in Friday's game, but it's not the only thing the Broncos need to worry about. Let's break down my three keys to a Broncos win on Friday.
The Broncos entered the week expecting to face the 43-year-old Aaron Rodgers, a future Hall of Famer. His numbers looked fine on paper — 60.9 completion percentage, 16 touchdowns, and six interceptions — but he's taken 31 sacks despite being pressured on just 20.3% of his dropbacks.
Rodgers doesn’t have the ability to extend plays as he did in his prime. Perhaps that’s one reason he was benched in favor of Rudolph , who is at least younger.
However, that may not be saying much, because Rudolph has taken 35 sacks in 38 career games (19 starts) while being pressured on 20.3 % of his dropbacks. He might be able to extend plays more than Rodgers at this point, but Rudolph still takes too many sacks.
The Broncos' defense needs to turn up the pressure and go after Rudolph whenever he drops back to pass. If the Broncos can do that, they'll either force him into a mistake or sack him.
The Broncos will need to have good coverage as well, because the Steelers' offensive line does a good job with pass blocking. If the Broncos' pass rushers can’t get to Rudolph, they need to keep him in the pocket rather than giving him a chance to extend the play.
Rudolph is a backup, but he’s shown he can make plays when the opportunity is there — and furthermore, he has quality playmakers around him that the Broncos must watch.
Broncos fans know about DK Metcalf, a talented receiver who made headlines this past week after being ejected for poking Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye.
Metcalf is a good player, and he's not facing a suspension this week, but he's not necessarily the biggest worry for the Broncos. Patrick Surtain II will often draw him in coverage.
Metcalf is a threat, but he isn't having the same impact with the Steelers that he did with the Seattle Seahawks. However, Warren and Friermuth are different stories, particularly when it comes to the Broncos' weaknesses on defense.
Let's start with Warren, who has averaged 5.5 yards per carry this season, leading all NFL running backs in that stat. He's the guy who sets the table for the Steelers' offense, even if he hasn't produced many touchdowns (he has just two rushing scores this season).
But we've seen the Broncos have issues letting running backs make big plays, whether on the ground or in the passing game. Warren is a good receiver, as evidenced by his 32 receptions on 45 targets for 321 yards this season.
And then there's Friermuth, who doesn't enter the conversation when people talk about the best tight ends in the game, but he's proven he can get the job done. He leads the Steelers in receiving touchdowns with five and has caught 32 receptions on 43 targets.
Tight ends producing big numbers against the Broncos has become a theme. Friermuth is worth watching, as he could make a bigger difference for the Steelers than Metcalf, given the weaknesses of the Denver defense.
The Broncos can't ignore Pittsburgh's other weapons, but Warren and Friermuth have to top the list, particularly to limit the effectiveness of a good running back and a good tight end.
The weather forecast for Friday in Pittsburgh may indicate the Broncos are better off running the football, but that plays to the strengths of the Steelers' defense.
The Steelers have given up just 840 yards rushing to opponents thus far, limiting opposing running backs to just 3.6 yards per carry, and ranking third in the NFL against the run.
While Jonah Coleman is coming off a strong outing — and you can't take that away from him — it did come against a Raiders defense that ranks low against the run. The Steelers aren't soft up front, so Coleman can't be expected to put the offense on his shoulders.
That means Bo Nix has to come through — and it means his receivers need to do their jobs too. Nix had a good game against the Raiders, but it might have looked better had it not been for a number of accurate passes being dropped.
The Broncos do have to be mindful of the Steelers' pass rush, which features TJ Watt (7.5 sacks) and Alex Highsmith (5.5 sacks, though Highsmith is dealing with an ankle injury ), but if the pass protection holds up and Nix stands tall in the pocket, he has a chance to exploit this secondary.
The Steelers have given up 2,303 yards to opposing quarterbacks this season and 6.1 yards per passing attempt, and they rank 24th against the pass. They do have seven interceptions, but teams must execute well in the passing game to prevail against Pittsburgh.
While one shouldn't expect Nix to have 300 yards passing or any receiver to eclipse the century mark, given the weather forecast, they need to produce to take the load off Coleman and whoever spells him for some carries — possibly Tyler Badie, who is designated to return from injured reserve as J.K. Dobbins serves a one-game suspension imposed by Sean Payton.
Coleman deserves praise for his breakout performance against the Raiders , but he has a tougher task ahead. The Broncos need the passing game to come through to help him out.
The Broncos' second-half schedule might be easier than the first half of this season, but the Steelers won't be an easy team to beat. They have good playmakers on offense, despite the quarterback change, and a quality defense, so the Broncos will have their work cut out for them.
It may not be the most ideal weather conditions, but the Broncos will have to deal with it the best they can, work for every score they get, and be consistent on defense.
A win would do a lot to help the Broncos' playoff standing — especially with the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs going at it on Thanksgiving. However, the Broncos have to remember they're facing an opponent that would be in the tournament if the playoffs started today.

title: Broncos Rule Out Two Players for Black Friday Game vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have released their final injury report prior to Friday's road clash with the Aaron Rodgers-less Pittsburgh Steelers.
Denver announced Wednesday that defensive lineman Sai'vion Jones (hamstring) and safety Taylor Rapp (quadricep) are ruled out for the Week 12 contest. Jones failed to practice Tuesday or Wednesday, while Rapp was a limited participant both days.
Five other players — running back Tyler Badie (thumb), wide receiver Pat Bryant (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), tight end Caleb Lohner (foot), and safety JL Skinner (shoulder) — were full participants and given no designation for the Black Friday tilt .
The Broncos are expected to leave for Pittsburgh on Wednesday evening, ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.
“We were originally going Thursday and then last week [Assistant to the Head Coach] Paul [Kelly] put the schedule up and Thursday looked really noisy," Payton explained to reporters. "I turned to him and I said, ‘Hey, no one’s got the schedule yet, right?’ He said, ‘Nope.’ I said, ‘All right.’ So then I said, ‘Are you sure no one’s got it?’ You have to know Paul, he said, ‘Well, I kind of told [QB Jarrett] Stidham.’ (Laughs) I said, ‘So someone has it.’ But anyway, just relative to that Thursday, and there’s a setup there where we can get a walkthrough in, then guys will have extra time after the game.”
On the Steelers' side , Rodgers (who's since been cut), outside linebacker Alex Highsmith, wide receiver Ben Skowronek, and defensive lineman Cameron Heyward did not practice on Wednesday. Safety DeShon Elliott, outside linebacker Nick Herbig, and inside linebacker Cole Holcomb were limited.
Rapp has been a nice find for the Broncos, an experienced former starter who began on Denver's practice squad and filled in admirably following injuries to starting safeties Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones.
Hufanga returned for last week's win over the Las Vegas Raiders and Jones is back this week to face the Steelers. And with JL Skinner joining Devon Key behind them on the depth chart, Rapp is needed much less than he was.
Jones has been a rotational contributor to Denver's defensive line in 2026, helping fill the shoes of John Franklin-Myers, whom the club lost in free agency this past spring.
To compensate for Jones' rule-out, the Broncos signed ex-Chiefs DL Khalen Saunders to the practice squad. It's also possible (if not probable) that third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim sees an increased snap count against the Steelers.

title: Broncos Sign Two-Time Super Bowl Champion Amid D-Line Injuries
full_text:
With injuries to the defensive line, the Denver Broncos added some veteran depth ahead of their Black Friday road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
On Wednesday, the Broncos signed eighth-year defensive lineman Khalen Saunders to the practice squad. The Broncos worked him and three other defensive trenchmen out on Tuesday, but they ultimately went with the 30-year-old Saunders.
Two weeks ago, the Broncos lost Eyioma Uwazurike to a shoulder injury. He's got a couple of games left until he could return from injured reserve.
In Sunday's 38-24 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, Broncos second-year defensive lineman Sai'vion Jones suffered a hamstring injury. Jones did not participate in Tuesday's practice, and the Saunders addition implies that Denver expects him to miss more time.
The Broncos' starting trio up front is Zach Allen, D.J. Jones, and Malcolm Roach, and with Jones out of commission, that leaves veteran Jordan Jackson and rookie third-rounder Tyler Onyedim as depth. The Broncos also have the 6-foot-3, 307-pound Jordan Miller on the practice squad, but he's relatively untested and is on the small side.
Saunders, 6-foot-0 and 324 pounds, was a Kansas City Chiefs third-round pick back in 2019. He appeared in 38 games with the Chiefs, with five starts. He contributed to two of Kansas City's World Championships.
In the spring of 2023, Saunders hit free agency, signing a three-year, $14.5 million deal with the New Orleans Saints. He started 30 games for the Saints over the next two years.
In August of last year, the Saints traded Saunders to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Alas, it didn't work out well in Jacksonville, and he was waived after appearing in just two games.
Saunders signed with the New York Jets a few days after being waived, and went on to appear in seven games last season. The Tennessee Titans signed him in early August, a little over a week into training camp, but he was waived in the final roster cutdowns later that month.
All in, Saunders has appeared in 77 NFL games with 32 starts, totaling 193 tackles (87 solo), 7.5 sacks, and one interception. His lone interception came as a Saint and was at the expense of Patrick Mahomes, his long-time teammate in Kansas City.
Saunders has played in some big games. That experience is important to a playoff-bound team like the Broncos.
Aside from his veteran experience, Saunders brings some mass and power to the Broncos' defensive line. The Broncos have prioritized athleticism up front, but opponents have been able to exploit the D-line's relative lack of size this season on the ground.
The Broncos enter Week 12's matchup with the Steelers ranked 22nd against the run, relinquishing 126.2 yards per game. I doubt we're going to see Saunders on a short week against the Steelers, but there's a chance he could be a practice squad elevation.
More likely, the elevation possibility comes after Black Friday's road game .
Saunders could be a short-term rental on the practice squad while Uwazurike is on IR and Jones is banged up. Then again, the Broncos could opt to hang onto Saunders down the stretch and into the playoffs, if he does well on the practice squad.
It's better to have and not need than to need and not have.

title: Broncos vs. Steelers: 2 Battles That Could Decide Black Friday
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are on a short-week turnaround as they prepare to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers in their house on Black Friday.
It's another trip to the East Coast, where the Broncos have historically struggled, but that was before Sean Payton came to Denver. There's been a lot of talk about how the Broncos got to 8-2, but the same is true of the 6-4 Steelers, a team with plenty of issues that has somehow managed to win.
The Steelers benched quarterback Aaron Rodgers on Tuesday, then released him, and head coach Mike McCarthy is under fire, but don't let that fool you; it's still going to be a tough game. Going into Pittsburgh is never easy, but winning these key matchups would go a long way toward the Broncos getting to 9-2 and beating one of the two plus-.500 opponents remaining on their schedule.
Let's break down the matchups.
Throughout the season, the Broncos' interior offensive line has had issues. Center Luke Wattenberg has been among the worst centers, left guard Ben Powers has played poorly enough to be replaced by Matt Peart, and even right guard Quinn Meinerz hasn't been the powerhouse blocker he usually is.
These issues led Payton to voice his dissatisfaction with the blocking up front during the bye, which prompted the aforementioned change at left guard, with Peart starting in place of Powers. Against the Steelers, though, this interior O-line is about to face a much bigger test.
The Steelers' defensive strength over the years has been their front seven, particularly their depth and consistency along the interior defensive line. Cameron Heyward leads the D-line, but Keeanu Benton, Derrick Harmon, and Yahya Black are all good players who can give the Broncos' interior blockers plenty of issues.
The Steelers are great against the run, with plenty of ability to generate pressure against any ground attack. Pittsburgh is currently the NFL's third-ranked rushing defense, and its 30 sacks rank sixth.
Heyward leads the group with 27 pressures, with the other three combining for 32, but Harmon has only played in six games this season. With the Broncos' interior issues, they have to be wary of this unit, especially in the running game, where they've struggled the most.
The Broncos can’t let the Steelers' defensive line control the trenches; otherwise, it could lead to a long day for Bo Nix and company, including Jonah Coleman, the AFC's reigning Offensive Player of the Week .
Flipping to the other side of the ball, it's another trench battle. The Steelers' offense goes through its ground game, and Frazier is a key part of the run blocking.
Frazier is technically sound on combo blocks, double teams, and climbing, so opponents have to account for him in the run game just to slow down the Steelers' rushing attack. That puts a lot of pressure on Jones, the Broncos' key run defender.
Jones is a solid run defender and a great one when he can force one-on-one blocks, but he struggles against double teams. He lacks the mass and length to hold up at the point of attack against double teams.
That means Jones must beat Frazier one-on-one and try to hold up against Pittsburgh's double teams. When Jones draws a double team, he just has to hold up long enough to keep those two blockers engaged, particularly Frazier, to prevent them from pulling off to the second level.
If Jones can hold the double teams, it'll give the Broncos another open man, running free to stop the run. This is one of the rare matchups where it's about a player doing his job in order to free up a teammate, rather than making a direct impact on the ball.
But if Jones can’t hold up against Frazier, individually and in a double team, it will likely allow Pittsburgh to control the trenches, which would be costly, given how badly the Broncos have struggled against the run at times, ranking 22nd in the NFL.

title: Broncos' Jonah Coleman Earns Major NFL Honor After Historic Day
full_text:
It's unfortunate what's happening with J.K. Dobbins and his suspension , but don't let it detract from the Denver Broncos' Jonah Coleman phenomenon.
Coleman rushed for 111 yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . The fourth-round rookie running back has been named the AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his historic day against Denver's oldest division rival, as well as the FedEx Air and Ground Player of the Week.
🎩🎩🎩 RT to help us congratulate @jonahcoleman8 on being named AFC Offensive Player of the Week! 👏 pic.twitter.com/dLq30d8EaH
Coleman is the third Bronco to win conference honors this season, joining safety Talanoa Hufanga and linebacker Alex Singleton. Both of those players are veterans, though.
Against the Raiders, Coleman became the first Broncos rookie to rush for 100-plus yards and three touchdowns in a game since Clinton Portis in 2002. Coleman wasn't born until August of 2003, the next summer.
It's been a while since the Broncos have had a running as prolific as Coleman out of the gates. This team went 19 games without a 100-yard individual rusher, but he finally got that monkey off Denver's back.
The last Broncos' rookie running back to make this kind of noise was Phillip Lindsay in 2018, but he didn't have any three-touchdown displays. However, what made Lindsay's emergence so unique was that he was an undrafted rookie, and he'd go on to eclipse 1,000 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns from scrimmage.
Lindsay became the NFL's first undrafted rookie running back to ever be selected to the Pro Bowl. He's also the first undrafted running back to produce back-to-back 1,000-yard rushing seasons to start his career.
As the Offensive Player of the Week, Coleman became just the 12th Broncos running back to earn the award, joining Lindsay (2018), Ronnie Hillman (2015), C.J. Anderson (2014, '15), Knowshon Moreno (2012), Clinton Portis (2003), Mike Anderson (2000), Olandis Gary (1999), Terrell Davis (1996, '97, '98), Gaston Green (1991), Tony Dorsett (1988), and Joe Dudek (1987). The award has only existed since 1984, and a Broncos skill-position player has won it 67 times.
Coleman has a shot at a 1,000-yard rookie campaign, but he'll have to continue producing close to how he did against the Raiders. With 302 yards and six touchdowns thus far, he's got seven games left to try and reach the milestone, and it won't be easy.
In Lindsay's case, he had the entire season to reach 1,000 yards. Coleman started his rookie campaign healthy, but suffered an ankle sprain in Week 2, which landed him a four-week stay on injured reserve.
Since his return in Week 7, though, Coleman has rushed for 263 yards and five touchdowns. If the Broncos' offensive line can continue to block like it did against the Raiders, there's a solid chance the rookie can crack 1,000 yards.
Coleman already leads all rookies with his six rushing touchdowns this season, which is one more than the next-highest guy — Kansas City Chiefs running back Emmett Johnson. I have little doubt that Coleman will rush for double-digit touchdowns as a rookie, but there might not be enough runway left to get him over 1,000 yards, given the four games he missed.
Another one for the rook. RT to congratulate @JonahColeman8 on being named a @FedEx Air & Ground Player of the Week! pic.twitter.com/uAovj84KFd
The Broncos are absolutely thrilled with Coleman. He may have gone in the fourth round, but he was one of the few complete backs in the 2026 draft class.
Teams saw a willing and able pass protector and a natural catcher of the football, to go along with Coleman's between-the-tackles vision, power, and burst. He's already caught 17 passes for 146 yards and six first downs, with a long of 51 yards.
Coleman may not have been the fastest running back in a straight line, but his burst is something special. And his jump-cut? Perhaps as potent as RJ Harvey's.
Suffice it to say, the Broncos got an enormous steal in Coleman. They're very fortunate he was still on the board at No. 108 overall. And he's just getting started.
Again, it's too bad that Dobbins is taking his diminished role poorly. But the Broncos aren't letting that get in the way of Coleman's continued rise.
The rookie will be put to the test this week with a Black Friday throwdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on deck, in their house. The Steelers currently have the NFL's third-ranked rushing defense, and the weather is expected to be cold and rainy.
It's likely to be a Jonah Coleman type of day.

title: Video Surfaces of Lions Fans Brawling With Bears Supporters at Ford Field
full_text:
The rivalry between the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears is among the most heated and contentious in the National Football League.
With so much at stake in the NFC North standings, both squads wanted to leave the Thanksgiving Day Classic with the victory.
A video has surfaced online of fans also battling in the stands at Ford Field. A supporter wearing an Amon-Ra St. Brown jersey is seen battling a Bears fan, with several onlookers trying to break up the scrap.
Another fan in attendance can be heard objecting to the fight, saying, "Come on, man, it's Thanksgiving."
Many took to social media to express it reminded them of when the Lions used to play at the Pontiac Silverdome, where fights were quite common in the stands.
Others noted that this is another example of why they decided not to attend NFL games in-person anymore.
Across the league, fights can be seen almost on a weekly basis. Alcohol typically ends up being the biggest reason fan interactions escalate.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Key Takeaways, Highlights, Analysis From 39-35 Loss to Chicago Bears
#Detroit Lions game on #Thanksgiving . pic.twitter.com/DpKRWUOvAy
When the Dallas Cowboys faced the San Francisco 49ers, there was a report of a fan that eventually passed away following a significant altercation at AT&T Stadium.
When asked about the fight during his weekly radio interview on 105.3 The Fan, Jones expressed no knowledge of the incident.
"No record of an incident at the game, and I just got that information. So, we had no record of an incident, and we'll be obviously looking into that," Jones said, when asked about the incident that reportedly began around the time of kickoff. "My understanding is that the individual went to the game, and didn't feel good at the game, and then left and then had been hospitalized. But, we weren't aware of any incident involving a fan at the game."
Ford Field has not seen that many brawls, as the organization has tried to create a more fan-friendly environment.
Given the amount tickets cost, it is not in the best interests of fans to do anything that could result in season-ticket memberships being revoked.

title: Grades: Detroit Lions Defense Falls Apart, Coaches Falter
full_text:
The Detroit Lions collapsed down the stretch, missing a massive opportunity on Thanksgiving.
After building an 11-point lead in the fourth-quarter, the Lions allowed two late touchdowns and missed a chance to put the game away late. They were beaten, 39-35, by the Chicago Bears in a game with first-place in the NFC North on the line.
With the loss, the Lions fall to 8-3 on the season and drop into second-place. Additionally, they fall to 1-5 under head coach Dan Campbell on Thanksgiving.
Here are grades for each position group based on performance in Thursday's game.
Jared Goff had some big moments early in the game, but his misses loomed large in the second-half. He finished 313 passing yards and a passing touchdown, which came at the end of a strong march at the end of the first-half.
Goff made two exceptional throws on that second-quarter drive, one to Jameson Williams on a corner route near the sideline and the next to Sam LaPorta when he threaded a tight needle for a touchdown.
However, he had two misses in the fourth-quarter that will be remembered. He had a pass go off the hands of Jameson Williams that was picked off by Dillon Thieneman, and led Brock Wright too far on an incompletion prior to the team's final turnover on downs.
Jahmyr Gibbs had a phenomenal showing on the national stage. He entered Sunday's game having never scored a touchdown on Thanksgiving, but notched three. Gibbs had a pair of 1-yard runs, but it was his 70-yard run in the fourth quarter that most will remember.
On the afternoon, Gibbs finished with 205 rushing yards on 21 carries, and notched 47 receiving yards on five catches. He had multiple electrifying runs, including a 33-yarder that looked to be a six-yard loss initially before he broke free.
Unfortunately for Gibbs, he was tackled short of the first-down on Detroit's final fourth-down conversion attempt on his final touch, which ultimately doomed the LIons.
The Lions got a huge showing from Amon-Ra St. Brown, who came up big with two catches on the first drive and approached the 100-yard mark by halftime. St. Brown finished with 146 yards on seven catches, including multiple impressive diving grabs.
Jameson Williams had six catches for 68 yards and a 12-yard run on a reverse, but the play he didn't make will be the one that is remembered the most. On a third-and-1 with less than six minutes remaining, Goff booted out and threw the ball to an open Williams, who had the ball deflect off his hands into Thieneman's for a crucial interception.
Sam LaPorta had a solid day with four catches for 44 yards and a touchdown. The score was his first since Week 5, and it was an impressive leaping grab between two defenders. He also had a big role in Gibbs' big day on the ground.
Brock Wright had one target and it was the key second-down late in the game when Goff led him just a touch too far. Tyler Conklin got into the mix with a first-half reception that went for nine yards.
Detroit's offensive line overcame an early scare when Tate Ratledge missed a series to have a pretty solid day. They paved the way for Gibbs to run for 200 yards, and the team averaged just under eight yards a carry against a tough Bears defensive line.
However, they also had some very critical mistakes that cost them. They had four false starts in the first-half, including three by center Juice Scruggs. There was some controversy about whether the Bears where imitating the snap count, but ultimately the mistakes fall on Detroit's shoulders.
Additionally, left guard Christian Mahogany was whistled for a taunting penalty after Gibbs' 70-yard touchdown run. This was critical, as it pushed Detroit's extra point back 15 yards and Jake Bates subsuquently missed it, which had a major ripple effect on the remainder of the game.
Down both of their opening day starters, the Lions relied on their youth to provide a spark in pass-rush. Derrick Moore continued his recent heater and did just that, coming up with two sacks and two forced fumbles.
Moore's second sack was a strip-sack that resulted in a safety, and he also had a punch out that ended Chicago's first drive. Alim McNeill also joined the effort, as he was credited for a sack when Caleb Williams was tripped up.
However, the pass-rush disappeared in the second-half as Williams began to dice up the defense. Undrafted rookie Anthony Lucas, who was elevated from the practice squad this week, was also whistled for taunting after Detroit forced a turnover on downs in the fourth quarter.
Malcolm Rodriguez tied for the team lead in tackles with seven, and had a sack, a fumble recovery and two quarterback hits. However, the story of the game for the linebackers will be their struggles in coverage.
Detroit was picked apart by Williams, particularly in the flats. With how much man-to-man coverage the defense plays, these responsibilities particularly lie with the linebackers. Derrick Barnes nearly came up with a huge play at the end, as he deflected a pass incomplete on the snap before Williams' game-winning touchdown to Rome Odunze.
Bears running back D'Andre Swift led the team with 97 receiving yards on seven catches, with many of those receptions coming in the dreaded flats that the Lions struggled to defend.
Detroit got D.J. Reed back in action, and the cornerback helped Detroit in spurts. However, the secondary struggled in the second-half as Chicago went up tempo and kept Detroit's defense out of a rhythm.
Rock Ya-Sin was on the wrong end of both touchdowns from Williams to Odunze. He was beat up the sideline for the first one, then got shook late in the game as the Bears connected for the game-winner with three seconds remaining.
Without Chuck Clark, the Lions relied on Andre Cisco to play a bigger role with Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph. Branch had a solid day with two tackles for loss, while Joseph was in coverage for a pass breakup on Chicago's fourth-down incompletion late in the game.
The ripple effect from Mahogany's taunting penalty will be talked about plenty. He hit both of his field goal attempts, but the missed 48-yard extra point sailed wide left and was the difference between a 12-point lead and an 11-point lead.
Punter Jack Fox had another solid day, as he averaged 50 yards per attempt on his three punts with a long of 61 yards. Jacob Saylors averaged 27 yards on his four kickoff returns.
Dan Campbell made two huge decisions in Thursday's game, and they worked out on opposite ends of the proverbial spectrum. First, he elected to accept a penalty that resulted in a safety rather than taking the ball deep in Chicago territory, and the team maximized that by scoring a touchdown on the ensuing drive.
However, his clock management down the stretch of the fourth quarter will be debated. Detroit went away from the run game on its final drive, and threw an incompletion on second-down that allowed the Bears to save a timeout.
They elected to go-for-it on fourth down and didn't get it on that drive, as a pass to Gibbs was thwarted by an impressive open-field tackle by T.J. Edwards.
Defensively, some of the coverage issues looked to be miscommunications that had plagued them throughout the early part of the season. As a result, the state of the defense amidst so many injuries will result in questions that Kelvin Sheppard will have to navigate for the remainder of the season.
Detroit has a favorable stretch over the next two weeks against Atlanta and Tennessee, but then the gauntlet of NFC North opponents begins. The Lions are still on solid ground as far as the playoff picture is concerned, but cannot afford to slip up ahead of that four-game stretch to end the year.

title: Everything Dan Campbell Said After Detroit Lions Loss to Bears
full_text:
The Detroit Lions lost Sunday, 39-35, to the Chicago Bears on a last-second touchdown pass from Caleb Williams to Rome Odunze. With the loss, the Lions fall to 8-3 on the season.
Here is a transcript of head coach Dan Campbell's postgame press conference after the Lions lost.
“Give credit to that team, man. They did what they had to do to win that game. It's frustrating for us. A number of things we didn't do well. Guys fought, but those are hard when you lose those types of games, man. You're in it, you're going. I just told the guys, 'Man, don't let this ruin your Thanksgiving. It's going to sting, and it should sting for a while, but man, put it behind you and try to enjoy your family. It's Thanksgiving, you got a couple of days off here, and then we move forward.' We clean it up. We'll clean it up Monday, and then we've got to get ready for whoever we play next. Questions?”
“Well, I mean, it was a heck of a throw, heck of a catch. Really was good coverage. I mean, (Bears WR Rome) Odunze made a heck of a catch back there, man, keeping his feet in. That was the one play. It's a credit to them.”
“Yeah, I would say we did a number of things really well. There was a number of really, really high-level plays that were made and just us handling our business. And then there's stuff that we haven't done in six weeks, man, some bad stuff that we have to clean up. Some self-inflicted wounds that really cost us some crunch time, so we got to clean those up. Can't have them. There again, we had our opportunities. We didn't capitalize. We didn't finish it.”
“Oh yeah. Yeah, we had other penalties that killed drives offensively , but those taunting killed us too. One of them, it changed the dynamic of the points because now you're going for two instead of just kicking a field goal, and now it changes the end of that game. But we talked about it, man, keeping your composure, and we didn't do that. We had two of them, and those hurt. Those hurt. When you get in big games, man, you got to stay disciplined, and we didn't do that. We've been really good over the last few weeks. We just got to lock back in, that's all.”
“I’m not discussing that.”
“Yeah, I mean, that plays into it. I thought we'd get it. First of all, I really believed we were going to get that. But then yeah, if you don't, it incentivizes a little bit the four downs. You're playing more for a field goal, but if you get down fast enough, you'll have some shots at the end zone, which they did. So, I don't regret that. I wish we'd have made that, but listen, sometimes that happens.”
“Well, I would say, man, we made some big plays early in that game. We got a fumble. It was a heck of a job by (Brian) Branch and Derrick Moore . Then the safety was huge right before halftime. That was big, so there were a number of things I thought we really did well. The ones that drive you up the wall are when we just blow an assignment, and those have not shown up in a while. It's been a minute. So we just, we had some miscommunication, man, that cost us in criticals. We'll get that cleaned up. We're going to have to.”
“I believed that we could get nine out of it instead of seven. And I mean, the seven, we’re already down there. They got timeouts. OK, you get seven and let's just say they were able to drive the length of field and you net four. I believe we could net nine and go in and we were able to pull it off. So, it's a credit to the offense.”
“Yeah, he did a heck of a job. I mean, he's special like we know, but I thought the O-line played their tails off too. We came off the football. It was a great job. Tight ends, receivers blocking. And I thought they came out and really played physical football. It was good. And Gibbs is special. He finds a crease, he goes. So, he's electric.”
“Oh, I don't know. I mean, it's a short week. You want to make sure you’ve got enough in, that can always play a little bit of a factor. I mean, I don't know. I just know we did. We didn't handle some things well like we have been.”
“I was hopeful we might have a chance to rebuttal once they got in field goal range. We'd answer to that depending on if they threw it and had some incompletions or something. And I used those two and that's what it was for.”
“He's getting better. I felt him get better in areas today too. I mentioned this, I feel like every week, the more he plays, the better he gets. The more looks he sees, the more he's having to adjust to things as they come at him. He's able to work his craft against different type of high-level players and you begin to get better. And I just feel like he is. He's getting better.”
“Yeah, I’ve got an idea on some of it.”
“No, I'm not going to share it. So, we'll be good on that. We'll be good. We've got to clean it all up and make sure that we just take care of our business. That's all. I mean, we did some good things, but we just didn't make the one extra play we needed to today. That's all.”
“Yeah, she was always visible and she's such a sweetheart. She loved the team . She loved the Detroit Lions. She was always available. She was great to certainly myself, my family, but she just , she loved the players. She loved everything about it. I mean, if you come out of a big game and you run the heck out of the ball, she would talk about the O-line. Just loved those double teams. And she was special that way. And really, she's part of a football family. I mean, they've owned this, the Lions, since the '60s, whatever, '63, '64. I mean, this is a football family, one of the few that are left. So, thoughts and prayers go out with the Ford family and her passing, but she was a special woman.”

title: Key Takeaways From Detroit Lions 39-35 Thanksgiving Loss Against Bears
full_text:
The Detroit Lions 2026 schedule has not featured many winning football teams, so the matchup against the Chicago Bears has been highly anticipated for weeks.
Both teams came into the Week 12 contest featuring a record of 8-2, with both seeking to keep their hopes of winning the NFC North strong and their seeding high in the NFC playoff chase.
Head coach Dan Campbell was asked earlier this week what the challenge was keeping players focused, due to families visiting from out of town and all the distractions that could come from playing an NFL game on a holiday.
“I think that's probably the biggest, and that comes with any team that plays at home on a holiday weekend or holiday game is just sometimes you do. I mean, all of our guys , most of our guys, coaches too, they've got family in," said Campbell. "You've got your own kin, then you've got your significant other, their family could be in. And I think sometimes what happens is the hard thing is you don't want to say no, right? That's where it gets tricky is, you're trying to entertain and you want to - and so it's hard to just tell somebody, 'Hey, look, I've got stuff I got to do.' But you just present it that way, just tell them about it. Listen, sometimes you've got to be the bad guy.
"They're in town to see you play and the best way for everybody to feel good about that is for you to be locked in, make sure you're prepared, do what you need to do," Campbell added further. "But, I feel like we'll be good. I mean, our guys get that. We've been through it and a number of our guys have been through this numerous times, so we know what it is and I think we'll handle it just fine.”
After 60 minutes of action, the Lions were not able to survive a tough contest against their division rival, losing again on Thanksgiving.
Caleb Williams was able to lead another fourth-quarter comeback drive, securing the Bears first division win of the 2026 season.
Here are the key takeaways from the Lions' 39-35 home loss.
Detroit won the opening coin toss and elected to receive. Led by Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown, the offense marched down the field to take an early 3-0 lead.
St. Brown excited the crowd early with an early one-handed grab that netted 27 yards and took the offense to the nine-yard line. Dennis Allen's defense clamped down and kept Jared Goff out of the end zone.
Unfortunately, right guard Tate Ratledge, who has had a stellar sophomore season, was injured on the opening drive and was replaced early in the game by Miles Frazier.
Special #14 pic.twitter.com/nGXEQIkYpr
Detroit's defense was going to be under the microscope this week, as Ben Johnson is one of the top offensive play-callers in the NFL.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard has steadied the ship the last six weeks, limiting opponents to less than 20 points consistently.
On their first offensive drive, the Bears were able to move the football into Detroit's territory, moving the chains without even needing a third-down.
Rookie Derrick Moore, who is now tasked with playing more at the defensive end position due to Aidan Hutchinson's injury, was able to punch out the football out from tight end Colston Loveland's possession.
Unfortunately for the Bears, Loveland was ruled out of the game with a knee injury.
After the Bears punted on their second offensive possession, Detroit's offense found the end zone for the first touchdown of the game.
Goff led the team on a 13-play, 75-yard drive that ate up just a little more of seven minutes off the clock.
Gibbs capped off the drive with a one-yard scamper.
The former first-round pick securd his fifth-straight game with a rushing touchdown, which is tied for the third-longest single-season streak in franchise history.
He later added a 70-yard explosive touchdown, extending Detroit's lead to 35-24 in the fourth quarter. A Christian Mahogany taunting penalty resulted in a Jake Bates missed extra point.
Best player on field Lions MVP: Jahmyr Gibbs pic.twitter.com/AhmSPIqlUm
Chicago was able to rally to tie the game, first with a field goal from Cairo Santos and then a rushing touchdown.
The Lions had a pivotal sequence near the end of the first half. After a good punt backed the Bears inside their own 10-yard line, a sack from Alim McNeill pushed Caleb Williams and company closer to their end zone.
Williams was strip-sacked by Derrick Moore, and a Bears lineman batted the ball out of the end-zone. Detroit was forced to decide between a safety and taking the ball inside the Chicago red-zone, and Campbell chose to take the points and the ball with 1:13 remaining in the first half.
False starts were an issue throughout the half, with the team recording four including three from center Juice Scruggs. They had two in a row to push them back on third-down, but Goff hit Gibbs for 11 yards then converted the fourth-down with a sneak.
After that, Goff hit Jameson Williams for 39 yards an d capped the drive off with a touchdown pass to Sam LaPorta. Detroit scored nine points in 67 seconds, and entered halftime with a 19-10 lead.
Chicago opened the second half with a 10-play, 68-yard touchdown drive to cut into Detroit's lead. Running back Kyle Monangai found the end one on a two-yard scamper.
With the game at 19-17, Detroit again targeted St. Brown and LaPorta and were able to move the football down the field.
Goff was surgical, connecting with St. Brown and LaPorta for 17-yard gains. Gibbs found the end zone for the second time, extending Detroit's lead to 26-17 early in the second half .
Jahmyr Gibbs reverses field for an impressive pickup of 32 yards! CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bkIRIvgBYj
Without DJ Wonnum and Chuck Clark, Detroit's defense consistently brought pressure. By the fourth quarter, Detroit's defense had sacked Williams a total of four times.
The Bears signal-caller was visibly frustrated on the sideline prior to Gibbs' explosive run, since the offensive line was struggling to block and gave up a crucial sack.
Moore had two sacks and linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez, who briefly left the game with an ankle injury, recorded his first sack of the 2026 season.
Chicago was able to break through with explosive plays of their own, as D'Andre Swift recorded a 30-yard touchdown in the third quarter and Rome Odunze cut Detroit's lead to 35-30 with a 41-yard touchdown. A successful two-point try brought the score to 35-32 midway through the final quarter.
After the Bears recorded an interception off Goff, safety Kerby Joseph was able to secure a key pass breakup in the fourth quarter, forcing a turnover on downs.
Needing a stop, the Lions defense failed to step up, allowing the Bears to win late in the fourth quarter. Williams hit Odunze again in the end zone with three seconds left, as Ben Johnson's squad came back from an 11-point defecit to win on Thanksgiving.

title: Lions Tate Ratledge Questionable to Return Against Bears
full_text:
Detroit Lions right guard Tate Ratledge suffered an injury on the team's first drive against the Chicago Bears and left the game.
He was replaced by Miles Frazier. Ratledge was officially diagnosed with ankle and knee injuries and ruled questionable to return.
Ratledge is in his second professional season after the Lions drafted him in the second-round of the 2025 NFL draft out of Georgia. He has not missed a game to this point in his career, starting all 28 possible games including Thursday's Thanksgiving matchup.
The second-year pro returned to the Lions' bench during their second offensive series and appeared to be preparing to re-enter the game. He would return to action for Detroit's third offensive series.
The Georgia product played over 1,000 snaps last year as a rookie, notching a 70.3 overall offensive grade via Pro Football Focus. He's one of three returning starters from last year, along with Penei Sewell and Christian Mahogany.
To help revamp their offensive line, the Lions brought in veterans Juice Scruggs and Cade Mays while drafting right tackle Blake Miller in the first-round of this year's draft. Scruggs has started nine games at center, while Miller has started all 10 of his appearances though he missed the Buffalo game with an injury.
The Lions have had some tough injury luck throughout the season. Defensive end Aidan Hutchinson is out for the season, while linebacker Jack Campbell is also on injured reserve with a neck injury. Detroit also lost rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard for the year to a knee injury suffered last week against the Buccaneers.
Frazier is also in his second NFL season, as the Lions drafted him in the fifth-round of the 2025 Draft out of LSU. He has made one start this season, that being at left guard when Christian Mahogany was benched for disciplinary reasons.
The LSU product appeared in five games as a rookie in 2025 after missing the start of the season with a lengthy bout of illness.
To make matters worse, the Lions were without defensive end D.J. Wonnum (back), safety Chuck Clark (hamstring) and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) for Thursday's game.
Detroit lead Thursday's game early, 3-0, on a Jake Bates field goal on their first drive. The defense, though shorthanded, came up big when rookie defensive end Derrick Moore forced a fumble on Chicago's ensuing offensive drive.

title: Setting Lions Fans Expectations for Jared Goff Against Bears
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are set to battle with the Chicago Bears with first-place in the NFC North on the line in front of a national audience.
Detroit has relied on its veteran quarterback Jared Goff to play at a high level each week, and he has done just that throughout the season. Through 10 games, Goff has thrown 20 touchdown passes against four interceptions.
Against the Bears and their high-powered offense, Goff may be lured into a shootout . Chicago's defense features a star on the interior line in Jeffery Simmons, who they acquired ahead of the trade deadline. Simmons has had five sacks since joining the Bears, including three last week against New Orleans.
As a result, Goff may have to air it out to give the Lions their best chance to win. He's facing off against his former offensive coordinator Ben Johnson on the other sideline, as Johnson is the Bears' head coach. Because of that, Goff will likely feel some added motivation to play well.
Sports Betting Dime's Drew Ellis believes a big day is in store for Goff, as he's predicting Goff to go over his projected over/under for passing yards in Thursday's game.
"I think these games with the Chicago Bears and Ben Johnson are a little more personal to Jared Goff than he lets on," Ellis told Lions OnSI. "His former OC has thrown some jabs at Goff since becoming Chicago’s head coach and Goff has responded with over 330 passing yards in both meetings with Johnson’s Bears. I expect Chicago to have more offensive success than Lions opponents have had over the last six games, so the Lions offense will have to produce a lot of points to win. That puts more on Goff to perform at a high level and I expect his yardage to pile up and reach at least 279 yards on Thursday."
Goff currently has a 1-4 record on Thanksgiving as a member of the Lions, with the lone win coming over the Bears in 2024. However, he has played well on the holiday with 1,202 passing yards, nine touchdown passes and zero interceptions in his appearances with the Lions on Thanksgiving.
Detroit went 2-0 against the Bears last season, and will be looking to extend their unbeaten streak against their former coordinator in what could be the biggest Thanksgiving matchup in franchise history.

title: Detroit Lions Week 12 Inactives List: Is DE Playing?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have released their official list of players that will not suit up against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field.
Cornerback Ennis Rakestraw was previously ruled inactive, as he continues to work his way back from a shoulder injury.
D.J. Reed and Kerby Joseph did not appear on the injury report and are set to play against Ben Johnson's squad.
Veteran defensive end DJ Wonnum has been ruled inactive after not participating in walkthrough practices this week. Undrafted free agent Anthony Lucas was elevated from the practice squad to provide insurance at the defensive end position.
Safety Chuck Clark will also be inactive this week. Against the Buccaneers, the talented defender was the green dot captain, given his prior experience leading a defense and communicating defensive calls.
Others ruled inactive include defensive lineman Tyrus Wheat and rookie cornerback Keith Abney.
“It's definitely some extra preparation for sure. I have not done it in three seasons, since 2022. So, just talking to myself at the house, saying the calls, making sure I'm not stuttering or mumbling up my words or whatnot, talking to the guys in the huddle and just not overthinking it, trying to get them all back on one page," said Clark. "I mean, that's the biggest thing. I know when I'm back there and I don't have a green dot, 'Hey, what's the call? What's the call?' So, guys want that call quick, fast so they can think and process, see the formation and we can go out there and make plays.”
He expressed he was proud of the defense and how they executed last week, especially since the Buccaneers had the top rushing offense in the National Football League.
“It felt good for sure," said Clark. "I mean, but it's always room to improve and grow. I mean, that's the cliche answer. I mean, we definitely left some things out there in that aspect of the run game. But we just definitely want to grow and get better. But facing a duo with tandem like that, man, we know those guys can take to the house at any time. So, that was big just to have that put out against them.”
