title: Kellen Moore Addresses Saints' Offensive Struggles After Bears Loss
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints had their opportunities to pull off an upset against one of the NFC's top teams Nov. 22, but the same offensive problems that have plagued them throughout the season proved costly once again.
After the Saints ' 21-13 loss to the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field, head coach Kellen Moore expressed frustration with his team's inability to capitalize on scoring chances, protect the football and execute in critical moments.
New Orleans fell to 3-7 after its offense committed two turnovers, and an injury-riddled offensive line gave up 6 sacks while repeatedly failing to finish drives, despite a defense that kept the game within reach.
The offensive struggles have become an increasingly concerning trend under Moore , particularly the team's inability to start fast. The Saints average just 0.9 points in the first quarter through 10 games, putting them in difficult situations before their offense can establish consistency.
Moore also addressed the team's ongoing ball-security problems, questionable fourth-down decisions, quarterback Tyler Shough 's performance and substitution issues that contributed to wasted timeouts and kept rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson off the field for an extended stretch.
"That's the NFL, and that's the frustration with it," Moore said. "I thought we battled. ... We just weren't able to make enough plays to win this football game."
The Saints will look to end their three-game losing streak when they travel to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 29.
Q: The Saints are averaging just 0.9 points per game in the first quarter. Have you tried everything to fix the slow starts?
Moore: "Obviously, it's as frustrating as anything. Again, we're not starting fast. I think we basically had one possession, and we stalled out. We drove it again and then stalled out once we got into plus territory.
"I feel like that's been too common in our opening drives. That's the challenging thing. It's not three-and-outs. It's just being able to finish a drive off."
Q: The offense had several possessions in Bears territory but struggled to capitalize. What's the biggest issue?
Moore: "Again, it's about sustaining drives and giving ourselves the chance to get the points at the end.
"We did have the one turnover on downs where we tried to get the touchdown instead of settling for the field goal. Then we just had some chances that we weren't able to take advantage of."
Q: How frustrating is it knowing the Bears weren't particularly explosive offensively and that a few plays could have changed the outcome?
Moore: "That's the NFL, and that's the frustration with it. I thought we battled. It's a really good offense. For our guys to create a couple turnovers was big, to create some short fields there.
"I thought there was some really good play there. We just weren't able to make enough plays to win this football game."
Q: The Saints have lost 23 fumbles since last season, the most in the NFL. Why has protecting the football remained such a persistent problem?
Moore: "Obviously, the disappointing part of it is just the fundamentals of protecting the football.
"The one that happened today was a catch-tuck, and they beat us to it before we could secure the football. They did a better job than us on that down. Obviously, we had the one interception after our own first down."
Q: What did you make of Tyler Shough's performance overall?
Moore: "I think he battled. Obviously, there are going to be things that we're going to have to look at, correct and improve as an offense. Ultimately, 13 points isn't enough to beat these guys."
Q: Do you think Shough has taken a step backward, and has the constant shuffling along the offensive line affected his decision-making?
Moore: "I think ultimately, collectively, we all want to play better football and coach better football. We have to do this thing together.
"Again, Tyler's battling. He gave us an opportunity to get back into that. He got us back down for a field goal opportunity for Charlie to kick that, and then we're down to one possession.
"That game wasn't without opportunities to make some plays. We just didn't get it done."
Q: What happened on Shough's interception?
Moore: "I'll have to look at it again more closely. Obviously, the safety came off. In the scramble phase, we've got to keep running our routes and give ourselves an opportunity so that guy doesn't have a chance to peel back.
"I did not see, based on where I was, where the location of the ball ended up. Obviously, a frustrating one for all of us."
Q: Did Shough need to get rid of the football quicker on the safety?
Moore: "We should be helping the right tackle on that play, and obviously, we just didn't execute it. The edge rusher had the angle."
Q: Was there supposed to be someone helping the right tackle with a chip block?
Moore: "There should be a chipper there, yes."
Q: Was that a missed assignment?
Moore: "No. Jordyn ran the route and didn't do the initial protection element of it. Chip, then run your route."
Q: What did you think about Shough's decision-making on the safety?
Moore: "Obviously, I don't think he's anticipating the edge rusher to be there that quickly. I felt like we'd have some presence there to be able to work through the progression.
"I think if we give ourselves just a touch more time, he's going to have a completion over the ball."
Q: Why did Tyson go approximately 12 consecutive snaps without playing? Was that related to his workload?
Moore: "Just the sequencing of those personnel groups. Again, I've got to do a better job of getting him in there on a few more of those occasions.
"We stayed on the ball a few times and tried to keep certain personnel groups on defense so we could execute some plays. That kind of kept Jordyn off on a few occasions."
Q: Was his absence related to the missed chip block or some form of punishment?
Moore: "No. We had a couple substitutions where we had Bryce and Barry in there for specific plays.
"Once we get into tempo, sometimes we're keeping those guys on the field so we don't allow them to substitute and get to some of their packages."
Q: Were those substitutions predetermined or based on the flow of the game?
Moore: "A lot of it's predetermined."
Q: What went well on Travis Etienne's 46-yard run?
Moore: "Obviously, I'll have to review it from a film perspective. I think being able to capture the edge was an important part, and him being able to get to the edge and make a play was important for us. We needed something like that."
Q: Why wasn't Etienne more involved during the first two offensive possessions?
Moore: "Just the flow of the sequencing there. Again, trying to get completions early based on the hashes and the direction in which we wanted to attack them.
"We probably didn't have as many run opportunities those first two drives, but I think he got in there the rest of the way."
Q: Did you consider kicking a field goal instead of going for it on fourth down late in the game?
Moore: "Yes. We obviously discussed it very briefly. Ultimately, we were going to need a touchdown. We felt like we were down there. It's third-and-two, fourth-and-two. We had an opportunity to get the touchdown at some point.
"It's also an 11-point game at that point, so you're going to have to have a two-point conversion as well. We felt like trying to score there and gather as much information as we could was important."
Q: Did analytics influence that decision?
Q: There appeared to be several issues with offensive substitutions. What happened?
Moore: "There were just some receiver substitutions. I've obviously got to do a better job of making sure we have cleaner communication there. We had to use a couple timeouts."
Q: How frustrating was it to lose timeouts because of a failed challenge and substitution problems?
Moore: "It puts you in a goofy spot at the end of the game because you're not going to have all the timeouts at the end.
"Obviously, we had some situations we've got to do better…

title: Saints Can't Get Out of Their Own Way in Disappointing Loss to Bears
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints ' offensive struggles and inability to protect the football proved costly once again Sunday afternoon.
Despite a strong defensive effort and a late comeback attempt, the Saints couldn't overcome two early turnovers, six sacks and missed scoring opportunities in a frustrating 21-13 loss to the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field.
The loss marks three straight for New Orleans and drops the Saints to 3-7, while Chicago improved to 8-2 with its fifth straight win.
The Saints finished with 307 total yards compared to Chicago's 311, but failed to score a touchdown on their final eight possessions, showcasing the Saints' inability to capitalize on the opportunities given to them, a criticism that head coach Kellen Moore has faced all season.
After a slow start by both teams, things deteriorated for New Orleans. Its second-quarter run game faltered when running back CJ Donaldson fumbled, giving Chicago excellent field position. That allowed the Bears to strike as Caleb Williams with a 3-yard touchdown pass to D'Andre Swift , extending the Bears' lead to 10-0.
Chicago got the ball back after quarterback Tyler Shough threw an interception to rookie safety Dillon Thieneman , and Williams connected with tight end Colston Loveland for a 15-yard strike to give the Bears a commanding 16-0 advantage.
New Orleans did finally show signs of life late in the first half.
Running back Travis Etienne Jr. broke free for a 46-yard run, setting up Shough's 1-yard touchdown pass to Alvin Kamara on fourth-and-goal to cut the deficit to nine.
The Saints defense then got another chance when linebacker Danny Stutsman intercepted Williams after a deflected pass. However, New Orleans’ special teams woes returned midway through the quarter as kicker Charlie Smyth missed a 47-yard field goal.
However, Smyth redeemed himself with a 56-yard field goal as time expired in the first half, cutting Chicago's lead to 16-10.
New Orleans couldn't build on that momentum.
The Bears extended their lead to 19-10 on Santos' third-quarter field goal before their defensive front took control and bullied the Saints' injury-depleted offensive line.
Chicago recorded six sacks, including three from defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . Montez Sweat delivered one of the game's biggest plays in the fourth quarter, sacking Shough in the end zone for a safety that extended the Bears' advantage to 21-10.
The Saints had another opportunity after Julian Blackmon recovered a Swift fumble, but their ensuing possession stalled on fourth down at Chicago's 10-yard line.
Shough finished 25 of 42 for 222 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Chris Olave led New Orleans with nine receptions for 102 yards, while Devaughn Vele added seven catches for 76 yards.
Smyth connected on a 51-yard field goal with 1:10 remaining, but Chicago recovered the ensuing onside kick to seal the victory.
New Orleans now turns its attention to next Sunday's road matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals , looking to avoid another disappointing result in a season rapidly slipping away.

title: Three Keys to Victory: Can the Saints Upset the Bears?
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints face an uphill battle Sunday when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears in a matchup between two teams heading in opposite directions.
Coming off another disappointing loss to the Carolina Panthers , the Saints (3-6) are looking to bounce back against a Chicago team (7-2) that has emerged as one of the NFC's top contenders.
However, pulling off an upset won't be easy for head coach Kellen Moore 's squad, especially against a Bears offense averaging nearly 27 points per game and a defense that ranks among the league's best .
For New Orleans to have any chance of leaving Chicago with a victory, it must eliminate the costly mistakes that have plagued it throughout the season while finding a way to slow down Caleb Williams and the Bears' explosive offense.
Here are three keys to victory for the Saints against the Bears.
This is a major necessity for the Saints.
New Orleans has 17 turnovers (tied for 27th in the NFL) and a minus-8 differential (29th). As great as Tyler Shough has been for the Saints, his seven interceptions and four lost fumbles have repeatedly put the Saints in tough spots.
Chicago also has 17 turnovers, including four interceptions from Williams against Tampa Bay. This gives the Saints defense an opportunity, with just nine takeaways (tied for 24th) and none in three games. Forcing turnovers can lead to great opportunities to put points on the board.
However, forcing turnovers requires the offense to capitalize, something New Orleans has struggled with all season.
The Saints have only scored nine first-quarter points through nine games (literally a point per quarter) and have gone scoreless in seven opening quarters. That will not work against a Chicago team averaging nearly 27 points per game. Moore's offense needs faster starts, fewer penalties, and touchdowns instead of field goals.
Do that, and the Saints’ chances of pulling off an upset get a little higher.
The Saints' defense faces a daunting task in slowing down one of the league's most potent offensive units.
Chicago's offense features top-tier production across the board: seventh in scoring (26.8 points per game), seventh in total yards (383.0 per game), and fourth on the ground (142.0 rushing yards per game).
Behind Caleb Williams, who has powered the Bears to four straight wins since returning from a hamstring injury, Chicago has put up 27 points or more in every game of that streak.
Given New Orleans' vulnerability against the pass, keeping Williams from finding a rhythm in the pocket is critical.
The Saints currently rank near the bottom of the league defensively—21st against the pass (231.0 yards per game allowed) and 29th overall (360.8 total yards per game allowed).
Defensive coordinator Brandon Staley needs to dial up pressure to disrupt Williams while keeping him contained inside the pocket to limit playmaking on the run.
Much of that pressure must come from edge rushers Carl Granderson and Chase Young , who have logged a combined 16.5 sacks on the season.
However, pressuring Williams is only part of the equation.
The Saints must also slow down a rushing attack that averages 142 yards per game, fourth-best in the NFL.
Running back D'Andre Swift leads Chicago with 576 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns, while Kyle Monangai averages 5.4 yards per carry with 324 yards and three touchdowns.
That does not bode well for a team ranked 27th in run defense, allowing nearly 130 rushing yards per game.
New Orleans has shown improvement against the run over its past two games, holding Cleveland to 95 yards and Carolina to 97.
Linebacker Kaden Elliss will be particularly important after recording 26 tackles and two sacks over those two contests.
If the Saints can limit Chicago's rushing attack and force Williams into obvious passing situations, they'll have a better opportunity to generate pressure and create turnovers.
Allowing the Bears to establish their running game would make an already difficult matchup even more challenging.

title: J.J. McCarthy's Third-Down Struggles Loom Large as Giants' Schedule Toughens
full_text:
The New York Giants offense has done enough to keep the team competitive, but if there is one area where the unit can be much better, it's on third down.
The Giants rank 17th in the league in third-down conversion rate, having converted 38.30% of their third-down opportunities this season.
A big part of that middling figure has been a lean toward the running game, with the passing game taking more of a back seat.
Overall, quarterback J.J. McCarthy has thrown just 33 passes on third down, 11 of which have gone for first downs, putting him 34th among quarterbacks.
Breaking those numbers down further, McCarthy has converted just one pass attempt on third downs requiring 10 or more yards, while throwing two interceptions and having one pass dropped on those attempts. He also has just one touchdown pass on those attempts.
On third downs requiring between one and five yards, McCarthy has attempted 11 passes, converting seven. He has no touchdown passes on third-down attempts requiring five or fewer yards.
Despite the better conversion rate on those shorter attempts, he still ranks toward the bottom of the league in third-down conversion rate, tied for 30th with Sam Darnold of Seattle and Jalen Hurts of Philadelphia.
With the Giants' schedule getting much more challenging starting in Week 13, when they host the San Francisco 49ers, better third-down passing production will be paramount if the Giants are to sew up their first NFC East title since 2011.
Speaking of division title holders, the Philadelphia Eagles apparently ain't dead yet.
The 4-7 Eagles, who mounted a historic comeback win over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving, can still find themselves in line to repeat as division champions, according to Rob Maaddi of the Associated Press .
For that to happen, the Eagles would need to go 4-1 against an opponent slate that includes Arizona, Indianapolis, Seattle, Houston and San Francisco, and the Giants would need to go 2-4 against their remaining opponents (Indianapolis, San Francisco, Seattle, Cleveland, Detroit and Dallas).
Realistically, any dreams of the NFC East title coming down to the Week 18 regular-season finale between the Giants and Eagles are just that: a dream.
The Giants need at least three more wins to clinch the NFC East, a division that, based on what's happening across the rest of the conference, will likely have only one representative in the postseason this year.
The other team that could spoil the Giants' quest is the Commanders (4-5-1), if Washington goes 3-3 against Arizona, Tennessee, Houston, Atlanta, Minnesota and Jacksonville. Washington, remember, holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Giants.
The Giants should be able to topple the Colts this weekend, leaving them with the challenge of finding two more wins after that. And as we learned last week, a dominant record doesn't guarantee anything.
Per The Athletic's playoff simulator, the Giants' most likely finish is 9-7-1 (31%) , which should be enough to win the division title (70%) and earn a spot in the postseason tournament (83%).
If they can find another win to reach 10 victories (which would be their first double-digit regular-season win total since 2016, when they went 11-5 in a 16-game season), the Giants' chances of winning the division jump to 94%, and their chances of a playoff berth rise to 99%.

title: Two Areas J.J. McCarthy Must Clean Up for the Giants' Playoff Push
full_text:
J.J. McCarthy has been playing some fine ball since coming to the New York Giants and taking over the starting quarterback role from Jameis Winston.
But as good as he's looked, two areas of his game are still very much a work in progress.
The first is his deep ball. McCarthy has 26 deep-ball attempts (20-plus air yards) this season, tied for 24th most among the league's 32 quarterbacks. He has completed a dismal 38.5% of those throws, which ranks tied for 19th among quarterbacks.
"At the end of the day, I just missed them," he said of his unsuccessful deep passing attempts since coming to the Giants.
"The big thing that kind of stood out to me was just put some more air on the ball and let the receivers be able to track it a little bit better, but that's an easy fix, and we'll get it fixed."
The second, and perhaps more important, area is passing touchdowns. McCarthy has just three passing touchdowns since coming to the Giants. That's the same number as injured starter Jaxson Dart, who reached that total in Week 1 alone.
For McCarthy, it's not so much a matter of arm strength. He has plenty of that to make the throws that need to be made.
But he's still getting up to speed on the playbook. He's also learning how each of his receivers reacts when he's covered or jammed at the line of scrimmage, and he has to commit each week's game plan to memory. With all that on his plate, it's fair to say McCarthy isn't playing at full speed yet.
All of that will come in time as he keeps leading the Giants' offense toward what they hope will be their first postseason berth since 2022.
"Just being able to get in here and work with the guys just constantly and just be able to get those reps over and over again. But I'm going to make those," he said on Wednesday after the Giants concluded practice.
"Those are things that are going to come and have shown up, but sometimes you just miss. In this league, you can't miss too many times. So just be able to be ready for that next opportunity and nail it."

title: Giants Are Thankful for the Eagles: Updated NFC East Race Breakdown
full_text:
It was a happy Thanksgiving indeed for the New York Giants .
Im so proud of the pigeons man!!! Good for yall!
The defending NFC East champion Philadelphia Eagles did Big Blue a huge favor on Thanksgiving, rallying from a 21-point deficit against the Dallas Cowboys to win 39-38 on a 60-yard walk-off field goal by Jake Elliott.
Philadelphia's rally is the largest comeback win on Thanksgiving in NFL history.
The Eagles (4-7) still have the lowest playoff chances in the division. According to The Athletic's playoff simulator , they have a 2% chance of winning the NFC East. Dallas, which dropped to 5-7, has an 8% chance of winning the division.
That leaves the Washington Commanders as the biggest threat to the Giants' hold on first place. Washington (4-5-1) has a 19% chance of winning the division, while the Giants (6-3-1) have a 71% chance.
Washington holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Giants thanks to its 24-21 win over Big Blue in Week 10.
The Giants' remaining strength of schedule ranks ninth-toughest in the league (.547), according to Tankathon . Their toughest remaining opponents are the San Francisco 49ers (Week 13), Seattle Seahawks (Week 14), Cleveland Browns (Week 15) and Detroit Lions (Week 16).
Washington has the third-easiest remaining strength of schedule, with its remaining opponents combining for a .411 winning percentage. Its two toughest remaining opponents are the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Minnesota Vikings.
Washington's next three games are against the Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans and Houston Texans, all teams with losing records.

title: J.J. McCarthy is Thankful for Being the Giants Starting Quarterback
full_text:
New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy is feeling exceptionally thankful this holiday season.
As Americans from coast to coast celebrate Thanksgiving on Thursday, the 23-year-old is expressing some extra gratitude for the turn of events that swept him from the Land of 10,000 Lakes to the blue side of the Meadowlands.
After all, this change of scenery made him the Giants' starting quarterback.
For McCarthy, however, it was simply the chance to play a part in what could be a special season for Big Blue.
"The thing that I'm so grateful for is just to be a piece of the puzzle, of this puzzle," McCarthy said.
"Just being able to kind of smoothly implement myself into this culture and what (Head) Coach (John) Harbaugh has as his vision for our team, week in and week out, I'm just so blessed to be a part of it."
After losing incumbent starter Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, the Giants sent a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for McCarthy, hoping to strengthen a thin quarterback room.
That trade began a journey that put the No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft in the driver's seat of coordinator Matt Nagy's offense.
Since taking over for 12-year veteran Jameis Winston in Week 6, McCarthy has completed 59.2 percent of his passes for 1,088 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions in six appearances.
McCarthy has quickly grasped the playbook and shown sound leadership both on the field and in the locker room. Despite his 3-1 record as New York's starter, the 6-foot-3, 219-pound quarterback has occasionally struggled with accuracy.
Though his output has been far from perfect, McCarthy remains driven by a burning desire to succeed. While he may be best suited to an offense built on zone reads, designed runs, and RPO packages, the Michigan product has also shown his prowess in the deep passing game.
Because McCarthy's skills are similar to Dart's, the Giants have been able to use some of the plays originally designed for New York's opening-day starter. To date, that has meant more ups than downs for Nagy's offense.
Still, McCarthy credits much of his success to his comfort in his new surroundings. After a tumultuous stay in Minnesota, the La Grange Park, Illinois, native has found a home in both the Empire and Garden states.
Based on his recent comments, McCarthy hopes to remain in the "New York Groove" for quite some time.
"New York City, New Jersey, absolutely so grateful to just be a citizen here and be able to engulf myself in the culture of this city and this place and just absolutely love it," McCarthy said.
"I think the blue-collar, hardworking people that you just see left and right, you know exactly where you stand with every single person that you come across," he added.
"That means a lot to me. It's a passionate state. It's a passionate fan base. Having that edge as a team is truly impactful. I'm excited to see them keep showing up and showing out.
"Everyone wants to see us succeed, and that's exactly where you want to be. Everyone's been so nice and welcoming since I've been here, and I] can't thank them enough for just making it feel like home."
Entering Week 12, the Giants are 6-3-1 and in sole possession of first place in the NFC East. According to The Athletic, New York has about a 67 percent chance to make the playoffs and a 65 percent chance to win the division.
To stay in front, McCarthy knows he and the offense need to improve quickly to keep the team in the win column this weekend against the Indianapolis Colts.
"We've got a great opponent this week, great defense," McCarthy said. "They play super fundamentally sound. They play really hard, and it's going to be a great test for our offense."

title: Giants Giving John Mara Extra Reason to Smile This Thanksgiving
full_text:
It's never a bad idea to make sure the boss has a smile on his face at work.
For the New York Giants , that goal has taken on a whole new meaning this season for team co-owner John Mara as he continues his fight against an undisclosed form of cancer first announced last fall.
And as anyone who has had cancer treatments knows, they are not easy to deal with.
There are often long chemotherapy sessions that unfortunately don't distinguish between the cancerous cells in the body and the healthy ones. Chemotherapy can leave one feeling physically and emotionally drained, not to mention the toll it can take on one's appearance.
Then there are the post-chemo treatments, which stimulate the bone marrow to jump-start white blood cell production and lower the risk of serious infection during chemotherapy.
Having been through cancer treatments and the post-chemo treatments designed to boost white blood cell counts, I speak from experience.
They are painful. You feel like someone took a sledgehammer to your body, to your bones. It's hard to move at normal speed, if at all, without assistance, lest you risk falling.
And it can take several days for the medication to do what it's intended to do which means a lot of discomfort that sometimes leaves you wondering if you're ever going to feel normal again.
I don't profess to know what kind of treatments the 71-year-old Mara is undergoing. I can only imagine what he has had to deal with given the peaks and valleys that cancer treatments can create for a person both physically and mentally.
That's why the saving grace for his mental state these days is undoubtedly seeing his team have the kind of success it's had under John Harbaugh, the head coach he and his family desperately wanted to save the flailing franchise.
Harbaugh's Giants have delivered impressive highlights, including nationally televised victories over the hated Dallas Cowboys and the "powerhouse" Jacksonville Jaguars.
They finally snapped the Philadelphia hex by beating the Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field for the first time in 13 seasons.
And at 6-3-1, they sit atop the NFC East for the first time in years, all without their starting quarterback, outside linebacker and inside linebacker, and now, moving forward, one of their starting cornerbacks.
"He's pretty happy," Harbaugh said on Wednesday. "I know one thing: he had a big smile on his face after that game (against Jacksonville) on Sunday."
Indeed. Mara, much like his father, Wellington, before him, takes a certain degree of joy in being around the team every single day, something his cancer treatments unfortunately might not always allow.
He enjoys watching practice and interacting with the players and coaches, a relationship that by all accounts is mutual.
"That's the idea, man," Harbaugh said. "You work hard, and he's worked hard. I know that's what he thinks about all the time: his team, the Giants. He's excited."
While Mara continues his battle against cancer, he has undoubtedly taken solace in knowing that, for the first time in years, he will have something extra to be thankful for this Thanksgiving: the state of the football franchise that has been a part of his life from the moment he entered the world.

title: From John Harbaugh to Arvell Reese: What Giants Fans Are Thankful for in 2026
full_text:
Thanksgiving has not been a pleasant football holiday for New York Giants fans for much of the last decade and a half. The playoffs often feel out of reach by Halloween, as focus shifts to mock drafts and free-agency theorizing. This year, however, everyone gets to bask in the present .
The Giants are giving their fan base a cornucopia brimming with pride and prosperity. They have given people many reasons to be thankful this Turkey Day, but we managed to whittle the list down to five.
John Harbaugh and Big Blue needed each other. The former set out for a fresh start after an 18-year run with the Baltimore Ravens, while the latter desperately searched for a legitimate head coach who could change the results on the field and the culture off it. Although everyone is still in the honeymoon phase, this union is going splendidly.
Sure, there have been some bumps, as in any relationship, but Harbaugh has quickly repaired much of the trust the organization damaged in the recent past.
The Super Bowl XLVII champion brought an experienced, creative coaching staff that has maximized players' strengths. Under his leadership, the G-Men are more disciplined, accountable, motivated and fundamentally sound. Most of all, they are better.
Whether by hiring forward-thinking coaches like Dennard Wilson , bringing over talent from Baltimore or holding more demanding practices, Harbaugh has boosted New York to first place in the NFC East.
If the Giants can hold their lead, they will celebrate their first division title since the Super Bowl-winning 2011 campaign. One man alone cannot rescue a franchise from the abyss, but he can certainly put it on the right trajectory.
Much like Squanto showed the Pilgrims the way, Harbaugh has helped a seemingly hopeless organization remember its identity. Or something along those lines.
New York pegged the Ohio State star as a future game-wrecker at the 2026 NFL Draft. But who would have predicted this?
Only 10 games into his NFL career, the fifth overall pick is already one of the team's most valuable players. He owns an NFL-best 57 solo tackles and a team-high 4.5 sacks. Reese is adapting expertly to the game script, plugging gaps as an impactful run-stopper one week and relentlessly pursuing the quarterback the next.
Beyond the stats, which are plenty impressive on their own, the 21-year-old embodies the intensity that fueled the team in its heyday. Harbaugh's first draft pick as the Giants' head coach is effectively laying the groundwork for how a new Giants player is supposed to carry himself on the field.
Most fans were excited about the Isaiah Likely signing, as he was a Harbaugh guy who flashed promise with the Ravens despite competing with fellow tight end Mark Andrews for targets.
Still, there was reason to be skeptical. Likely had never carried a large workload over an entire season and was coming off the worst year of his NFL career.
In these situations, the player often fails to meet expectations. Likely has shattered them. The 2022 fourth-rounder has already set career highs across the board , with 56 receptions for 610 yards and seven touchdowns. And there are still seven regular-season games remaining.
From supporting cast member to offensive igniter. From Andrews' shadow to potential All-Pro. Given the Giants' past free-agency blunders, they should be mighty thankful to have landed a bargain at $40 million.
Deonte Banks was widely regarded as a bust. Fellow former first-round pick Greg Newsome II was not playing up to his potential, either. Paulson Adebo had fallen off a cliff. Colton Hood was inexperienced. Jevon Holland was coming off another rough campaign. Ar'Darius Washington was flying well under the radar.
"New York needs more help in the secondary." I wrote that sentence plenty of times during the offseason, and others felt the same.
The cornerback room may as well have been the island of misfit toys, and the safeties were walking question marks. Sure, the group had talent, but it had little to no momentum.
Dennard Wilson has transformed the unit, implementing more aggressive man-coverage schemes that let players like Banks and Newsome flourish. Of course, the players themselves deserve significant credit.
Banks is allowing just 9.5 yards per catch and a 64.9 passer rating , according to Pro Football Focus. He has two interceptions, including a pick-six that clinched a win over the Arizona Cardinals. His 14 pass breakups are tied for the league lead.
Newsome boasts a 62.0 passer rating allowed and played well enough to earn a contract extension with $32 million guaranteed. He will be sidelined for multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain , but Adebo just had his best performance as a Giant in a Week 11 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Holland has four interceptions, including a game-sealer against the Tennessee Titans, and Washington has been incredibly active.
An anticipated weakness has become a surprise strength.
Excitement turned to devastation when Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 2. Jameis Winston rode the roller coaster, and New York found ways to win. But the offense was built for a mobile quarterback.
Harbaugh and general manager Joe Schoen took advantage of the Minnesota Vikings' apparent exasperation and acquired J.J. McCarthy for only a 2027 fifth-rounder. A team with its own quarterback issues, both short and long term, decided to part with a 23-year-old who had only 10 games of NFL experience.
Despite struggling against the Jaguars and posting a 59.2% completion rate across six games, McCarthy has been a net positive for the Giants.
The former No. 10 overall pick gives offensive coordinator Matt Nagy more flexibility, and he has proven he can make layered throws. More consistency is obviously needed, but the Giants have time to develop him.
Considering how desperate some teams are under center, Harbaugh should be quite appreciative of the Vikings this Thanksgiving.

title: Giants Not Relaxing After Jaguars Upset
full_text:
There really has never been any reason to question the New York Giants ' focus this season. Sure, they've scuffled through bouts of poor execution, but they've overcome enough missteps to sit atop the NFC East, with a two-game lead in the loss column heading into Thanksgiving.
Are they thankful? You bet. Will they relax on Sunday against the Colts in Indianapolis (3-8), even for a moment? Not a chance.
The players' reaction to upsetting the Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) last weekend should have hammered home any evidence one needed to understand the Giants' mindset.
"The next thing, that's all we're focused on," quarterback J.J. McCarthy said.
"We're focused on getting into these meetings, that team meeting, watching the film with our units and focusing on how we could get better and make sure that every individual play coming into the next game against Indy is going to be something that we absolutely maximize and optimize when we get those opportunities. For us, the future is that next moment, and that's all we care about."
Indeed, the victory celebration was much more subdued than some might think after a win in which few gave the Giants much of a chance. After all, the Jaguars had been on a roll and were perceived as a big step up in competition.
"I think we proved that the only thing that's going to get in our way is us, and that gives us a lot of confidence," McCarthy said.
"There are so many great teams in this league, and just really focusing on doing things our way, the right way every single time we get an opportunity to do that. At the end of the day, as I said, we're just focused on that next thing and how we could get better in attacking that."
McCarthy, who arrived in a trade with the Vikings in late September, didn't need long to catch on to the team's mantra. It all stems from head coach John Harbaugh's weekly message about going 1-0.
And he's not about to pull it back.
"It's going to be a different challenge next week," Harbaugh said, "and we’ve got to be up for that challenge, too, because this football team [the Colts] is cornered and they’re hungry and they’re going to be ready to play their best football game and we’ve got to be up for it.. We've got to be ready."

title: Giants Refuse to Overlook Depleted Colts: 4 Storylines to Watch This Week
full_text:
On paper, the upcoming matchup between the New York Giants and the Indianapolis Colts suggests this week should be a cakewalk for the Giants.
The Colts have unloaded several key players, including guard Quenton Nelson, receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. They have also moved on from quarterback Daniel Jones and plan to start Anthony Richardson Sr. this week.
But that's not how the Giants are viewing the matchup.
"We know we're going to get the Colts' best this Sunday. They're not going to go out there and not play hard," said right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor.
"They're going to play as hard as they possibly can, especially with the gravity of the game for us, but then also, we're in first place. I'm sure they're saying in their locker room, 'Let's go out there and beat the first-place team of the NFC East and see what we can do.' We're going to take that, go in there and play as hard as we can."
And, of course, hope that they come out with a victory.
Now for this week's storylines.
Once again, a key starter has been claimed by the injury bug. This time it's cornerback Greg Newsome II. He suffered a high ankle sprain in Sunday's win over the Jaguars and had TightRope surgery to speed his recovery. He will miss at least four weeks.
The Giants have been relatively lucky with the next man up keeping the team afloat:
The Giants have been relatively lucky when it comes to the next man up keeping the team above water.
Jameis Winton stepped in for Jaxson Dart at cornerback, Kayvon Thibodeaux has stepped into a bigger role at outside linebacker following the ACL injury suffered by Brian Burns, Micah McFadden has been mostly solid after the team lost inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, and Dawaune Smoot and Trace Ford have both done well to fill the voids left by Roy Robertson-Harris and Chauncey Golston on the defensive line.
Paulson Adebo is set to fill Newsome's spot. Adebo played well on Sunday after Newsome's early exit, and the hope is that he can rise to the challenge.
The Giants are tied with the Green Bay Packers for second in the league with 18 fumbles, one fewer than the Los Angeles Chargers. Running back Cam Skattebo has five of them. That ties him for seventh among all offensive players and for first among running backs, alongside Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.
A big part of the problem appears to be that Skattebo seeks contact. That's all well and good, but in some situations a running back is better off avoiding contact that puts the ball in harm's way.
It would be surprising for the Giants to repeat the "quasi-benching" of Skattebo they handed him in Week 6 against the Saints. Still, this carelessness with the ball in traffic can't continue.
You could argue that Dominic Zvada's missed 32-yard field goal was actually good, and to our eyes it looked that way. But that's irrelevant.
What is relevant is that Zvada needs to get back to his early-season form, when his kicks were stress-free no matter which hash they came from.
The Giants' offense was meant to be powered by its running game, but that hasn't always been the case.
New York ranks 24th in the league at 3.8 yards per rushing attempt. When it comes to closing out games in the fourth quarter, the Giants average only 3.4 yards per attempt, which ranks 23rd.
They are also tied for third in the league with two fourth-quarter fumbles, one of which was lost. Their 13 rushing first downs in the fourth quarter tie them for 26th in the league.
In short, those aren't glowing numbers. They may help explain why the Giants have just a plus-6 point differential in the fourth quarter, and why head coach John Harbaugh is believed to want to add to the running back room at some point.

title: Jets Confidence Meter: Judging David Bailey's All-Pro Case Before Week 12 vs. Dolphins
full_text:
This Thanksgiving season, the Jets should be thankful for many things . At the top of their list is second-overall rookie edge rusher David Bailey.
Since being drafted by the Jets out of Texas Tech, Bailey has recorded 9.5 sacks and six forced fumbles through his first 10 games played. No rookie in NFL history has ever put up a stat line like that.
If the season ended today, Bailey would be named the 2026 NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year. Giants linebacker Arvell Reese has had a stellar season himself, but Bailey has been the lone bright spot on a bad Jets defense .
That said, could Bailey's rookie year put him in rare company as a potential All-Pro in Year 1? The chance of that may be a lot longer than people realize.
Few players in Jets history have provided as positive an impact on the team as Bailey has through his first 10 games. His work as an edge rusher is already elite, but his high motor and run defense have been far brighter spots in his game than people realized.
There's a reason David Bailey was the No. 2 pick 💪 NYJvsLAC on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/8sIdm9IXOx
In short, Bailey has been everything the Jets could have hoped for when they took him with the second overall pick.
"I'm a huge believer in you build a team from the inside out, and when you have someone of the magnitude that you know has a chance to affect the game by affecting the quarterback," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said of Bailey. "That makes a huge difference in winning and losing."
New York hasn't done a lot of winning this year.
Despite Bailey's heroics, the Jets are 3-8 with a matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday . Despite the numerous losses and the team's struggles as a whole on defense, Bailey deserves all the praise he gets.
His impact, both on and off the field has been shared by many leaders on the Jets' roster.
But is Bailey's maturity and high motor enough to be a first-team All-Pro? That's not something I'm confident in... yet.
It's incredibly rare for a rookie to be named an All-Pro. New York saw that in Sauce Gardner in his first year as the former fourth-overall selection, but his career has taken a nosedive after two elite years to begin his career.
The last two edge rushers to be named an All-Pro in their rookie season were Micah Parsons in 2021 and Lawrence Taylor in 1981. Taylor recorded an unofficial 9.5 sacks in his first year and also accounted for four fumbles forced and a fumble recovered. Parsons, meanwhile, recorded 13 sacks in a hybrid LB/EDGE role.
Bailey's standing as a pure EDGE will hurt him in this case. Will Anderson in Houston currently has 11.5 sacks and is considered the favorite for NFL Defensive Player of the Year ( -120, 1st on DraftKings Sportsbook ). The Bears' Jeffery Simmons (+300) and the 49ers' Fred Warner (+700) round out the top three.
Bailey, meanwhile, is in a 17-way tie for the 19th-best odds (+10000), putting things into perspective.
The best way for the Jets to watch their top edge rusher get All-Pro honors this season is for Bailey to either break the single-season forced-fumbles record (10) or the rookie sack record (14.5). He is four forced fumbles and five sacks away from reaching either mark.
It's possible, but it's not something I'm counting on for the final six games of the year.

title: 3 Lessons Jets Must Learn From This Year's Thanksgiving Day Games
full_text:
It's been 14 years since the Jets last played on Thanksgiving Day . Their 4-4 all-time record on Turkey Day shows they have as much success as struggles.
The three slated games this season brought plenty of excitement in some games and utter domination in others. Through all three of Thursday's contests, though, the Jets have key lessons to learn if they want to build a winning organization.
Let's get to the three most important lessons right now.
Boy, the Bears and Lions game Thursday afternoon was fun, huh? Chicago came back from down 11 late in the fourth quarter to win on a last-second throw from Caleb Williams to Rome Odunze. In total, the teams combined for 74 points and over 1,000 yards of total offense.
Chicago's defense came into the game ranked in the top 10 in points allowed and yards. Detroit's run defense ranked top-10 in rushing.
After that, the Eagles and Cowboys combined for nearly 80 points in the 4:45 p.m. ET game.
It simply didn't matter. In the modern NFL, offenses win games more often than defenses. A strong strategic coaching staff that understands the rules of the NFL and where the game is going will put his team in position to win more games than not.
Until the Jets accept that this is what the team needs to become, they will be a step behind the rest of the league.
New York's biggest lesson to learn from the second Thanksgiving Day game is to just not be the Dallas Cowboys.
Coaches who are hired to install a culture into an organization are met with immediate expectations to win. When they don't, they normally don't have strategic plans in order to fix what the team is struggling with most.
That's where the important lesson of Philadelphia's comeback win over the Cowboys come through. Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni has been to the playoffs in each of his first five seasons with the team. They have found ways to win throughout his tenure including two Super Bowls and a championship win. The team's 2-7 start to the season was nothing short of a disaster. But because of Sirianni's culture of winning, they have turned around their season in the last two games.
Maybe the Eagles don't make the playoffs this season. Perhaps they don't look as good as they did in the fourht quarter of Sunday's win. But Sirianni showed the team remains behind him despite the down year. And his past success is a big reason why.
Do the Jets have that with Glenn at the moment ?
Jets fans continue to set their sights on the 2027 draft as the best chance to get their quarterback of the future. Many looked at the team choosing not to tank the final six games of the season as a bad sign for their chances at a top pick.
But as we learned from the Bills and Chiefs, teams don't need the top pick to come away with an elite quarterback. Patrick Mahomes was the second quarterback taken in his draft class. Josh Allen was the third quarterback taken in the 2017 class that also came via a trade-up.
What's the lesson the Jets need to learn from that?
It's not about getting the highest pick to take a quarterback; it's about picking the right one for the offense they want to run. The right one that fits the talent across the offensive position group.
The Jets can't look at the Chiefs and Bills Thanksgiving game as an example of needing the top overall pick. They need to look at it as a blueprint for why they need to pick the right guy above everything else.

title: 3 Defensive Prospects Should Already Be on Jets' 2027 Draft Radar Before the Bye Week
full_text:
The Jets’ defense has taken a step up this season . New York currently ranks 13th in opponent yards per game in 2026—a massive change from being ranked 25th last year.
That said, the Jets still have evident defensive concerns. For example, Gang Green is still below average in points allowed, ranking 22nd this season. With holes still on the roster, look for New York to address them in the 2027 NFL Draft.
Entering Week 12, New York holds three of the first 15 picks of the 2027 draft . It is safe to assume Gang Green will use at least one of those picks on the defensive side of the ball.
Cornerback, linebacker, edge rusher, and an interior defensive lineman are New York’s biggest needs going into the draft. If the Jets want to address the defense early on Day 1, these three players should already be on their shortlist before they reach their Week 13 bye.
Dylan Stewart is trying to be the first South Carolina Gamecock to be drafted in the top five since Jadeveon Clowney in 2014. The edge rusher may be on his way to that mark if the Jets are looking to address the position early. Stewart is 6’5", weighs 250 lbs, and looks the part of an NFL edge rusher.
He figures to be one of the first defensive players off the board , and New York has the draft capital to make that happen.
Stewart has only recorded two sacks in his injury-shortened 2026 season. However, the edge looks the part despite his low sack numbers. New York could place him on the other side of David Bailey , which would be a nightmare for opposing quarterbacks.
Stewart’s physical presence would make an immediate impact in New York, and the Jets should look to bring him to Florham Park in April.
The Sauce Gardner trade is one of the main reasons the Jets hold the draft capital they do in 2027 . While the return has been more than worth it for the Jets, a Gardner-sized hole still remains in the secondary. Leonard Moore could easily fill that spot for New York.
Moore has been one of the best corners in the nation in 2026. The 21-year-old has allowed only 11 receptions in the nine games he has played this season. He has also yet to give up a touchdown in coverage this season. Moore could be an immediate starter for a team that needs a lockdown corner.
Top 10 Fastest Max Speed | Week 12 1 | 22.8 MPH  Leonard Moore @LeonardKevMoore CB Notre Dame #ReelSpeed pic.twitter.com/cBEajTNtcg
The Jets should look to make themselves the team that benefits when the draft arrives.
Xavier Gilliam has been one of the best interior defensive linemen in the nation in 2026. The Tennessee Volunteer has shown he can wreck games against both the pass and the run. The defensive tackle may be the perfect addition for a team that traded away Quinnen Williams in 2025.
If Gilliam falls to the teens of the first round, New York shouldn’t hesitate to draft him.
The defensive tackle has been dominant during his time in Tennessee. So far this season, Gilliam has eight sacks to go along with 24 run stops. He is multidimensional in the middle of the D-line, which is something New York has been missing. His presence in the middle could immediately impact a Jets defense that ranks 30th against the run.

title: Aaron Glenn Proves Jets Have Right Mindset Heading Into Must-Win Dolphins Revenge Game
full_text:
Don't look now, but the Jets have a path to get back into contention in the AFC.
The Steelers, Patriots, Raiders and Ravens are all starting backup quarterbacks for the remainder of the season. It may seem ludicrous to throw the 3-8 Jets as a team in contention, but the math is actually there.
All the team has to do to build on that momentum is defeat the one-win Dolphins in Sunday's Week 12 action.
Of course, that's easier said than done.
New York is Miami's only win of the season after losing to them at home in a 28-25 loss in Week 7. With little rope left and an 0-9 record in divisional play, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn knows a win in South Florida is of paramount importance.
It happened early in that Week 7 game.
The Jets walked into the contest at 2-4, but had hopes that victories against the then-winless Dolphins and young Raiders would be enough to save their season. What they didn't expect, though, was to fall into a 21-7 deficit before losing by three.
The Dolphins, for how poorly they have played, punched the Jets in the mouth to the tune of 156 rushing yards and scores on three of their first four possessions of the game. Yes, New York began outplaying Miami in the second half, but it wasn't enough: the defense simply wasn't good enough in that game.
It's not like their defense is any better now. New York is currently the third-worst run defense in the league and still has questions along its front seven.
But New York doesn't want to tank. The Jets don't want to purposely lose down the stretch, despite most of their fans wanting it. They believe they are close enough to put wins together to put themselves in a position to compete in December.
The path is there for them. A win against the Dolphins would move the team to 4-8, and if the Steelers lose on Friday, they'd be just three games back of the final wild-card slot. Crazier things have happened.
But the Jets are also 6-22 under their current coach. They haven't won a divisional game. There are five other teams in front of them to fight for a playoff spot. If New York wants to prove it's ready to compete, Gang Green will need to do the bare minimum in routing a bad Dolphins roster.
It's clearly on the minds of the organization after their initial loss to them just a month ago.

title: Thursday's Grim Omar Cooper Jr. Injury News Leaves Jets With No Other Option in Week 12
full_text:
The Jets need to beat the Dolphins in Week 12 to keep their long-shot playoff hopes alive. Momentum from last week's much-needed win over the Chargers will likely provide a boost, but winning down south may be easier said than done if the Jets face the Dolphins without electric rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr.
Ankle injuries have limited this year's 16th overall pick to six appearances in New York's first 11 games, and he's currently sidelined with another. Cooper missed Wednesday's practice , prompting fans to worry about his upcoming availability.
Much to their dismay, Thursday's injury report added to those concerns, as the Jets announced that Cooper was a non-participant yet again.
Thursday’s injury report for #NYJvsMIA pic.twitter.com/VTsnhHG8dg
It's starting to look like Cooper won't be healthy enough to face the Dolphins, who he absolutely torched earlier this season. Even though they didn't pick up the win that afternoon, the Jets sure looked like winners as Cooper finished with five catches for a career-high 115 receiving yards and a touchdown.
With only days to go before the must-win AFC East showdown, it's clear the Jets have only one legitimate decision they can make this weekend.
It's entirely possible that Cooper could feel good enough to practice on Friday and be cleared in time to face the Dolphins on Sunday. That said, even if he's healthy enough to open that door, the Jets should leave their first-year stud on the sidelines for at least another game.
After all, Gang Green's bye is coming up in Week 13, giving Cooper another seven days to heal. That means the former Indiana Hoosier will have almost a full month off between his last game (Nov. 15) and when the Jets return to action at home against the Broncos in Week 14 (Dec. 13). It makes more sense to have him return then rather than rushing him back this week, only to potentially reaggravate his ankle injury.
The Dolphins may have gotten the last laugh in Week 7, but the Jets have every reason to believe they can win this weekend—even if Cooper doesn't play. Since that encounter, Miami has lost four straight games by an average margin of 8.5 points, which includes being held to nine points in two of its last three.
The Jets' passing offense hasn't been perfect, but quarterback Geno Smith has enough weapons (Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Breece Hall, Kenyon Sadiq, Mason Taylor, etc.) to do some real damage to the Dolphins' secondary, sans Cooper. We're talking about a Miami defense that just surrendered 310 passing yards to Buffalo last week.
The final stretch coming out of the bye week could also be a decent way to see what the Jets have in Cooper heading into Year 2.
Aside from the Cardinals, four of New York's five remaining opponents after the bye currently have records of .500 or better, offering competitive chances for Cooper to prove himself, even if the team is out of the playoff race by then.
It's also hard for fans to handle a player's absence when they're as explosive and impactful as Cooper. There will be many more seasons filled with highlight-reel plays, but only if his health is there, though. That makes it clear that, even if it isn't easy, the Jets need to do the right thing by resting Cooper for at least one more game before unleashing him to end the season.

title: D'Angelo Ponds May Have Already Sealed One Jets Defender's Fate
full_text:
After outlasting the lowly Chargers in Los Angeles and establishing some momentum ahead of a Week 12 rematch against the Dolphins, the Jets have a shot to string together back-to-back wins before their looming Week 13 bye.
While a lot of the talk has been centered around the poor coaching and execution that has kept Gang Green from hanging around for all four quarters, the five-game losing streak is officially behind them as head coach Aaron Glenn looks to finally pick up a win against an AFC East opponent with an 0-9 record so far.
One of the prevailing themes this season for the Jets has been how much their depth has been tested for multiple reasons. While key injuries have played a role for most on the roster, third-year cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was a healthy scratch once again against the Chargers and may have had his fate sealed in Gotham as rookie D'Angelo Ponds flashed some positive signs while playing a season-high 35 defensive snaps.
Since the Jets traded for Brownlee during the 2025 season, he has left a lot to be desired, particularly this season. After recording 36 tackles in just seven games with the Jets last season, Brownlee only has 16 in eight games this season to go along with one sack, and the fact that he has been a healthy scratch multiple times suggests it could be harder to see a Jets future with him in it, especially with his four-year rookie deal set to expire after next season.
Ponds was not perfect against the Chargers, but he still had four tackles and it could be more likely that the Jets see what they have in someone like him if they know their season is lost or there is not much to gain from putting Brownlee out there.
Even though Ponds was not perfect against the Chargers, it makes sense to keep giving him experience as someone who is learning the nickel position essentially on the fly after being used in the boundary during his collegiate career at Indiana.
After all, while Brownlee technically has one year remaining on his rookie deal, he carries zero dead cap space if the Jets release him (h/t Spotrac ) by virtue of the Titans absorbing the remaining prorated signing bonus money as part of the trade.
With nothing to lose by letting Brownlee go a year early, it is certainly possible that Ponds could have a huge opportunity in front of him if he continues to get more snaps and becomes more acquainted to the nickel position. Sure, he has only appeared in nine games and has not put enough on the field yet to really know what he is truly capable of at the professional level, but it is important that the Jets give him more time and snaps on the field to show what he can do .
Just because Ponds was on the field a lot more against the Chargers does not immediately guarantee anything after the quiet Week 10 that preceded it. However, it's not his fault that the defensive front has been plagued by injuries and not held up its end of the bargain. Still, they decided to put a bigger player like safety Malachi Moore on the field instead of adding a third corner of Ponds' 5-foot-8 stature, a clear sign that they need to see more from the rookie to fully reward him.
However, Moore only played 10 snaps against the Chargers and has not exactly proved himself, either. That said, Ponds flashed some promise in that game as a tackler and with just one reception allowed for three yards. Some bumps should be expected for a player who has little experience playing nickel and needs to improve in coverage, but the uptick in snaps and lack of playing time that Brownlee has been receiving point to a player who simply needs to show some progression over the final six games .
With three of those six games coming against teams that currently possess a winning record, what better time to throw Ponds into the fire more and see what he has to offer with Brownlee's fate hanging in the balance?

title: Latest Jets Practice Squad Signing Hints Harrison Phillips Injury Could Be Worse Than Expected
full_text:
The Jets remain focused on an improbable (but not impossible) playoff berth as they aim for their second consecutive win against the Dolphins in Week 12 . As lowly as Miami has been this season, its lone victory of the year came against New York in Week 7, so it's safe to say that head coach Aaron Glenn and Gang Green will be hunting for revenge Sunday afternoon.
That said, most teams are more than just banged up at this point in the season, and the Jets aren't an exception. New York is dealing with a handful of injuries heading into the pivotal clash with its AFC East rival, especially on defense. Veteran defensive tackle Harrison Phillips is among those navigating medical obstacles, as he's been dealing with an ankle injury for the last few weeks .
Although the Jets have yet to rule Phillips out of Week 12's AFC East festivities, the sight of a familiar face might hint that Glenn & Co. are preparing for the worst-case scenario.
On Thursday morning, the Jets announced defensive tackle Payton Page's return to the practice squad. The signing comes a day after Phillips missed New York's first practice of the week .
We've signed DT Payton Page to the practice squad
The former undrafted free agent has been in an on-and-off relationship with the Jets since joining the organization after the 2025 NFL Draft. He's played four games and was even promoted to the active roster on Halloween, but was eventually released from the 53-man roster on Tuesday.
Page's return to the practice squad suggests the Jets like him a lot, but it also might hint that Phillips isn't as far along in his recovery as the team hopes. All of Page's four appearances came after he was signed to the active roster, meaning Gang Green can still elevate him three times from the practice squad—a valuable tool if Phillips can't suit up.
What's interesting is that a potential absence against the Dolphins would mark Phillips's first missed game since the 2021 season. He played all 51 potential games during his time with the Vikings and hasn't missed an opportunity to suit up for the Jets since being acquired in the 2025 offseason.
That said, dealing with a lingering ankle injury as his 31st birthday approaches in January certainly adds to an uncertain future in Gotham. Phillips will be an unrestricted free agent in March, and being the 89th-ranked DT out of 132 with a Pro Football Focus grade of 53.6 doesn't help him, nor does his run-defense grade dropping from 76.4 to 57.7.
But improving those numbers will have to wait until Phillips is healthy. In the meantime, Page might have an opportunity to extend his own time in Gotham, and if he's successful, the Jets might have one fewer reason to bring Phillips back in 2027.
As mentioned before, Page is no stranger to the Jets, with four appearances this season and just as many last year. He's split his 2026 playing time fairly evenly, with 34 snaps coming on defense and 29 more on special teams. The dual role has led the ex-Clemson Tiger to record three tackles along the way, including one solo effort against the Chiefs in Week 9.
If given the chance to suit up, Page will hopefully perform better than he did in Week 11. The 6'4", 310-lb defender finished the win over the Chargers with a career-worst 29.7 PFF run-defense grade in 12 snaps. He could get back on track if he faces the Dolphins, who've averaged just 84.7 rushing yards in their last three games—the NFL's seventh-worst average during that stretch.
Every Jets player will be under intense scrutiny down the stretch, whether they're a main cast member or in a supporting role. It's time to find out whether guys like Page can be squeezed into diamonds, and what that could mean for veterans like Phillips down the stretch.

title: What T'Vondre Sweat's Return to Jets' Practice Means for 2026 Season and Beyond
full_text:
The numbers are a disaster for the New York Jets.
A year after fielding the fourth-worst rushing defense in the NFL, the team has gotten worse, ranking the third worst across the league. It's been a big reason why the team currently sits at 3-8 despite clear improvement elsewhere.
This wasn't supposed to be the plan, though. New York acquired run-stopping nose tackle T'Vondre Sweat in the offseason. They also signed aging veteran tackle David Onyemata to help their run defense. Both players have missed a majority of the season to injuries.
Onyemata's practice window was opened last week, and the Jets have welcomed his return. On Wednesday, the Jets welcomed back Sweat with hopes their run struggles may soon be at an end.
But are those changes likely?
New York activating the practice window for Sweat is a welcome thing for the organization, but it does not guarantee that he will see the field this week, next week, or the week after. All it means is that he can begin practicing with the team again.
If anything, Onyemata is closer to seeing the field than Sweat is, and the Jets are thrilled to be getting at least one of their run-stopping players back.
"[He's] a veteran presence and someone that knows the system inside and out," Glenn said of Onyemata. "Extremely tough, extremely violent, and there is a trust there. The thing is we want to make sure we get him right because we still have games left to go play. We want to make sure that when he's in there, that he’s right and ready to go."
Despite prior years of success in stopping the run, Onyemata had struggled to begin the season. Potentially getting him healthy and in playing shape, though, would fundamentally change how the Jets can attack opposing offenses in terms of formation alone.
Sweat's near return would make it even more so. The former Tennessee Titan was the 20th-ranked defensive tackle in the league and one of the best run defenders before his injury. He may be a two-down player, but with the Jets unable to stop the run, his return would be a welcome addition.
It would help in 2027 as well.
It's hard to see Onyemata being brought back next season regardless of who the coach is for the team. Sweat, meanwhile, has a year remaining on his rookie deal with New York. He is expected to be a building block for the defense beyond just this season when he returns.
Once he's back on the field, Sweat could change how the Jets' defense looks. And it's very important for a team trying to play for their head coach to get back to how they intended for things to look in December.

title: It’s Time for the Jets to Turn the Page on Jelani Woods
full_text:
Jelani Woods, simply put, hasn’t seen much of the field in 2026. The tight end is on a one-year, $1.2 million contract, and it figures it will be his last year as a Jet . He is clearly the odd man out in his position group. It may make sense for New York to move on from the 28-year-old to free up roster space for the rest of the season.
Woods was a healthy scratch in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. It marked the second week in a row that the tight end did not suit up for a game. That is not a good trend for Woods or the Jets. He already wasn’t playing much, but not playing at all may be a sign the writing is on the wall for Woods.
The tight end saw his most snaps in a Week 3 loss to the Detroit Lions, in which he played only 25 snaps. Since Detroit, Woods has only hit the 20-snap mark once in the six games he has appeared in. He had been trending toward these healthy scratches, and now it might lead to the end of his time as a Jet.
The tight end has shown flashes, most notably his 20-yard juggling catch against Detroit. Unfortunately, it seems they were always just flashes. Woods has seen his snaps first dwindle and now disappear. If he isn’t going to be on the game-day roster, it may be time to open up Woods' spot.
Woods has had the opportunity to earn a larger role on the roster; it just hasn’t been seized. Woods was a part of the fabled 05 personnel that Frank Reich was so excited to run. It just looks like Woods may be the Marlon of the tight end family. Even with injuries and questions at the position, Woods couldn’t make his mark to stay on the game-day roster.
Mason Taylor missed Weeks 3 and 4 with a thumb injury . Woods had two catches for 31 yards in those games. The tight end showed promise in the two games without Taylor, but it didn’t lead to more playing time. He has two catches for eight yards in the four games he played since Taylor returned. There just doesn’t seem to be space for Woods in the offense.
Woods has not had more than one target in a game this season. That doesn’t lead to anything but a wasted roster spot. He is not as dynamic in the receiving game as Taylor, Kenyon Sadiq , or Jeremy Ruckert. He also does not block as well as Andrew Beck. Five tight ends are a lot to carry on a 53-man roster. If Woods can’t stand out, the Jets may have to send him on his way.

title: Aaron Rodgers Gives One Last Reason the Jets Made Right Call (In the End)
full_text:
Despite how poor the 2026 season has gone, do you think the New York Jets can take a step back and be thankful on Thanksgiving ?
Thankful for the decision that led them to move on from Aaron Rodgers in the first place?
Since moving on from Rodgers during the 2025 offseason, the Jets have won just six games. During that same time, they watched their former quarterback lead the Pittsburgh Steelers to the playoffs and a 6-4 record this year.
Then all hell broke loose, and it should leave the Jets feeling vindicated in their original decision, even if they won't publicly call it out.
Here's how the last 24 hours have gone for the Pittsburgh Steelers:
Just another day when covering the future Hall of Famer.
The Jets were asked today specifically about Rodgers' comments, but he took the high road.
"I saw it," Jets receiver Garrett Wilson said. "I just worry about what's going on over here."
Wilson had a feud with Rodgers during their short time together in New York. There was concern had the team kept Rodgers in the first year of the Aaron Glenn era that Wilson would have requested a trade. New York chose Wilson and even gave him an extension instead.
But Rodgers' comments highlighted two main truths for the organization.
First is that the team could have kept Rodgers for the 2025 season and probably won more than the three games they did with Justin Fields.
Second, they were right to move on because while they would have won more games, it wouldn't have been enough to keep Rodgers out of the news with his interviews.
All New York did was essentially tell Rodgers that his off-field mouth wrote checks his play could no longer cash. The Jets may be only 3-8, but they have improved as a collective offense. There is excitement surrounding that group for the first time in decades. It may not have been that way had Rodgers run the show.
New York has gotten a lot of stuff wrong since Glenn was hired as head coach. One move they unequivocally come away victorious with, though, is letting Rodgers walk.
Clearly, the 42-year-old quarterback is more than willing to tank his career—regardless of who he brings down with him.

title: Eagles Must Take Off Kid Gloves With Eli Stowers After Dallas Goedert’s Injury
full_text:
The Eagles accomplished the improbable when they clawed back from a 21-point deficit to beat the Cowboys 39-38 in a Thanksgiving Day thriller. It was a game that had everything, from DeVonta Smith's 200-yard performance to Joe Milton's coming-out party , another polarizing Nick Sirianni celebration and just about anything else you can think of in between.
Unfortunately, the "everything" in this situation also includes a slew of injuries. Saquon Barkley dealt with a stinger, Marcus Epps was carted off and Cooper DeJean was ruled out with a concussion . That's without mentioning how Dallas Goedert was forced out of the win with a shoulder injury and was spotted after the game with his right arm in a sling, according to The Athletic 's Zach Berman.
Dallas Goedert’s right arm was in a sling after the game. He exited with a shoulder injury.
Whether he misses time or not, another injury isn't great for Goedert's outlook in Philadelphia . That said, when one door closes, another opens. A potential absence for the veteran tight end might be the perfect excuse for the Eagles to finally take the kid gloves off with his rookie counterpart, Eli Stowers.
The Eagles made it clear they were preparing for an eventual life without Goedert when they used a second-round selection on Stowers in April. The talented playmaker was coming off an All-American performance in his last year at Vanderbilt, racking up career highs in catches (62) and receiving yards (769) in 12 games and scoring four touchdowns along the way.
As excited as fans were to see how Stowers would fit into offensive coordinator Sean Mannion's unit, the rookie TE's debut was delayed. Quad and hamstring injuries forced the 23-year-old pass-catcher to begin the 2026 season on injured reserve, eventually making his debut against the Cowboys in Week 7.
Although it's been nice to see him healthy, it goes without saying that Stowers's early usage hasn't been what fans expected. He's only been targeted five times in as many games, all while playing 53 offensive snaps—an average of just 10.6 per appearance. Twenty-one of those snaps came against Philadelphia on Thanksgiving, almost certainly because Goedert was knocked out of the contest.
It’s a joke that Eagles rookie TE Eli Stowers only played seven snaps on offense in Week 9. Meanwhile, veterans with no future in Philadelphia played more snaps against the Giants. Here’s the effort that Stowers showed on one play: pic.twitter.com/3ngBWOsWq1
The Eagles clearly wanted to take their time to acclimate Stowers to the NFL level, but the time to be patient is over. He's the only tight end who'll be under contract with Philadelphia in 2027, as Goedert, Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and Grant Calcaterra will all be unrestricted free agents . There's a good chance Stowers will be in the TE1 role when training camp begins, so it's important for the Eagles to know what they have in him as soon as possible.
The good news is that Stowers has shown that he can be effective in his limited usage. It's a small sample size, but the 17.7 yards he's averaging on three receptions is actually the best rate on the Eagles, 2.5 yards more than second place (Darius Cooper, 15.2 yards per reception). He's also done a solid job at helping clear lanes in the trenches, as shown by his 66.5 run-block grade on Pro Football Focus .
After playing on Thanksgiving, the Eagles will have about a week and a half off before returning to action against the Cardinals on Dec. 6. Assuming that Goedert misses that contest or still isn't at 100%, Week 13 could be the perfect time for Philadelphia to unleash Stowers.
The Cardinals have been slightly below average at defending the pass this season, and that's especially true when tight ends are targeted. Entering Week 12, Arizona is tied for giving up the sixth-most receptions to TEs (61), while the 10 touchdowns they've surrendered to the position trail only the Lions (11), underscoring how juicy a matchup this could be for Stowers.
Hopefully, the Eagles' offensive explosion vs. the Cowboys signals that Milton will be looking to air the ball out as much as possible moving forward. Siranni and Mannion would be wise to get Stowers in on the action. Getting their rookie TE involved is not only key to preparing for a post-Goedert life, but it's also a must if the Eagles want to keep accomplishing the improbable as they remain in the NFC East race for at least another week.
