title: 6 Eagles Winners & 4 Losers From 39-38 Thanksgiving  Thriller vs. Cowboys in Week 12
full_text:
The Eagles’ string of five straight years with a playoff berth, which includes a pair of Super Bowl runs, may end on the second weekend of January, but they and the fan base will always give thanks for Thanksgiving.
There were plenty of winners from the Eagles’ scintillating 39-38 win , achieved after falling behind 31-10 late in the third quarter. It was the largest come-from-behind win in the history of Thanksgiving football.
That said, even when there are winners, there were some losers, too.
He’s first on this list because of his impact in just 19 defensive snaps. He notched the first sack of his career, and what a moment for it. Dallas was trying to ice the game by converting a fourth-and-1 with less than a minute left in the game and the Eagles out of timeouts. Then Robinson charged into Prescott’s midsection to sack him for a 9-yard loss at midfield. Robinson made four tackles.
Then there was the special teams Robinson. He blocked a punt that was recovered at the 3 by Kenny Moore, who stumbled into the end zone for a touchdown that brought Philly to within 31-24 just 74 seconds into the last quarter. It was the Eagles’ first blocked punt for a TD since Sept. 28, 2025, at Tampa Bay, when Cam Latu scored the block, and Sydney Brown scored a touchdown off of it.
Make a 59-yard field goal with two seconds to win a game? How can he not be in the top spot? Well, you could put him there if you feel better about it, and you would get no argument from anyone.
JAKE ELLIOTT FROM 60 YARDS OUT EAGLES COMEBACK IS COMPLETE PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LJoGRn56xr
Elliott was in the top last week after going 4-for-4 with a pair of 50-plus-yard field goals in a 19-16 win over the Steelers.
Can you imagine if he plays as he did against Dallas for the rest of the season? The Eagles may very well find their way to the top of the NFC East if he does.
Milton accounted for four touchdowns —three passing and one running. His poise and confidence are rubbing off on his teammates. How in the world did the Cowboys not make him the No. 2 QB behind Dak Prescott instead of Sam Howell? They left him exposed on the practice squad, and the Eagles grabbed him, and he is making this season fun again.
You could put him No. 1 or 2 on this list after a career-high 200 yards receiving and tying a career high in catches with 11 and doing it on 14 targets.
Nine tackles for a defensive tackle? That’s what Young collected in his 39 snaps (51%). This came on the heels of the two sacks he had in the win over the Steelers four days earlier.
It’s time to see more of the 6'3", 220-lb rookie safety. He played the first defensive snaps of his career, earning eight of them. He wasn’t afraid to stick his nose into the action, and he made two tackles in those limited snaps.
The head coach should be on the winner's list, but his boneheaded move to try to high-five Eagles fans behind the bench when the game ended nearly turned into a fistfight with some Cowboys fans.
Nick Sirianni celebrated in front of the Cowboys fans after the Eagles comeback win 😅 (📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/mR8isTM2Zh
Just go shake hands and head to the locker room. This isn't the first time Sirianni has gotten into it with fans. When will he learn?
\ Referee Adrian Hill’s crew was bad for both sides, but from the Eagles’ standpoint, here are two ridiculous calls. First, Javonte Williams’s forward progress was ruled stopped at the goal line, preventing what would have been a 95-yard-or-more return for a touchdown by Riq Woolen.
Second, the crew waved off a pass interference against the Cowboys in the final seconds that would have made Elliott’s kick closer because they said it was uncatchable. It was wrong. Hill and his crew called 19 penalties that were accepted, with both teams backing up 86 yards each.
It was a rare bad game by Quinyon Mitchell, and losing Cooper DeJean to a concussion on Dallas’ first offensive drive didn’t help.
Mailata was caught holding during a two-point conversion pass that would have tied the game with just over two minutes left. The penalty pushed the Eagles back 10 yards, and they weren’t able to complete a pass to tie it from the 12-yard line.
It didn’t matter in the end, but taking two points off the board in a big spot can’t happen.

title: McMullen: Joe Milton Etches His Name Into NFL Thanksgiving History
full_text:
For most of the afternoon, it looked like another chapter in the same old tired story for Philadelphia.
The Eagles were down 31-10 late in the third quarter at AT&T Stadium, missing Jalen Hurts for the season, losing Cooper DeJean, Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert in-game, and still carrying the woe-is-me scars of a recent seven-game losing streak.
Then “The Rocket Man” took over. No, Elton John wasn’t playing at halftime. That honor went to Miranda Lambert, but fledgling Eagles quarterback Joe Milton did show off the strongest arm in the NFL and started launching his own rockets that were so awe-inspiring they almost looked AI-generated.
The former Cowboys practice-squad quarterback gouged his old team by completing 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards and three touchdowns, added a 15-yard rushing score, and helped produce the largest comeback in Thanksgiving Day history as Philadelphia stunned Dallas 39-38 on Jake Elliott’s 59-yard field goal with two seconds remaining.⁠
When it was all said and done, Milton, in just his third career start after a month with the Eagles, was accepting the John Madden Trophy and Tom Brady’s LFG Player of the Game award in the NFL’s highest-profile regular-season window that’s expected to push 50 million viewers for the FOX/Tubi simulcast.
Milton had been signed off Dallas’ practice squad on Oct. 16 after the Cowboys decided Sam Howell, ironically an Eagles backup to Hurts in 2025, was the better option behind Dak Prescott, a Milton mentor.
The Eagles only moved to Milton after Tanner McKee lost three consecutive starts in relief of Hurts. In Milton’s first two starts, the embattled Eagles' offense continued to limp along and arrived in North Texas ranked dead last at No. 32 overall.
On Thanksgiving, Milton’s arm was the difference, producing a half-dozen high-level throws you rarely see at even the highest level of football.
Both of the QB’s long touchdowns to DeVonta Smith traveled well over 40 air yards—the first a 64.4-yard heave (according to Next Gen Stats) on the move across his body that left teammates and Brady in the booth shaking their heads.
Even rockets need help. Smith finished with a career-high 11 catches for 200 yards and two scores. A blocked punt by Ty Robinson returned for a touchdown by Kenny Moore and a late defensive stand buoyed by a Robinson sack also contributed to the historic rebound, as did Elliott's storied clutch gene.
The Eagles are now 4-7 and alive in the NFC East, albeit still on life support. They have won two straight with Milton after that seven-game skid. The structural questions about the offense under Sean Mannion have not magically disappeared because one night of deep shots and improvisation worked against a soft Dallas defense.
The harder part for Milton will be developing the week-to-week consistency that defines great NFL quarterbacks.
Wherever his career turns moving forward, this performance by Milton will always be remembered.
Madden once famously said, “There's no place that I would rather be today on Thanksgiving than right here, right now, at a football game.”
On this Thanksgiving Day, Milton joined an exclusive club. The decades of holiday football have produced many indelible moments: Clint Longley’s 1974 backup-quarterback miracle against Washington, Randy Moss’s three-catch, three-touchdown day in a 1998 “revenge game” against the Cowboys for not drafting him, Leon Lett’s snowy blunder in 1993, even the Butt Fumble.
Now football fans will always remember “The Rocket Man.”

title: Joe Milton Had 4 Touchdowns, but Plenty of Help in Eagles' Instant Classic vs. Cowboys
full_text:
Joe Milton made one play after another. The Eagles quarterback threw touchdown passes of 50 and 45 yards to DeVonta Smith. He threw a 24-yard strike to rookie Makai Lemon. He ran 15 yards for a touchdown. That’s four, count ’em, four, touchdowns on Thanksgiving.
Even better, he helped lead the Eagles to a 39-38 win in an instant classic, a Thanksgiving thriller, if you will.
When asked by The Athletic ’s Zach Berman what his favorite play of the day was, it wasn’t any of those things.
“Shoot, I remember every single one,” said Milton, who then thought about it for a few seconds. “I'll say getting Jake [Elliott] in the position to make the field goal. He's a great kicker … just put him in a situation to go ice the game. That's something that he's good at, uh, great at, if that. That's probably one of my favorite moments, just icing the game and letting the kicker go be him.”
Even Batman had help, and there were plenty of Robins supporting Milton in this one.
Start with Jake Elliott. The kicker has been on a roll this season, and it continued with a 59-yard field goal with just two seconds left to ice the win, which was the Eagles’ second straight after ending a seven-game losing streak against the Steelers just four days earlier.
WHAT A MOMENT 🦅 pic.twitter.com/QO08FqciEx
“I'm human, I'm human,” said Elliott when a reporter asked him if he was nervous. “Definitely nervous, but you just go back to your process. I mean, everything, every drive is the same. I treat it the same, and just kinda have my process. What balls I'm hitting into the net, at what times, and when I feel comfortable about the timing of everything, everything usually goes well.”
Elliott was 4-for-4 in the 19-16 win against the Steelers, including a pair over 50 yards.
The Eagles are now 3-0 all-time in Dallas on Thanksgiving. More importantly, they are 4-7, with a trip to Arizona to play the Cardinals next Sunday. After that, they have three straight home games. There is life, especially now that the Cowboys are 5-7 and have a defense that is downright awful.
The Eagles fell behind 28-10 at halftime, a lead the Cowboys extended to 31-10 with 3:40 to go in the third quarter. It looked like the end for the Eagles. Looks were deceiving, in this case, thanks to Milton and Smith.
Smith shredded Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter, who couldn’t cover him. The Eagles receiver, who battled through an injury, set a career high with 200 yards and tied a career high with 11 catches. Smith had touchdown catches of 50 and 45 yards. He did it all on 14 targets.
Last week, he was targeted 12 times and caught five passes for 41 yards. Their connection was a work in progress, and it happened just four days later.
Milton was amazing against his former team. He completed 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards and three touchdowns, adding 15 yards rushing, including a 15-yard run with 9:17 to play in the final quarter that pulled the Eagles within 38-30.
He became the first Eagles QB to throw multiple 45-plus TDs in a game since Carson Wentz on Sept. 8, 2019 against Washington when Wentz threw them from 51 and 53 yards.
MILTON MANIA pic.twitter.com/mfPgJV1Nk1
Milton wasn't done. He found rookie Makai Lemon from 24 yards away with 2:10 to play that made it 38-36.
“He played his butt off,” Nick Sirianni told reporters in Dallas about Milton. “He played really good, made some throws that only he can make. He played an outstanding game, was super composed throughout. He played the next play consistently.”
The Eagles appeared to have converted the two-point play after Lemon’s TD that would have tied it on a Milton-to-Smith throw, but Jordan Mailata was called for holding. The ensuing try after the penalty was incomplete.
The Eagles' comeback was jump-started by a blocked punt from Ty Robinson that was scooped up by Kenny Moore at the 3-yard line. He took it in from there. Suddenly, the 31-10 Cowboys lead was down to 31-24 with 13:46 to play in the fourth quarter.
Robinson had four tackles from his defensive tackle post and picked up his first career sack.
The defense did its job in the second half. Defensive tackle Byron Young was a force, collecting nine tackles, and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. shows no signs of slowing down, leading the team with 12 tackles and collecting a sack.
The Eagles played a lot of the game without tight end Dallas Goedert, safeties Cooper DeJean and Marcus Epps, and running back Saquon Barkley, each of whom left with various injuries.
“It was an extremely exciting, extremely fun game to be a part of at times,” Sirianni said. “Man, it was something. I’m kind of at a loss for words for how hard our guys fought all the way through. Just everybody on that field fought till the end, and as long as there was time on that clock, that we were gonna fight, and we did a good job of that.”

title: Dallas Goedert Injury Adds Uncertainty to His Eagles Future After Week 12 Comeback Win
full_text:
What was left of the Eagles' slim odds of winning the NFC East were bolstered by an incredible 39-38 nail-biting win over the rival Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day. Unfortunately, the must-win matchup wasn't without some bad news, as the injury bug forced multiple Eagles out of the game.
First, a concussion forced cornerback Cooper DeJean out of the game after the team's first defensive series. Shortly after, tight end Dallas Goedert— who was dealing with a shin issue —sustained a shoulder injury in the first quarter; although he was initially listed as questionable, the Eagles eventually ruled him out.
Dallas Goedert has been downgraded to out. https://t.co/cAq0RPVGEV
Saquon Barkley, Marcus Epps and DeVonta Smith were among the players who were either temporarily sidelined or left the game entirely, too.
Eagles fans aren't strangers to having to deal with Goedert missing time, as his rookie year (2018) was the only time he played a full season. That said, it is the 31-year-old's second notable injury this season, after an MCL sprain caused him to miss two games earlier .
As the saying goes, Father Time is undefeated, and another injury likely adds more uncertainty to Goedert's already-cloudy Eagles outlook.
Regardless of how many games he misses (if any), Goedert's latest injury could impact his remaining time in Philadelphia.
After all, the veteran pass catcher is playing on a one-year contract, meaning he'll be an unrestricted free agent in March. The expiring contract, combined with the Eagles' losing record, was a major reason why Goedert was viewed as a potential trade candidate earlier this month. Philadelphia opted not to make any major deadline moves other than moving Jordan Davis, keeping Goedert safe for the time being.
But now the Eagles have to decide whether to re-sign or replace an aging veteran who's no longer as productive as he once was, even if he's a beloved fan favorite.
After scoring a career-high 11 touchdowns last year, Goedert has only two in his first nine games this season, along with 355 receiving yards on 33 catches. He hasn't found the end zone since Week 1 and, including Week 12, has more games with fewer than 40 yards (five) than more (four). Pro Football Focus also currently grades him with the third-worst pass-blocking grade of his career (58.3) .
The Eagles could also look at Goedert's injury as another reason to give their tight end room a hard reset this offseason. As it stands, rookie Eli Stowers is the only tight end Philadelphia has under contract for 2027, as Goedert, Zach Ertz, Grant Calcaterra (who was a healthy scratch on Thursday) and Johnny Mundt will all be UFAs when free agency opens.
Unless Goedert is ready to play second fiddle to Stowers and take a pay cut from the fully guaranteed $7.9 million he's making this season , we might be entering his final stretch as an Eagle. He might feel like he can still compete at a high level and wants a change of scenery, especially with Jalen Hurts's future uncertain in its own way .
As it stands in all-time franchise history, Goedert currently ranks fourth in receptions (442), 11th in receiving yards (5,031) and eighth in receiving TDs (37). It's safe to say that he won't be forgotten by Eagles fans anytime soon.
Hopefully, Goedert has a speedy recovery and returns to the Eagles' lineup as soon as possible. It'd be even better if he could prove that he still has plenty of juice in the tank, perhaps prompting general manager Howie Roseman to seriously explore re-signing him.
But, if not, fans should brace for a potential Goedert-less future.

title: 5 Eagles Who Will Likely Be Inactive vs. Cowboys in Week 12
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles didn't have long to dwell on their Week 11 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers, as they'll be right back in action against the Cowboys in Dallas on Thanksgiving Day. It will be the second meeting of the season between the two teams, as Dallas pulled out a 38-21 victory over Philadelphia in Week 7.
If the Eagles are going to pull out a holiday win, they'll have to overcome some absences. Here's a look at five Eagles players who have either already been ruled out of the game against Dallas or are unlikely to be active.
Jonathan Jones played well for the Eagles in their win over the Steelers in Week 11. He recorded five total tackles (two solo tackles) in the game, and he also led the Eagles with three passes defended. Unfortunately, he suffered an ankle injury late in the game and didn't return.
He was unable to practice with the team throughout the week due to the injury, and he's officially been ruled out of the Thanksgiving showdown with Dallas as a result. At this point, the main questions are when, and if, we'll see him out on the field for the Eagles again this season.
Linebacker Arnold Ebiketie tallied three combined tackles for the Eagles against Pittsburgh in Week 11, but he also apparently suffered an oblique injury in the game. He was sidelined for the week due to the injury, and like Jones, he's also been ruled out of the game against Dallas.
Considering that the Eagles were willing to move on from Ebiketie prior to the trade deadline, they probably won't miss him too much out on the field on Thanksgiving Day.
In addition to Ebiketie, the Eagles will also likely be without another linebacker in Smael Mondon Jr. Mondon was inactive for Philadelphia against Pittsburgh in Week 11 due to an ankle injury, and it wouldn't be surprising if he popped up on the inactive list again this week.
He was listed as a "DNP" on Philadelphia's estimated injury report on Monday and he was listed as limited for the other two days. Given his limited practice status, he certainly seems to be trending towards a second consecutive week of inactivity.
After leading the Eagles to a win over the Steelers on Sunday, Joe Milton will get the third start of his career against his former franchise on Turkey Day. Milton showed some flashes over his first two starts, and the Eagles will want to continue to evaluate him as the season moves forward.
Tanner McKee will continue to serve as the backup behind Milton, which leaves rookie quarterback Cole Payton as the odd man out, as Philly isn't going to have three QBs active for the game. Like last week, Payton will likely serve as the emergency third QB for Philly in Dallas.
The Eagles claimed offensive lineman Ajani Cornelius off of waivers just last week after he was waived by Dallas , and it seems unlikely that he'll be ready to contribute on the field this week. He was one of Philadelphia's five inactive players last week, and he's likely in store for a similar fate this week.

title: 3 Things the Eagles Should Be Thankful For This Thanksgiving
full_text:
As a holiday, Thanksgiving is all about gratitude, and while it may not necessarily seem like it given the way the current campaign has unfolded, Philadelphia Eagles fans have plenty of reasons to be grateful. Here's a look at three things that the Eagles organization and fanbase should be thankful for this Thanksgiving.
The 2026 NFL season has been rough for the Eagles as an organization as well as for Philly fans. There's no doubt about that. But, perspective is important, and as a fanbase, Eagles fans could have it a lot worse. After all, this is a team that just won the Super Bowl last year . It may feel like five years ago at this point, but it was just 21 months ago that Jalen Hurts, Nick Sirianni and company were hoisting the Lombardi Trophy in New Orleans.
A couple of years before that, the Birds made it all the way to the Big Game and came up slightly short. Overall, the Eagles have been to three Super Bowls over the past nine years and won two of them. That's not too shabby, and their recent success has provided Philly fans with ample opportunity for celebration lately. Just think, you could be a fan of a team that has never even won a Super Bowl like the Tennessee Titans or Arizona Cardinals, or even worse, a team that has never even been to the Super Bowl like the Detroit Lions or Cleveland Browns. So, while this season has certainly been a slog, Eagles fans could have it much worse.
Even in a down season, Eagles fans can lean into some optimism knowing that they have an elite general manager in Howie Roseman who isn't just going to sit on his hands. Roseman has shown an ability to consistently rebuild or retool the roster when necessary, and we shouldn't expect anything different this time around.
In Howie we trust pic.twitter.com/S7dLBN8Yr1
"In Howie we trust" is a popular slogan among the Eagles community, and for good reason. Roseman has already taken major steps in that regard by flipping declining players like A.J. Brown, Cam Jurgens and Jordan Davis for major draft capital over the next few years that the Eagles will be able to use to build themselves back into a contender.
If you're looking at the Lincoln Financial Field rafters, one thing that really jumps out is how many more banners there are since Jeffrey Lurie took over as the owner of the team in 1994 compared to before that point.
Four of Philadelphia's five Super Bowl appearances, and both of their Super Bowl wins, have occurred since Lurie took over ownership. Similarly, the Eagles have won the NFC East 12 times since Lurie became the owner, compared to just two times prior. Lurie is clearly an owner with a high standard, and that standard has permeated the rest of the organization ever since he first purchased the team.
Philly fans can take solace in the fact that they have an owner who clearly cares about the team and is willing to spend as much as it takes to keep the Eagles in the contender conversation consistently. Not all organizations can say the same.

title: Eagles-Cowboys Round 2: Who Wins & Why In NFC East Clash On Thanksgiving
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Four days after ending their losing streak, the Eagles will try to play spoiler in the NFC East when they visit Dallas on Thanksgiving. With the teams above them in the NFC East each winning in Week 11, the Eagles’ playoff hopes were diminished.
At 3-7, they are three games behind the Giants, two games back of the Cowboys, and one game off the Commanders in the win column. It’s a lot of ground to make up with just seven games left.
Putting a dent in the Cowboys’ hopes would make some fans happy, given how they are despised, but it might also make some fans unhappy because a two-game winning streak would push them deeper down next spring's draft order.
Nevertheless, here are five matchups to watch with my final score prediction:
Two Eagles to watch: quarterback Joe Milton and running back Saquon Barkley.
Milton is coming off his first win as a starting quarterback, and he did it in just his second start. Now, he returns to the team he spent nearly 19 months with before the Eagles signed him off the Cowboys’ practice squad last month.
“Just going to go play another football game,” he said. “I mean, obviously, I was just there a month ago, but it's going to be a great game. ... Know those guys' mentality a little bit, so therefore we just got to come with it. We’ve got to show up and show out no matter what.”
As for Barkley, injuries limited him to just 10 snaps in the teams’ first matchup in Week 8. He’s dealing with a shoulder injury now, which popped up against the Steelers.
“I won't really get too much into that,” he said. “I just look forward to rehabbing this week and getting ready for Thursday.”
Asked if he could play on a short week with the injury, he said: “I believe so.”
It’s worth noting that Dallas’ defense has given up at least 20 points in 18 straight games.
Quinyon Mitchell should be good to go on Thursday, per defensive coordinator Vic Fangio. How effective he can be with a hamstring injury remains to be seen. Jonathan Jones, who came off the bench and played well against the Steelers, is likely out, which means more Riq Woolen, who was benched for Jones.
It’s not a good matchup for the league’s second-ranked passing offense. CeeDee Lamb leads the league in receptions with 88 and is second in receiving yards with 1,108 and second in receiving touchdowns with nine. George Pickens isn’t far behind with 57 catches for 780 yards and six TDs.
Williams shredded it in the first meeting, rushing for a career-high 155 yards on 25 carries, a touchdown, and 6.2 yards per carry. Since then, linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr., has come into his own . In three starts since playing 24 snaps against Dallas, he has become an every-down player. Since that Week 8 matchup against the Cowboys, he is fifth in average tackles with 11.0 over that three-game stretch.
Dallas’ offensive line has allowed just 15 sacks of quarterback Dak Prescott, but the Eagles have been riding a hot streak over the past two games, collecting 11 sacks in that span. They sacked the Giants’ McCarthy six times, following that up by sacking the Steelers’ Aaron Rodgers five times.
This will be the eighth time the Eagles play on Thanksgiving, and the bar is high. They are 6-1 on this holiday, including 2-0 against the Cowboys in Dallas.
Verdict: Cowboys 27, Eagles 21 Season record: 9-1

title: Steelers Make QB2 Decision Between Will Howard, Drew Allar
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers' young quarterbacks are taking a step up on the depth chart in Week 12 against the Denver Broncos.
With Mason Rudolph set to make his first start of the season, Will Howard will serve as his backup while third-round rookie Drew Allar is inactive as the emergency No. 3 signal caller.
Pittsburgh rounded out its list of inactives with Alex Highsmith (ankle), Cole Holcomb (heel), Kaden Wetjen, Gabriel Rubio, Eli Heidenreich and Sean Murphy-Bunting.
Aaron Rodgers , of course, was released on November 25 shortly after his fiery and dramatic appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" that came after the Steelers announced he would be inactive vs. Denver. During that interview, Rodgers he called out head coach Mike McCarthy for sleeping during meetings and breaking down the Steelers' halftime huddle during the team's Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles with a "1, 2, 3, Packers!" chant, among other issues he raised.
Now, Pittsburgh is turning to Rudolph while standing behind McCarthy as the responsibilities of Howard and Allar have suddenly risen following all of the chaos surrounding the organization the last handful of days.
Though it's under less-than-ideal circumstances for the entire franchise, Howard is now on the edge of making his regular season debut for Pittsburgh.
The 2025 sixth-round pick lost over half of his rookie year due to a hand injury he suffered during training camp that resulted in him residing on the reserve/injured list through Week 11 while missing the entirety of the preseason.
Howard did not play in any games for the Steelers last year as a result, and he hasn't done so thus far in 2026 either. In fact, he hasn't been active yet this season while having previously been the team's emergency No. 3 quarterback while Rodgers was the starter and Rudolph was the backup.
The 25-year-old had some momentum on his side back in the summer, as there was some thought that he was the favorite over Rudolph to earn the backup job entering training camp.
That didn't come to be, however, as Rudolph won that battle while Howard struggled during the preseason, completing 26 of his 39 passing attempts for 229 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions.
Pittsburgh saw enough to keep him on the 53-man roster, though, and now he could potentially be called upon at some point if Rudolph is benched or suffers an injury.
Though Allar has seemingly made some real strides since entering the NFL, particularly with his footwork and overall mechanics, it's not surprising that he remains last on the depth chart for Pittsburgh at quarterback.
He has all of the tools to eventually become a starting quarterback, but he still has plenty of development in front of him as he continues to adapt to the league.
The excitement for Allar is palpable, especially after he put some highlight plays on film during the preseason while throwing for 351 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions in the preseason.
The wait to see him suit up during the regular season continues for the time being, however, and understandably so from the Steelers' perspective.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers' Jaylen Warren Facing Biggest Game of Career
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- As the Pittsburgh Steelers search for answers and stability, they need someone to step up.
The Steelers are losers of two straight and have made a sudden shift at quarterback ahead of their Week 12 contest. Out goes Aaron Rodgers, and in comes Mason Rudolph. The timing of the change was shocking, given it came less than 72 hours before they took on the Denver Broncos, but the decision to bench Rodgers makes a ton of sense when you look at his recent performance.
Regardless, the quarterback position is currently a volatile one for the Steelers. Needing a win and someone to take charge, the Steelers now look to one player to stem the tide - running back Jaylen Warren.
The odds stacked against the Steelers' starting running back loom large ahead of this Week 12 contest, but that's exactly why it's such an important game for Warren. Just like Rodgers and the rest of the offense, the past two games have been awful for the running game. Warren has a combined 43 yards on 16 carries the past two games, while pitching in an additional 27 yards in the air.
The thing with Warren, however, is that he has built a career despite having no expectations and frequently having his back against the wall. The undrafted running back forced his way onto the Steelers' active roster after impressing the coaching staff as a rookie in 2022.
It didn't stop there. Despite the team investing a first-round draft pick in Najee Harris to address the position, Warren wouldn't be denied. posting three consecutive seasons with at least 500 rushing yards and 300 receiving yards between 2023 and 2025.
The Steelers and Cleveland Browns met for a heated matchup in Week 8. Ahead of the game, Browns EDGE rusher Jared Verse has plenty of trash talk for the Steelers. In response, Pittsburgh trounced Cleveland by 21 points.
Warren also got the last laugh, sharing a zinger of a postgame comment when he said , "Some walk, some talk," in response to the trash talk the Browns shared before the game.
Now, it's time for Warren to do the walking once again. After running for at least 90 yards in five out of six games between Weeks 3 and 8, he's been held to a total of 43 yards combined in Weeks 10 and 11.
A huge piece of that dip in production is the loss of starting left guard Mason McCormick, and the offensive line's inability to make up for his absence. Whatever the cause, Warren has to overcome the obstacle once again.
His back is up against the wall, something he's very familiar with. If Warren can do what he usually does when he's counted out, he will lead the Steelers back to the win column. If he continues to struggle, the Steelers will too.
Either way, it's the biggest game of Warren's career.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: How It Happened: Every Piece of the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers Downfall
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are the biggest story in the NFL. NBC Sports decided to delay the Goo Goo Dolls halftime show on Thanksgiving Day just to air an interview with their former head coach, Mike Tomlin, discussing how big of a "dumpster fire" the whole ordeal is.
But how did they get here? How did a franchise go from 6-4, losing in Philadelphia and preparing for the Denver Broncos with Aaron Rodgers, find themselves with Mason Rudolph as their QB1, Rodgers a free agent and the entire franchise in shambles over a head coach who has an ice cream sandwich assistant?
The timeline is short, but it's loaded. Monday at 3 p.m. ET, head coach Mike McCarthy stood in front of the media and declared, "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback." Just before midnight on Tuesday, Rodgers was benched and the team put out a public statement about it.
So, what happened? And how did it all get as dramatic as it is today?
Things went downhill on Tuesday, which seemed to be the breaking point between McCarthy and Rodgers. According to reports, tensions had been building between the two for some time, but in this particular week, they boiled over.
Rodgers said he met with McCarthy several times and was determined to pull play-calling duties away from his head coach in an effort to better the offense. Rodgers claims McCarthy was falling behind on film study and didn't know the gameplan heading into weeks, and therefore, he wanted to take over the play-calling duties.
Things seemingly fell into place for the 42-year-old quarterback, as McCarthy somewhat agreed to the idea. But Rodgers wasn't done there.
After not liking the gameplan that was laid out for him and the offense, he gave McCarthy an ultimatum - change it to what I believe works or cut me.
Pittsburgh called his bluff.
McCarthy, Art Rooney II and general manager Omar Khan met until late into the night on Tuesday and decided to bench Rodgers. They left the team facility around 1 a.m. after everything was finalized and they were ready to move forward.
Rodgers found out from Pat Freiermuth, who called him after the team released a statement on social media. The team tried to reach Rodgers before announcing the news, but according to McCarthy, could not reach him.
On Wednesday morning, the team sat in a meeting at 8 a.m. with everyone in attendance but Rodgers. He was given the day off to let everything cool down. The players were told the news, which they did not respond to well, and then moved on with their day.
Hours later, the Steelers were walking off the practice field. At the same time, Rodgers was making an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show , and giving maybe the greatest tell-all in sports history. Without holding back, the former Steelers QB told of McCarthy sleeping during meetings, skipping walk-throughs, not watching film, not connecting with the defensive players and calling the Steelers the Packers during halftime of the Philadelphia Eagles game in Week 11.
Pandora's box was open, and almost instantly, things started being confirmed. Things started to leak from inside the building that almost all of what Rodgers said was true and some. That offensive players were upset with the way McCarthy was going about things and that those who were used to Mike Tomlin were struggling with the change.
It was revealed that McCarthy has an assistant who brings him ice cream sandwiches and that he truly has no relationship with most of the defensive side of the locker room.
BREAKING NEWS: @AaronRodgers12 addresses being benched by the Pittsburgh Steelers #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/6rggspWDGX
Hours later, McCarthy stood at the same podium he backed Rodgers at two days earlier and answered about it all. The only thing he denied was holding a grudge against Rodgers for "getting him fired" in Green Bay in 2018. Besides that, he nor anyone else within the Steelers has denied anything said by Rodgers.
McCarthy didn't spend Wednesday preparing for the Broncos in a way he usually would. Instead, he met with a player council which is formed of leaders within the locker room. They discussed what was happening and some of the issues the locker room has with their new head coach.
It was eye-opening for McCarthy.
"My focus is just on the reality of it," McCarthy said. "This would be a definition of a distraction, and that's why I think when you are going through these moments, it's important to do the best you can to focus. And just some of the things that were talked about in the player council meeting — the fact that we're not talking about beating the Denver Broncos right now is not where we should be. So, I just really appreciate and respect the urgency that everybody came out of that meeting with."
In Pittsburgh, that counsel likely included T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward, Patrick Queen and others. It's easier to think of defensive players than offensive ones, which may have given one side of the football an opportunity to tell their coach that he needs to form better relationships with them.
The next day, Team President Art Rooney II spoke with Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac to share his thoughts on everything that happened.
Without skipping a beat, Rooney backed his head coach and made it known that McCarthy will remain with the team despite many former players and a large chunk of the fanbase and media questioning whether or not he should.
"I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Rooney said. "The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that."
He then proceeded to call out Rodgers.
"There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload," Rooney said. "He talks about wanting to be a good teammate but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure.
"In general, I think, historically, what's in the locker room stays in the locker room. That's the way it's always been. That's the way it should be as far as I'm concerned."
Despite probably the craziest week in team history, the Steelers are set to step into Acrisure Stadium and take on the Denver Broncos. They're on a two-game losing streak and will now face one of the best defenses in the league with a new starting quarterback.
One that had a walk-through to prepare for the game.
It won't be easy, and the fanbase may make it worse with chants calling for McCarthy's job. But Pittsburgh has tied themselves to their horse and are trying to prove everyone wrong.
Can they? Well, it would certainly be impressive if they can put all of this to the side and compete in Week 12. McCarthy is going to try to. He needs to win to avoid this getting any worse.
But after the most intense three days in franchise history and a team that feels completely lost in Week 12 despite a winning record, the Steelers are going to play football.
And everyone will be watching.

title: Expect the Same With Mason Rudolph as Steelers QB
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers made a shocking change at quarterback just days ahead of their Week 12 contest against the Denver Broncos. Just over 24 hours after head coach Mike McCarthy emphatically stated that Aaron Rodgers was the team's starting quarterback, the organization sent out a statement in direct opposition.
The Steelers announced that Mason Rudolph would start against the Broncos, and Rodgers would be inactive for the contest. Eventually, that led to a disastrous tell-all interview with the Pat McAfee Show , Rodgers' release from Pittsburgh and plenty of worry about the head coach.
As the dust settles from this gigantic shakeup in Pittsburgh, one question looms large: will Rudolph bring the change this offense needs?
Sadly, the Steelers should expect more of the same with another veteran under center.
The Steelers have to hope that the change at quarterback provides a spark, because there is no statistical reason to believe swapping Rodgers for Rudolph benefits this offense.
Looking at Rudolph's previous time as a starter with the Steelers and the Tennessee Titans, a very clear message is conveyed: he's not a very good starting quarterback. In his career, he's appeared in 38 NFL contests, starting 19 of them. Over those 19 starts, he's produced a 9-9-1 record, with five of those victories coming during the 2019 season. He also went 3-0 as the starter in 2023.
But let's take a closer look at his biggest opportunity as a starter in the NFL back in 2019. That season he started eight games after Ben Roethlisberger suffered a season-ending injury. In eight contests, he completed 176 out of 283 passing attempts for 1,765 yards, 13 touchdowns and nine interceptions.
At the time, he was just 24 years old and one year removed from being drafted. Those numbers were promising, but he's failed to improve upon or reach that level of success since.
In 2024, he received his next legitimate chance to be a starter with the Titans. He appeared in eight contests and started five. He led the Titans to a 1-4 record as the starter, and he threw for just over 1,500 passing yards, nine touchdowns and nine interceptions.
With the team moving forward without Rodgers, that means Rudolph is the guy until he proves he isn't. That means the team's young quarterbacks, Drew Allar and Will Howard, are not far from regular-season action.
Howard is the next man up behind Rudolph. He will serve as the backup in Week 12, with Allar serving as the emergency third quarterback on game day.
If Rudolph struggles or is injured, Howard will get the chance to make his NFL debut.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Mike Tomlin Gets Honest About Steelers, McCarthy Saga: 'Dumpster Fire'
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- It's hard to imagine things can be any worse for the Pittsburgh Steelers. They're in the midst of a two-game losing streak, just released their starting quarterback and then watched said quarterback go on live TV and raise hell for their head coach.
Aaron Rodgers went scorched Earth on head coach Mike McCarthy during an interview on the Pat McAfee Show after being benched and eventually released by the Steelers. He made allegations of falling asleep in meetings, calling the Steelers the Packers during halftime of a game, not building relationships with his players, and not watching film in a timely manner.
Things are rough in Pittsburgh, and even their former head coach agrees. Being interviewed during halftime of the Kansas City Chiefs-Buffalo Bills Thanksgiving Day game, Mike Tomlin made his thoughts on the Steelers clear.
"I'm upset about it. It's a dumpster fire," Tomlin said. "And I don't say that in a judgemental way. I presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset."
Tomlin also added that McCarthy can overcome this situation only through his relationships with players. This may be a challenge as Rodgers claims he does not have relationships with some of the bigger names in the locker room, especially on the defensive side of the ball.
"It certainly created some challenges and challenges is an understatement if those things are true, but his ability or inability to overcome that is based on relationships and the depth of those relationships and how those guys buy into what he's selling," Tomlin said.
The Steelers are turning to Mason Rudolph as their starter and will try to turn their season around at 6-4. But they are losing a key piece to their leadership group in Rodgers, who was beloved in the locker room this season , and was beloved last season as well, Tomlin acknowledged.
Will McCarthy be able to overcome the challenges in front of him? Time will tell. But Tomlin's words make it clear that this is not going to be easy, and that if everything is true - which McCarthy or ownership have not denied most of it - it'll require pretty significant effort from Pittsburgh's new head coach.
The Steelers take on the Denver Broncos in Week 12 before hosting the Houston Texans and then traveling to the Jacksonville Jaguars. All three games could decide their playoff fate, and they'll do so with plenty of distractions and a head coach with everything to prove.

title: 5 Things Steelers Can Be Thankful For This Year
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are reeling after losing two consecutive games. Their starting quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, is no longer with the franchise, and Mason Rudolph will make his first start of the season against the Denver Broncos.
After losing to the Cincinnati Bengals and the Philadelphia Eagles, the Steelers are 6-4 and preparing to take on a playoff-bound Broncos squad on Black Friday.
Despite back-to-back losses and the strangest week in recent memory, the Steelers have plenty to be thankful for this year.
The Steelers have to get back to the ground game as they claw out of their skid. Head coach Mike McCarthy and quarterback Aaron Rodgers both reiterated the need for that following the Week 11 loss.
It's obvious why that's their goal. Running back Jaylen Warren is the team's best player on either side of the ball this season. He's produced 747 rushing yards on 135 carries, averaging 5.5 yards per carry. He's also caught 32 passes for 321 yards.
The formerly undrafted running back is enjoying a career year, and the Steelers should be most thankful for this star performance from Warren.
The passing game might not be a bright spot in Pittsburgh, but rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard surely is. The second-round pick has 38 receptions, 324 yards and a touchdown through his first ten games in the NFL. He's forced Rodgers to go to him more and more as the season has progressed.
He's still learning and growing, but he has the tools and mindset to be a number one wideout and star in the NFL.
While the coaching staff is receiving some much-deserved criticism, defensive coordinator Patrick Graham has been a gift to this organization. The defense was torched against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10, but they remain in the top 10 total defenses this season.
That's thanks to Graham's coaching and schematic decisions. Despite having a less-than-stellar secondary and injuries hampering the entire group, he's helped this unit find more success in 2026.
Speaking of Graham helping this defense find more success, the best example is the resurgence of T.J. Watt. Through 10 games, he's posted 23 total tackles, 7.5 sacks, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, an interception and four passes defended.
After a down year in 2025, Watt is on pace to post double-digit sacks for the sixth time in his illustrious NFL career.
The Steelers have received contributions from some unlikely sources this season, and that's always a reason to be thankful.
That includes the likes of guard Brock Hoffman, who has been solid at right guard since replacing Spencer Anderson.
Defensively, rookie safety Robert Spears-Jennings has been one of the most impressive first-year defenders in the entire NFL. He's taken on a larger role throughout the campaign, and he's entrenched himself as a starter now and moving forward.
It also includes Max Hurleman , who made his NFL debut in Week 11. He led the team in receptions and receiving yards while posting his first career touchdown. Moving forward, Hurleman has earned the right to be on the active roster and that might lead to more offense.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers President Art Rooney II Backs Mike McCarthy, Calls Out Aaron Rodgers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have the biggest spotlight in the NFL on them after Aaron Rodgers went on the Pat McAfee Show and called out his former head coach, Mike McCarthy, with multiple accusations, including sleeping during meetings and calling the team the Packers during halftime of a game.
Both of which McCarthy did not deny when asked about them.
But Rodgers is the only one who's gone. The Steelers benched and eventually released their former starting quarterback just days before his 43rd birthday, ending an almost two-year run together. Afterward, they shared their support for McCarthy, and now, Team President Art Rooney II is making that stance even stronger.
Speaking with Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, Rooney  shared his support for McCarthy while making it known that Rodgers was an issue within the organization.
"I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Rooney said. "The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that."
The ultimatum Rooney is speaking of is Rodgers telling McCarthy that he believes he should be calling offensive plays instead of the head coach. McCarthy said no, and Rodgers reportedly told the team to release him then.
They benched him at first, but then released him after his tell-all interview on the Pat McAfee Show, where he claimed McCarthy was not watching film in a timely manner, falling asleep during quarterback meetings and said, "1, 2, 3 Packers" during hafltime of the Philadelphia Eagles game when he was breaking a huddle in the locker room.
Rooney sided with McCarthy despite the accusations and then made sure to share his thoughts about Rodgers' timing of things and how he put his teammates in a tough situation.
"There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload," Rooney said. "He talks about wanting to be a good teammate but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure.
"In general, I think, historically, what's in the locker room stays in the locker room. That's the way it's always been. That's the way it should be as far as I'm concerned."
He's not wrong about the timing. Pat Freiermuth, Drew Allar and others were asked about it just after Rodgers spoke on the McAfee Show and were having trouble finding the right words that would not get them in trouble.
At this point, the story is over between Rodgers and the Steelers, with Rooney putting a stamp on it. But how Pittsburgh performs the rest of the season may have more to say about the future of the franchise.

title: Aaron Rodgers' Ultimatum to Mike McCarthy Revealed, and It's Eye-Popping
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The breakup between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Aaron Rodgers was messy, public and brought up way more than anyone could have imagined. But how did it start? Where did it all suddenly come from?
Just over 24 hours before Rodgers was benched by the Steelers in a public statement made on their website and social media pages, head coach Mike McCarthy made it known that "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback." It was shocking to see the news that he changed his mind, and the fallout that happened afterward felt so dramatic that it clearly meant something significant happened to cause it all.
McCarthy and Rodgers met multiple times throughout the day before his benching, discussing the future of the offense and how they can move forward. McCarthy acknowledged in his press conference after Rodgers' release that the quarterback gave him an ultimatum that was "above his pay grade," and that eventually led to him being benched and cut.
According to Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac, that ultimatum was for Rodgers to take over play-calling duties, removing McCarthy from the role.
SOURCES: In a Tuesday evening meeting, Aaron Rodgers gave Mike Mike McCarthy an ultimatum: I want to call all the plays or just release me. They called his bluff and released him.
Rodgers seemingly gave the reason for this, stating that McCarthy was falling asleep in offensive and quarterback meetings and was not watching film on opponents in a timely manner.
Rodgers claims he's worried about McCarthy's health and wanted him to lead team meetings and focus on a smaller role as a head coach, instead of play-calling duties. He also claims that he thought the two were on the same page prior to his benching.
The Steelers weren't budging, though. This team will move forward with a new quarterback, not play-caller. McCarthy remains the man in charge, and the organization shared their support of him publicly to make sure everyone was aware of the situation and which side they were choosing.
For now, the only change in Pittsburgh is the release of Rodgers. They sit 6-4 and McCarthy is leading the charge. He believes he's the right man for the job and will continue to be throughout the season - now with a new starting quarterback to work with.
"I know how to win, and that's the facts," McCarthy said when asked why he's the right man for the job moving forward. "This is my third program, and I plan on winning here because of the men, because of this organization. We've got started, and the opportunity we have to learn and grow today because of some of the things that, frankly, should have been talked about earlier. So, this is a growth opportunity that I intend to take full advantage of."
Pittsburgh's season may be rocky, but it's still alive. And McCarthy isn't changing how this operation will run for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

title: Steelers' Mike McCarthy Situation Seemingly Ends One of Two Ways
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are swirling. This team lived through possibly the craziest day in franchise history, and somehow woke up with their head coach still in place, a game in 24 hours and a 6-4 record that shows they're still right in the thick of it.
If you looked at them on paper, the Steelers are right on course. If you watched how things unfolded in real time, you'd be shocked that the building is still standing.
But here they are, preparing for the Denver Broncos in Week 12, with a locker room that just lost their starting quarterback and a public opinion that is anything but positive. Head coach Mike McCarthy has his sights on winning, but it doesn't seem like he has much of a grip on the locker room. Things may be falling apart for the Steelers, and that means it's all seemingly going to end in one of two ways.
For those who missed it, Aaron Rodgers unloaded on the Steelers' head coach, calling out instances of McCarthy sleeping in meetings or missing them altogether, for calling the Steelers the Packers during halftime of the Philadelphia Eagles game, and for not trying to connect with the defensive players at all.
It was jaw-dropping watching Rodgers l ambast his former head coach on the Pat McAfee Show, pulling back the curtain on a situation that was so much worse than a two-game losing streak and a benched quarterback could have ever portrayed.
Afterward, even more came out, with players trying to show their confidence in the head coach , but not displaying it with their body language. The locker room felt like someone had just lost their family pet and was not stuck with the evil stepmother to comfort them.
And that wasn't all. NFL insider Jordan Schultz made it known that players have had issues with McCarthy for some time, and that the locker room may be slipping on the head coach during his first season. Offensive players are disappointed in how things are happening, and players who worked with Mike Tomlin for years are struggling to connect with McCarthy.
Sources: The relationship between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy has not been in a good place, and a path back together is considered “highly unlikely.” The frustration is not just with Rodgers. Multiple position groups have been upset, and I’m told McCarthy has not been what… https://t.co/1GHeWUIQOv pic.twitter.com/Kezunpjcmn
Here's the thing: the Steelers' front office and ownership will decide how this ends , because it appears to be headed in one of two directions.
Route one is that the Steelers move on from McCarthy either during or after the season. The head coach did not deny falling asleep in meetings and confirmed calling the team the Packers during halftime of a critical Week 11 loss. Former players like James Harrison, Rod Woodson and others have made it known how unacceptable it is and how surprised they are that McCarthy remains the team's leader.
This also isn't the first time I've heard that former players are upset with McCarthy and the way he's handling things. This goes back to training camp, when he first started interacting with the few alumni who showed up to practice.
Route two is that the team doesn't do anything. They let McCarthy remain the head coach and show support that this is "his team." Once that happens, everything changes.
Players like Cam Heyward, T.J. Watt and others may be on their way out. McCarthy begins to build what he believes is the right roster, which is probably a much younger group of players. And in a year, the locker room looks much, much different than it does today.
Roster turnover is needed for the Steelers, and has been for some time. How much is the question. If McCarthy is still here, it's probably a good idea to expect a lot.
But that's on Art Rooney II, Omar Khan and anyone else who's involved in the decision to keep McCarthy or let him go. They'll decide what the future of the Steelers looks like after, maybe, the craziest day in franchise history.

title: Inside the Steelers Facility as Aaron Rodgers Lambasted Mike McCarthy
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Aaron Rodgers didn't hold back on "The Pat McAfee Show". He didn't hide any of the stories he once felt he was covering up about his head coach. And as it was happening, the Pittsburgh Steelers were walking off the practice field, with Mike McCarthy making his way to the second floor of UPMC Rooney Sports Complex to prepare for the Denver Broncos, with Mason Rudolph as his starting quarterback.
To set the scene, reporters are required to wait in the lobby of the practice facility as the team comes off the practice field. This allows players to settle before the media rushes in for interviews. It also allows the coaching staff to make their way to their offices after talking post-practice.
On this particular day, the Steelers ended practice at 1:37 p.m. Coincidentally, their former starting quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, was speaking on "The Pat McAfee Show" at 1:40 p.m.
Usually, the McAfee Show is on the television in the lobby of the facility every weekday at noon until it ends. ESPN almost never gets turned off at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex. But just seconds before Rodgers was set to make his appearance, someone came in and changed the channel.
So, everyone turned to their phones. Crowds of reporters huddled around each other, listening to the words of Rodgers as he unleashed havoc on the Steelers and their head coach. And as he told stories of McCarthy "snoring" in meetings and chanting "1,2,3 Packers" to the team, the head coach himself came walking through the crowd.
"Excuse me," McCarthy said as he shuffled through the crowd and made his way onto the elevator, only to hear Rodgers say, "I'm concerned about his health" in the background.
BREAKING NEWS: @AaronRodgers12 addresses being benched by the Pittsburgh Steelers #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/6rggspWDGX
The moment was surreal. You knew that McCarthy knew, but it's hard to imagine he knew what was actually happening. That his once long-standing friendship evaporated as Rodgers let the entire world know that McCarthy is failing Pittsburgh as their lead man. That he would be the biggest topic of conversation across multiple platforms, radio shows, TV programs and Thanksgiving catch-ups, and not because he benched a future Hall of Famer, but because he's falling asleep in meetings.
With the release of Rodgers following his appearance on the show, the Steelers have made their stance clear. McCarthy isn't going anywhere, but it's hard to tell right now what that means for the future of the franchise.
"I love Aaron Rodgers and I love the Pittsburgh Steelers," Will Howard summed it up.
Truthfully, that's the line everyone is walking right now. This team was blindsided. Then, so was McCarthy. The mood of the locker room after the Rodgers interview was like everyone just found out they got coal for Christmas.
Fans, players and the organization need to pick a side. Some already have, and some are trying to let it cool before they do.
The Steelers are in a whirlwind, though. Most reporters in the room would tell you that they have never witnessed anything like this before, because there may have never been anything like this before.
To witness it in real time was jaw-dropping. This situation may be over, but the moment will last forever. And surreal may be underplaying how powerful it felt at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex.

Meanwhile, the resurgent Los Angeles Rams, winners of five straight games, have moved past the Seahawks in the division standings. Fortunately, Macdonald and company still have two games this season against Sean McVay’s squad.

WHAAAAAT IS HAPPENING?!? 😱 ANOTHER Seahawks fumble and the 49ers jump on it in the end zone 🤯 19+ pic.twitter.com/UNkQfu4xVI
Under Kyle Shanahan and including a pair of postseason meetings, it’s the Seahawks that have the one-game edge (11-10) dating back to 2017. However, dating back to 2022, this series has pretty much belonged to the 49ers thanks to eight victories in the clubs’ last 11 clashes.

title: 3 Score Predictions for Seahawks vs. 49ers Rematch
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are getting ready for their Week 12 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers inside Levi's Stadium.
It's a big game for the Seahawks , who can really improve their playoff chances with a win on the road against their top division rival. The Niners are hoping to keep their place as the No. 1 seed in the NFC, which would grant them homefield advantage throughout the playoffs.
Some members of the Seattle Seahawks On SI staff gave their score predictions for the matchup.
It appears that Sam Darnold is ready to make his return and if Mike Macdonald’s club is to avenge that Week 5 home loss to the NFC West leaders, the nine-year pro has to snap his personal six-game stretch of throwing at least one interception.
But let’s not bury the lead. It’s the league’s second-ranked offense against the NFL’s No. 1 defense in terms of yards gained and yards allowed, etc. And Kyle Shanahan’s balanced attack is clicking on all cylinders. A late Seattle rally falls short.
“I don’t know how much I believe in anyone ever actually ‘deserving’ a championship, you go win it. But if that does exist, I would argue no one in football deserves one more than Kyle Shanahan… Maybe it’s [the 49ers'] year.” @getnickwright explains: pic.twitter.com/vhARlsAGbQ
This game could very easily go down to the wire, which could mean it goes in either direction. I like the Seahawks in this matchup because they are coming off the bye week, which is a strategic advantage, and they have already faced and lost to the Niners this season.
It is incredibly difficult to beat a divisional opponent twice in one year, especially one of the Seahawks' caliber, but I believe their players returning to full health and the urgency and desire to win this football game should push Seattle over the top.
The Seattle Seahawks should play a much more clean game than in Week 5 where everything was against them.
Seattle comes in with a more focused running game and a defense that is looking to show why they are the best in the league. It's going to be a four quarter battle, but the Seahawks are more desperate to save their season and their divisional title hopes.
Kickoff between the Seahawks and 49ers is scheduled for Sunday at 1:25 p.m. PT inside Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara. Fans can watch the game on FOX or stream it on the FOX One app.

title: Seahawks Can’t Afford for Sam Darnold to Pick Up Where He Left Off
full_text:
Last offseason, Seattle Seahawks’ general manager John Schneider signed journeyman quarterback Sam Darnold to a three-year, $100.5 million contract. Originally the third overall pick in the 2018 NFL draft by the New York Jets, the Seahawks are his fifth different employer.
After three seasons with Gang Green, he was dealt to the Carolina Panthers in 2021. He would wind up in San Francisco in 2023 and a year later inked a one-year deal with the Minnesota Vikings.
The 2024 season proved to be a turning point for the former USC product. He enjoyed a career year with Kevin O’Connell’s club, led the Vikings to a 14-3 record and a playoff berth, and was named to his first Pro Bowl. But there was an awful Week 18 performance at Detroit, followed by a disastrous showing in the wild card round vs. the Los Angeles Rams.
Still, Schneider was all in when it came to adding the improving signal-caller, trading Geno Smith to the Las Vegas Raiders. A season ago, Darnold completed 67.7 percent of his passes. He threw for 4,048 yards and 25 touchdowns, but did commit a league-high 20 turnovers via 14 interceptions and six lost fumbles in 17 regular-season outings for the NFC West champions.
The Seahawks don’t make it this far if Sam Darnold doesn’t have the best game of his career against the Rams In the NFC Championship Game: - 346 YDS / 3 TDS - Outdueled Matthew Stafford This was Darnold’s Mona Lisa pic.twitter.com/oTHJvVLH38
In Seattle’s three-game playoff run, Darnold was effective in the sense that he and the team played turnover-free football. The veteran hurler connected on just 61.5 percent of his throws, albeit for a combined 672 yards and five scores. But that completion percentage left a lot to be desired.
Still, he played perhaps his best game of the season in the NFC title clash with the Los Angeles Rams. He hit on 25-of-36 passes for 346 yards and three touchdowns in the 31-27 triumph.
The Commanders PICK OFF Sam Darnold and take it back for SIX 😤 pic.twitter.com/f4eKS6Fjw0
Now comes 2026. In the season debut vs. the New England Patriots, he lasted just five plays and would be sidelined for not only the rest of that contest but sat out Week 2 as well. He made his return in Week 3 at Washington and while he put up good numbers, he also served up a pick-six which proved to the difference in a 33-31 loss.
Once again, his lack of accuracy is worth noting. In his seven appearances, he’s connected on just 60.2 percent of his passes for 1,478 yards and nearly as many interceptions (9) as touchdown tosses (10). He’s been picked off at least once in six consecutive games, the worst-such streak of his career.
Darnold, who has sat out the last two games (oblique), is expected back this week as the Seahawks look to avoid a sweep at the hands of the NFC West leading San Francisco 49ers. It’s safe to say that Mike Macdonald and the reigning Super Bowl champions need to see a different version of the player that has disappointed in his second season in Seattle.

title: Seahawks Injury Report, Good News For Lawrence, Bad News For Purdy
full_text:
Thursday’s injury report is where things typically start to get real, so let’s see what both teams have to offer up. Yesterday’s initial report was long and had some serious points of concern for both teams, so today is important. I can tell you that a couple members of the Seattle Seahawks got good news today, while the San Francisco 49ers may be down their top player.
Sam Darnold (quadricep) is still a full participant, so he’ll be under center on Sunday. One significant improvement was Charles Cross (ankle), who got full participation after a limited one yesterday. Nick Kallerup (ankle) similarly upgraded to full, and while Nick is a backup, he’s become a fairly important one in this offense thanks to his blocking.
Anthony Bradford (knee, illness), Ernest Jones (knee), Drew Lock (right elbow), Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) and Leonard Williams (stinger) all held at limited. Pat O’Connell (toe) was downgraded from full to limited, although that’s obviously of very limited impact. Much more important is DeMarcus Lawrence (shoulder) being limited, indicating that he’ll play.
The newcomer today was Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) , who was limited with either a new injury or a recurrence of an old one. It’s not yet possible to decipher what the injury might mean, but Nwosu is a player that has gone through a lot of injuries in recent seasons, so it wouldn’t surprise me if it’s serious. Tomorrow will tell us much more about the circumstances.
Jalen Milroe (illness), Abraham Lucas (ankle), and Quenton Nelson (knee) remain out of practice, although there’s not much to say there since Milroe is a third stringer and Lucas and Nelson are already announced as out. Jarran Reed (toe) is still a DNP, a concerning sign that he may not be available, although hope remains he’s just getting extra rest.
Mostly, things are fine in San Francisco. Romello Height (hand), Khalil Kareem (ankle), and Mykel Williams (hand) remained full participants. Keenan Allen , Christian McCaffrey and Trent Williams went from rest days yesterday to full practices today, so no issue there either. Austen Pleasants (knee) also went full, so he’ll be available in the event of a tackle injury.
Deommodore Lenoir (foot) and Carver Willis (illness) were limited again, I have to imagine both will play. Dre Greenlaw (neck) and Upton Stout (shoulder, neck) were also limited, but I’m less sure about their availability due to the nature of their injuries. Mike Evans (achilles) was limited, and we all know he’s playing anyway. Mostly, it’s going according to plan.
Siran Neal (knee, foot) and Jordan Watkins (groin) look on track to miss the game after DNPs, but that’s not the big headline here. They’re both backups. Brock Purdy (ankle) is not, and after a second straight DNP, it’s now seeming fairly likely he misses the game on Sunday and we get Mac Jones. Check in tomorrow for the final word, when all eyes will be on that ankle.

title: Why Josh Jones Starting in Week 12 is a Boost for the Seahawks
full_text:
Injuries have plagued a lot of teams in the league through the first 11 weeks of the 2026 NFL Season. The Seattle Seahawks (6-4) are encountering injuries on both sides of the ball . They are experiencing another injured starting offensive lineman, with right tackle Abraham Lucas out for Week 12 at the San Francisco 49ers.
While replacing starters is difficult, the Seahawks can turn to their solid depth chart to fill in for the injured starters. One player they can shift around is Josh Jones, who started a few games in place of the injured Charles Cross. With Cross back, Jones will start in place of the injured Lucas. This move should be a big boost for the Seahawks going against the 49ers rather than a problem.
​Jones will be starting in his fourth consecutive game for the Seahawks, but this time at right tackle. He started the past three games at left tackle in place of the injured Cross, who is set to return on Sunday. Jones has shown he is capable of being a reliable starter for the Seahawks.
Jones has earned a Pro Football Focus grade above 70 overall in each of his three starts. He has allowed only five pressures and no sacks during that span. PFF currently has Jones with an overall grade of 84.4, a pass-blocking grade of 83.4 and a run-blocking grade of 82.5.
​Jones will have a big test on Sunday against a 49ers defense that is trying to boost their pass rush. In the five games since returning from injury, 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa has only accumulated eight total tackles, four solo tackles, four quarterback hits, three tackles for loss and no sacks.
The 49ers haven’t seen much production from their edge players and newly traded defensive tackle/end DeForest Buckner. San Francisco looks to put as much pressure on Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold as possible.
​Lucas has been incredibly disappointing as the starting right tackle this season . Through 10 games played until he got injured, Lucas allowed 26 pressures, six sacks and four quarterback hits. He was the lowest-graded offensive lineman in the 32-29 Week 5 loss to the 49ers with an overall grade of 50.8. Lucas has found himself beaten often by Bosa in quick pass protection.
The Seahawks will have a more stable offensive tackle in Jones at right tackle. With the 49ers still figuring out their pass-rush tempo, the Seahawks’ offense has a chance to use the newfound momentum they gained in the Week 9 and 10 wins and developed through the bye week to create a solid performance at the line of scrimmage on Sunday.

title: Seahawks’ Front Office Suffers Rare Loss With Rookie Avery Smith
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have one of the best front offices in the league thanks to a collective effort of ownership, general manager John Schneider, and the scouts. Schneider has created two Super Bowl-winning teams under two different rosters. Very rarely does the Seahawks make mistakes with their roster or any moves. There are players that don’t fit with the team’s long-term plans, but that isn’t a failure of the front office. On Wednesday, the Seahawks learned the hard way about the utilization of a rookie.
The Seahawks waived former undrafted rookie cornerback Avery Smith on Tuesday to make some room on the roster. On Wednesday, the Los Angeles Chargers claimed Smith on waivers. Smith re-joins the Chargers after the Seahawks traded for him following the end of training camp . This marks one of the conclusion of a gamble from Schneider that didn’t pay off.
The Seahawks traded a sixth-round pick to the Chargers for Smith. This came after the Seahawks looked to upgrade the defensive backs. Smith would be among the rookies that have played the most games for the Seahawks this season, but they have all been on special teams. Smith played six games for Seattle, which included 56 snaps on special teams and none on offense . Smith accounted for five total tackles, including two solo tackles.
With the Seahawks still making moves, they are constantly moving players around their active roster and the practice squad. After being partly on special teams, the Seahawks attempted to get Smith on the practice squad for a more impactful player, but this left the Chargers a chance to get their player back and still keep their sixth-round pick.
The Seahawks didn’t just lose a player; they lost an investment. Through the first ten weeks of the season, Smith had the third-most snaps by a rookie behind running back Jadarian Price and guard Beau Stephens. It was clear that Smith wasn’t going to be a key defensive contributor, but he was still an asset on special teams and still learning from leaders.
With the Chargers reclaiming their undrafted free agent, the Seahawks lose out on Smith becoming a key asset in the future. Schneider essentially traded a 2027 NFL Draft sixth-round pick for 56 special teams snaps. The Seahawks had 11 total picks for the 2027 Draft thanks to the compensatory picks , but one was lost with the Smith trade.
With the 2027 NFL Draft being a highly talented draft class, any picks to select a key asset or used to trade up for a higher draft pick would be beneficial. This is one of the rare times that Schneider failed to visualize the possibility of an outcome or where his gambles didn’t work.

title: Seahawks Mailbag: 3 Questions Leading Into The 49ers Game
full_text:
This week, the Seattle Seahawks have their last real chance of convincing the NFL world that they can still be real contenders this season, so all eyes are on Santa Clara. I asked my discord server what their biggest questions about the team are right now. Let’s take a look at what’s on the mind of the fans. The wording of the questions has been lightly edited for this article.
“What will it take for Sam Darnold to get benched?”
My theory is that they’re going to keep him out there until they feel like they’re certain that he’s not the guy. That might be frustrating for some fans, but it’s somewhat understandable. The Seattle Seahawks are a few months away from making a franchise-altering decision on extending Sam Darnold for massive money. They want more data.
That mentality might end up costing this team a postseason spot, but they might also believe that Drew Lock is capped and isn’t good enough to win in the playoffs. A year after winning the super bowl, the standard is higher than just making the dance. I understand it, although I’m not sure I agree with the assumption about Lock. I feel like Sam’s leash is still long.
“What do the Seahawks need to do for the offense to be more consistent with Sam?”
I think this one is pretty straightforward. Despite Sam’s tremendous amount of success on third down in the game against the Kansas City Chiefs, the Seahawks must stay out of third down and pass situations. That means being more successful on first and second down. I’m looking at Brian Fleury to call a better game, and the running game to grind out more yards.
Even with these adjustments in place, I don’t expect much. There’s reason to believe that Darnold was, to an extent, figured out last season at the halfway point . I don’t believe the early-season MVP-caliber Sam Darnold will ever come back. But he can be a good starter, good enough to have a lot of success on a team with a defense this elite.
“Is there any possibility for Anthony Bradford and Quenton Nelson to both start at guard when Nelson comes back?”
I have an appreciation for Anthony Bradford, and I do believe he has been over-hated in previous seasons, but I think it’s time to move on. His play since returning from his knee injury has been brutal, and I find it hard to believe the juice is worth the squeeze anymore. He’ll be gone in the offseason, we may as well play the players who are part of the future.
I don’t think there’s a good answer for Seattle’s offensive line problems this season. I do believe that Grey Zabel is destined to move to center next year , but he needs an offseason and training camp to learn how to consistently snap and call out blocking assignments. It’s just not reasonable for him to learn it on the fly. It’s suboptimal, but he’s right guard for now.
