title: The Best, Worst and Likeliest Scenarios in Seahawks vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are facing off against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12, and the stakes could not be higher.
The Seahawks are 6-4 on the outside of the playoff picture in the NFC , but a win against the 49ers, whom they lost to in Week 5 at Lumen Field, will not only settle the score but help their chances of reaching the postseason. Here's a look at the best, worst, and likeliest outcomes from the game between the two NFC West rivals.
The last time the Seahawks were at Levi's Stadium, it was in Week 18 for the NFC West Championship. The winner got the No. 1 overall seed in the NFC, while the loser was forced to be the top wild card. The Seahawks managed to stifle the Niners with a 13-3 win, giving them the first-round bye, the division title, and the momentum they needed to win it all.
While the stakes aren't as high as that particular game, the Seahawks face a pretty close-to-must-win game for them, with the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams breathing down their necks and fighting for one final wild card spot. The Seahawks have to do everything they can to separate themselves from the pack. A win against the Niners would not only give them reason to believe they can beat any team in the NFL, but it would get them one step closer, mathematically, to the playoffs.
The Seahawks have the No. 1 defense in the league, so that should give them a chance to beat any team in the league, including the Niners, who have the league's top-scoring offense after dropping 35 points or more in each of the last three games.
As I previously mentioned, the Seahawks have the No. 1 offense in the league, and they made light work of the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday Night Football in Week 11. The Vikings have the second-best defense in the league, but the Niners were able to dismantle them.
The same could happen in San Francisco this time around, so the Seahawks need to make sure they have the proper game plan that can contain all of the weapons on the Niners' offense.
Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, Debo Samuel, Mike Evans and George Kittle form one of the toughest offensive attacks in the league. The Seahawks need to be ready for all the ways San Francisco can beat them.
Any game between two top teams is likely to come down to a couple of plays in the fourth quarter. Whichever team makes the most plays late should be able to come out on top in this one, just like things did in Week 5.
The Seahawks held a lead in the fourth quarter, but they were unable to hold it after an Evans touchdown with 11 minutes to go. The plays made down the stretch gave the Niners the win, which kept their record undefeated at the time.
Given that it is so hard to beat a divisional opponent twice in one season and Seattle's stronger need for desperation, I like the Seahawks' chances of evening the score with the Niners and pulling out a much-needed win.

title: 5 Things the Seahawks Should Be Thankful For This Thanksgiving
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are going into Thanksgiving Day with a lot on their plate and in their minds.
The team is 6-4, fresh off their bye week , and looking forward to competing in the final seven games of the season with the hope of returning to the playoffs and repeating as Super Bowl champions. Here's a look at five things the Seahawks should be thankful for during the holiday season.
The Seahawks are in the third year of the Mike Macdonald era, and it has proven to be a resounding success so far. Macdonald remains one of the youngest head coaches in the league at just 39 years old, setting himself up for a very long career in the Pacific Northwest.
Macdonald arrived in Seattle after being the defensive coordinator for the top defense in the NFL, and he has maintained that standard in Seattle. The dark-side defense was tops in the NFL last year, and it led to a Super Bowl title. This year, they are still on top of the leaderboard, and they have a chance to win every single football game because of them and the work Macdonald and his coaching staff put in.
The Seahawks have been very meticulous about their free agency and draft process, which could lead to them having an excess of picks when the draft comes about next April. The team currently has 11 picks to work with after acquiring multiple compensatory selections from great players like Kenneth Walker III, Coby Bryant, Riq Woolen and Boye Mafe leaving in free agency.
With 11 picks, the Seahawks can use them to move up and acquire players they really covet, or they can add a bunch of prospects that give them a better chance to churn out some strong contributors in 2027 and beyond. This gives them a chance to sustain their success and be one of the top teams in the league for many years to come.
In a season that could have gone totally awry after the first series, when Sam Darnold went down with an injury, backup quarterback Drew Lock has kept this team afloat. Lock has been the player under center for most of Seattle's wins this season, and he is playing near-flawless football.
While Lock had two fumbles in his most recent start against the Las Vegas Raiders, he has yet to throw an interception and has seven touchdowns so far this season. If the Seahawks make it to the playoffs, Lock's contributions should not go unnoticed, even if he doesn't play another down for the rest of the regular season.
As I alluded to earlier, the Seahawks have the best defense in the NFL, and it isn't particularly close. The Seahawks average 236.1 yards per game, which is 44 fewer than the next-highest team.
The Minnesota Vikings have the second-best defense in terms of yards and are ranked number one in terms of points allowed. The Seahawks are just behind the Vikings, with 175 points allowed, which means they've only allowed two more touchdowns than them over 10 games this season.
The Seahawks provide elite matchups on all three levels of the defense, forcing opponents to pick their poison, which usually doesn't go very well. The Seahawks have held their opponent to 10 points or fewer four times this season and are 4-0 in those games. It's a true testament to how strong the defense has been this year, and as more games go on, it is only going to become more crucial for the defense to step up.
In addition to having the league's best defense, the Seahawks also have the league's top wide receiver, who also isn't very close. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is one of two receivers this season to surpass the 1,000-yard mark. The only other player to do so is Dallas Cowboys star CeeDee Lamb, who has 1,108 yards in 11 games, compared to JSN's 10.
Smith-Njigba also is the only receiver this season to find the end zone 10 times, and he has two multi-touchdown games already this season. Smith-Njigba is trying to win his second consecutive Offensive Player of the Year award. If he can be the first wide receiver in league history to record 2,000 yards, he might as well have that award locked up.
He still has a long way to go to reach that goal, but if he continues to reach his season average of 120.7 yards per game, he should be able to make NFL history.

title: Seahawks Injury Report, Charles Cross, Sam Darnold, Much More
full_text:
Back to the grind for the Seattle Seahawks. The bye week is over, and it’s the Wednesday before a game, so we’ve got a new injury report. Brace yourself, it’s quite long, but applying context clues makes the situation a little bit more transparent. The San Francisco 49ers have their own concerns, by the way. So let’s get into it, starting with the Seahawks.
Two players were listed with injuries but got full participation today anyway. Pat O’Connell (toe) was one, which is of minimal impact, and Sam Darnold (quadricep) , which is of massive impact. Since Macdonald has indicated the plan is to start Darnold on Sunday if he gets through a full week of practice, and Darnold is already a full participant today, he’s the guy.
Limited players included Anthony Bradford (knee, illness), Charles Cross (ankle) , Ernest Jones (knee), Nick Kallerup (ankle), Drew Lock (right elbow), Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle), and Leonard Williams (stinger). There’s certainly nuance for each player, but I would expect all of these guys to be ready to roll on Sunday. And we’ll need most of them.
As for players who sat out entirely, we’ll separate them into three groups. First, we have the irrelevant one, Jalen Milroe (illness). Then, we have DeMarcus Lawrence (shoulder) and Jarran Reed (toe) , who are likely just being cautious due to their age and are probably playing on Sunday. We’ll see where it goes, but I’d expect both players to be available.
And then, Abraham Lucas (ankle) and Quenton Nelson (knee), who are already out of the picture this week. Macdonald made it clear that neither player is really on the table to be ready, although Nelson sounds like he might be back for the Cowboys game. This is the real issue for the Seahawks this week, as they’re down two starters on the offensive line.
For San Francisco, Romello Height (hand), Khalil Kareem (ankle), and Mykel Williams (hand), all edge rushers, were full participants today. Keenan Allen was limited, and Christian McCaffrey and Trent Williams were out, but all three were just resting. Expect all six of these players to be available and healthy by Sunday. That’s not the big problem for the 49ers this time.
Dre Greenlaw (neck) led the limited participant group, which is worth watching since neck injuries are no joke. Deommodore Lenoir (foot), Austen Pleasants (knee), and Carver Willis (illness) were also limited. Same for Upton Stout (shoulder, neck). See the Greenlaw sentence above why that might be significant, despite being able to practice some.
Mike Evans (achilles) was held out today, but we all know he’s going to play through it. Siran Neal (knee, foot) and Jordan Watkins (groin) were also out, although that is of minimal impact. The big one, however, is Brock Purdy (ankle), who was already indicated to be in genuine danger of sitting out on Sunday by Kyle Shanahan. Stay tuned on this one.

title: Why the 49ers Can't Solely Rely on Mike Evans to Beat Seattle
full_text:
Mike Evans was a madman against the Seattle Seahawks back in Week 5. He proved in that game he was the missing piece for the San Francisco 49ers.
Evans tallied seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown. The Seahawks must still be having nightmares about his performance, especially cornerback Josh Jobe.
He had the unfortunate responsibility of facing Evans 14 times in Week 5. Evans was targeted on seven of those matchups, catching six passes for 98 yards and a touchdown, in addition to a two-point conversion.
If Brock Purdy sees Evans lined up across from Jobe again, he'll certainly take advantage of the mismatch. However, I don't believe Evans can carry the 49ers again on Sunday as he did in Week 5. They'll need to get others involved to beat Seattle.
The Seahawks are a prideful group, especially on defense. Knowing Evans eviscerated them must have left a sour taste since the initial matchup.
They are going to do everything they can to slow Evans down in the second matchup. They'll be better prepared, too, since they're coming off their Bye Week.
Seattle is rested, has had ample time to prepare, and has all the motivation in the world. They will make it personal to keep Evans in check.
No other receiver has hurt them like Evans did, especially on vertical routes. Evans was targeted on five of 14 vertical routes, totaling three receptions for 66 yards.
Entering Week 12, Evans stands as the only receiver to have gained more than 50 yards on such routes against the Seahawks' defense this season.
That certainly has been a talking point all week, if not longer, in the Seahawks' locker room. They know that if they can limit or even remove Evans from the equation, they can win.
And it's true. If the Evans is a non-factor in a game, winning will be tough, especially against an elite defense like the Seahawks'. The 49ers needed Evans to pop off in Week 5 to win.
He was their only effective receiver. No other 49ers receiver had more than 24 receiving yards. Seattle will take their chances in letting the rest of the skill players beat them.
They will make the 49ers try to beat them with anyone other than Evans. That means Deebo Samuel, Keenan Allen, George Kittle, and Christian McCaffrey will need to help lead the way.
With all that said, that doesn't necessarily mean Evans will be quiet. He will still have a major impact, even if he only catches four balls for 60 yards. It's still helpful.
But the odds of him exploding as he did in Week 5 are unlikely. Seattle's defense will throw everything at him to prevent it from happening. They'll allow anyone else to beat them, not Evans.
I wouldn't expect Jobe to match up with him too much. Seattle will have formulated an adequate game plan to neutralize Evans, forcing Purdy to rely on his other weapons.

title: Dominick Puni Still Can't Believe How Good the 49ers Offense Is
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are 9-1 on the season and are on the brink of securing a playoff spot.
They look increasingly likely to clinch a spot in the coming weeks. The Chicago Bears are just one game behind in the NFC North, but the advantage of the Los Angeles Rams and the Seattle Seahawks is a few games.
Despite their incredibly fortunate position, there is work to do and there are crucial matchups ahead. But before thinking about any possible postseason fixture, it's all about taking one game at a time.
The 49ers squashed the narrative that their ageing offensive players could derail their season. Both Kenaan Allen's arrival and the reunion with DeForest Buckner make them even older, but so far their impact shows why they are veterans at their positions.
For one player, guard Dominick Puni, he had a sudden realization in their recent encounter with the Minnesota Vikings just how lucky he is to be working alongside players who undoubtedly will make the Hall of Fame.
“We were in the huddle in Mexico last week and I saw Mike [Evans] and Keenan [Allen] standing next to each other in the huddle during the TV timeout and I was like, 'I don’t know if I’ll ever be on an offense this good ever again in my life or at least this talented', I mean, everywhere you look there’s a Hall of Famer," he said.
But this quote puts things into perspective further. San Francisco also has left tackle Trent Williams , running back Christian McCaffrey, tight end George Kittle and linebacker Fred Warner. These are more names that are in the conversation or are close to being nailed-down names.
The reminder shows that despite all the talent the 49ers currently have at key positions on both offense and defense, no one truly knows how long each player will be around for and performing at the highest level.
The perfect and most fitting ending would be a Super Bowl ring for all these veterans. While Mike Evans already has one, the rest don't, but adding this accolade only cements their legacy in Canton.
Still, seven games are left to play, and that doesn't even include potential playoff spots. It's a matter of taking each game as it comes and producing to the best of their abilities on each Sunday.
But Puni's thoughts deserve to be shared with the world as a reminder of the caliber of players currently on the 49ers' roster.

title: 49ers Coach Reveals Plan to Replace Colton McKivitz
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' plan at right tackle appears to be coming into focus now that Colton McKivitz is out for the season with his ankle injury. While the team opened the practice window for depth tackle Austen Pleasants, the plan right now is for the team to start Vederian Lowe for the foreseeable future, according to head coach Kyle Shanahan .
When asked if the veteran free agent would hold down right tackle until anything else changes, Shanahan made it clear that would be the case. Shanahan thought that Lowe played well considering he faced a strong defense, and he has mostly practiced and played in the NFL at left tackle.
“I thought he played really well coming in, especially going against that defense, just all the problems that they present,” said Shanahan.
While Lowe has 1,415 snaps at left tackle and 276 snaps on the right side, Shanahan said that they brought him in because they feel he can hold it down on the right side.
“That's why we brought him here,” said Shanahan. “I mean, any time you have a swing tackle, that means you better be capable of starting. And he started a lot of games in this league and has played like a starter, and that's why we targeted him as a swing tackle.”
However, the team also has Austen Pleasants on the IR. They just activated his practice window. So, they have until December 16 to activate him or they will have him revert back to the season-ending IR. Shanahan noted that Plesants has been healthy; the team just didn’t have a roster spot open so they did not open his window. With McKivitz out, they are going to see what he has.
“He's been healthy for a few weeks now, and, with losing Colton, it makes sense to get him out at practice, and we'll see how this week goes,” added Shanahan. “But he's been healthy for a bit; we'll see how his practices go, see if he's ready to go, and if he is, we'll make a decision.”
They used their roster spot from McKivitz to activate Nate Hobbs. So, if they want to bring Pleasants up to the active roster, they will have to release someone. For now, Lowe will start. Either rookie Enrique Cruz will be active, or they will use a practice squad elevation on Foster Sarrell. They have until Saturday to make that decision.

title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Gives Simple Response to Brandon Aiyuk's Move to Commanders
full_text:
One of the biggest developments in San Francisco 49ers land this week was the departure of Brandon Aiyuk .
The 49ers released him, and in what felt like no time at all, he found a new team. That team is the Washington Commanders, where he'll join their practice squad.
It's hardly a surprise. Aiyuk, whether alone or with his new agent, has made it clear for months that he wants to represent that organization. His wish has now come true.
Speaking to the media for the first time since Aiyuk's inevitable move east to Washington, D.C., head coach Kyle Shanahan offered a simple response with his thoughts.
"None. It was just a transactional thing and it's good for Washington. They got a good player," he stated.
The obvious takeaway is that Shanahan has become increasingly indifferent to the situation. Whenever Aiyuk is brought up, he appears to show little to no reaction, suggesting that the situation no longer warrants much of his attention.
While it's difficult to know exactly what he thinks, it's reasonable to assume there is some frustration or disappointment over how Aiyuk has handled things, particularly given the impact on the team and the organization.
Ultimately, Shanahan has always been focused on the team's success, and to his credit, he did a good job of ignoring all the noise. At this point, he will likely be more than happy to move forward without Aiyuk.
To quit on the team in the way Aiyuk did is something so unconventional in the NFL, but Shanahan probably did the right thing by simply not releasing him until the last possible moment. Neither side was going to come forward to reconcile.
Aiyuk joining his best mate, Jayden Daniels, in Washington felt like the inevitable conclusion , but what happens next will be the intriguing part.
He hasn't had a single reception since 2024, but everyone saw his impact before that injury against the Kansas City Chiefs. The world knows what a player he can be, and it wouldn't be at all surprising if he starts to perform now that he's landed exactly where he wants to be.
The 49ers shouldn't care what he does, and nor will they. Aiyuk was one of the rare players in their ranks who didn't seem dedicated to representing the city of San Francisco. His departure allows everyone to move forward.

title: Why the 49ers are Confident in Colton McKivitz's Replacement
full_text:
It was devastating to see San Francisco 49ers starting right tackle Colton McKivitz suffer a gruesome ankle fracture against the Minnesota Vikings .
The vibes were high in the Estadio Banorte up until that point. You could hear a pin drop from how silent the 10 minutes were during McKivitz’s placement on the cart to exit the game in the second quarter.
Losing him will be tough. McKivitz was playing at a Pro Bowl-caliber level this season. Even Kyle Shanahan acknowledges that, and that his loss will sting the 49ers.
“I thought he was playing really well,” Shanahan said. “I was really hurt for him that he couldn’t finish this year because he's had a hell of a year.”
With McKivitz out for the year, Vederian Lowe will be the one who takes over. He was the player who filled in the rest of the game for McKivitz, and he actually did a pretty fine job.
“I thought he played real well. Coming in, especially going against that defense, just all the problems that they present, so I thought he came in and stepped it up really well,” said Shanahan. “That’s why we brought him here.”
“Anytime you have a swing tackle, that means you better be capable of starting. He’s started a lot of games in this league and has played like a starter and that’s why we targeted him as a swing tackle.”
Lowe could’ve easily been a liability on the offensive line against the Vikings. Their vaunted defense has made actual starters overwhelmed and confused, so imagine a backup who is cold.
But he held up nicely. If that’s how he’s going to play for the rest of the season, then the 49ers will be in pretty good shape. Now, you can expect there to be issues at times.
Defensive coordinators will certainly try to exploit any weaknesses Lowe has, despite how well he performed in Mexico City. This is part of the process of uncovering what player he is.
The 49ers will learn about him as well through those hard times. Should he begin to struggle, it will make it difficult for Shanahan and Brock Purdy to execute the offense.
Shanahan will need to allocate help for Lowe as well as carefully consider some of his play calls. Purdy will also need to be conscientious of pressure and get the ball out more quickly.
For now, the 49ers are confident in Lowe. And after the performance he had in Mexico City, it’s easy to see why.

title: Why Mike Evans Deserves 49ers’ Biggest Thanks on Thanksgiving
full_text:
There’s a lot for the San Francisco 49ers to be thankful for on Thanksgiving.
For starters, I’m sure they’re extremely happy they don’t have to play on the feasting holiday. They get to enjoy their evening as every normal person does. I’m sure they’re giving thanks for that.
But the very next thing they should be thankful for is star receiver Mike Evans. He deserves the 49ers’ biggest thanks on Thanksgiving. He’s been everything as advertised and more.
Evans is the reason the 49ers managed to beat the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5. He went ballistic in that game, tallying seven catches for 113 yards and one touchdown. All three stats are season highs for him.
Without Evans, the 49ers most likely lose. In his first press conference, Evans said he was the missing piece to their offense. He was right. Look at how they were able to get over the hump against Seattle.
The same can be said for this past week in Mexico City as well. The 49ers always struck out against the Minnesota Vikings because defensive coordinator Brian Flores had an impeccable scheme.
Turns out, all the 49ers needed was Evans to finally crack the code. Of course, the game plan implemented by Kyle Shanahan was amazing, and Brock Purdy was incredible as well. They’re all a perfect match.
Just imagine if Evans chose money as his priority in free agency. He never would’ve joined the 49ers. They didn’t have the means to sign him to a lucrative deal. He would’ve gone elsewhere had that been the case.
He prioritized winning, which led him to Santa Clara. Plus, if he didn’t believe the 49ers were the team that gave him the best chance of winning another Super Bowl, he would’ve gone to the Buffalo Bills, who made him an offer.
Evans would’ve gotten a better quarterback, but he wouldn’t have gotten a better team. Besides, Evans knew Purdy was already a good quarterback. If he teamed up with Purdy, he’d only improve him.
Sure enough, that’s been the case this season. Purdy has a 150.2 passer rating, five touchdown passes, and 0 interceptions when targeting Evans, the highest passer rating by any quarterback-receiver duo in a season in the last five seasons, per Next Gen Stats.
Thanks to Evans, Purdy is in the running for MVP again. He’s also the reason the 49ers can win the Super Bowl, which I believe they will if he stays healthy. What an addition he’s been.
No one else on the 49ers deserves a bigger thanks on Thanksgiving than Evans.

title: 5 Things the 49ers Should Be Thankful For This Thanksgiving
full_text:
As the San Francisco 49ers get ready for Thanksgiving, there are plenty of things for the fans to get excited about. What are some of the biggest reasons to be thankful for the 2026 49ers?
Sure, the 49ers have not been healthy this year. They have had plenty of issues. At the same time, it looked worse at this point last year. Nick Bosa and Fred Warner are back. They were unsure how healthy Brock Purdy was. George Kittle and Mykel Williams suffered season-ending injuries.
They got through a lot of injuries, and right now Colton McKivitz is the only impactful starter who will not be there for a playoff run.
The 49ers offseason was a hit. They added Mike Evans and Osa Odighizua. Both players have impacted both sides of the football. The draft found them role players, but Kaelon Black, Romello Height, Jaden Dugger, and James Thompson have carved out roles.
Then, the additions of DeForest Buckner and Keenan Allen have them trending up. This was a huge success.
49ers fans have to sit back and reflect and feel satisfied that Shanahan finally found his quarterback of the future. There were questions as recently as last year when he suffered his injury, and the team held firm with Mac Jones. However, at his best, Purdy is an MVP candidate, and that is showing this year. The 49ers have had a head coach and quarterback together for a long time. That is huge.
The 49ers lost Robert Saleh, who got promoted to being an NFL head coach. The defense did not take a hit and might even be better with Morris. Morris made the right moves, the right changes, and could be a head coach in a few years again after what he did.
The 49ers' start is hot, but the division rivals who were so tough last year do not look as daunting. Sam Darnold has seen the clock strike midnight, and the Los Angeles Rams do not appear healthy enough to make a serious postseason run. San Francisco has beaten both teams once already and will be favored against them both the second time around. Things are falling into place.

title: Brock Purdy Misses First Week 12 Practice With New Injury
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers held out five players in their first Week 12 practice against the Seattle Seahawks, including Brock Purdy.
At his press conference today, Kyle Shanahan revealed that Purdy is nursing an ankle sprain. He suffered the injury in the second quarter against the Minnesota Vikings.
Shanahan was asked if he thinks Purdy can participate in practice later this week, to which he responded, "We'll see." He also said it's possible Purdy misses the game against Seattle.
The bright side is that Purdy is considered day-to-day. He's not dealing with a high ankle sprain, which is encouraging news. His absence on Wednesday is to keep him from aggravating it.
If Purdy can't go, Mac Jones will start in his place against Seattle. The 49ers were kept afloat last year thanks to Jones. He's a perfect fit in the 49ers' offense.
It's for times like this that justify why the 49ers didn't trade Jones, or why they held such a high price on him for anyone who wanted to acquire him.
The 49ers would've been forced to go with Kurtis Rourke. They stand no chance of beating the Seahawks, or any team, for that matter, with Rourke at the helm.
However, the Seahawks are an opponent the 49ers need Purdy to beat. Purdy's ability to keep plays alive, his in-rhythm passing, and his rapport with Mike Evans are crucial.
I wouldn't be confident the 49ers can beat the Seahawks, who are coming off a Bye Week, with Jones, as solid as he is. Purdy will need to be active for Friday's practice to keep his availability alive.
As for the other four 49ers that missed practice: Dre Greenlaw (neck), Siran Neal  (knee/foot), Evans (Achilles), and Jordan Watkins (groin).
Greenlaw was inactive against the Vikings with a neck injury despite getting in a limited practice before game day. He's in a volatile situation, but Shanahan said the 49ers aren't concerned about his longevity this season.
They will certainly want him back for Seattle, especially since he didn't finish the game in Week 5. His tone-setting physicality is needed for this matchup.
As for Evans, his absence is a moot point. This is part of the load management for him, and rightfully so. They need to keep his Achilles as fresh as can be for game days.
All eyes will be on Purdy throughout the week.

title: Former 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk Signs With a New Team
full_text:
After only a day as a free agent, former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has found a new home.
Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders to their practice squad, per ESPN's Adam Schefter . This was always bound to happen from the moment he cleared waivers on Tuesday.
He conducted himself on social media in the Summer as if he were already signed to them. Although there was a stretch when it seemed he would never join the Commanders.
Aiyuk and Jayden Daniels had gotten into a back-and-forth on social media, but they reportedly reconciled. The Commanders signing him proves that.
Otherwise, if there had still been a conflict, the Commanders would never have signed Aiyuk. Now, they are banking on the former All-Pro receiver to get up to speed and help their team make a playoff push.
Aside from the connection to Daniels, the Commanders needed a receiver. Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon against the 49ers on Monday Night Football in Week 6.
Stefon Diggs is their only viable receiver, with rookie Antonio Williams beginning to step it up. It made perfect sense for Aiyuk to join the Commanders.
It's better that he signs with them than with the Los Angeles Rams or the Seattle Seahawks. I had thought Aiyuk might've considered them for a petty incentive since they are the 49ers' divisional rival.
In any case, Aiyuk lands on a team, despite a bunch of 49ers fans believing he was never going to get picked up. The reality is, Aiyuk burning his bridge with the 49ers isn't that serious.
Yes, it's immature, weird, and annoying, but that's all social media. He wasn't toxic in the locker room or anything. It doesn't significantly detract from a team's interest in him.
So, of course, a team was going to give him a chance, especially a wide receiver-needy one like the Commanders. It's the NFL. If anyone has intriguing talent despite their baggage, they will be on a team.
He just couldn't be on the 49ers anymore. He took shots at them throughout the Summer. There's no coming back from that. In the end, the 49ers handled the Aiyuk situation perfectly.
This two and a half year weirdness is finally over. Both sides seem to be in a good spot. Although the 49ers are in a dramatically better spot with Mike Evans.

title: Why the 49ers Should Be Thankful Brock Purdy Is Their Franchise QB
full_text:
It's Thanksgiving for our American readers this week, so don't forget to be thankful that Brock Purdy is the franchise quarterback for the San Francisco 49ers.
There are many reasons for this. He's taken San Francisco to the NFC Championship Game, the Super Bowl and more recently the NFC Divisional Round. That's some effort.
But when looking beyond that, he's always played at a high level, and the level is even higher this year. The 49ers should be thankful that Purdy’s statistics reflect his effectiveness as a quarterback, as he's recorded 2,624 passing yards across 10 games, with a 71.0% completion rate and 23 touchdowns. His 118.2 passer rating speaks volumes.
But this points to a bigger reason to appreciate Purdy. Beyond his performances on game day, he embodies exactly what the 49ers, or any NFL franchise, would want in a quarterback.
His focus remains solely on football , with no distractions or unnecessary drama. Instead, he is constantly looking for ways to improve, whether through marginal adjustments or significant gains. This relentless desire to develop is undoubtedly one of his greatest qualities.
San Francisco lucked into a quarterback who was selected as the last pick of the draft and has established himself as an elite quarterback in the league. Yes, it helps that Kyle Shanahan of all people is his head coach, but all of Purdy's attitude and mentality towards the game is entirely down to him.
This mental aspect of the game is something that can't be taught, requiring natural composure, resilience and self-belief. His ability to handle pressure, learn, not be bothered by setbacks and maintain confidence separates him from many others.
The 49ers have their franchise quarterback for the years to come, and the Purdy era is well and truly underway. It's an exciting time to watch Purdy let it rip, whether he's connecting with future Hall of Famers like Mike Evans and Christian McCaffrey or making the most of opportunities with depth pieces such as Brandin Cooks and Jake Tonges.
But don't forget what he promised this offseason: he wants to win a Super Bowl for the city of San Francisco .
With the 49ers sitting at 9-1 and defeating opponents that mainstream media expected them to lose to, Purdy is certainly backing up those words. He's giving everything he has to deliver on that promise, and the city has every reason to believe in what he and this team are building.

title: Crucial Buccaneers Player's Return Looking More and More Likely
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers need a win on Monday more than they have all year. At 3-7, they're two games back from the 5-5 Carolina Panthers — a win keeps them in the hunt, and a loss buries them down far enough that they may not climb out.
The Bucs are looking for as many players to contribute as they can against the Panthers, and that includes some players they haven't had for a bit. One of those players is wideout Jalen McMillan, who injured his knee in preseason, returned in Week 2 of the regular season against the Cleveland Browns and then injured it again, landing on injured reserve for most of the year to this point.
McMillan activated his 21-day practice window earlier this week. And it looks like the NFL will get to see him back in action sooner rather than later.
McMillan was listed as a full participant on Thursday, were the Bucs to hold a practice on Thanksgiving Day (they did hold a practice on Wednesday but were not required to give an injury report). McMillan also practiced on Friday, which is a great sign for his potential availability.
Josiah Trotter (pictured here), Jacob Parrish and Jalen McMillan are all practicing. Benjamin Morrison and Antoine Winfield Jr. aren’t practicing, and Elijah Simmons is in a non-contact jersey. pic.twitter.com/G0XIB5kaD3
McMillan still has to be activated off of injured reserve within his 21-day window to play on Sunday. Once it was initially announced that he had opened that window, it was unknown just how far along he was in his recovery — but the way McMillan spoke in the locker room on Wednesday seems to indicate that he's ready to get back to it.
"It was a long road," McMillan said Wednesday. "Had some ups and downs, but I'm excited to be back and I'm excited to produce for the team."
The Bucs could certainly use a player of McMillan's caliber. Tampa Bay's leading receiver is Emeka Egbuka, who has just 296 yards on 59 targets.
McMillan has been one of Tampa Bay's best separators when he's played, but he's struggled with that in recent years — a scary neck injury kept him out for almost all of 2025, and he's missed most of 2026 so far.
The Bucs play the Panthers at 8:15 on Monday. When they do, it looks like McMillan will be involved, and he'll try to help lead the Bucs to a win to stay alive in the NFC South.

title: NFL Insider Gives Update on Todd Bowles' Hot Seat With Buccaneers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be looking for just their fourth win of the season when they host the Carolina Panthers on Monday Night Football.
However, if they are unable to come away with a victory, it seems like the season will be almost completely wrapped up with Tampa Bay falling to 3-8 and three games out of the NFC South lead.
Todd Bowles has consistently been at the center of fans' frustrations, but this year his defense has been playing at an elite level, with many of the issues coming from Zac Robinson and the offensive side of the ball.
Despite Bowles' improved defense, NFL insiders Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler still believe that his coaching seat is hot as we head into the final stretch of the season.
"Situations I'm watching for potential change at the end of the season include the Jets, Buccaneers, Colts, Eagles and maybe Commanders, though Dan Quinn seems to be turning things around in D.C.," Graziano wrote.
"The Bucs could wait until season's end for clarity on Todd Bowles' future, though Monday night vs. Carolina feels important (the Bucs would be three games out in the NFC South with a loss)," Fowler added.
Bowles took over as the Bucs' head coach in 2022 when Bruce Arians handed him the keys, but his tenure has been plagued with lackluster rosters, poor in-game decision-making, and, outside of this year, declining defensive play.
Bowles has consistently been under scrutiny and at the top of hot-seat lists throughout his time in Tampa Bay.
Still, if the Bucs were to lose to the Panthers on Monday night and miss the playoffs in back-to-back seasons, it would be hard to imagine that the Glazers would retain him for another season despite their admiration for him as a man and person.
It would be hard-pressed to see the Glazers fire Bowles midseason, as they have never once done so since owning the team, but a loss against the Panthers would likely be the writing on the wall for the future of Bowles as the Bucs' head man.
If Bowles is out in Tampa Bay at the end of the season, there will be rumblings on whether or not general manager Jason Licht will also be retained.
It's an all-important matchup for everyone in One Buc this weekend, and if Bowles and his staff want to remain with the team, they must go out and put up a performance similar to the first meeting against the Panthers.

title: Saints Coach Points to Bucs’ Bucky Irving When Asked About the Ideal RB
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a crucial game against the Carolina Panthers on Monday.
The Bucs are two games out from the Carolina Panthers and can narrow the gap with a win, keeping them alive in the NFC South race. If they lose, though, their season could be over, and it would likely be because their passing offense is among the worst in the league.
The rushing offense, however, has been quite excellent. It's been spearheaded by Bucky Irving, who has been one of the league's best running backs. He's been the entire offense, and he may have to continue to be for the Bucs to stay in it.
Irving has drawn plenty of attention across the league — and that includes a coach on one of his biggest division rivals.
New Orleans Saints running backs coach Joel Thomas said on a recent appearance with the Senior Bowl that he's been watching some film of Irving lately — and that Irving is the exact type of running back he's looking for whenever he's scouting players.
"I like that chip, I like that edge, I like that tough guy mentality when you're playing that position," Thomas said. "I'm watching Bucky Irving playing against Chicago. And he is a dog," Thomas said. "The he way he runs, it's relentless. It's 'I'm full-go, I'm going to get this first down. I'm not going down first contact.' Those are the type of guys that we're looking for and that we're training."
What does Saints RB coach Joel Thomas look for in a running back? There’s a certain back playing for a division rival who checks those boxes 👀 #TheDraftStartsInMobile pic.twitter.com/Mozb4m3bog
The compliment is a kind one from a division rival, but when you look at the numbers, it's not hard to see why he might admire Irving as opposed to his own players.
Quarterback Tyler Shough is the Saints' leading rusher, believe it or not, with 221 rushing yards. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. is the second-best rusher at 218 yards on the year, and the Saints are averaging 93.1 yards per game on the ground — the 28th-best number in the NFL.
Irving, meanwhile, has been a phenom this year. He's put up 893 yards for 4.8 yards per carry and eight rushing touchdowns, on pace for the best season of his career. He ran for 170 yards against the Atlanta Falcons and 165 against the Dallas Cowboys, both games coming close to Shough's entire rushing total this year.
In that case, divisional envy makes a lot of sense. And Thomas won't have to wait too long to watch Irving in person.
The Bucs and Saints square off in Week 15 on Dec. 20 before playing each other to end their seasons (the regular season, at least) in Week 18 at a time to be determined. The NFC South remains close, with the Bucs and Saints both two games out from the Carolina Panthers.
We'll see if those matchups end up holding real weight later in the season. For now, though, Thomas will have to keep admiring Irving from afar on film.

title: Bucs Coach Named Potential Candidate for Glenn Schumann's FSU Staff
full_text:
The state of Florida has an illustrious history when it comes to the game of football.
The Miami Dolphins and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers each have two Lombardi Trophies, and the likes of the big three college teams — Florida State, Florida and Miami — have plenty of National Championships of their own.
However, the Seminoles of Florida State have struggled lately, ultimately leading to the firing of Mike Norvell and the hiring of Glenn Schumann as the next head coach.
With Schumann's hiring, he will be putting together a staff, and one Buccaneers' coach is being tabbed as a potential hire.
"McClendon has a vast background coaching receivers, working at Georgia, South Carolina, and Oregon, prior to leaping to the NFL in 2024. He was the wide receivers coach and pass-game coordinator for the Bulldogs in 2022-23, spending two seasons alongside Schumann," OnSI's Dustin Lewis wrote .
"The Buccaneers could make a coaching change, with the franchise on pace to miss the postseason for the second straight year. If so, McClendon will be looking for a new job. FSU would probably have to throw a co-OC title, at a minimum, to lure him back to college."
As mentioned by Lewis, McClendon came into the Bucs' organization in 2024, becoming a part of one of the most lucrative offenses in recent team memory under Liam Coen.
McClendon has become known as a player-first, no-ego coach who has blended young talent with veteran presence since his arrival in Tampa Bay.
Despite a lack of experience at the NFL level, McClendon is highly regarded in NFL and collegiate circles, and he has been challenged throughout his NFL tenure by a lack of consistency from players missing time due to injury.
Even though McClendon has done a fantastic job during his short time with the Bucs, things have taken a nosedive for his unit in 2026 following the departure of Mike Evans and the lack of development from players like Emeka Egbuka.
Depending on how the rest of the season pans out for Tampa Bay, McClendon could see this as an opportunity to head back to the college ranks and join coach Schumann in Tallahassee.
If McClendon were to leave and head to Florida State this offseason, it would set him up as a prime candidate to receive a promotion to offensive coordinator in the future.
As for the impact on the Bucs, it would be a shot to a group that has seen success under McClendon and leave them searching for a replacement on top of a likely change at offensive coordinator of their own.

title: Positive Signs Emerge at Buccaneers’ Wednesday Practice
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are still trying to win the NFC South and make the playoffs. But for all intents and purposes, their Week 12 game on Monday Night Football is a playoff game already.
The Bucs face off against the Carolina Panthers on Monday Night Football. The Panthers have a two-game lead in the division at 5-5, while the Bucs sit at 3-7. If the Bucs beat the Panthers, they sweep Carolina and move within one game of the division — lose, and their playoff chances are almost certainly over three games back.
The Bucs will need everyone they can muster to help win that game. And the good news is that they could have some crucial players for that contest.
Cornerback Jacob Parrish was back at practice on Wednesday after leaving the game with a back injury on Sunday. Parrish was replaced by Benjamin Morrison, who was also injured in that game — Morrison was not at practice, but Parrish was.
Parrish has been one of the best corners in football this season, netting 14 passes defended and two interceptions so far this year. He's a crucial part of the defense, so having him will be important.
Perhaps the bigger story, however, is that wideout Jalen McMillan began his 21-day practice window. McMillan injured his knee in the preseason and had a procedure to rectify it, but he re-injured that knee during Tampa Bay's Week 2 game against the Cleveland Browns. He's been out since then, but now, he could return as soon as Monday.
McMillan isn't guaranteed to be back. But if he is, he'd be very valuable — Tampa Bay's wide receiver corps has been very lackluster so far this season. McMillan has been strong against man coverage and is a good separator when he plays, so the Bucs could really use his skill set as soon as possible.
The Bucs will play the Panthers at 8:15 p.m. on Monday. Whether or not Parrish or McMillan plays remains to be seen, but it's very encouraging to see them at practice.

title: Todd Bowles Says Buccaneers Are 'Running Out of Time'
full_text:
It might appear that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 2026 season is a loss when you look at their 3-7 record, but they are still in the playoff mix as they sit just two games back of the NFC South lead with an all-important prime time matchup against the Carolina Panthers on deck.
There have been positives and negatives to take away from how the Bucs have performed this season, but head coach Todd Bowles doesn't believe that it's one thing — or even a couple — that is keeping this team from having a better record through 10 games.
“It’s few more than one or two things, but you know, the effort is not even a question,” Bowles said on Movin’ The Chains on SiriusXM NFL Radio . “The guys’ gonna fight every week. It’s just about cleaning up the little things and it’s the guy here or there and, you know, we’re running out of time... You know, you gotta correct those things.”
Bowles isn't wrong in his statement. The players have been fighting their tail off, but it has come to no avail.
However, it is worrisome that even Bowles is noticing that the Bucs haven't been able to take care of the little things, given the point of the season we are in.
But one thing is for sure — the Bucs are running out of time, and they must have a fire lit under them to finish the season strong if they hope to make the postseason.
Being just two games out of first place in the division should be motivation enough to go out there and get it right. On top of that, Tampa Bay has one of the easiest schedules remaining, with games against the Panthers, the Los Angeles Rams, the Los Angeles Chargers, the New Orleans Saints and the Atlanta Falcons, who have a combined winning percentage of just .333.
Things are lining up for the Bucs to win the majority of their remaining games, but they must make sure everything is buttoned up in order to do so.
They will have to battle injuries and somehow figure out how to improve their passing game if they hope to rip off a winning streak.
There is minimal room for error for this Bucs team, but they clearly are better than their record shows. If they want to hush the doubters and turn things around, they will need to get the little things right the rest of the way.

title: This Buccaneers Rookie is Turning Heads in 2026
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers defense has been the strong suit of the team this season, the opposite of what we thought heading into the season.
The likes of Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish have been the big players on defense, but as a whole, the unit has exceeded expectations, becoming one of the top defenses in the league through the midway point of the season.
One player in particular has taken the bull by the horns — rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter.
Trotter has gone vastly unnoticed in his rookie season, mainly due to the Bucs underwhelming on the season. However, he is now starting to get the attention he rightfully deserves.
NFL analyst Ben Fennell took to X to point out how well Trotter has been playing and highlighting his natural instincts, particularly against the run.
Bucs Josiah Trotter is one of the most gifted rookie LBs I've ever seen/studied. 21 years old lol Dude has an insanely quick/confident trigger on his run reads... but isn't ever out of control - feels run action so so well. pic.twitter.com/ueuA95kTmj
Fennell's post made it's way around the web, and led to others chiming in on Trotter.
"Bucs are so bad he probably isn’t getting the attention he deserves, but he’s right up there behind Reese for DROY runner up imo," NFL analyst Jon Ledyard posted .
CBS Sports' JP Acosta also chimed in — "Real ones knew."
There were worries about Trotter's game when he was selected in the NFL Draft by the Bucs, but he has since quelled all worries since taking over as a full-time starter for the defense.
Trotter has been one of the best linebackers in the league against the run and has also shown great promise as a blitzer, creating pressure in the backfield. He has also improved drastically from his collegiate days when it comes to securing tackles, only being knocked for six missed tackles on the season.
He is also the only rookie defender to have a pick-six.
All signs point towards Trotter having a great career in the NFL with how he has performed so far, but he will have to improve in certain areas, most notably when it comes to coverage in space.
Trotter has been performing well up to the levels of Arvell Reese and Jacob Rodriguez, with Sonny Styles and Anthony Hill Jr. also performing above expectations early in their careers.
The 2025 linebacker class is looking like one of the best in quite some time, and for Trotter to be a part of that means the Bucs have a good one for years to come.

title: This Stat is a Huge Reason Why Baker Mayfield Has Been Struggling
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' offense has struggled all year. The run game has been a success, but the passing game is among the league's worst and has hurt Tampa Bay week in and week out.
There are a lot of reasons why the offense is struggling. The play calling has been lackluster from offensive coordinator Zac Robinson, and the lack of talent in the wide receiving corps has made facilitating the passing game quite difficult. A big part of the equation, however, is quarterback Baker Mayfield.
Mayfield — whom the Bucs extended on a three-year, $55 million per year deal this offseason — has played very poor football dating back to the latter half of 2025. There are plenty of reasons for that, with injuries and decision-making being key factors, but there's another huge reason why he's struggled this year.
When Mayfield gets pressured by opposing defenses, he tends to get sacked. And that kills Tampa Bay's offense.
Sacks are not solely the fault of the offensive line. They certainly play a role, but sacks are just as much a quarterback stat as they are an offensive line stat — maybe even more so.
If the quarterback gets the ball out in good rhythm, he will naturally avoid sacks. That includes throwing it to receivers and throwing the football away, and obviously, it also accounts for mobility in the pocket and shedding rushers. Sacks are incredible swings in the defense's favor — the more a quarterback can avoid them of his own volition, the better the entire offense is.
Pressure-to-sack ratio, then, asks how often a quarterback is sacked when he is pressured. Good quarterbacks avoid getting sacked when pressured, either by getting the ball out or evading the defender. It's an important stat to gauge how long a quarterback holds the ball and how often he is costing the offense by going down.
Baker Mayfield, historically, is very, very bad at this. This year, he's 34th of 34 quarterbacks in pressure-to-sack ratio, getting sacked on 22 of his 80 pressured dropbacks, per SumerSports (27.5%). His best year since 2022 was 2025, when his 15.5% was ranked 16th of 45, but in that same time span, he's had seasons ranked 42nd of 46 (2024, 23.5%) and 44th of 47 (2022, 26.7%).
If you look cumulatively since 2022, he's ranked 63rd of 88 among quarterbacks with at least 100 dropbacks (20.5%). If you narrow that further and only go from quarterbacks with a comparable number of dropbacks to Mayfield — within 25% either way of his 2,509 dropbacks since 2022 — he's dead last, 19th of 19 quarterbacks.
This problem has plagued Mayfield his entire career. It's a big reason why he's been able to excel with strong coordinators, but when he's dealing with worse situations in coaching and the team's wide-receiving talent, he's unable to elevate the offense by himself as a player.
Perhaps the worst part of this equation is that Mayfield is 31 years old and is playing in his ninth NFL season. This aspect of the game gets less and less fixable every year he's in the league — this is simply who he is, and it's a major negative aspect of his game that anyone starting him has to deal with.
Right now, that team is the Bucs. They committed to Mayfield before the offseason with a three-year, $55 million extension, and after a better year on this front last year, he's regressed back to his usual ways.
Mayfield is currently dealing with a foot injury, which makes his mobility tougher than it would be when healthy. He moved around well in Detroit, but he still took a few sacks, including a strip sack and a crucial sack on fourth-and-12 to essentially end the game.
The Bucs play the Panthers on Monday night at 8:15. Mayfield will have to find ways to avoid going to the ground, because if he doesn't, this passing offense will continue to suffer.

title: Buccaneers Could Be in Serious Trouble After Two Players Need MRIs
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers play arguably the most important game of the season on Monday night when they face off against the Carolina Panthers — a win keeps them alive in the NFC South, and a loss almost certainly ends their season.
Bad news for the Bucs? They might have a very, very thin secondary for that matchup.
Defensive back Jacob Parrish left the Detroit game early with a back injury, and he was replaced by cornerback Benjamin Morrison. Morrison gave up two touchdowns during the game, but he also injured his hamstring and had to leave as well.
Head coach Todd Bowles gave an update on both players on Monday, and it seems the injuries are at least worrisome enough that they need to get second looks.
Bowles confirmed on Monday that both Parrish and Morrison are getting MRIs to gauge the severity of their injuries.
"They're both getting MRIs today, so we'll have a better update later this afternoon," Bowles said.
The results of those MRIs won't be known until Wednesday, but the Bucs will have been hoping to get some good news. Parrish has been one of the best cornerbacks in football this year, and while Morrison struggled against Detroit, he provides good depth for the team in case of an emergency and has played well in spurts prior to that game this year.
So who's next if both aren't healthy? It's Kevin Knowles, who was brought in this offseason to play special teams. Behind him will have to be either Ayden Garnes, an undrafted free agent who made the team this offseason, or Josh Hayes, a veteran Bucs player who is still on injured reserve and in the middle of his 21-day practice window.
Either way, losing just one of Parrish or Morrison would be unfortunate, given the importance of the Panthers game next Monday. Parrish is the crucial player, though, so it will be interesting to see if he practices on Wednesday ahead of the Monday matchup.
The Bucs play the Panthers at 8:15 on Monday Night Football.

title: Buccaneers Play Most Important Game of Their Season Next Week
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are no strangers to pressure or to the prime-time lights. They've won their division close in a few of Todd Bowles' seasons as head coach, and they've had to play in prime time plenty.
On Monday, they'll face both. The Bucs play the division-leading Carolina Panthers at home on Monday Night Football, and it comes after Bowles and the Bucs lost their Week 11 game against the Detroit Lions to fall to 3-7 on the year.
The game is not just important. It's arguably the most important game the Bucs will play all year, and that's something the coaching staff knows as well.
With the Atlanta Falcons' bye week, the NFC South is now all caught up on games played. And after winning two games in a row, the Carolina Panther are two games out from the entire rest of the field.
Simply put, this game against the Panthers is the singular most-important game the Bucs will have all year. A win puts Tampa Bay within one game of the NFC South lead and gives them the ultimate tiebreaker over the Panthers — if Tampa Bay can keep it close for the rest of the year, they'll hold the match point over Carolina at season's end.
Lose, though? The Panthers will be three games out from Tampa Bay, and the two will have split the series, eliminating that tiebreaker for the Bucs. If the Panthers emerge victorious on Monday Night Football, Tampa Bay's season is as good as over at 3-8.
The Bucs know that. Bowles said as much on Monday.
"Yeah, [the players are] aware of it. They understand," Bowles said. "They know where we stand. It starts with us in this room, so we've got to correct everything and turn that thing around. We've got to do it a game at a time."
The Bucs' entire playoff hopes hinge on this game. And if Tampa Bay doesn't win it, any hope Bowles has of retaining his job as head coach is probably gone, too, so he'll really be looking to win this game on Monday night.
Things went well for the Bucs last time they played Carolina on the road. Will it be the case at home? If Tampa Bay wants to stay alive, it simply must be.

title: Titans Injury Update vs. Jaguars Makes Bad Defensive Outlook Even Worse
full_text:
It's no secret that the Tennessee Titans' secondary has been the team's most disappointing aspect this season. Not only is that specific group losing the team games, but it also just so happens to be the one that Tennessee invested millions of their league-high cap space in this past offseason.
The Titans are in over $100 million deep between CBs Alontae Taylor, Joshua Williams, and Cor'Dale Flott, and now the latter of that trio (and arguably the best) will miss the team's Week 12 rematch with the Jacksonville Jaguars. S Terrell Burgess is also out for the contest.
Flott exited the Titans' Week 11 loss to the Dallas Cowboys with a neck injury, and Burgess with a knee issue. Those absences, combined with a few other limiting circumstances, led to Dallas hanging 51 points on Tennessee's defense - the most the Titans have allowed all year.
Week 12 was already situated as an uphill battle for the Titans. It's on the road against the best team in their division; the same team that handily beat Tennessee two weeks ago in Nashville. With this injury update, a bad thing only get worse for Robert Saleh's team.
In place of Flott and Burgess, the Titans will look to the remaining Taylor, as well as reserves Micah Robinson and Isaiah Oliver for relief. Taylor has been moved to nickel as of late due to his struggles on the outside, and Robinson playing behind Flott says everything about his potential as a starter.
It's a tough break for a team that has allowed 40+ points for three straight games now, threatening the worst kind of franchise history if the Jaguars cross that mark this coming Sunday.
The only potential grace Tennessee's secondary will see against the Jaguars is that QB Trevor Lawrence will be without his premier receiver, Parker Washington. Per Adam Schefter, Washington suffered a shoulder injury in practice yesterday.
Washington leveled the Titans in Week 10 for 7 receptions, 152 yards, and one touchdown. He was by far Jacksonville's most unstoppable weapon, and a notable reason that game got out of control in the second half.
That is to say, it's not a complete loss for a defensive position group that needs all the help it can get. Look for recently-picked-up CBs Derrick Canteen and Corey Thronton to try and help pick up the slack against a 7-3 Jaguars offense playing with a vengeance after their defeat last week.

title: How 1 Terrible Stat Proves Titans' Defensive Problems Go Much Deeper Than Robert Saleh
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans' defense is historically bad right now. That's a literal statement; if the Titans allow more than 40 points in Week 12 to the Jacksonville Jaguars (the same team that scored 40 on them two games ago), they'll have done so for four straight opponents.
That would be the first time in franchise history that Tennessee has given up 40+ points in four consecutive contests. You don't have to look much further than that to see that things are flying in the wrong direction on that side of the ball. Things only get complicated when weighing who to blame.
The natural inclination is always to point the finger at the head coach, especially when he's calling the defensive plays. But it isn't that easy for Tennessee. In fact, I'd argue that it's far too early to be blaming Saleh for much of anything that he inherited.
One number posted by PFF tells the whole story. Over the last three seasons, the Titans have allowed 1228 points to opponents. That's good for second most in the NFL during that time, and by a cushy 35-point margin.
The Cowboys defense has had a tough time pic.twitter.com/WcJSwEVB1E
Tennessee's defense has been bad, and that was part of the reason Saleh made for an appealing hire in the first place.
I'll be the first to admit that the first batch of free agents brought in after Saleh's hiring aren't panning out. CBs Alontae Taylor, Cor'Dale Flott, and Joshua Williams have formed one of the worst collective units in football. Saleh doesn't have unending slack in Nashville.
However, this number reflects just how broken the Titans were as a franchise before he came on. It's also no coincidence that the three-year period goes back to when Brian Callahan was hired in 2024. The quick-pull Vrabel firing giving way to Callahan coming on was a brutal one-two punch.
It's a punch that the Titans have yet to recover from. On top of two regime changes in rapid succession, Tennessee traded away both DT Jeffery Simmons and S Amani Hooker this season. It's clear that those moves were a means to fully rebuild in the draft.
We just have to let Tennessee get there. General manager Mike Borgonzi didn't bring Saleh in to drive the boat only to weight his drafts with offensive picks and smoke his coach out of the job. Titans fans can expect a stronger defensive lean in 2027 as this group looks to recover.
Let's take a look back at Saleh's first season with the New York Jets. In 2021, the Jets' defense allowed 29.6 points per game and 504 points in total; both were good for the worst in the league.
Fast forward to the very next season? The Jets skyrocketed all the way up to fourth in both categories, with the metrics falling to 18.6 and 316, respectively. New York finished 12th the following year; not quite as strong as fourth, but much better than 32nd.
What does all this mean? Well, beyond calls for patience regarding Saleh's process as this team's leader, it means the Titans need a knockout draft next spring. We'll see where things go on that front. For now, it may be a comfort to know it was always going to take a while to turn this defense around.

title: 2 Keys to Titans' First Win in Jacksonville in a Half-Decade: WR Duo Must Dominate a Great Defense
full_text:
On paper, the Jacksonville Jaguars are the kind of team that have an advantage in every category above most of the league. Good, competitive teams don't fare well against the Jaguars; you can imagine where that puts the Tennessee Titans heading into Week 12.
The outlook is bleak, and that's putting it lightly. Tennessee already fell to Jacksonville by three scores at home in Week 10, and now, the Titans are again forced to face their division rival in a place that they haven't won in October of 2021.
Derrick Henry was still a Titan then. It's been a long, long time.
Still, we're not here to sound the alarm the day after Thanksgiving. Titans fans know exactly what this matchup is. Instead, we're here to provide two keys to a potential upset victory. It all starts with a rising WR duo tasked with making waves vs. one of the NFL's best defenses.
Per TeamRankings, the Jaguars' defense sits at third in opponent's points per game (16.7) and touchdowns per game (1.7). The Jags' pass defense is slightly weaker than their run-stopping, with Jacksonville's 221.5 average passing yards allowed sitting at a middling 15th in the league.
That's where Carnell Tate and Chimere Dike, spearheaded by Cam Ward's generally trustworthy precision, under center. Dike led the Titans in receiving in Week 11 vs. the Dallas Cowboys, hauling in six receptions for 69 yards. He's led the unit two out of the last three games.
Tate, in his return from a two-week absence, scored an improbable 59-yard touchdown. That was one of two catches in the comeback for Tennessee's WR1. Having gone without Tate and Dike not yet seeing an jump in touches the last time these two teams met, Tennessee has a new hope in the duo.
They'll need to take advantage of the only semi-weakness in DC Anthony Campanile's defense.
QB Trevor Lawrence lit the Titans up on their home field two games ago. He threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns, only turning the ball over once due to a tipped pass. Tennessee will need a lot more than a tipped INT to get Lawrence where they want him in Week 12.
Robert Saleh's maligned defense has to find a way to pressure Lawrence this time around, and turnovers can't be exclusively left to LB Cedric Gray's elite awareness. It doesn't help that Tennessee only managed one sack back in Week 10.
Compare that to Jacksonville's Week 11 loss to the New York Giants, where Lawrence was sacked three times and picked off twice. The Jaguars scored just 18 points in the defeat.
The Giants have a much better defense than Tennessee (evidenced by them holding the Titans to a season-low seven points in Week 3), so the comparison only goes so far. But the formula for beating Lawrence comes down to forcing him to take mistakes.
Tennessee has the worst pressure rate in the NFL. That will have to give to some extent for the Titans to have a chance at a favorable outcome on Sunday.
