title: Robert Saleh Must Push Every Button to Avoid Making Awful Titans History in Week 12
full_text:
Over the past three games, the Tennessee Titans have allowed an average of 42 points to opponents. Of course, all three contests ended in a loss for Tennessee, the most recent of which saw Robert Saleh's defense give up 51 points to the Dallas Cowboys in a road embarrassment.
The Titans hadn't allowed 40+ points in three consecutive games since 2004. If you think that's bad, take this one in: Tennessee has never in franchise history given up 40+ points in four straight contests. All signs point to that streak being broken in Week 12.
Tennessee is set to rematch with Jacksonville after the Jaguars handed them a 40-23 loss in Week 10. QB Trevor Lawrence threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns in a game that, while at times close, was never really in question. The Jaguars have an iron grip on the AFC South at 7-3.
i'm not trying to be a pessimist here; in my own prediction for the incoming duel, I have Tennessee holding Jacksonville to 38 points. In a loss, sure, but that's a positive beat for the defense.
But it's necessary to point out that the Jaguars are entering this matchup with the perfect mix to break 40 anyway. For starters, they did so just two weeks ago, and now the Titans could be without CB Cor'Dale Flott after he injured his neck in Week 11.
If every game for the 1-9 Titans is a trial run for what could be, the Jaguars are in the opposite position. This is a team that went all out at the trade deadline, adding multiple defensive juggernauts, to try and make a run in the present.
This is a team that had scored 40+ points in two of their last three games before putting up an 18-point dud in a loss to the New York Giants. Lawrence has a whopping 22 TDs on the year up to now.
For Coach Saleh, this means flipping all the switches to make sure that his defense doesn't get destroyed again in front of a jolly crowd on the road. Yesterday, Saleh said that in trying to make his defense simpler to up the speed against Dallas, it actually slowed them down.
This is the same way that went on to call the defense "dog----" following their defeat. The wheels have long flown off and left the Titans' defense stranded on the side of the road. Nobody is coming to save them, not last-second signings nor the guy driving the car in the first place.
I don't know what a solution looks like at this point that isn't outright tearing down and rebuilding the defense, starting in the secondary. But I can tell you that a defensive HC making this sort of history in his first season is about as bad as it gets.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: The 3 Trends I'm Watching Most in Titans' Week 12 Rematch vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans will face the Jacksonville Jaguars for the second time in three weeks, and if recent history is any indication, it could be another long afternoon.
The Titans have lost five straight games against the Jaguars, the last three of which have come by an average of 24 points. A rivalry that was once dominated by the Titans has suffered a complete 180 over the last few years.
Despite the Titans’ slim chances, there’s still plenty of intriguing storylines to watch in this one. Here are the three biggest that I'll be keeping an eye on in Week 12.
Over the last three weeks, the Titans have given up 40+ points per game. To make matters worse, things appear to be going in the wrong direction.
They allowed 36 against the Bengals and then followed it up by giving up 40 against the Jaguars one week later. Then, Things completely fell apart last Sunday in Dallas after they gave up a whopping 51 points in a game they somehow lost by three touchdowns despite their own offense scoring 30.
It’s becoming clear that regardless of what this offense does, they won’t be able to overcome this type of defensive ineptitude. Everyone knew there would be a drop-off once they traded away DT Jeffery Simmons and S Amani Hooker, but I don’t think even the most pessimistic fan could envision it falling apart like this.
It’s gotten so bad that there are even growing concerns that HC Robert Saleh could be on the hot seat if things don't improve sooner rather than later.
Nobody is expecting the Titans to suddenly start reeling off a bunch of wins, but this defense led by Saleh has to start being more competitive than what they’ve been lately. Unfortunately, those calls for a replacement will only continue to get louder if the Jaguars show up and drop another 40+ points in a lopsided loss.
For everybody’s sake, let’s hope that’s not the case.
Over the last three weeks, QB Cam Ward has accounted for 866 yards (783 passing, 83 rushing), six passing touchdowns, one rushing touchdown, and one interception, all while completing nearly 70 percent of his passes.
Ward has thrown for at least 230 yards and two touchdowns in each of those three games. However, all of that is for naught when the team is constantly playing from behind at the rate they are. Ward certainly isn’t blameless for the 1-9 record, but he’s also far from the biggest problem right now.
In fact, he’s one of the few players fans genuinely feel optimistic about going forward. But all of that can change at a moment’s instance if Ward resorts back to the lackluster performances we saw earlier this season.
I don’t expect that, but another tall task awaits him on Sunday where he’ll have to go prove it. In their meeting a couple of weeks ago, the Jaguars had barely acquired DT Jordan Davis and S Jessie Bates, so they were inactive during the Week 10 contest.
That won’t be the case on Sunday, so Ward has to be ready to face an even stronger version of the defense he played back on November 15th. Will Ward start to regress, or will he have another solid individual performance for the fourth straight week? We’ll find out on Sunday.
There’s a realistic chance that the Titans could be down three starting offensive linemen on Sunday. LG Peter Skoronski is on injured reserve, while rookie RG Fernando Carmona is trying to return from IR.
Sadly, Saleh insinuated that Carmona likely won’t be ready this week, so it’ll be RG Atonio Mafi once more in all likelihood.
But the growing concern is at LT where Dan Moore Jr. isn’t practicing on Wednesday due to a knee injury he suffered last Sunday. Moore hasn’t been stout by any means, but he’s at least an average-caliber tackle that gives this offense a chance to function properly.
If he’s out on Sunday, the entire left side of the offensive line will be revamped, and that could lead to some major issues offensively. If Moore is unable to go, look for James Hudson III to get the start.
Shaun is a longtime Titans fan who has years of experience in the field. He missed being on the team beat, and is here to change that. He also writes scripts for EA Sports' Madden games, where fans may have heard his work.

title: Could Titans Draft Their RB of the Future With a Second-Round Steal in 2027?
full_text:
In the 2026 NFL Draft, the Titans took LB Anthony Hill Jr. in the second round. Hill came onto the scene as a promising defensive prospect from the jump, but it took no time at all for him to blossom into a bonafide defensive star. He's Tennessee's tackle leader, and already looks like a long-term stud.
I'm here today to posit a scenario where the Titans repeat that second-round luck in 2027, but on the opposite side of the ball. With one of their two second-rounders, Tennessee should be kicking the tires on Boise State RB Dylan Riley.
The Broncos' Ashton Jeanty replacement has quietly had an elite season as a junior. The springy, multi-tool weapon is being overshadowed by other players at his position, but if anything, that would allow the Titans to steal an already underrated prospect off the board.
For Tennessee to end up with one of Jadan Baugh or Kewan Lacy, the two top RBs in 2027, they'd likely have to consider burning their later first-round pick. With as many defensive needs as the Titans have, as well as the near-guarantee of taking WR Jeremiah Smith at first overall if Tennessee keeps that pick, loading up with an RB that early doesn't seem feasible.
The door is wide open, however, in the second round. That's right where Riley falls. The Boise State back comes in at 42nd on ESPN's 2027 big board, and Bleacher Report even has him slated as their RB2 in the class.
Naturally, competing in the Pac 12 (the new one, at that) means Riley isn't facing SEC-caliber defenses on a weekly basis. But Riley has strengths that should translate to the NFL, and the Titans should have him circled as a quality succession plan for Tony Pollard for that reason.
At 5-foot-10, 192 lbs, Riley's game is all about his quickness and ability to make defenders miss. He's got a varied move-set (including a hurdle, pictured above) and the ability to explode through gaps and footrace opponents to the end zone .
This season, Riley has 213 carries for 1,360 yards (sixth in the nation). That's 6.4 yards per carry to go along with his 11 rushing touchdowns. Riley also has 25 receptions for 317 yards and two extra scores.
Riley's skillset has prepared him for the jump to the NFL, and for Tennessee, you couldn't ask for a more compelling pick past the first round. If Pollard and Spears both go in free agency, the RB1 role will likely fall on the shoulders of a rookie.
Given the team's needs and general offensive makeup, I believe Dylan Riley has a great case to be that rookie.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: 4 Things the Titans Should Be Thankful For This Thanksgiving — No Current Player Takes the Top Spot
full_text:
If you're reading this before you chow down on some Thanksgiving turkey with friends and family, don't let your favorite 1-9 football team bog down the holiday spirit today. There's always something to be thankful for, even with the Tennessee Titans.
In fact, if you look at things the right way, there's a lot to smile about in Nashville. Maybe not a full, toothy smile, but a corner-mouth grin. A smile is a smile all the same.
Here's my ranking of four things the Titans should be thankful for this Thanksgiving, upcoming divisional brawl and all.
If you can't find much to be happy about right now, look to the horizon. The Titans have an absurdly exciting draft outlook over the next two seasons.
The team's deadline trades hampered their current efforts, but the Titans now have two first-round and second-round picks in 2027 and 2028. Not only that, but Tennessee currently holds the first overall pick next spring, which would likely yield generational WR Jeremiah Smith.
Rookies and second-year players make up the beating heart of this Titans team. Youth is the name of the game in Nashville right now, and that will only become more true in the years to come.
Cam Ward might not take the top spot, but Tennessee should be thrilled with their QB's recent development.
Over the past three weeks of football, Ward has thrown just one interception to six touchdowns. He's performing well in an offense progressively suited to his strengths and just returned rookie sensation Carnell Tate to the lineup - more on Tate later.
Ward has safely moved into the middle of the pack of NFL signal callers, and is still steadily climbing. He's not perfect, but questions about his potential benching have been long forgotten. For now, at least, the Titans don't have a question under center.
That's worth a plate of celebratory seconds.
In the same vein as Ward's success, Tennessee should be singing the praises of their turn to the no-huddle offense today.
Brian Daboll's move to this system in Week 8 (when the Titans eclipsed 40% usage for the first time this season) directly coincided with the offense's first 30+ point game of the year. Per Sharp Football Analysis, the Titans' no-huddle rate on the year is up to 25.3%.
That's comfortably the highest in the NFL. If it ain't broke don't fix it, especially not after it was broken for the first five games of the season. Daboll has found a balance, and he should keep feeding it throughout the rest of this year.
Finally, I'd be remiss not to mention Tennessee's mostly outstanding rookie class. EDGE Keldric Faulk looks to be an unfortunate exception, but today is not the day to pick that wound.
The aforementioned Tate, as well as LB Anthony Hill Jr., each secured rookie of the month honors from the NFL this season. RG Fernando Carmona Jr., before being sent to IR after Week 3, came in as a surprise starter on the offensive line.
No draft is flawless, but general manager Mike Borgonzi reeled in multiple quality rookies this past spring. Between these guys and the draft picks the Titans have, it may be the truth that no team in the league has as much promise on this front as Tennessee.
What isn't exciting now can be exciting later. Borgonzi has the tools to get this franchise out of the mud as early as next season. To the Titans fans that celebrate: Have a happy Thanksgiving, and don't be afraid to revel in what this team could become with a few more well-picked rookies.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: 3 Titans Developments Fans Should be Watching Weekly as 2026 Season Winds Down
full_text:
Over the offseason, Tennessee Titans' GM Mike Borgonzi introduced Robert Saleh as the franchise's next head coach and approached free agency aggressively, spending more than $265 million with hopes of dawning a success era in Nashville. They even debuted new threads with the color palette paying homage to their predecessor, the Houston Oilers, with a modern twist ahead of their final season in Nissan Stadium.
However, the Titans find themselves sitting at the bottom of the NFL standings at a 1-9 record, in the same spot they were last season only weeks after firing their head coach, Brian Callahan.
Tennessee has underperformed beyond the expectations of pundits, fans, and the coaching staff in what has been one of the most challenging seasons in franchise history. “These last couple of weeks, I'm not gonna try to sugarcoat anything," Saleh said to the media this week . "It's been dog----."
There's little to be optimistic about for Titans' fans. Nonetheless, there are still eight games remaining on the schedule that will impact the future of the franchise. While Tennessee may not win another game for the remainder of the season, here are three developments every Titans fan should keep an eye on.
The Titans are currently in possession of the No. 1 pick in the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft.
Unlike other professional sports leagues that use a lottery system to determine draft order, the NFL assigns the top pick to the team with the fewest wins. Tennessee edges out fellow one-win teams, the Los Angeles Chargers and the Miami Dolphins, due to the Titans facing a greater strength of schedule .
The Titans have an opportunity to secure the number one pick if they continue to lose. Later this season, the Chargers and Dolphins will face off, which could help Tennessee keep the top spot. Looking ahead at the Titans' schedule, they play Jacksonville, Washington, Detroit, Indianapolis, Las Vegas, Pittsburgh and Houston.
Each of the Titans' opponents are looking to win because they're either in the playoff picture or in the hunt. Even the lowly 3-8 Colts, because the Jets have ownership of their first-round pick.
Another important draft contingent for Tennessee is the Chicago Bears. The midseason Jeffery Simmons deal included a first-round draft pick in 2027, which will likely be a late-round pick because the Bears have an 8-2 record.
However, the pick still has a chance to fall because the Bears play in the highly competitive NFC North, with every team having at least six wins. Chicago has one more game against each NFC North rival remaining on their schedule.
Following a loss to the Houston Texans 26-3 in Week 5, the buzz around QB Cam Ward peaked. At that game in Nissan Stadium, Titans' fans were holding up signs mocking the young quarterback. However, Ward has helped turn Tennessee into the sixth-highest scoring offense in the NFL since Week 8, according to StatMuse .
In the month of November, Ward has thrown for 783 yards, scored seven touchdowns and only one interception on an efficient 68.8% completion percentage across three games. For two of those games Ward was without his No. 1 target, WR Carnell Tate, and a game-and-a-half without WR Wan'Dale Robinson, the WR2.
Without a doubt, the second-year quarterback has been playing the best football of his pro career. Ward's improved play lifts pressure off the shoulders of the Titans' front office.
Tennessee shouldn't spend a second- or third-day draft selection on a potential replacement or feel tempted to spark a desperate trade for an aging veteran. Instead, the front office should focus on improving a Tennessee defense that has allowed almost 45 points per game in the last three games.
Week-to-week Ward has been improving and finding a rhythm regardless of who's on the field for the Titans. In November, Ward's six touchdown throws have been to six different receivers. Titans' fans should be encouraged by Ward's recent uptick in production and have more optimism about their young quarterback heading into next season.
As previously mentioned, Ward has found six different receivers in the end zone this month; half of those targets are age 25 or younger. Robinson is 25, Tate is 23, and WR Chimere Dike is 24. Although he hasn't scored this month, WR Elic Ayomanor's 140 receiving yards is the second-highest number of receiving yards of any Titan in November. He's only 23 years old in his second season.
Tennessee's depth at receiver has been pivotal for Ward's development. The next-man-up mentality when Tate and Robinson have missed time with injuries has allowed Dike and Ayomanor a chance to prove themselves as reliable receivers.
Prior to his injury in Week 7 against Cleveland, Tate was the favorite to win AP Offensive Rookie of the Year. Still, despite missing two-and-a-half games this season, Tate is second in receiving yards and receiving touchdowns and fifth in receptions amongst all rookies this season, according to StatMuse .
Tate has the shot at becoming the first Titan to win the award since Vince Young in 2006. Currently, Tate has the third-best odds to win on DraftKings, only behind Broncos' RB Jonah Coleman and Raiders' QB Fernando Mendoza, per ESPN .
If the Titans lock in the top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, the front office will have an opportunity to add to Tennessee's offensive firepower by selecting the consensus No. 1 pick, Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith.
He's widely considered a generational talent. Smith is the most hyped receiver coming out of college since Calvin Johnson, who was selected No. 2 in 2007 by the Detroit Lions and later became a first-ballot Hall of Famer.
Whether or not Smith joins Tate and Ward in Nashville, there's already significant talent to build on in the future.
Isaiah is an award-winning journalist and photojournalist. A graduate from the University of Kentucky, he has previously been published by BloodHorse, KY Insider, and the Kentucky Kernel for multimedia sports coverage. Isaiah is a Tennessee Volunteer at heart bringing his local expertise to Titans coverage.

title: How 1 Underrated Signing is Redeeming Titans' Free Agency Pickups From 2026 Offseason
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans were one of the most active teams in NFL free agency this past offseason, as the team invested big money in premium positions, including wide receiver with Wan'Dale Robinson, defensive tackle with John Franklin-Myers, and cornerback with Alontae Taylor.
Robinson is on IR, Taylor has had perhaps the worst season of his career, and Myers was left virtually alone on the defensive line after the Jeffery Simmons trade. The outlook is bleak.
However, one signing that flew a bit under the radar was center Austin Schlottmann, whom the Titans signed to a two-year deal worth up to $9 million . Schlottmann began his career with the Denver Broncos, and also had two-year stints with the Minnesota Vikings and New York Giants.
Entering 2026, Tennessee was banking on Schlottmann providing serviceable center play and helping anchor the offensive line to an improved season. So far, he's done that and has been a bright spot on a unit that has endured its fair share of ups and downs.
Is Schlottmann an elite interior offensive lineman? No. But the veteran has quietly been a solid piece of the Titans' offensive line and is making the case to be the starting center for another year.
Through 10 starts this season, Schlottmann has allowed just one sack and 12 quarterback pressures, earning a 64.3 Pro Football Focus pass-blocking grade . Though he is leaving a lot to be desired in the run game, posting a 53.2 run-blocking grade, Schlottmann is coming off his highest-graded game of the season against the Dallas Cowboys last week.
In Tennessee's 51-30 loss to Dallas on Sunday , Schlottmann surrendered one quarterback pressure, tallied an 80.3 PFF grade , including an 82.2 run-blocking mark, and didn't commit a penalty for the second straight contest. The 31-year-old is making the Titans' decision to sign him to a cheap, low-risk contract a savvy move.
Even after signing Schlottmann in March, the Titans selected Pat Coogan in the sixth round of April's draft, likely with plans to eventually hand the Indiana product the starting gig . However, if Schlottmann continues to be one of the more impactful contributors on Brian Daboll's offense, Tennessee will have to seriously consider naming him the 2027 starting center and keeping Coogan on the bench.
The Titans will look to capture their second win of the season this weekend at EverBank Stadium against the Jacksonville Jaguars. We'll see if Schlottmann can turn in another steady outing and help Tennessee get back in the win column after dropping two in a row coming out of the bye.
Dharya Sharma is a sportswriter from Nebraska who has been covering the Tennessee Titans through his website, SharmSports, since 2023. He is also an NFL and NBA writer for The Sporting News and had a previous stop with Sportsnaut. Follow him on X @SharmSports

title: Why Any Smoke Around Robert Saleh's Job is Way Too Premature for Titans
full_text:
Today, in reporting NFL head coaches potentially on the hot seat, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler mentioned Robert Saleh toward the end of his update. The Tennessee Titans head coach hasn't been mentioned in any sort of "could-be-fired" capacity, so his sudden drop here came as a surprise.
"Tennessee seems like one to watch because of the Titans' penchant for firings in recent years. I'm curious whether Tennessee breaks precedent and gives Robert Saleh time..." Fowler wrote. "The a 51-30 loss to Dallas prompted Saleh to call his defense "dogs---" in a news conference. I'm not sure where to go with that, but what I'm saying is Tennessee is usually a wild card based on recent history."
This appears to be nothing more than smoke on the surface, but Fowler's reptuation demands Titans fans at least give this one a look. It wasn't all that long ago that Brian Callahan was fired for producing just four wins in 23 games.
Saleh has one in 10. Could a one-season firing actually be in the cards?
Probably not. There are a number of reasons why Saleh's scenario is different than Callahan's; perhaps the most notable of which is that he didn't get his say at a QB. Cam Ward was drafted under a waning Callahan regime. So were WRs Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike, among others.
Not only that, but Callahan took a franchise that wasn't far removed from success under Mike Vrabel and lowered the bar to levels the team hadn't seen in years. Saleh inherited a far worse scenario than Callahan, and the early returns (despite the win column) are more promising.
Ward and the offense are developing at a rapid pace. Tennessee traded two key defenders for draft capital that could turn this team around in the matter of an offseason. Saleh also recently said he has "100% support" from Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk.
Take that for what it's worth, but two-year-or-less firing and hiring cycles don't get a team anywhere. The process has to be waited out at some point, and this feels like the perfect juncture for Tennessee.
A 1-16 finish would likely mean otherwise, but with the Colts, a post-Aaron Rodgers Steelers team, the Commanders, and the Raiders coming up, Tennessee is almost bound to get lucky a time or two.
Let's say Saleh finishes this season 3-14, just as Callahan did in his first year. Do you fire him when you didn't fire Callahan? Or do you let him see it through one more season, equipped with two first-round picks and a QB who is trending to have settled into his role by then.
The Titans' rebuild depends on those last two points, no matter who is steering the ship. With Ward getting better and GM Mike Borgonzi gearing up for his most important draft in the position, the whole process is simply bigger than Saleh.
Whether or not he's the solution is hard to tell, especially with this roster, but it's far too early to know if he's the problem. As of now, Titans fans should treat this season as a trial run for what Saleh could bring to the table in 2027.
Maybe we revisit this discussion then. Right now, however, there's no fire to the smoke.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Commanders’ Receivers Are Producing. What Can Brandon Aiyuk Add?
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers-to- Washington Commanders rebounding-receiver pipeline spat out yet another weapon to help support Jayden Daniels' thin pool of playmakers this season. Except unlike Deebo Samuel, the aging flex option who turned in passable, if unexciting, results as a one-and-done Commander last year, Washington's more recent acquisition stands out as a head-turner around the league.
Brandon Aiyuk has spent most of 2026 in the league's rumor mill, having yet to play an NFL snap in over two years. He shredded his knee against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7 of the 2024 campaign, just a few months removed from losing to that same team in Super Bowl LVIII, peppering the time since his last full season with a lengthy rehabilitation, a stint on San Francisco’s reserve/left squad list, and, most recently, his release.
The 28-year-old's self-imposed sentence to NFL purgatory bred too many Commanders rumors to count, given the team's need for receiving depth and the receiver's ties to Daniels from their days together at Arizona State University, but it seemed as if the franchise had momentarily decided against trading for the 49ers star once they elected to sign another controversial receiving name in Stefon Diggs shortly before the start of this season.
That was before Terry McLaurin sustained his own catastrophic leg injury , further depleting the receiving room. And with the Commanders surging to three wins in their last four matchups, this practice-squad signing gives Washington a chance to evaluate him without changing its game-day lineup yet.
The good news is that, given how well the admittedly skimpy assortment of receivers are playing, there's no pressing need for Aiyuk to immediately start if he earns a game-day role. Diggs, Antonio Williams , Treylon Burks , and Chig Okonkwo have done the job in aiding Daniels' downfield attack, but the hurting bench has given them absolutely nothing since their bye week (outside of the occasional Van Jefferson gem).
The front office and coaching staff are already trying to make sense of Aiyuk's strange context in balancing the lengthy time he's missed with the potential he can still offer. Offensive coordinator David Blough praised the receiver's speed and range, while General Manager Adam Peters reflected on how he held up during his Commanders workout earlier this week. Blough got more specific Thursday : the Commanders will be intentional about Aiyuk’s scout-team routes while he learns the offense, and the coordinator also singled out his downfield blocking. Antonio Williams played 57 of Washington’s 68 offensive snaps against Cincinnati , with Treylon Burks at 49 and Stefon Diggs at 45, so Aiyuk’s first task is earning work within a rotation that is already playing.
Commanders GM Adam Peters talking about the type of impact Brandon Aiyuk might make this season. Peters said, "anytime somebody hasn't played in two years you really have to temper the expectations...he looked really good. He looked like the guy that we knew." pic.twitter.com/7zl4nYqA3L
During Aiyuk's second-team All-Pro season in 2023, he ranked seventh in the NFL in total yards with 1,342 over 16 games, scoring seven touchdowns with some of the best hands in the game. He memorably flexed his 71.4% catch percentage during the regular season, then helped deliver the dagger to the Detroit Lions just under a year before his new team dealt the NFC power a blow.
Commanders WR Brandon Aiyuk pic.twitter.com/5XqwapbXGC
His 2023 production showed an elite wideout who could block and win with his routes. The question of whether he can hold up after missing a fair chunk of his mid-20s remains, and given the need for a high-end big-play wideout to complement the older Diggs, the rookie Williams, and regular contributors like Okonkwo and Burks, someone with the proven resume to produce alongside talented casts seems worth a shot in a vacuum.
Now, worries about how much the wily Aiyuk can be trusted won't go away as he enters his next stop, however long that may be. All of social media saw him directly challenge Daniels' leadership style while recording himself dancing in Commanders apparel over the last few months, and there's no guarantee that he'll get everything he wants, whatever that may be, during the 4-5-1 team's quest to top their slumping division.
Daniels, who's averaged over 279 all-purpose yards over outings he's started and finished, has plenty to gain, as do the receivers who could afford to slide down the depth chart . And with the scoring scheme lagging behind the more aggressive defense, maybe a wild-card spark with proven pedigree is what's required to push the Commanders through their easier scheduled stretch.
Follow us on Facebook for the latest Washington Commanders news, injury updates, analysis, and more from Commanders on SI.
Henry covers the Washington Wizards with prior experience as a sports reporter with The Baltimore Sun, The Capital Gazette, and The Lead. A Bowie, MD, native, he also handles On SI’s Wizards beat, extending his DMV coverage, and has earned his journalism degree from the University of Maryland.

title: Commanders News: Cowboys' Collapse Puts Washington Ahead With Fewer Wins | Burgundy Roundup
full_text:
A very unexpected but wonderful thing happened on Thanksgiving. While America was recovering from their afternoon meals, the Dallas Cowboys somehow lost a 31-10 lead to the Joe Milton-led Philadelphia Eagles. The 39-38 result marked the biggest comeback in the history of Thanksgiving Day games. Which might be the best line I write today. In the process, Dallas fell to 5-7 and moved into third place in the NFC East, while Washington moved into second at 4-5-1, ahead of the Cowboys by winning percentage. The Giants still lead the division by two games.
- The Commanders made Brandon Aiyuk's signing official Thursday, adding him and cornerback Ambry Thomas, a 2021 third-round pick by San Francisco, to the practice squad while releasing receiver Malik Heath. Aiyuk has no announced game role or return date . Thomas has appeared in 42 NFL games, starting 11, and gives Washington another option at corner if he is elevated from the practice squad. - Seeing Amik Robertson (ankle) on the injury report Thursday as a nonparticipant is a problem. All eyes will be on what he does on the practice field Friday. - Treylon Burks (foot) and Charles Omenihu (rib) were both limited Thursday. Jayden Daniels (left elbow/left hand), Rachaad White (heel), and Sonny Styles (ankle) participated fully. Stefon Diggs came off the report after being listed as a nonparticipant Wednesday for personal reasons. - The Arizona Cardinals are still trying to figure out who will take snaps under center in Week 12. Rookie quarterback Carson Beck did not practice for a second straight day Thursday. Josh Johnson is expected to get his second straight start if Beck cannot practice Friday. Johnson is a player Washington fans certainly are aware of, having spent two different stops in burgundy and gold in 2018 and 2025, appearing in nine games and starting five. - Arizona has questions along both lines, too. Right guard Jon Gaines II missed a second straight practice with an ankle injury, and Mike LaFleur indicated he is unlikely to play. On defense, Josh Sweat sat out Thursday with a shoulder issue and rest designation. That doesn't settle his status for Sunday. Safety Budda Baker and left guard Isaac Seumalo returned to full practice, while defensive lineman Zach Carter practiced fully but still needs to be activated from injured reserve before he can play. Friday's report should clear up which of those matchups Washington is actually getting. - Washington will also be the first team to face Arizona's defense with Teryl Austin calling the plays. The Cardinals fired Nick Rallis on Monday, and Austin said he will work from the sideline. He isn't promising to remake the defense in a week. “I'll try to prioritize a little bit of simplicity to try and give our guys some freedom,” Austin said Thursday . Daniels and David Blough will get their first look at what that means on Sunday. - Zaven Collins offered a little more to go on. He said some of the rules from Rallis’ defense have been dropped, giving Arizona’s edge rushers and defensive linemen more freedom. The Cardinals have also worked in some new plays and spent part of Wednesday’s practice on takeaway drills. Collins said the basic approach is “still see the ball, get the ball.” Washington can study the old defense, but it won't know exactly what Austin kept until the game starts. - Blough had more to say Thursday about Antonio Williams than just praising his big night against Cincinnati. He pointed to the work Williams and Daniels had already done on the throws that won the game, saying their connection had shown up in practice. “He has a natural knack for spaces and timing,” Blough said. Williams is going to keep getting chances to show it, with Burks still working through his foot injury and Aiyuk just beginning his time with the team. - Daronte Jones sees Washington’s defense getting quicker at a different part of the job: recognizing its assignments and talking through them together. That gives the players more time to deal with what the offense is showing them. title: Commanders Power Rankings Climb Again as National Writers Change Their Tune on Dan Quinn
full_text:
Each week during the regular season, we'll look at what the national media is saying about the Washington Commanders via various publications' NFL Power Polls. With it now being Week 12, Washington has suddenly given the national media something different to talk about. The Washington Commanders are suddenly doing something they struggled to do earlier this season. Win close games. Monday night's 22-20 win over the Cincinnati Bengals gave Washington consecutive wins for the first time since 2024, and apparently the national media is starting to take notice. All nine publications we track each week moved the Commanders up in their latest power rankings for the second straight week. Not bad for a team that was sitting at 2-5-1 just a few weeks ago. * Side note: Many have asked whether these polls are helpful, which is a fair question. One way to look at them is as a way to broaden your perspective on what others believe. Not to mention, sometimes it's fun to see the national media guys bump around in the dark, chasing their tails, clueless.

Now NFL.com's Nick Shook is talking about Quinn's seat cooling off, while FOX Sports' Ralph Vacchiano is giving the head coach credit for keeping this team fighting. Funny how winning a couple of games changes the conversation. Of course, Quinn certainly wasn't getting much help from his own decisions earlier in the season, but Washington deserves some credit for refusing to go away. Then there's WalterFootball, which now has the Commanders ranked No. 13, ahead of both the Giants and Cowboys. The site believes Washington is the most balanced team in the NFC East, which is quite a statement considering the Commanders are still two games behind New York. I'm not sure I'm ready to call Washington the division's best team, but watching Jayden Daniels deliver two straight game-winning drives certainly makes the argument a little more interesting. In new coordinator Daronte Jones' defense, Luvu plays inside and has been an effective blitzer. Perhaps even more importantly (from a morale-focused perspective), Dan Quinn’s seat has cooled after the last two outings. That’s a nice development for a franchise that could use some good news. Their defense did some number on Joe Burrow and that passing attack. They are now 3-2-1 in their last six, which keeps them within striking distance of the NFC East-leading Giants. Yeah, they’re two games back, but they own the tie-breaker. And they can make up a lot of ground over the next four weeks when they play the Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons. — Ralph Vacchiano Sports Illustrated had this to say (15th): Unbelievable. Gutsy. Freeing. A win against one of the best teams remaining on their schedule, in prime time, where they had to manage the clock and spike the ball with seconds to play. This is a poetic way for the season to completely hinge on a moment.   — Conor Orr
Yahoo Sports had this to say (18th): Jayden Daniels is still capable of looking like a superstar at quarterback. When the Commanders looked like they had lost to the Bengals on a field goal with 46 seconds left, Daniels hit two passes to rookie Antonio Williams for a total of 64 yards, which set up a game-winning field goal as time expired. They were two great throws from Daniels and a great job by Williams to get open. Daniels finished with 289 yards, 122 of which went to Williams. The Commanders remain two games behind the Giants in the NFC East. But Daniels and Williams kept the Commanders' season alive with two great plays in the final minute on Monday night. — Frank Schwab Pro Football Talk had this to say (17th) For the second time in three years, Jayden Daniels outdueled Joe Burrow in prime time. — Mike Florio The Athletic had this to say (19th) The Commanders quarterback played only seven games last year due to multiple injuries. Walter Football had this to say (13th) The Redskins are +430 to win the division on DraftKings in the wake of their win over the Bengals. That doesn't seem like a bad bet, considering that Washington is the most balanced team in the division. The Redskins have a better quarterback than the Giants do and a better defense than the Cowboys. They're not great anywhere, but they're at least not incompetent on either side of the ball.
Put all nine together, and the Commanders land at an average ranking of No. 17.2, up from last week's 20.1 and a considerable improvement from the No. 25.0 average just two weeks ago. Washington is now 4-5-1, with a trip to Arizona coming Sunday and a chance to finally get back to .500. The national media is starting to believe in this team again. title: Commanders Winners and Losers From Brandon Aiyuk’s Signing: The Biggest Loser Isn’t a Player
full_text:
The Washington Commanders officially signed Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad after Wednesday’s workout. Head coach Dan Quinn liked what he saw, but set no timetable for the former 49ers star receiver to return to action. It appears the staff will rightfully make Aiyuk earn a game-day role, which should be an interesting situation.
Jayden Daniels The player on the roster who knows Brandon Aiyuk best is Jayden Daniels. He's also the person who stands to gain the most from adding a competitor with Aiyuk's skill set. Daniels already knows how Aiyuk runs routes, and he compared renewing their chemistry to riding a bike, adding that he hasn't thrown him the ball in a long time. One thing to remember: familiarity from years before doesn't guarantee anything; that said, the two recently made up for whatever issues that arose during the offseason and are ready to focus on football. David Blough Washington's first-year offensive coordinator could add another weapon to the mix. One that has, in the past, had game-changing receiving abilities. Washington either lucked into a premier talent or took a small chance on a former All-Pro who doesn't end up working out. Currently, I'm hoping for the former and do believe that the stars are aligning for it to work. Against Cincinnati, Washington gained 428 yards , but converted only 2 of 10 on third downs and managed only one touchdown on four red-zone trips. The last of those trips was the game-winning kick with four seconds left, so that one went exactly as it should have. In Aiyuk’s last full season, 61 of 75 catches gained first downs; five of six receptions inside the opponent’s 20 scored touchdowns . Once he's ready, Aiyuk could expand Blough's options considerably. Antonio Williams Some may believe having another target like Aiyuk in the lineup takes away from the job rookie receiver Antonio Williams has been doing . I believe that's the wrong way to look at it, as having both in the same rotation will help Williams grow as a player. The team has already learned what he brings to the lineup this season, and there is no reason to hand that work to Aiyuk before he earns it. Stefon Diggs When Stefon Diggs signed with Washington, the plan was to line him up next to Terry McLaurin with the two dazzling fans as a one-two combo. Aiyuk could bring some of that possibility back if he can still play at that level. Diggs can work at Z or in the slot, leaving room for Aiyuk outside if he earns it.
Commanders GM Adam Peters talking about the type of impact Brandon Aiyuk might make this season. Peters said, "anytime somebody hasn't played in two years you really have to temper the expectations...he looked really good. He looked like the guy that we knew." pic.twitter.com/7zl4nYqA3L
Van Jefferson I've always viewed Van Jefferson's time with Washington as a security blanket behind a room of receivers who all hit from different angles. With several in that room out with injuries, Jefferson has found his way into games this season, but he played only 16 offensive snaps against Cincinnati. Those reps could come under pressure if Aiyuk eventually earns a game-day role. Treylon Burks Treylon Burks is in a different position from Jefferson. He played 49 snaps Monday and has earned a regular place outside. Aiyuk isn't taking that job today. Still, if Washington eventually decides Aiyuk is ready for a meaningful offensive role, some of those outside opportunities will have to come from somewhere. Burks now has another player to hold off, and his two catches for 30 yards against Cincinnati give him reason to keep making his own case. Malik Heath Here's one receiver who already has an answer. Washington signed Aiyuk and cornerback Ambry Thomas to the practice squad and released Malik Heath in the same roster update . Heath had joined the practice squad just a week earlier. Jefferson and Burks might lose work later; Heath lost his spot now. An Immediate WR Fix The elephant in the room is that Aiyuk will likely solve nothing while he gets back up to speed in practice and learns what the team needs from him. Quinn said he has no target date. He wants to see routes and combinations in practice, beyond what Wednesday’s workout showed. Aiyuk can't help Washington finish drives from the practice squad. Before he gets that chance, the Commanders have to elevate him for a game or sign him to the 53-man roster. Then Blough can find out whether he gives Daniels another answer on third down and inside the 20, where the windows close faster and timing matters more than a clean workout. Aiyuk's 2023 production gives Washington a reason to find out, but it says little about what he can do this week. Until he shows it against NFL defenders, Washington still has to finish drives with the receivers it already has. The biggest loser is the idea that bringing in Aiyuk has already fixed that problem. title: 5 Things Commanders Fans Can Be Thankful For This Thanksgiving—and 1 Problem They Can’t Ignore
full_text:
As we all sit down for Thanksgiving dinner today, everyone has things to be thankful for, and exactly what varies from person to person. For fans of the Burgundy and Gold, it all starts with the direction the franchise is currently heading. Washington fans aren't dumb and can see right through empty promises made by those in executive positions. They've been scarred by years of "getting it right" under several different coaching staffs, so when one goes 1-4-1 to start year three, they tend to stop listening. Since that start, though, the Commanders have gone 3-1 and are coming off a 22-20 walk-off win over what was the hottest team in the NFL, the Cincinnati Bengals. Then, Wednesday brought an agreement to sign former All-Pro receiver Brandon Aiyuk to the practice squad.
Big things are centered around D.C. and Washington Football again. The 2027 NFL Draft is coming to the nation's capital on April 29–May 1. League and team officials unveiled a countdown clock at Union Station on Monday , with the draft itself planned around the National Mall. The District has also advanced a plan for the RFK campus that includes a proposed new Commanders stadium, with early development expected within the year, as the stadium is scheduled to open in 2030.
Washington is 4-5-1, but take a look at who’s next. The Commanders visit Arizona (3-8) and Tennessee (1-9) before coming home to face Houston (4-6) and Atlanta (3-7). Arizona fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis on Monday , and quarterback Carson Beck missed Wednesday’s practice with back spasms. Josh Johnson is preparing to start if Beck can’t play. None of that wins Sunday’s game for Washington, but if the Commanders can’t improve their record over the next month, it’ll be hard to blame the schedule.
For all the things fans have had reason to complain about this season, giving the ball away hasn’t been high on the list. Washington has turned it over seven times in 10 games and taken it away 14, leaving the Commanders at plus-seven, tied for second in the NFL. Neither team had a turnover Monday, so that margin stayed right where it was. Being 4-5-1 with those numbers tells you there are still things to fix, but at least Washington isn’t handing opponents extra possessions.
Sonny Styles has played every game and leads Washington with 85 tackles. He’s also made five tackles for loss and has a sack, an interception, and a forced fumble. Those aren’t numbers the Commanders are waiting for him to reach someday; he’s put them up in the first 10 games of his career. Antonio Williams caught nine passes for 122 yards Monday, bringing him to 37 receptions for 448 yards and two touchdowns. Drew Stevens made all five of his field-goal attempts against Cincinnati and has hit 19 of his last 20; the NFL named him NFC Special Teams Player of the Week. Williams and Stevens are also two of the four nominees for Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week. Washington has a rookie leading the team in tackles, another leading it in receiving yards, and a kicker who just won a game as time expired. That’s a lot to get from one class this early.
individual player runouts 📈 pic.twitter.com/dLxQkeM7Od
Say what you will, but as my grandfather always told my sister and me, the proof is in the pudding. And when the game is on the line, Daniels flips the switch and hits another level. It's like he gets better when the pressure goes up. Against the Bengals on Monday, Daniels threw for 289 yards and rushed for 55 without turning the ball over. With only 39 seconds and no timeouts to work with, his two completions to Antonio Williams gained all 64 yards Washington needed to set up Drew Stevens’ winning kick. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn framed it perfectly: "It's not on second-and-1 in the second quarter, but it is in the fourth quarter when the game's on the line. And that is when I feel him come to fully express who he is." Commanders fans may not have everything, but when the game comes down to one possession, they can relax knowing they have JD5. One honest concern since Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury is the receiver room and how much actual talent the team has. Washington made a move Wednesday that looks to improve that situation with a player Daniels already knows: Brandon Aiyuk, with the two already spending time together in college at Arizona State. Aiyuk hasn't played an NFL snap since October 2024, though, and Washington still has to find out how much of his old form is left.
Washington moved the ball well enough Monday to do something no NFL team had done in 45 seasons: finish with six straight scoring drives of at least 50 yards . How did that produce just one touchdown? The Commanders went 1-for-4 in the red zone. A false start at Cincinnati’s 13 turned second-and-9 into second-and-14 on one trip, and another reached first-and-goal at the 8 before ending in a field goal. Drew Stevens’ final kick was exactly what Washington needed. Those earlier trips are why they needed him to win the game with no time left. title: Commanders-Cardinals Injury Report: Amik Robertson’s Ankle Revives Washington’s Cornerback Question
full_text:
The Washington Commanders released their first injury report of Week 12 , and while it lists several players, only three carry serious weight right now. Cornerback Amik Robertson was listed as an estimated nonparticipant Wednesday with an injured ankle; receiver Treylon Burks (foot) and defensive lineman Charles Omenihu (rib) were limited, while Stefon Diggs was listed as a nonparticipant for personal reasons. Robertson hurt his ankle on the last play of Friday’s practice and was inactive Monday against Cincinnati . With him out, Rasul Douglas and Trey Amos played all 58 defensive snaps. Fabian Moreau played 10, and Mike Sainristil got four. Thursday’s report will tell us whether Robertson is any closer to playing Sunday. Jayden Daniels’ left hand appeared on the report alongside his left elbow, but he was listed as full. Head coach Dan Quinn said Daniels banged up his non-throwing hand on a scramble against Cincinnati and had some swelling. Quinn said Tuesday that “ it wasn't anything that limited him .” Burks played 49 offensive snaps Monday, and Omenihu played 31 on defense before appearing on this report with a rib issue. Rachaad White (heel) and Sonny Styles (ankle) were listed as full, as were John Bates (shoulder), Quan Martin (shoulder), Andrew Wylie (hip), and Colson Yankoff (knee). White had been questionable against Cincinnati but played. Washington has not issued any game designations for Sunday.
Arizona has its own quarterback question. Carson Beck (back) didn’t practice Wednesday, and head coach Mike LaFleur said Josh Johnson is preparing for another start if Beck can’t play. Beck remains day-to-day. Guard Jon Gaines II (ankle) also sat out after a setback, while linebacker Cody Simon (calf) was limited. Both teams will update their reports Thursday before listing game designations Friday. title: Instant Grade of the Commanders’ Brandon Aiyuk Move
full_text:
ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that after Wednesday's visit and workout, Brandon Aiyuk will join Washington's practice squad, according to Aiyuk's agent Drew Rosenhaus.
Look, we all get it: Brandon Aiyuk hasn't played football since the 2024 season, and his issues with the San Francisco 49ers ended badly. That said, for the Washington Commanders to get a former All-Pro at 28 in their building immediately without using a 53-man roster spot or shifting the roles already on the depth chart is worthy of an A- grade. There are some drawbacks, but a practice-squad deal gives the team time to see what he can still do on a football field. Commanders GM Adam Peters worked in San Francisco's personnel department when the 49ers took Aiyuk with the 25th pick in the first round of the 2020 NFL Draft. He was also there when Aiyuk had 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven TDs before being named a second-team All-Pro just three years later. While Peters was doing his weekly spot on 106.7 The Fan on Wednesday morning, he spoke about why Aiyuk is worth evaluating: "One of the things that I don't think anybody can dispute is his work ethic, and he was one of the hardest workers on the team, and that's how he became an All-Pro type player for us in San Francisco." It certainly helped his case that he and Jayden Daniels are friends and former college teammates. The truth here has always been that Aiyuk has not played a single snap since October 20, 2024, after tearing the ACL, MCL, and meniscus in his right knee. Peters said he hasn't spoken with Aiyuk over the past couple of years, adding: "I think we'd all be foolish to say that he's gonna jump right on where he left off."
Commanders GM Adam Peters talking about the type of impact Brandon Aiyuk might make this season. Peters said, "anytime somebody hasn't played in two years you really have to temper the expectations...he looked really good. He looked like the guy that we knew." pic.twitter.com/7zl4nYqA3L
After Wednesday’s workout, Quinn liked what he saw: "He looked healthy. He looked good. He looked strong and explosive," Quinn said. "You're looking for people who can get in and out of breaks quickly and accelerate. And obviously, those are the things that you want to see. And he demonstrated all that." Peters said the real test is in an NFL practice: “You can't replicate what you do out on the football field in a practice, in an NFL practice, or in an NFL game. So, those are the things we're going to look at and see where he's at.” Once Aiyuk signs, Washington can watch him work against its own defenders, see how quickly he picks up David Blough's offense, and find out what the timing with Daniels looks like now. A practice-squad spot doesn't put him in a game. The Commanders would have to elevate him or sign him to the 53-man roster first. And there's no empty receiver room waiting for him. Antonio Williams just caught nine passes for 122 yards against Cincinnati and played 57 of Washington's 68 offensive snaps . Stefon Diggs and Treylon Burks have their own roles , too. The practice-squad plan lets Washington find out what Aiyuk has left while Williams keeps doing the job he's earned. Washington has seven games left. Give Aiyuk the practice work and see whether he can still help Daniels. If he can, then Commanders head coach Dan Quinn and Blough have a decision to make. For a practice-squad move, I'd take that chance. Follow us on Facebook for the latest Washington Commanders news, injury updates, analysis, and more from Commanders on SI.

title: Commanders News: Two Rookies, One Award, but Jayden Daniels Needs Better Snaps | Burgundy Roundup
full_text:
After their huge win on Monday Night Football, the Washington Commanders have two of the four rookie nominees for this week's Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week award. Antonio Williams caught nine passes for 122 yards, including two clutch plays in the game's final minute , and Drew Stevens made five field goals, including the walk-off game-winner. The other two nominees are Denver's Jonah Coleman and Kansas City's Emmett Johnson; voting ends Thursday at 11 a.m. ET . - Monday's win didn't come without some, let's say, rough spots. Center Lucas Patrick played all 68 offensive snaps, but one thing stood out the entire game: when the Commanders were in shotgun, his snaps had Daniels reaching all over the place. After reviewing the game, Quinn said they felt "inconsistent in terms of location and the speed." Which describes it pretty well.
Lucas Patrick with the ephus snap @PFTCommenter pic.twitter.com/oa6mHumlxt
- Commanders head coach Dan Quinn was asked Tuesday about the viral clip of Stefon Diggs shouting for the ball on Washington’s sideline. His response: "I love his fire. I do. I love what he brings, there's a lot that comes good with it where it can sound like it's mad, but it's like, some energy that comes behind it," Quinn said. "So, I love the competitor. If something didn't feel right, I would certainly step in and address it. But that's not been the case with me." - Apparently, Jayden Daniels injured his non-throwing hand in Monday's 22-20 win over the Bengals. Quinn said Tuesday that Daniels' hand was: "Not lingering, but he definitely did get banged up on the non-throwing side. Just got hit on the scramble that went out of bounds to our offensive right, but it wasn't anything that limited him." - With Amik Robertson sidelined Monday, Rasul Douglas and Trey Amos each played all 58 defensive snaps; Fabian Moreau played 10 and Mike Sainristil four. In other news, the Chicago Bears claimed Isaac Yiadom off waivers from Washington on Tuesday after the Commanders released him when activating running back Jacory "Bill" Croskey-Merritt before the Bengals game. - Some running back snap counts : Bill played 28 offensive snaps in his return, Austin Ekeler added 24, and Rachaad White 15. Quinn said, "We felt we wanted to see if we could get some push inside. In our last game, some of the outside zones just didn't feel as productive as we were hoping they would be. And in this game, we thought the best format for us would get more downhill, and I thought we got more push on those. We had Bill back in, but it was the same true with [RB Austin] Ek [Ekeler] or otherwise. But yeah, we did have more inside and some pullers that went with it as well." - With the pressure on them to produce, the defensive front put in the work despite Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw now being on injured reserve. Tim Settle Jr. had 1.5 sacks and two quarterback hits in 23 defensive snaps. Shy Tuttle played 22 snaps and Jer’Zhan "Johnny" Newton 20. Quinn explained the rotation: "What I've seen, and it was good to see Tim make a play honestly on the first sack of the game. So, I thought I just kinda see him on the improving side. His movements, his mobility, I think coming off the injury, it took time for him to get those movements back. I've always been impressed by Shy, how square he can play. It won't go into the stat sheet much, but the third-down stop that he got underneath before [LB] Frankie [Luvu] got the fourth-down stop was a significant play. [S] Nick Cross ended up hitting the receiver that came into the C-gap on an inside-style run, but Shy had very good leverage inside." "He does a lot on and off the field. He's somebody that's got some leadership to him that the guys follow. So, I've been pleased with what I've seen with him, [DT Jer’Zhan] Newton, Settle, and then [DE Charles] Omenihu on some of the passing downs, playing on the inside. But those are big shoes for those guys to fill. And so, I don't think it was one player but a nice combination of them." - Washington released running back Craig Reynolds from the practice squad Tuesday. While there is no evidence beyond his scheduled meeting with the team on Wednesday, my hunch is that the team opened that practice-squad spot for the recently released Brandon Aiyuk . We'll likely find out more on Wednesday. - The Commanders' next opponent, the Arizona Cardinals, fired their defensive coordinator, Nick Rallis , Monday after the team lost 34-7 to the Kansas City Chiefs. In fact, the team stumbled, gaining only 27 yards on 15 plays across their first four possessions, all of which ended with Tress Way working his magic. After that, Washington scored on their next six possessions: one touchdown and five field goals. NFL Network said the Commanders are the first team in 45 seasons to finish a game with six straight scoring drives of at least 50 yards . That said, the real question here is: how did that much sustained offense still leave Washington behind in the final minute?
The Washington Commanders' Week 11 result served as the team's most cathartic moment of the season, bar none. In fact, you'd have to go back a couple of years to their iconic 2024 campaign to locate a moment that meant as much for their tired fan base as this 22-20 win over the Cincinnati Bengals did, especially after the number of instances in which loyal viewers' hopes had been dashed in identical contexts.

title: Commanders Get Brandon Aiyuk’s First Visit. Monday Night Changed What Awaits Him
full_text:
According to a report by ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Washington Commanders will meet with free-agent wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk on Wednesday. Drew Rosenhaus, Aiyuk's agent, confirmed the visit to Schefter. Washington will be Aiyuk’s first stop, according to the Associated Press . Aiyuk cleared waivers Tuesday afternoon after no team claimed his San Francisco contract, leaving him free to sign anywhere.
Aiyuk last played an NFL game on Oct. 20, 2024, when he tore the ACL, MCL, and meniscus in his right knee. Rosenhaus has said Aiyuk passed a physical in San Francisco and has been running routes on his own. That’s encouraging. ESPN reports Aiyuk is expected to work out during Wednesday’s visit. Washington will get its own look at his movement and conditioning after more than two years away from NFL games. His last full season was 2023, when he earned second-team All-Pro honors. Washington has seven regular-season games left. Aiyuk would have to learn offensive coordinator David Blough’s offense, build timing with Daniels, his former Arizona State teammate ( the two recently spoke ), and get enough practice work to earn a role. That makes Wednesday’s meeting a calendar question, too.
Monday night made that question more interesting. Antonio Williams caught nine passes for 122 yards against the Bengals, including gains of 22 and 42 yards on the final drive that set up rookie kicker Drew Stevens’ winning field goal. Stefon Diggs caught four passes for 45 yards, and Treylon Burks caught two for 30. Williams played 57 of Washington’s 68 offensive snaps Monday . With McLaurin out, the Commanders have reason to examine another receiver, but Williams has already earned a substantial role. Aiyuk’s 2023 resume alone shouldn’t put him ahead of Williams , who has earned the snaps he’s getting.
Antonio Williams had his first career 100 yard game and came through when Washington needed him most. 9 REC, 122 REC YDS, 11 TGT vs Bengals. The third round rookie is starting to make some noise in the OROY conversation. https://t.co/ZMPIVSM2sV pic.twitter.com/ilQUrSPHdc
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport has suggested a practice-squad start , which would let Washington bring Aiyuk into the offense without immediately opening a spot on the 53-man roster. That remains a possibility, not an agreement. It also would not put a date on his first game. Wednesday’s workout could show Washington how close Aiyuk is to playing. Then the Commanders can decide whether to sign him and, if they do, where he starts. title: Alex Ovechkin’s Pregame Moment With Jayden Daniels Was a Passing of the D.C. Torch
full_text:
Alex Ovechkin has worn No. 8 in Washington for more than 20 years, but Monday night’s version was a black Commanders jersey with his name across the back. The Capitals captain joined Jayden Daniels on the field at Northwest Stadium, and the two tossed a football during warmups before Washington played Cincinnati .
Go deep, O #ALLCAPS x #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/6ALwaIW5p5
Ovechkin had worn Daniels’ No. 5 under his suit jacket to a Capitals game in January 2025, the day Washington played Detroit in the NFL playoffs. Three months later, Daniels wore a black Ovechkin jersey to the Capitals’ playoff game against Montreal. He joined Marcus Mariota and Sam Hartman in throwing signed footballs into the crowd, then met Ovechkin after the Capitals won 3-1. Daniels said it was his first hockey game; Ovechkin gave him a signed stick and signed the jersey, too. “A lot of energy. It was dope,” Daniels said of his night . On ESPN’s Monday Night Countdown , Ovechkin told Pat McAfee and Jason Kelce that D.C. is “ my second home .” He said he has supported Washington’s football team since coming to the city. Ovechkin led the Capitals to their first Stanley Cup in 2018 and became the NHL’s all-time goals leader in 2025. When he began his 22nd season in October, he passed Senators legend Walter Johnson as the longest-tenured athlete in D.C. professional sports. He also announced that this will be his last season in the NHL. Ovechkin spiked the ceremonial spear before kickoff and told the ESPN hosts he hoped Washington would win. He got his wish, though Daniels and the Commanders made him wait: kicker Drew Stevens hit a 26-yard field goal as time expired to beat Cincinnati 22-20 .
